Allah the Exalted says, praising His noble Self and commending Himself for creating the heavens and the earth as a dwelling for His servants, and for making the darknesses and the light a benefit for His servants in their nights and their days. He gathered the word "darknesses" in the plural and made "light" singular, because it is more noble, as He said: ﴿Of the right and of the left﴾ [al-Nahl: 48]. And as He said at the end of this surah: ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow the [other] ways, for they will separate you from His way﴾ [al-An'am: 153].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾, meaning: despite all this, some of His servants disbelieve in Him, and they set up with Him partners and equals, and they took for Him a consort and offspring, exalted is He far above that by a great exaltation.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿It is He who created you from clay﴾, meaning: your father Adam, who is your origin, from whom they came forth, then they spread out to the east and the west.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then He decreed a term, and a term specified with Him﴾, Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ means death, ﴿and a term specified with Him﴾ means the Hereafter.

Similarly it is narrated from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Zayd ibn Aslam, 'Atiyyah, al-Suddi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and others.

As for the saying of al-Hasan, in one report from him: ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ he said: what lies between one's creation and one's death; ﴿and a term specified with Him﴾, what lies between one's death and one's resurrection. This returns to what has preceded, namely the determination of the specific term, which is the lifespan of each person, and the determination of the general term, which is the entire lifespan of this world, then its ending, its conclusion, its passing away and its transfer, and the arrival at the Hereafter.

And from Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid: ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ means the duration of this world, ﴿and a term specified with Him﴾ means the lifespan of a person until the time of his death. It seems this is derived from His saying after this: ﴿And it is He who takes you in sleep at night and knows what you have committed by day. Then He revives you therein that a specified term may be fulfilled. Then to Him is your return﴾ [al-An'am: 60], and the verse that follows.

'Ata' said, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ means sleep, in which He takes the soul, and then it returns to its owner upon waking; ﴿and a term specified with Him﴾ means the term of a person's death. This is a strange opinion.

As for the meaning of His saying ﴿with Him﴾: that is, none knows it except Him, as in His saying: ﴿Its knowledge is only with my Lord; none will reveal it at its time except Him﴾ [al-A'raf: 187], and as in His saying: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when is its arrival? In what are you of mention of it? To your Lord is its finality﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 42-44].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then you [still] doubt﴾, al-Suddi and others said: meaning you doubt concerning the matter of the Hour.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And He is Allah in the heavens and on the earth; He knows your secret and your open, and He knows what you earn﴾, the interpreters of this verse have differing opinions, after agreeing on the refutation of the view of the first Jahmiyyah, who said that He, exalted is He far above what they say, is in every place, for they interpreted the verse according to that. The most sound of the opinions is that He is the one worshipped in the heavens and on the earth, that is, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth worships Him, affirms His oneness, and acknowledges His divinity, and they call Him Allah, and they call upon Him in hope and in fear, except those among the jinn and mankind who disbelieve. * *

As for His saying: ﴿and He knows what you earn﴾, meaning all of their deeds, the good and the bad of them.

[In A: "tabaqu" (they covered).] [Al-Faqih Muhammad ibn Rizq Tarhuni, in his book Mawsu'at Fada'il al-Qur'an (1/258), said: "The narration has in its chain three who are weak in memorization, namely those mentioned before Asma'. Besides this, there are other defects:

The first: the phrase "on a journey" entered into it from the narration about the revelation of al-Ma'idah, transmitted by Ahmad and others from Layth, on the authority of Shahr, on the authority of Asma', where she said: "I was indeed holding the halter of al-'Adba', the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when al-Ma'idah was revealed to him in its entirety, and it nearly struck the camel's shoulder with its weight." Ahmad narrated it (6/455): Abu al-Nadr narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah, i.e. Shaybān, narrated to us, on the authority of Layth.

The second: the mention here of the revelation of al-An'am is in fact from Layth or Shahr, and Shurayk has no part in it. It was narrated by Ahmad ibn Mani' (see Ittihaf al-Mahara, 74/b/4) and al-Tabarani (24/178), and Ibn Mardawayh (see al-Durr, 3/2). Ibn Kathir, God knows best, quoted it suspended from his own tafsir (3/233), through the path of Layth, on the authority of Shahr, on the authority of Asma', who said: "Surah al-An'am was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) all at once, while I was holding the halter of the Prophet's (ﷺ) she-camel, and its weight was so great that it nearly broke the camel's bones." Sufyan al-Thawri and Ishaq ibn Yusuf narrated from Layth. What comes through this path is the mention of the revelation of al-Ma'idah, as already stated, and the error entered into it on the part of Layth or Shahr. Asma's narration concerns the period after the Hijrah, certainly, while al-An'am is Meccan without disagreement. Had it not been that the weight of al-Ma'idah is not a special merit of it alone, but rather applies to the Qur'an as a whole, I would have mentioned the supporting reports of Asma's narration in that regard at Surah al-Ma'idah.

The third: Shurayk erred in attributing the narration to Asma'; it is in fact one of the mursal reports of Shahr. Ishaq ibn Rahawayh narrated it in his Musnad (265/a/4): Jarir informed us, on the authority of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab: "Surah al-An'am was revealed with a roar of angels who had filled the lowest heaven to the earth." In its chain are Layth and Shahr, both weak due to their memory. Al-Firyabi and 'Abd ibn Humayd also narrated it (see al-Durr, 3/3)."]] And al-Suddi, on the authority of Murrah, on the authority of 'Abd Allah, said: Surah al-An'am was revealed, accompanied by seventy thousand angels.

A similar report was transmitted by another route from Ibn Mas'ud.

Al-Hakim said in his Mustadrak: Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Hafiz and Abu al-Fadl al-Hasan ibn Ya'qub al-'Adl narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab al-'Abdi narrated to us, Ja'far ibn 'Awn informed us, Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Suddi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to us, on the authority of Jabir, who said: When Surah al-An'am was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) glorified Allah, then said: "Indeed, seventy thousand angels escorted this surah, filling the horizon." Then he said: Sahih according to the condition of Muslim. [Al-Mustadrak (2/314). Al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (no. 2431) narrated it through al-Hakim. Al-Dhahabi criticised al-Hakim, saying: "No, by Allah, Ja'far al-Suddi did not meet him, and I think this is fabricated." I say: It meets the condition of Muslim regarding contemporaneity, for al-Suddi died in 127 AH and Ja'far ibn 'Awn was born in 109 AH, so a meeting between them is possible. Al-Dhahabi's statement, "I think it is fabricated," has no basis, for the narrators of this chain are narrators of Muslim, so upon whom is the blame?!]

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Durustawayh al-Farisi narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Salim narrated to us, Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us, 'Umar ibn Talhah al-Raqqashi narrated to me, on the authority of Nafi' ibn Malik Abi Suhayl, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Surah al-An'am was revealed with an escort of angels, filling what lies between the two horizons; for them is a roar of glorification, and the earth quakes beneath them," while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was saying: "Glory be to Allah the Mighty, glory be to Allah the Mighty." [Al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (no. 2434) and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat (no. 3317) narrated it through various routes from Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Salim. Its chain includes Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Salim, whom I do not know.]

Then Ibn Mardawayh narrated, from al-Tabarani, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Na'ilah, on the authority of Isma'il ibn 'Amr, on the authority of Yusuf ibn 'Atiyyah, on the authority of Ibn 'Awn, on the authority of Nafi', on the authority of Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: "Surah al-An'am was revealed to me all at once, and seventy thousand angels escorted it, with a roar of glorification and praise." [Al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat (no. 3316) and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (3/44) narrated it through Ibrahim ibn Na'ilah. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/20): "It contains Yusuf ibn 'Atiyyah al-Saffar, who is weak."]

* *

Allah the Exalted says, praising His noble Self and commending Himself for creating the heavens and the earth as a dwelling for His servants, and for making the darknesses and the light a benefit for His servants in their nights and their days. He gathered the word "darknesses" in the plural and made "light" singular, because it is more noble, as He said: ﴿Of the right and of the left﴾ [al-Nahl: 48]. And as He said at the end of this surah: ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow the [other] ways, for they will separate you from His way﴾ [al-An'am: 153].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾, meaning: despite all this, some of His servants disbelieve in Him, and they set up with Him partners and equals, and they took for Him a consort and offspring, exalted is He far above that by a great exaltation.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿It is He who created you from clay﴾, meaning: your father Adam, who is your origin, from whom they came forth, then they spread out to the east and the west.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then He decreed a term, and a term specified with Him﴾, Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ means death, ﴿and a term specified with Him﴾ means the Hereafter.

Similarly it is narrated from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Zayd ibn Aslam, 'Atiyyah, al-Suddi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and others.

As for the saying of al-Hasan, in one report from him: ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ he said: what lies between one's creation and one's death; ﴿and a term specified with Him﴾, what lies between one's death and one's resurrection. This returns to what has preceded, namely the determination of the specific term, which is the lifespan of each person, and the determination of the general term, which is the entire lifespan of this world, then its ending, its conclusion, its passing away and its transfer, and the arrival at the Hereafter.

And from Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid: ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ means the duration of this world, ﴿and a term specified with Him﴾ means the lifespan of a person until the time of his death. It seems this is derived from His saying after this: ﴿And it is He who takes you in sleep at night and knows what you have committed by day. Then He revives you therein that a specified term may be fulfilled. Then to Him is your return﴾ [al-An'am: 60], and the verse that follows.

'Ata' said, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ means sleep, in which He takes the soul, and then it returns to its owner upon waking; ﴿and a term specified with Him﴾ means the term of a person's death. This is a strange opinion.

As for the meaning of His saying ﴿with Him﴾: that is, none knows it except Him, as in His saying: ﴿Its knowledge is only with my Lord; none will reveal it at its time except Him﴾ [al-A'raf: 187], and as in His saying: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when is its arrival? In what are you of mention of it? To your Lord is its finality﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 42-44].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then you [still] doubt﴾, al-Suddi and others said: meaning you doubt concerning the matter of the Hour.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And He is Allah in the heavens and on the earth; He knows your secret and your open, and He knows what you earn﴾, the interpreters of this verse have differing opinions, after agreeing on the refutation of the view of the first Jahmiyyah, who said that He, exalted is He far above what they say, is in every place, for they interpreted the verse according to that. The most sound of the opinions is that He is the one worshipped in the heavens and on the earth, that is, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth worships Him, affirms His oneness, and acknowledges His divinity, and they call Him Allah, and they call upon Him in hope and in fear, except those among the jinn and mankind who disbelieve. This verse, according to this view, is like His saying: ﴿And He is the one who is God in the heaven and God on the earth﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 84], meaning He is the God of those in the heaven and the God of those on the earth. On this view, His saying ﴿He knows your secret and your open﴾ is either a predicate or a circumstantial clause.

The second opinion: that the meaning is that Allah is the One who knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, of secret and open. Thus His saying ﴿He knows﴾ is connected to His saying ﴿in the heavens and on the earth﴾; its sense being: And He is Allah, who knows your secret and your open in the heavens and on the earth, and He knows what you earn.

The third opinion: that His saying ﴿And He is Allah in the heavens﴾ is a complete pause, and then the statement resumes: ﴿and on the earth He knows your secret and your open, and He knows what you earn.﴾ This is the choice of Ibn Jarir.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and He knows what you earn﴾, meaning all of their deeds, the good and the bad of them.

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Allah, exalted is He, says, reporting about the polytheists who deny and are obstinate: Whenever a sign (āyah) comes to them, that is, a proof, a miracle, or an argument from among the indications of the Lord's oneness, exalted and majestic is He, and of the truthfulness of His noble messengers, they turn away from it. They do not reflect upon it, and they pay it no heed.

Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed they have denied the truth when it came to them, so there will come to them the news of that which they used to mock.﴾ This is a threat and a severe warning to them for their denial of the truth, that the news of what they are engaged in of denial will surely reach them, and they will certainly find its consequence, and they will certainly taste its harm.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said, admonishing and warning them, that there may befall them from the punishment and worldly retribution what befell their likes and counterparts among the earlier generations, who were stronger than them, greater in number, and greater in wealth, children, and in exploiting the earth and cultivating it. So He said: ﴿Did they not see how many generations We destroyed before them, whom We had established on the earth as We have not established you?﴾ That is, in wealth, children, lifespans, wide prestige, abundance, and armies. ﴿And We sent down the heaven upon them in abundant rain.﴾

That is, one thing after another. ﴿And We made rivers flow beneath them.﴾ That is, We increased for them the rains of the sky and the springs of the earth, meaning as a gradual lead-on and respite for them. ﴿Then We destroyed them for their sins.﴾ That is, for their wrongs and their evil deeds which they committed. ﴿And We brought into being after them another generation.﴾ That is, the earlier ones passed away like yesterday's passing, and We made them into tales. ﴿And We brought into being after them another generation.﴾ That is, another age, so that We might test them; they did like their deeds, so they perished as those had perished. So beware, O you who are addressed, lest there befall you what befell them, for you are not more honored in the sight of Allah than they were, and the Messenger whom you denied is more honored in the sight of Allah than their messenger; so you are more deserving of punishment and of the swift hastening of retribution than they were, were it not for His gentleness and His kindness.

Ibn Kathir said, in his commentary on verses 7–11 of Surah al-An'am:

Allah the Exalted says, informing about the disbelief of the polytheists, their obstinacy, their stubborn denial of the truth, their deception, and their disputing about it: ﴿And if We had sent down to you a written document on paper, and they had touched it with their hands﴾, meaning they had witnessed it, seen it descend, and handled it directly, ﴿the ones who disbelieved would have said, "This is nothing but obvious magic."﴾ This is like what Allah the Exalted said, informing about their denial of what is perceptible to the senses: ﴿And even if We opened for them a gate from the heaven and they kept ascending through it, they would say, "Our eyes have only been dazzled. Rather, we are a people bewitched."﴾ [Al-Hijr: 14, 15]. And He said: ﴿And if they saw a piece of the sky falling, they would say, "It is just layered clouds."﴾ [At-Tur: 44].

﴿And they said, "Why has an angel not been sent down to him?"﴾ [meaning, so that he would be a warner with him] [[Addition from A.]] Allah said: ﴿And if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and then they would not be reprieved.﴾ That is, if the angels descended in their own form, the punishment from Allah would have come upon them, as He said: ﴿We do not send down the angels except with truth, and they would not then be given respite.﴾ [Al-Hijr: 8], [and] [[Addition from A.]] He said: ﴿On the Day they see the angels, there will be no good news that Day for the criminals, and they will say, "A barrier forbidden [to be crossed]."﴾ [[Addition from M, A; in H: "the verse".]] [Al-Furqan: 22].

* *

As for His statement: ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man and would have confused them as they now confuse themselves﴾, meaning: if We had sent down an angel along with the human Messenger, that is, if We had sent to mankind a Messenger who was an angel, he would have appeared in the form of a man so that they could understand his address and benefit by taking knowledge from him. And if that were the case, the matter would have been confused for them, just as they confuse themselves [[In D, M: "as they themselves are confused".]] regarding accepting the message of a human being. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "If there had been upon the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down to them from the sky an angel as a messenger."﴾ [Al-Isra': 95]. Among the mercy of Allah the Exalted toward His creation is that He sends to each kind of creature messengers from among them, so that some may call others, and so that some may benefit from others in address and questioning, as He said: ﴿Allah has certainly conferred favor upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from themselves, reciting to them His verses and purifying them﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 164], and the rest of the verse.

Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His statement ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man﴾, the verse, that he said: "If an angel came to them, he would come to them only in the form of a man, because they would not be able to look at the angels in their light." ﴿And We would have confused them as they confuse themselves﴾, meaning: We would have mixed up for them what they mix up. Al-Walibi reported from him: "And We would have made them uncertain."

* *

As for His statement: ﴿And messengers before you were certainly mocked, but those who mocked them were enveloped by what they used to mock﴾, this is consolation for His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) regarding the denial of those among his people who denied him, and a promise to him and to the believers in him of victory and a good outcome in this world and the Hereafter.

Then He said: ﴿Say, "Travel through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers."﴾ That is, reflect upon yourselves, and consider what Allah brought down upon the earlier generations who denied His messengers and opposed them, of punishment, retribution, and chastisement in this world, along with what He has stored up for them of painful punishment in the Hereafter, and how He saved His messengers and the believing servants.

(593), from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, may Allah be pleased with him.] Therefore He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants﴾, meaning: He is the One before whom necks submit, before whom the tyrants are humbled, before whom faces are abased, who subdues everything, to whom all creatures are subservient, and before the greatness of whose majesty, pride, magnificence, exaltedness and power all things humble themselves, become meek and are reduced to nothing before Him and under His judgment and dominion.

﴿And He is the All-Wise﴾, meaning: in all that He does, ﴿the All-Aware﴾ of the places and loci of things, so He gives only to those who deserve, and withholds only from those who deserve to be withheld.

Then He said: ﴿Say: "What thing is greatest in testimony?"﴾, meaning: who is the greatest of things in testimony? ﴿Say: "Allah is Witness between me and you."﴾, meaning: He is the One who knows what I have brought to you and what you say to me. ﴿And this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches﴾, meaning: he is a warner to everyone it reaches, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever among the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place﴾ [Hud: 17].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Waki' and Abu Usamah and Abu Khalid narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ubaydah, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, regarding His saying: ﴿and whoever it reaches﴾ [he said]: whoever the Qur'an reaches, it is as if he has seen the Prophet ﷺ — Abu Khalid added: "and spoken with him."

Ibn Jarir narrated it through the route of Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: whoever the Qur'an has reached, Muhammad ﷺ has indeed conveyed to him.

Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿that I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches﴾: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Convey from Allah; whoever has received a verse of the Book of Allah, then the command of Allah has reached him."

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: It is incumbent upon whoever follows the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to call (to Allah) as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called, and to warn as he warned.

* *

His saying: ﴿Do you indeed testify that there are other gods with Allah?﴾ [O you polytheists]. ﴿Say: "I do not testify."﴾ As He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if they testify, then do not testify with them﴾ [al-An'am: 150]. ﴿Say: "He is but one God, and indeed I am free from what you associate."﴾

Then He said, informing about the People of the Book: they recognize this which you have brought to them just as they recognize their sons, through what they have from the reports and narratives about the earlier messengers and prophets, for all the messengers gave good tidings of the existence of Muhammad ﷺ, his sending, his description, his land, his emigration, and the description of his community. For this reason He said after this: ﴿Those who have lost themselves﴾, meaning: they have lost with complete loss, ﴿so they do not believe﴾ in this clear, manifest matter which the prophets gave good tidings of and which was mentioned in ancient and recent times.

Then He said: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His signs?﴾, meaning: there is no one more unjust than one who fabricates against Allah, claiming that Allah sent him when Allah had not sent him; then there is no one more unjust than one who denies the signs of Allah, His proofs, His evidences and His indications. ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed﴾, meaning: neither this one nor that one will succeed, neither the fabricator nor the denier.

The Most High says, reporting about the polytheists: ﴿And on the Day We gather them all﴾ (the Day of Resurrection), He will ask them about the idols and the rivals they used to worship besides Him, saying [to them] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] ﴿Where are your partners whom you used to claim?﴾ As He said in Surat al-Qasas: ﴿And on the Day He calls to them and says, "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ [Verse 62].

* *

As for His words, ﴿Then their fitnah will be nothing﴾, meaning: their argument (hujjah). 'Ata' al-Khurasani reported from Ibn 'Abbas: meaning their excuse (ma'dhirah). Qatadah also said the same. Ibn Jurayj reported from Ibn 'Abbas: meaning their statement (qiyl). Al-Dahhak also said the same.

'Ata' al-Khurasani said: ﴿Then their fitnah will be nothing﴾, meaning their trial when they were tested, ﴿except that they will say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."﴾

Ibn Jarir said: "The correct reading is: 'Then their statement will not be [[In manuscript A: "تكن"]] at the time of Our testing them [[In manuscript M: "فتنتهما"]] except as an excuse for the shirk they had committed against Allah, ﴿except that they will say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."﴾" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/300).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Yahya al-Razi narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Abi Qays, from Mutarrif, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A man came to him and said, "O Abu 'Abbas [[In manuscripts M and A: "O Ibn 'Abbas."]], I heard Allah say: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.﴾" He said: As for His words, ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾, they saw that none would enter Paradise except the people of prayer, so they said, "Come, let us deny," and so they deny. Then Allah seals their mouths, and their hands and feet bear witness, and they cannot conceal from Allah a single word. "Is there now anything in your heart? There is nothing in the Qur'an except that something has been revealed about it, but you do not know its meaning [[In manuscript A: "ترك"]]." [[In manuscript A: "لا يعلمون".]]

Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas: This [verse] is about the hypocrites.

But this is open to question, for this verse is Makki (revealed in Mecca), whereas the hypocrites existed only in Madinah. The verse revealed about the hypocrites is the verse of al-Mujadilah: ﴿On the Day Allah will raise them all, and they will swear to Him as they swear to you, and they think they are upon something. Unquestionably, they are the liars﴾ [Al-Mujadilah: 18]. Similarly, about these [polytheists] He said: ﴿See how they have lied against themselves, and what they used to invent has strayed from them﴾, as He said: ﴿Then it will be said to them, "Where is that which you used to associate besides Allah?" They will say, "They have strayed from us," [rather, we did not used to invoke anything before. Thus Allah leaves astray the disbelievers]﴾ [Ghafir: 73–74].

* *

As for His words, ﴿And among them are those who listen to you, but We have placed over their hearts coverings so they do not understand it, and in their ears deafness. And if they should see every sign, they will not believe in it﴾: meaning, they come to you to hear your recitation, but it benefits them nothing, because Allah has placed ﴿over their hearts coverings﴾, meaning veils, so that they do not comprehend the Qur'an, ﴿and in their ears deafness﴾, meaning deafness to beneficial hearing. They are, as He said: ﴿And the example of those who disbelieve is like one who calls out to that which hears nothing but a call and a cry; deaf, dumb, and blind, so they do not reason﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 171].

* *

As for His words, ﴿And if they should see every sign, they will not believe in it﴾, meaning: however many signs, proofs and clear arguments they see, they will not believe in them. For them there is neither understanding nor fairness, as He said: ﴿And had Allah known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while they were refusing﴾ [Al-Anfal: 23].

* *

As for His words, ﴿Until, when they come to you disputing with you﴾, meaning they argue with you and contend with you about the truth using falsehood, ﴿the disbelievers say, "This is not but the myths of the former peoples."﴾ Meaning: what you have brought is only taken from the books of the ancients and transmitted from them.

* *

* *

* *

As for His words, ﴿And they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves﴾: regarding the meaning of ﴿they forbid others from it﴾ there are two opinions. The first: that it means they forbid people from following the truth, from believing the Messenger, and from submitting to the Qur'an, and they keep away from it themselves, meaning they both keep away from it and do not allow anyone who would benefit to benefit. They combine the two ugly acts: they do not benefit, and they do not let anyone benefit, [and they keep away] [[Addition from manuscripts M and A.]]. Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: The disbelievers of Quraysh would not come to the Prophet ﷺ, and they would forbid [others] from him.

Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and others besides them said the same. This view is more apparent, and Allah knows best, and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir.

The second opinion: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated it from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from one who heard Ibn 'Abbas say about His words, ﴿And they forbid others from it﴾: "It was revealed about Abu Talib, who used to forbid people from the Prophet ﷺ, lest he be harmed." [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (11/313) and by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/315) through the chain of Sufyan.]] Likewise al-Qasim ibn Mukhaymirah, Habib ibn Abi Thabit and 'Ata' ibn Dinar said: it was revealed about Abu Talib. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

The Most High says, reporting about the polytheists: ﴿And on the Day We gather them all﴾ (the Day of Resurrection), He will ask them about the idols and the rivals they used to worship besides Him, saying [to them] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] ﴿Where are your partners whom you used to claim?﴾ As He said in Surat al-Qasas: ﴿And on the Day He calls to them and says, "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ [Verse 62].

* *

'Ata' al-Khurasani said: ﴿Then their fitnah will be nothing﴾, meaning their trial when they were tested, ﴿except that they will say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."﴾

Ibn Jarir said: "The correct reading is: 'Then their statement will not be [[In manuscript A: "تكن"]] at the time of Our testing them [[In manuscript M: "فتنتهما"]] except as an excuse for the shirk they had committed against Allah, ﴿except that they will say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."﴾" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/300).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Yahya al-Razi narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Abi Qays, from Mutarrif, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A man came to him and said, "O Abu 'Abbas [[In manuscripts M and A: "O Ibn 'Abbas."]], I heard Allah say: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.﴾" He said: As for His words, ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾, they saw that none would enter Paradise except the people of prayer, so they said, "Come, let us deny," and so they deny. Then Allah seals their mouths, and their hands and feet bear witness, and they cannot conceal from Allah a single word. "Is there now anything in your heart? There is nothing in the Qur'an except that something has been revealed about it, but you do not know its meaning [[In manuscript A: "ترك"]]." [[In manuscript A: "لا يعلمون".]]

The Almighty describes the state of the disbelievers when they stand on the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. They see its chains and shackles and witness with their own eyes these great and terrifying matters. At that moment they say, ﴿Would that we could be sent back, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers.﴾ They wish to be returned to the worldly abode so that they may do righteous deeds, not deny the signs of their Lord, and become believers.

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Nay, but there has become apparent to them what they used to conceal before.﴾ That is: rather, there became apparent to them then what they had concealed within themselves of disbelief, denial and obstinacy, even if they denied it in the world or in the Hereafter, as He said shortly before this: ﴿Then their trial will be only that they will say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists." Look how they lied against themselves.﴾

It is also possible that what became apparent to them was what they had known within themselves of the truthfulness of what the Messengers brought in the world, even though they used to show their followers the opposite. Allah, the Exalted, said, reporting about Musa (Moses) that he said to Fir'awn (Pharaoh): ﴿You know well that none sent these down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as evidence﴾ [Al-Isra: 102]. And He said, reporting about Fir'awn and his people: ﴿And they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance﴾ [An-Naml: 14].

It is also possible that the intended people here are the hypocrites who used to show faith to the people while concealing disbelief. In that case this is a report of what will happen on the Day of Resurrection from the speech of a group of the disbelievers. This does not conflict with the fact that this surah is Meccan, since hypocrisy was only found among some people of Madinah and the Bedouins around it. Allah has mentioned the occurrence of hypocrisy in a Meccan surah, which is Al-'Ankabut, where He said: ﴿Allah will surely make known those who believe, and He will surely make known the hypocrites﴾ [Al-'Ankabut: 11]. On this view, it is a report about the state of the hypocrites in the Hereafter, when they witness the punishment, and then there becomes apparent to them the outcome of what they used to conceal of disbelief, opposition and hypocrisy. And Allah knows best.

As for the meaning of the transition (al-idrab) in His saying ﴿Nay, but there has become apparent to them what they used to conceal before﴾: they did not request to return to the world out of desire and love for faith, but out of fear of the punishment they witnessed as the recompense for the disbelief they had been upon. So they asked to be returned to the world in order to escape what they had seen of the Fire. For this reason He said: ﴿And if they were returned, they would revert to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars.﴾ That is, in their wish to be returned, out of desire and love for faith, they are liars.

Then He said, reporting about them: if they were returned to the worldly abode, they would revert to what they were forbidden [of disbelief and opposition] ﴿and indeed they are liars﴾. That is, in their saying: ﴿Would that we could be sent back, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers.﴾ ﴿And they said, "There is no life but our worldly life, and we will not be resurrected."﴾ That is: they would revert to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars, and they would say: ﴿There is no life but our life﴾, meaning there is nothing but this worldly life, with no return after it. For this reason He said: ﴿and we will not be resurrected.﴾

Then He said: ﴿If only you could see when they are made to stand before their Lord.﴾ That is, they will be made to stand before Him. He said: ﴿Is this not the truth?﴾ That is, is this Resurrection not true, and not false as you used to think? ﴿They will say, "Yes, by our Lord." He will say, "Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve."﴾ That is, for what you used to deny. ﴿Taste it today.﴾ ﴿Is this magic, or do you not see?﴾ [At-Tur: 15]

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

Allah, exalted is He, informs us about the loss of the one who denied the meeting with Allah, and about his disappointment when the Hour comes upon him suddenly, and about his regret over what he neglected of deeds and what he committed in advance of ugly actions. Thus He says: ﴿Until, when the Hour comes upon them suddenly, they will say, "O our regret over what we neglected concerning it!"﴾

This pronoun (in "concerning it") may refer back to the life of this world, or to the deeds, or to the Hereafter, i.e., concerning its matter.

* *

His saying ﴿while they carry their burdens upon their backs. Unquestionably, evil is what they carry!﴾ means: they bear them. Qatadah said: they do (i.e., they perform them).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Khalid narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Qays, from Abu Marzuq, who said: The disbeliever, or the wicked person, is met when he comes out of his grave by the most hideous form he has ever seen and the foulest smell, and he says, "Who are you?" It says, "Do you not recognize me?" He says, "No, by Allah, except that Allah has made your face ugly and your smell foul." It says, "I am your evil deed. Thus you were in the world, of evil deeds and foul stench. You rode upon me much in the world; come, I will ride you." This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿while they carry their burdens upon their backs. Unquestionably, evil is what they carry!﴾

[Footnote: This narration is mursal, and Abu Marzuq al-Tujibi — Ibn Hibban said: it is not permissible to use as proof what he alone narrated. This report is also transmitted as a statement (mawquf) on 'Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i without mention of Abu Marzuq. Al-Tabari narrated it in his tafsir (11/327) from Ibn Humayd, from al-Hakam ibn Bashir, from 'Amr with the same wording.]

And Asbat narrated from al-Suddi that he said: There is no wrongdoing man who dies and enters his grave except that there comes to him a man with an ugly face, black in color, foul in smell, wearing filthy clothes, until he enters the grave with him. * *

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

Allah, exalted is He, informs us about the loss of the one who denied the meeting with Allah, and about his disappointment when the Hour comes upon him suddenly, and about his regret over what he neglected of deeds and what he committed in advance of ugly actions. Thus He says: ﴿Until, when the Hour comes upon them suddenly, they will say, "O our regret over what we neglected concerning it!"﴾

This pronoun (in "concerning it") may refer back to the life of this world, or to the deeds, or to the Hereafter, i.e., concerning its matter.

* *

His saying ﴿while they carry their burdens upon their backs. Unquestionably, evil is what they carry!﴾ means: they bear them. Qatadah said: they do (i.e., they perform them).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Khalid narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Qays, from Abu Marzuq, who said: The disbeliever, or the wicked person, is met when he comes out of his grave by the most hideous form he has ever seen and the foulest smell, and he says, "Who are you?" It says, "Do you not recognize me?" He says, "No, by Allah, except that Allah has made your face ugly and your smell foul." It says, "I am your evil deed. Thus you were in the world, of evil deeds and foul stench. You rode upon me much in the world; come, I will ride you." This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿while they carry their burdens upon their backs. Unquestionably, evil is what they carry!﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, they do not deny you, but it is the wrongdoers who deny the signs of Allah﴾, meaning: they do not accuse you of lying in reality. ﴿But it is the wrongdoers who deny the signs of Allah﴾, meaning: rather, they obstinately oppose the truth and push it away with their chests. This is as Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Najiyah ibn Ka'b, from 'Ali [may Allah be pleased with him][[Addition from A.]], who said: Abu Jahl said to the Prophet ﷺ: "We do not deny you, but we deny what you have brought." So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, they do not deny you, but it is the wrongdoers who deny the signs of Allah﴾. [[Related by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 4064, through Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham, from Sufyan with this chain, and al-Tirmidhi said: "This is more authentic." Al-Tabari in his Tafsir (11/334) also related it through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, and Yahya ibn Adam followed him, from Sufyan, as a mursal report.]]

Al-Hakim also related it through the route of Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, and then said: "Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not include it." Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn al-Wazir al-Wasiti narrated to us in Makkah; Bishr ibn al-Mubashshir al-Wasiti narrated to us, from Salam ibn Miskin, from Abu Yazid al-Madani: that the Prophet ﷺ met Abu Jahl and shook his hand. A man said to him: "Do I not see you shaking hands with this Sabi'?" [[The word used is "al-Sabi'," which here refers to one who has left his religion.]] He said: "By Allah, I know that he is indeed a Prophet, but when were we ever followers of the Banu 'Abd Manaf?" Abu Yazid then recited: ﴿Indeed, they do not deny you, but it is the wrongdoers who deny the signs of Allah﴾.

Abu Salih and Qatadah said: "They know that you are the Messenger of Allah, but they deny (it)."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated, from al-Zuhri, the story of Abu Jahl when he came at night to listen to the recitation of the Prophet ﷺ, together with Abu Sufyan Sakhr ibn Harb and al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, each one not aware of the others. They listened until morning. When dawn broke they dispersed, but the road brought them together. Each said to the others: "What brought you here?" Each told the others what had brought him. Then they agreed among themselves not to return, for they feared the knowledge of the young men of Quraysh about them, lest they be tempted by their coming. But when the second night came, each of them came, supposing that his two companions would not come, because of the earlier agreements. When they woke up, the road brought them together again, and they reproached one another. Then they agreed not to return. When the third night came, they came again. When they awoke, they agreed not to return to the like of it [then they dispersed][[Addition from A.]].

When morning came, al-Akhnas ibn Shariq took his staff and went out until he came to Abu Sufyan ibn Harb in his house. He said: "Tell me, O Abu Hanzalah, your opinion about what you heard from Muhammad." He said: "O Abu Tha'labah, by Allah, I heard things that I recognise and I know what is meant by them, and I heard things whose meaning I did not understand and I do not know what is meant by them." Al-Akhnas said: "By Him by whom you swore, I too (felt the same)."

Then he left him and went to Abu Jahl, entered upon him in his house, and said: "O Abu al-Hakam, what is your opinion about what you heard from Muhammad?" He said: "What did I hear? We and the Banu 'Abd Manaf competed for honour. They gave food and we gave food; they bore burdens and we bore burdens; they gave gifts and we gave gifts, until when we were neck and neck on our knees, like two horses in a race, they said: 'Among us is a Prophet to whom revelation comes from heaven! When will we attain this?' By Allah, we will never believe in him or accept him." He said: Then al-Akhnas got up from him and left him. [[Sirat Ibn Ishaq, no. 232, ed. al-Maghrib.]]

Ibn Jarir narrated, through the route of Asbat, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿We know indeed that what they say grieves you... But it is the wrongdoers who deny the signs of Allah﴾: When the day of Badr came, al-Akhnas ibn Shariq said to the Banu Zuhrah: "O Banu Zuhrah, Muhammad is your sister's son, so you have the most right to restrain yourselves from him. If he is a Prophet, you will not fight him today; and if he is a liar, you have the most right to refrain from your sister's son. Stop here until I meet Abu al-Hakam. If Muhammad is overcome, you will return safe, and if Muhammad prevails, your people will not do anything to you." That day al-Akhnas was named (the name he had been given was "Ubayy"). Al-Akhnas met Abu Jahl and was alone with him, and said: "O Abu al-Hakam, tell me about Muhammad: is he truthful or a liar? There is no one here from Quraysh except you and me to hear our conversation." Abu Jahl said: "Woe to you! By Allah, Muhammad is truthful, and Muhammad has never lied; but when the Banu Qusayy take the banner, the watering rights, the chamberlainship and the prophethood, what will remain for the rest of Quraysh?" That is His saying: ﴿But it is the wrongdoers who deny the signs of Allah﴾. The signs of Allah are Muhammad ﷺ.

* *

Then help came to them in this world, just as they will have help in the Hereafter. Therefore He said: ﴿And none can alter the words of Allah﴾, that is, the words He decreed concerning victory in this world and the Hereafter for His believing servants, as He said: ﴿And Our word has already preceded to Our servants, the messengers, that they would indeed be given victory, and that Our soldiers would indeed be the victorious﴾ [al-Saffat: 171–173], and He said: ﴿Allah has decreed: "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers." Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 21].

* *

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "al-Nafaq is a passage (al-sarb), so that you might go into it, ﴿and bring them a sign﴾, or make for yourself a ladder into the sky so that you might ascend in it and bring them a sign better than what you have brought them—then do it." 

Qatadah, al-Suddi and others said likewise.

If he is a Prophet, you will not fight him today; and if he is a liar, you have the most right to refrain from your sister's son. Stop here until I meet Abu al-Hakam. If Muhammad is overcome, you will return safe, and if Muhammad prevails, your people will not do anything to you." That day al-Akhnas was named (the name he had been given was "Ubayy"). Al-Akhnas met Abu Jahl and was alone with him, and said: "O Abu al-Hakam, tell me about Muhammad: is he truthful or a liar? There is no one here from Quraysh except you and me to hear our conversation." Abu Jahl said: "Woe to you! By Allah, Muhammad is truthful, and Muhammad has never lied; but when the Banu Qusayy take the banner, the watering rights, the chamberlainship and the prophethood, what will remain for the rest of Quraysh?" That is His saying: ﴿But it is the wrongdoers who deny the signs of Allah﴾. The signs of Allah are Muhammad ﷺ.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And messengers before you were denied, but they were patient over what they were denied and harmed, until Our help reached them. [And none can alter the words of Allah]﴾ [[Addition from M.]]: This is a consolation for the Prophet ﷺ and a comfort to him regarding those of his people who denied him, and a command to him to be patient as the steadfast messengers (ulu al-'azm) were patient, and a promise to him of victory as they were victorious, and of triumph until the final outcome was theirs, after what they suffered of denial from their peoples and grievous harm. Then help came to them in this world, just as they will have help in the Hereafter. Therefore He said: ﴿And none can alter the words of Allah﴾, that is, the words He decreed concerning victory in this world and the Hereafter for His believing servants, as He said: ﴿And Our word has already preceded to Our servants, the messengers, that they would indeed be given victory, and that Our soldiers would indeed be the victorious﴾ [al-Saffat: 171–173], and He said: ﴿Allah has decreed: "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers." Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 21].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And there has certainly come to you some of the news of the messengers﴾, meaning: some of their reports, how they were helped and strengthened against those of their peoples who denied them. You have in them an example and a model.

Then He said: ﴿And if their turning away has been difficult for you﴾, meaning: if their turning away from you has been hard upon you, ﴿then if you are able to seek a tunnel in the earth or a ladder into the sky﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "al-Nafaq is a passage (al-sarb), so that you might go into it, ﴿and bring them a sign﴾, or make for yourself a ladder into the sky so that you might ascend in it and bring them a sign better than what you have brought them—then do it." 

Qatadah, al-Suddi and others said likewise.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance, so do not be among the ignorant﴾. This is as He said: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, all those upon the earth would have believed, all of them together. Then would you compel the people until they become believers?﴾ [[Addition from M, A; in H: "the verse."]] [Yunus: 99]. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance﴾: He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was eager that all people would believe and follow him (or pledge allegiance to him) upon guidance, so Allah informed him that none believes except those for whom happiness has already been decreed by Allah in the Primordial Decree (al-dhikr al-awwal).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Only those who listen will respond﴾, meaning: only those who hear the speech, understand it and comprehend it will respond to your call, O Muhammad. This is like His saying: ﴿That he may warn whoever is alive and that the word may be justified against the disbelievers﴾ [Ya-Sin: 70]. As for His saying: ﴿And the dead—Allah will resurrect them﴾, He means by this the disbelievers, for they are dead of heart, so Allah likened them to the dead of body and said: ﴿And the dead—Allah will resurrect them; then to Him they will be returned﴾. This is a form of mockery toward them and contempt for them.

The Lord, exalted is He, says, consoling His Prophet ﷺ regarding his people's denial of him and their opposition to him: ﴿We know indeed that what they say grieves you﴾, meaning: We have certainly encompassed with knowledge their denial of you, and your sorrow and grief over them. ﴿So let not your soul waste away in regret over them﴾ [Fatir: 8]. As He said in another verse: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not believe﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 3], and ﴿So perhaps you would consume yourself with grief over their traces, if they do not believe in this message﴾ [al-Kahf: 7].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, they do not deny you, but it is the wrongdoers who deny the signs of Allah﴾, meaning: they do not accuse you of lying in reality. ﴿But it is the wrongdoers who deny the signs of Allah﴾, meaning: rather, they obstinately oppose the truth and push it away with their chests. This is as Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Najiyah ibn Ka'b, from 'Ali [may Allah be pleased with him][[Addition from A.]], who said: Abu Jahl said to the Prophet ﷺ: "We do not deny you, but we deny what you have brought." So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, they do not deny you, but it is the wrongdoers who deny the signs of Allah﴾. [[Related by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 4064, through Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham, from Sufyan with this chain, and al-Tirmidhi said: "This is more authentic." Al-Tabari in his Tafsir (11/334) also related it through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, and Yahya ibn Adam followed him, from Sufyan, as a mursal report.]]

Al-Hakim also related it through the route of Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, and then said: "Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not include it." [[Al-Mustadrak (2/315). Al-Dhahabi criticised this, saying: "They (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not include anything from Najiyah ibn Ka'b."]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn al-Wazir al-Wasiti narrated to us in Makkah; Bishr ibn al-Mubashshir al-Wasiti narrated to us, from Salam ibn Miskin, from Abu Yazid al-Madani: that the Prophet ﷺ met Abu Jahl and shook his hand. A man said to him: "Do I not see you shaking hands with this Sabi'?" [[The word used is "al-Sabi'," which here refers to one who has left his religion.]] He said: "By Allah, I know that he is indeed a Prophet, but when were we ever followers of the Banu 'Abd Manaf?" Abu Yazid then recited: ﴿Indeed, they do not deny you, but it is the wrongdoers who deny the signs of Allah﴾.

Abu Salih and Qatadah said: "They know that you are the Messenger of Allah, but they deny (it)."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated, from al-Zuhri, the story of Abu Jahl when he came at night to listen to the recitation of the Prophet ﷺ, together with Abu Sufyan Sakhr ibn Harb and al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, each one not aware of the others. They listened until morning. When dawn broke they dispersed, but the road brought them together. Each said to the others: "What brought you here?" Each told the others what had brought him. Then they agreed among themselves not to return, for they feared the knowledge of the young men of Quraysh about them, lest they be tempted by their coming. But when the second night came, each of them came, supposing that his two companions would not come, because of the earlier agreements. When they woke up, the road brought them together again, and they reproached one another. Then they agreed not to return. When the third night came, they came again. When they awoke, they agreed not to return to the like of it [then they dispersed][[Addition from A.]].

When morning came, al-Akhnas ibn Shariq took his staff and went out until he came to Abu Sufyan ibn Harb in his house. He said: "Tell me, O Abu Hanzalah, your opinion about what you heard from Muhammad." He said: "O Abu Tha'labah, by Allah, I heard things that I recognise and I know what is meant by them, and I heard things whose meaning I did not understand and I do not know what is meant by them." Al-Akhnas said: "By Him by whom you swore, I too (felt the same)."

Then he left him and went to Abu Jahl, entered upon him in his house, and said: "O Abu al-Hakam, what is your opinion about what you heard from Muhammad?" He said: "What did I hear? We and the Banu 'Abd Manaf competed for honour. They gave food and we gave food; they bore burdens and we bore burdens; they gave gifts and we gave gifts, until when we were neck and neck on our knees, like two horses in a race, they said: 'Among us is a Prophet to whom revelation comes from heaven! When will we attain this?' By Allah, we will never believe in him or accept him." He said: Then al-Akhnas got up from him and left him. [[Sirat Ibn Ishaq, no. 232, ed. al-Maghrib.]]

They were also being obstinate, as they said: ﴿We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth﴾, and the verses that follow (Al-Isra': 90).

For if He sent it down according to what they asked, and they then did not believe, He would have hastened their punishment, as He did with the earlier nations. As Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them. We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her. And We send the signs only as a warning﴾ (Al-Isra': 59). And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿If We willed, We could send down upon them a sign from the sky, and their necks would remain humbled before it﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara': 4).

* *

His saying: ﴿There is no creature on the earth, nor bird that flies with its two wings, but they are communities like you﴾. Mujahid said: That is, kinds classified and known by their names. Qatadah said: The birds are a community, mankind is a community, and the jinn are a community. As-Suddi said: ﴿but they are communities like you﴾ means: creatures like you.

* *

His saying: ﴿We have neglected nothing in the Book﴾. That is, the knowledge of all of them is with Allah, and He does not overlook any one of them in regard to its provision and its management, whether it is on land or at sea. As He said: ﴿There is no creature on the earth but that its provision is upon Allah, and He knows its place of rest and its place of storage; all is in a clear Record﴾ (Hud: 6). That is, clearly set out with their names, their numbers, and their places, and comprehensive of their movements and their stillness. Allah the Exalted also said: ﴿And how many a creature does not carry its provision; Allah provides for it and for you, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ (Al-'Ankabut: 60).

Al-Hafiz (the memorizer, a title for a leading hadith scholar) Abu Ya'la said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Ubayd ibn Waqid al-Qaysi Abu 'Abbad narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn Kaysan narrated to me, Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to us, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: Locusts became scarce in one of the years of 'Umar's rule, may Allah be pleased with him. He asked about them, but was not informed of anything, and he became worried about this. So he sent a rider to such-and-such a place, another to Syria, and another to Iraq, asking: Has any locust been seen or not? The rider who had gone toward Yemen came to him with a handful of locusts and threw them before him. When he saw them he said "Allahu akbar" three times, then said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, say: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created a thousand communities, six hundred of them in the sea and four hundred on land. The first of these communities to perish is the locust, and when it perishes they follow one another like the beads of a necklace when its string is cut."
[Musnad Abi Ya'la al-Kabir, as cited in Majma' al-Zawa'id (7/322); also related by Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (5/352) and al-Khatib in Tarikh Baghdad (11/218) through 'Ubayd ibn Waqid from Muhammad ibn 'Isa. Its chain contains 'Ubayd ibn Waqid and Muhammad ibn 'Isa, both of whom are weak.]

* *

His saying: ﴿Then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from his father, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿Then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾, he said: Their gathering is their death.

Similarly, Ibn Jarir related it through the route of Isra'il, from Sa'id, from Masruq, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The death of the beasts is their gathering. Al-'Awfi also related it from him.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It has also been related from Mujahid and ad-Dahhak, the same.

The second view is that their gathering is their resurrection on the Day of Resurrection, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾ (At-Takwir: 5).

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sulayman, from Mundhir ath-Thawri, from some of their shaykhs, from Abu Dharr, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, saw two goats butting each other, and said: "O Abu Dharr, do you know why they are butting?" He said: No. He said: "But Allah knows, and He will judge between them."
[Al-Musnad (5/162). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/352): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih, but there is a narrator who is unnamed."]

'Abd ar-Razzaq also related it, from Ma'mar, from al-A'mash, from one whom he named, from Abu Dharr, who said: While I was with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, two she-goats butted each other, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, said: "Do you know why they butted?" They said: We do not know. He said: "But Allah knows, and He will judge between them." Ibn Jarir related it, then related it through the route of Mundhir ath-Thawri, from Abu Dharr, and mentioned it, adding: Abu Dharr said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, left us, and no bird flapped its two wings in the sky without his having given us knowledge of it.
[Tafsir 'Abd ar-Razzaq (1/200) and Tafsir at-Tabari (11/348).]

'Abdullah ibn Imam Ahmad said in the Musnad of his father: 'Abbas ibn Muhammad and Abu Yahya al-Bazzar narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj ibn Nusayr narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-'Awwam ibn Maradim (or Muzahim), from the Banu Qays ibn Tha'labah, from Abu 'Uthman an-Nahdi, from 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, said: "Indeed the hornless one will take retribution from the horned one on the Day of Resurrection."
[Al-Musnad (1/72). Its chain contains Hajjaj ibn Nusayr, who is weak. It has a supporting report from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, which is the following hadith.]

'Abd ar-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, from Abu Hurayrah, concerning His saying: ﴿But they are communities like you. We have neglected nothing in the Book. Then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾. He said: All creatures will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection: the beasts, the animals, the birds, and everything. Allah's justice will be such on that day that He will take retribution for the hornless one from the horned one. Then He will say: "Be dust." It is for this reason that the disbeliever says: ﴿Would that I had been dust!﴾ (An-Naba': 40). This has also been related as a marfu' report (traced directly to the Prophet) in the hadith of the Trumpet.
[Tafsir 'Abd ar-Razzaq (1/200), and from his route at-Tabari in his Tafsir (11/347).]

* *

His saying: ﴿Those who deny Our signs are deaf and dumb, in darknesses﴾. That is, their likeness in their ignorance, their lack of knowledge, and their lack of understanding is like a person who is deaf, who does not hear, and dumb, who does not speak, and who is also in darkness and cannot see. How could such a person find the way, or be brought out of what he is in? As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Their likeness is that of one who kindled a fire, and when it lit up what was around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darknesses, not seeing. Deaf, dumb, blind, so they do not return﴾ (Al-Baqarah: 17–18). And as Allah [the Exalted] said: ﴿Or like darknesses in a deep sea, covered by waves, above which are waves, above which are clouds: darknesses, one above another. If he extends his hand, he can hardly see it. And whomever Allah does not give light, for him there is no light﴾ (An-Nur: 40). For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whomever Allah wills, He leaves astray; and whomever He wills, He places on a straight path﴾. That is, He is the one who disposes of His creation as He wills.

They said: We do not know. He said: "But Allah knows, and He will judge between them." Ibn Jarir related it, then related it through the route of Mundhir ath-Thawri, from Abu Dharr, and mentioned it, adding: Abu Dharr said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, left us, and no bird flapped its two wings in the sky without his having given us knowledge of it.
[Tafsir 'Abd ar-Razzaq (1/200) and Tafsir at-Tabari (11/348).]

[Al-Musnad (1/72). Its chain contains Hajjaj ibn Nusayr, who is weak. It has a supporting report from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, which is the following hadith.]

'Abd ar-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, from Abu Hurayrah, concerning His saying: ﴿But they are communities like you. * *

His saying: ﴿Those who deny Our signs are deaf and dumb, in darknesses﴾. That is, their likeness in their ignorance, their lack of knowledge, and their lack of understanding is like a person who is deaf, who does not hear, and dumb, who does not speak, and who is also in darkness and cannot see. How could such a person find the way, or be brought out of what he is in? As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Their likeness is that of one who kindled a fire, and when it lit up what was around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darknesses, not seeing. Deaf, dumb, blind, so they do not return﴾ (Al-Baqarah: 17–18). And as Allah [the Exalted] said: ﴿Or like darknesses in a deep sea, covered by waves, above which are waves, above which are clouds: darknesses, one above another. If he extends his hand, he can hardly see it. And whomever Allah does not give light, for him there is no light﴾ (An-Nur: 40). For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whomever Allah wills, He leaves astray; and whomever He wills, He places on a straight path﴾. That is, He is the one who disposes of His creation as He wills.

Allah the Exalted says, reporting about the polytheists, that they used to say: ﴿Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord?﴾ That is, a miraculous sign conforming to what they wanted. They were also being obstinate, as they said: ﴿We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth﴾, and the verses that follow (Al-Isra': 90).

﴿Say: Indeed, Allah is able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know.﴾ That is, He, the Exalted, is able to do that, but His wisdom requires that it be delayed. For if He sent it down according to what they asked, and they then did not believe, He would have hastened their punishment, as He did with the earlier nations. As Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them. We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her. And We send the signs only as a warning﴾ (Al-Isra': 59). And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿If We willed, We could send down upon them a sign from the sky, and their necks would remain humbled before it﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara': 4).

* *

His saying: ﴿There is no creature on the earth, nor bird that flies with its two wings, but they are communities like you﴾. Mujahid said: That is, kinds classified and known by their names. Qatadah said: The birds are a community, mankind is a community, and the jinn are a community. As-Suddi said: ﴿but they are communities like you﴾ means: creatures like you.

* *

His saying: ﴿We have neglected nothing in the Book﴾. That is, the knowledge of all of them is with Allah, and He does not overlook any one of them in regard to its provision and its management, whether it is on land or at sea. As He said: ﴿There is no creature on the earth but that its provision is upon Allah, and He knows its place of rest and its place of storage; all is in a clear Record﴾ (Hud: 6). That is, clearly set out with their names, their numbers, and their places, and comprehensive of their movements and their stillness. Allah the Exalted also said: ﴿And how many a creature does not carry its provision; Allah provides for it and for you, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ (Al-'Ankabut: 60).

Al-Hafiz (the memorizer, a title for a leading hadith scholar) Abu Ya'la said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Ubayd ibn Waqid al-Qaysi Abu 'Abbad narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn Kaysan narrated to me, Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to us, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: Locusts became scarce in one of the years of 'Umar's rule, may Allah be pleased with him. He asked about them, but was not informed of anything, and he became worried about this. So he sent a rider to such-and-such a place, another to Syria, and another to Iraq, asking: Has any locust been seen or not? The rider who had gone toward Yemen came to him with a handful of locusts and threw them before him. When he saw them he said "Allahu akbar" three times, then said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, say: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created a thousand communities, six hundred of them in the sea and four hundred on land. The first of these communities to perish is the locust, and when it perishes they follow one another like the beads of a necklace when its string is cut."
[Musnad Abi Ya'la al-Kabir, as cited in Majma' al-Zawa'id (7/322); also related by Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (5/352) and al-Khatib in Tarikh Baghdad (11/218) through 'Ubayd ibn Waqid from Muhammad ibn 'Isa. Its chain contains 'Ubayd ibn Waqid and Muhammad ibn 'Isa, both of whom are weak.]

* *

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It has also been related from Mujahid and ad-Dahhak, the same.

* *

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, 'Iraq ibn Khalid ibn Yazid narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Ibrahim ibn Abi 'Ablah, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit [may Allah be pleased with him], that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: "Indeed Allah [Blessed and Exalted], when He wants a people to endure, or to flourish, provides them with moderation and chastity.
