As for His saying: ﴿We send the messengers only as bearers of good tidings and warners﴾, meaning: bearers of good tidings to the believing servants of Allah of good things, and warners to those who disbelieve in Allah of retributions and punishments. For this reason He, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿Whoever believes and makes amends﴾, meaning: whoever's heart believes in what they brought and whose deeds are made righteous by following them. ﴿There will be no fear for them﴾, meaning, regarding what lies ahead of them, ﴿nor will they grieve﴾, meaning, regarding what has escaped them and what they left behind them of worldly affairs and their pursuits. Allah is their protector regarding what they left behind, and their guardian regarding what they abandoned.

Then He says: ﴿And those who deny Our signs, the punishment will touch them for their defiance.﴾ Meaning: punishment will befall them because they disbelieved in what the messengers brought, departed from the commands and obedience of Allah, committed His prohibitions and forbidden matters, and violated His sacred limits.

Allah says to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): Say to these deniers, the obstinate ones: ﴿Tell me, if Allah were to take away your hearing and your sight﴾, meaning, deprive you of them just as He gave them to you, ﴿who is the god other than Allah who could bring them back to you?﴾ Then He says: ﴿Say: "It is He who brought you into being and made for you hearing, sight and hearts; little are you grateful."﴾ [Al-Mulk: 23]

It is possible that this is an expression for preventing them from benefiting from these faculties in the legally prescribed way. For this reason He says: ﴿and sets a seal upon your hearts﴾, just as He says: ﴿Or who controls hearing and sight?﴾ [Yunus: 31], and He says: ﴿And know that Allah comes between a man and his heart﴾ [Al-Anfal: 24].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿What god other than Allah could bring it back to you?﴾, meaning: Is there anyone other than Allah who is able to return that to you once Allah has taken it from you? No one besides Him is able to do so. For this reason He, exalted is His majesty, says: ﴿See how We vary the signs﴾, meaning, We explain them, make them clear and expound them, as evidence that there is no god but Allah, and that what they worship besides Him is false and misguidance. ﴿Yet still they turn away﴾, meaning: despite this clarification, they turn away from the truth and bar people from following it.

Al-Awfi related from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿yasdifun﴾ means "they deviate." Mujahid and Qatadah said: "they turn away." As-Suddi said: "they bar (others)."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Say: "Tell me, if the punishment of Allah comes upon you suddenly﴾, meaning, while you are unaware of it until it overtakes and surprises you. ﴿Or openly﴾, meaning, visibly and plainly, ﴿will any be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?﴾, meaning: Only those who wrong themselves by associating others with Allah, exalted and mighty is He, will be destroyed, while those who worshipped Allah alone, with no partner, will be saved: ﴿no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve.﴾ As Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing—for them is security, and they are guided.﴾ [Al-An'am: 82]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿We send the messengers only as bearers of good tidings and warners﴾, meaning: bearers of good tidings to the believing servants of Allah of good things, and warners to those who disbelieve in Allah of retributions and punishments. For this reason He, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿Whoever believes and makes amends﴾, meaning: whoever's heart believes in what they brought and whose deeds are made righteous by following them. ﴿There will be no fear for them﴾, meaning, regarding what lies ahead of them, ﴿nor will they grieve﴾, meaning, regarding what has escaped them and what they left behind them of worldly affairs and their pursuits. Allah is their protector regarding what they left behind, and their guardian regarding what they abandoned.

Then He says: ﴿And those who deny Our signs, the punishment will touch them for their defiance.﴾ Meaning: punishment will befall them because they disbelieved in what the messengers brought, departed from the commands and obedience of Allah, committed His prohibitions and forbidden matters, and violated His sacred limits.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verses 50–54 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Say: I do not tell you that with me are the treasures of Allah﴾, meaning: I do not possess them, nor do I dispose of them. ﴿Nor do I know the unseen﴾, meaning: nor do I say that I know the unseen. That belongs only to the knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; I have access to none of it except what He makes me aware of. ﴿Nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾, meaning: I do not claim to be an angel. I am only a human being among mankind, to whom revelation comes from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He has honoured me with it and bestowed His favour upon me by it. Therefore He said: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾, meaning: I do not深 deviate from it by a hand's breadth or less.

﴿Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?﴾ meaning: are those who follow the truth and are guided to it equal to those who have strayed from it and have not submitted to it? ﴿Will you not then reflect?﴾ This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Is he who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth equal to one who is blind? Only people of understanding take heed﴾ [al-Ra'd: 19].

* *

His saying: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, having besides Him no protector and no intercessor﴾, meaning: warn, O Muhammad, by this Qur'an those ﴿who fear their Lord in awe﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 57], and those who ﴿fear their Lord and dread the evil of the reckoning﴾ [al-Ra'd: 21].

﴿Those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿They will have, on that day, besides Him, no protector and no intercessor﴾, meaning: they will have no relative and no intercessor who can save them from His punishment, should He intend it for them. ﴿That perhaps they will fear Allah﴾, meaning: warn of this Day, on which no judge exists except Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿that perhaps they will fear Him﴾, so that they act in this world with deeds by which Allah will save them from His punishment on the Day of Resurrection, and multiply for them His abundant reward.

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance﴾, meaning: do not push away from yourself those characterised by this quality; rather, make them your companions and your intimates, as He said: ﴿And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance, and let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life; and do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who follows his desire and whose affair has been [ever] in neglect﴾ [al-Kahf: 28].

* *

His saying: ﴿who call upon their Lord﴾, meaning: who worship Him and ask Him. ﴿Morning and evening﴾: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Mujahid, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: what is meant by this is the obligatory prayers.

This is like His saying: ﴿And your Lord says: Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾ [Ghafir: 60], meaning: I will accept from you.

* *

His saying: ﴿seeking His countenance﴾, meaning: they seek by that deed the noble Countenance of Allah. Thus they are sincere in what they do of acts of worship and obedience.

* *

His saying: ﴿You are not accountable for their account at all, nor are they accountable for yours at all﴾, as Nuh (peace be upon him) said in reply to those who said: ﴿Shall we believe you when the lowest people follow you?﴾ He said: ﴿And I have no knowledge of what they used to do. Their account is only upon my Lord, if you could perceive﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 112–113], meaning: their account is only with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and I am not accountable for their account at all, just as they are not accountable for my account at all.

* *

His saying: ﴿So that you would drive them away and thereby be among the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: if you were to do this in such a state.

Imam Ahmad said: Asbat, that is Ibn Muhammad, narrated to us: Ash'ath narrated to us, from Kurdus, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while with him were Khabbab, Suhayb, Bilal and 'Ammar. They said: O Muhammad, are you content with these? Then the Qur'an was revealed concerning them: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ [al-An'am: 53].

[Al-Musnad (1/420). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/21): "The narrators of Ahmad are the narrators of the Sahih, except Kurdus, who is trustworthy."]

Ibn Jarir also narrated it through the route of Ash'ath, from Kurdus, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while with him were Suhayb, Bilal, 'Ammar, Khabbab and others of the weak among the Muslims. They said: O Muhammad, are you content with these from your people? Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us? Should we be followers of these? Drive them away from you, for perhaps if you drive them away, we will follow you. So this verse was revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance﴾, and ﴿Thus We have tried some of them through others﴾, up to the end of the verse.

[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/374).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated to us: 'Amr ibn Muhammad al-'Anqazi narrated to us: Asbat ibn Nasr narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Sa'id al-Azdi, who was the reciter of the Azd, from Abu al-Kanud, from Khabbab, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾. He said: al-Aqra' ibn Habis al-Tamimi and 'Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari came and found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sitting with Suhayb, Bilal, 'Ammar and Khabbab, along with some of the weak among the believers. When they saw them around the Prophet (ﷺ), they belittled them. They came to him, spoke to him privately and said: We wish that you would set aside for us a gathering with you, by which the Arabs would recognise our merit, for the delegations of the Arabs come to you, and we are ashamed that the Arabs should see us sitting with these slaves. When we come to you, remove them from us; and when we have finished, sit with them if you wish. He said: "Yes." They said: Then write for us a document against yourself. He said: So he called for the parchment and called 'Ali to write, while we were sitting in a corner. Then Jibril descended and said: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord [morning and evening, seeking His countenance. You are not accountable for their account at all, nor are they accountable for yours at all, so that you would drive them away and thereby be among the wrongdoers]﴾. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) threw down the parchment, then called us, and we came to him.

[Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Asbat, with the same chain. Ibn Majah also narrated it in al-Sunan, no. (4127), through the route of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Qattan with the same chain, and al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/276): "This chain is sahih."]

This is a strange hadith (gharib), for this verse is Meccan, while al-Aqra' ibn Habis and 'Uyayna only embraced Islam long after the Hijrah.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh, from his father, who said: Sa'd said: This verse was revealed concerning six of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), among them Ibn Mas'ud. He said: We used to hasten to the Prophet (ﷺ), draw near to him and listen to him, and Quraysh said: These people are brought closer than us. So it was revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾.

[Al-Hakim narrated it in his al-Mustadrak through the route of Sufyan and said: "It is according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim)." Ibn Hibban also narrated it in his Sahih through the route of al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh, with the same chain.] [Al-Mustadrak (3/319).]

* *

His saying: ﴿And thus We have tried some of them through others﴾, meaning: We tested, examined and tried some of them through others, ﴿that they might say: Is it these whom Allah has favoured from among us?﴾ That is because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the beginning of his mission was mostly followed by the weak of the people, men and women, slaves and maidservants, while only a few of the nobles followed him. Just as the people of Nuh said to Nuh: ﴿And we see not following you except those who are the lowest among us, at first thought﴾ [Hud: 27], and as Heraclius, the king of the Romans, said to Abu Sufyan when he asked him those questions, saying to him: Did the weak of the people follow him, or their nobles? He said: Rather, the weak among them. He said: They are the followers of the messengers.

[The story is in Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (7), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him.]

The point is that the polytheists of Quraysh used to mock those of their weak who believed and would torment whomever among them they could. They used to say: ﴿Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?﴾ That is, Allah would not guide these people to good, if what they had come to were good, and leave us, as they said: ﴿Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 11]. And as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieved say to those who believed: Which of the two groups is better in position and finer in assembly?﴾ [Maryam: 73].

Allah, Exalted, said in reply to that: ﴿And how many generations before them have We destroyed, who were better in appearance and in show﴾ [Maryam: 74]. And He said in reply to them when they said: ﴿Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?﴾: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾, meaning: is He not most knowing of those who are grateful to Him, by their words, their deeds and their inner selves? So He grants them success, guides them to the paths of peace, brings them out of darkness into light, and guides them to Himself on a straight path, as He, Exalted, said: ﴿And those who strive for Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways, and indeed Allah is with the doers of good﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 69]. And in the sahih hadith: "Indeed Allah does not look at your forms, nor at your colours, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds."

[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2564).]

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim narrated to us: al-Husayn narrated to us: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ikrimah, concerning His saying: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, having besides Him no protector or intercessor, that they may become righteous. And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face﴾ to His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ He said: Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah, Mut'im ibn 'Adi, al-Harith ibn Nawfal, and Qaraza ibn 'Abd 'Amr ibn Nawfal came, among the nobles of the Banu 'Abd Manaf from the people of disbelief, to Abu Talib and said: "O Abu Talib, if only your nephew Muhammad would drive away from himself our clients (mawali) and our allies (hulafa'), for they are only our slaves and our lowly ones, it would be greater in our hearts, more obedient to him among us, closer to our following him, and to our affirming him."

He said: So Abu Talib came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him what they had said to him. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "If you did that, you would see what they want and where their talk leads." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, having besides Him no protector or intercessor, that they may become righteous. And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾

He said: They were Bilal, 'Ammar ibn Yasir, Salim the client of Abu Hudhayfah, Suhayb the client of Usayd, and from the allies: Ibn Mas'ud, al-Miqdad ibn 'Amr, Mas'ud ibn al-Qari, Waqid ibn 'Abd Allah al-Handhali, 'Amr ibn 'Abd 'Amr, Dhu'sh-Shimalayn, and Marthad ibn Abi Marthad, and Abu Marthad was from Ghanm, an ally of Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, and their likes among the allies.

And it was revealed concerning the leaders of disbelief among the Quraysh, the clients and the allies: ﴿And thus We tried some of them through others, that they might say, "Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?"﴾ the verse. When it was revealed, 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, came and apologized for his statement, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And when those who believe in Our verses come to you [say, "Peace be upon you"]﴾ the verse.

* *

His saying: ﴿And when those who believe in Our verses come to you, say, "Peace be upon you."﴾ means: honor them by returning their greeting, and give them good news of Allah's vast mercy, which encompasses them. Therefore He said: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾, meaning He made it obligatory upon His noble Self, out of His bounty, kindness and generosity. ﴿That whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾. Some of the salaf (righteous predecessors) said: Everyone who disobeys Allah is ignorant.

Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman said, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrimah, concerning His saying: ﴿whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾: "The whole world is ignorance." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

﴿Then repents after that and makes amends﴾, meaning: he turns back from what he was upon of sins, gives them up, resolves not to return to them, and makes his action right in the future. ﴿Then indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: "This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us," saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah finished creating the creation, He wrote in His Book, which is with Him above the Throne: 'Indeed My mercy has overcome My wrath.'" It is recorded by the two Shaykhs in their Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). Likewise, al-A'mash narrated it from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, and Musa ibn 'Uqbah narrated it from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah. Similarly al-Layth and others narrated it from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, with the same wording.

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated, through the route of al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah has finished judging between the creatures, He will bring out a book from beneath the Throne: 'Indeed My mercy has preceded My wrath, and I am the Most Merciful of the merciful.' Then He will take a handful or two handfuls and bring out from the Fire a people who did no good, written between their eyes: 'Freed by Allah.'"

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from 'Asim ibn Sulayman, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman, concerning His saying: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾, he said: "We find in the Torah two passages: that Allah created the heavens and the earth, and created one hundred mercies (or: made one hundred mercies) before He created the creation. Then He created the creation and placed among them one mercy, and kept with Himself ninety-nine mercies. By it they show mercy to one another, by it they show compassion, by it they give to one another, by it they visit one another, by it the she-camel yearns for her young, by it the cow lows, by it the sheep bleats, by it the birds follow one another, and by it the fish follow one another in the sea. When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will gather that mercy together with what He has, and His mercy is more excellent and more vast."

This has been narrated as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) through another route: Muslim recorded it in his Sahih (no. 2753) through the route of Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah has one hundred mercies. From them is one mercy by which the creatures show mercy to one another, and ninety-nine are for the Day of Resurrection."

Many hadiths agreeing with these will come at His saying: ﴿My mercy encompasses all things﴾ [al-A'raf: 156].

Among the hadiths that also suit this noble verse is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ to Mu'adh ibn Jabal: "Do you know what the right of Allah upon the servants is?" That they worship Him and do not associate anything with Him. Then he said: "Do you know what the right of the servants upon Allah is when they do that?" That He will not punish them. It is recorded by al-Bukhari (no. 7373) and Muslim (no. 30). Imam Ahmad also narrated it through the route of Kumayl ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verses 50–54 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Say: I do not tell you that with me are the treasures of Allah﴾, meaning: I do not possess them, nor do I dispose of them. ﴿Nor do I know the unseen﴾, meaning: nor do I say that I know the unseen. That belongs only to the knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; I have access to none of it except what He makes me aware of. ﴿Nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾, meaning: I do not claim to be an angel. I am only a human being among mankind, to whom revelation comes from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He has honoured me with it and bestowed His favour upon me by it. Therefore He said: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾, meaning: I do not深 deviate from it by a hand's breadth or less.

﴿Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?﴾ meaning: are those who follow the truth and are guided to it equal to those who have strayed from it and have not submitted to it? ﴿Will you not then reflect?﴾ This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Is he who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth equal to one who is blind? Only people of understanding take heed﴾ [al-Ra'd: 19].

* *

His saying: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, having besides Him no protector and no intercessor﴾, meaning: warn, O Muhammad, by this Qur'an those ﴿who fear their Lord in awe﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 57], and those who ﴿fear their Lord and dread the evil of the reckoning﴾ [al-Ra'd: 21].

﴿Those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿They will have, on that day, besides Him, no protector and no intercessor﴾, meaning: they will have no relative and no intercessor who can save them from His punishment, should He intend it for them. ﴿That perhaps they will fear Allah﴾, meaning: warn of this Day, on which no judge exists except Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿that perhaps they will fear Him﴾, so that they act in this world with deeds by which Allah will save them from His punishment on the Day of Resurrection, and multiply for them His abundant reward.

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance﴾, meaning: do not push away from yourself those characterised by this quality; rather, make them your companions and your intimates, as He said: ﴿And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance, and let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life; and do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who follows his desire and whose affair has been [ever] in neglect﴾ [al-Kahf: 28].

* *

His saying: ﴿who call upon their Lord﴾, meaning: who worship Him and ask Him. ﴿Morning and evening﴾: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Mujahid, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: what is meant by this is the obligatory prayers.

This is like His saying: ﴿And your Lord says: Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾ [Ghafir: 60], meaning: I will accept from you.

* *

His saying: ﴿seeking His countenance﴾, meaning: they seek by that deed the noble Countenance of Allah. Thus they are sincere in what they do of acts of worship and obedience.

* *

His saying: ﴿You are not accountable for their account at all, nor are they accountable for yours at all﴾, as Nuh (peace be upon him) said in reply to those who said: ﴿Shall we believe you when the lowest people follow you?﴾ He said: ﴿And I have no knowledge of what they used to do. Their account is only upon my Lord, if you could perceive﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 112–113], meaning: their account is only with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and I am not accountable for their account at all, just as they are not accountable for my account at all.

* *

His saying: ﴿So that you would drive them away and thereby be among the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: if you were to do this in such a state.

Imam Ahmad said: Asbat, that is Ibn Muhammad, narrated to us: Ash'ath narrated to us, from Kurdus, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while with him were Khabbab, Suhayb, Bilal and 'Ammar. They said: O Muhammad, are you content with these? Then the Qur'an was revealed concerning them: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ [al-An'am: 53].

[Al-Musnad (1/420). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/21): "The narrators of Ahmad are the narrators of the Sahih, except Kurdus, who is trustworthy."]

Ibn Jarir also narrated it through the route of Ash'ath, from Kurdus, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while with him were Suhayb, Bilal, 'Ammar, Khabbab and others of the weak among the Muslims. They said: O Muhammad, are you content with these from your people? Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us? Should we be followers of these? Drive them away from you, for perhaps if you drive them away, we will follow you. So this verse was revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance﴾, and ﴿Thus We have tried some of them through others﴾, up to the end of the verse.

[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/374).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated to us: 'Amr ibn Muhammad al-'Anqazi narrated to us: Asbat ibn Nasr narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Sa'id al-Azdi, who was the reciter of the Azd, from Abu al-Kanud, from Khabbab, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾. He said: al-Aqra' ibn Habis al-Tamimi and 'Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari came and found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sitting with Suhayb, Bilal, 'Ammar and Khabbab, along with some of the weak among the believers. When they saw them around the Prophet (ﷺ), they belittled them. They came to him, spoke to him privately and said: We wish that you would set aside for us a gathering with you, by which the Arabs would recognise our merit, for the delegations of the Arabs come to you, and we are ashamed that the Arabs should see us sitting with these slaves. When we come to you, remove them from us; and when we have finished, sit with them if you wish. He said: "Yes." They said: Then write for us a document against yourself. He said: So he called for the parchment and called 'Ali to write, while we were sitting in a corner. Then Jibril descended and said: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord [morning and evening, seeking His countenance. You are not accountable for their account at all, nor are they accountable for yours at all, so that you would drive them away and thereby be among the wrongdoers]﴾. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) threw down the parchment, then called us, and we came to him.

[Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Asbat, with the same chain. Ibn Majah also narrated it in al-Sunan, no. (4127), through the route of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Qattan with the same chain, and al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/276): "This chain is sahih."]

This is a strange hadith (gharib), for this verse is Meccan, while al-Aqra' ibn Habis and 'Uyayna only embraced Islam long after the Hijrah.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh, from his father, who said: Sa'd said: This verse was revealed concerning six of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), among them Ibn Mas'ud. He said: We used to hasten to the Prophet (ﷺ), draw near to him and listen to him, and Quraysh said: These people are brought closer than us. So it was revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾.

[Al-Hakim narrated it in his al-Mustadrak through the route of Sufyan and said: "It is according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim)." Ibn Hibban also narrated it in his Sahih through the route of al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh, with the same chain.] [Al-Mustadrak (3/319).]

* *

His saying: ﴿And thus We have tried some of them through others﴾, meaning: We tested, examined and tried some of them through others, ﴿that they might say: Is it these whom Allah has favoured from among us?﴾ That is because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the beginning of his mission was mostly followed by the weak of the people, men and women, slaves and maidservants, while only a few of the nobles followed him. Just as the people of Nuh said to Nuh: ﴿And we see not following you except those who are the lowest among us, at first thought﴾ [Hud: 27], and as Heraclius, the king of the Romans, said to Abu Sufyan when he asked him those questions, saying to him: Did the weak of the people follow him, or their nobles? He said: Rather, the weak among them. He said: They are the followers of the messengers.

[The story is in Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (7), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him.]

The point is that the polytheists of Quraysh used to mock those of their weak who believed and would torment whomever among them they could. They used to say: ﴿Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?﴾ That is, Allah would not guide these people to good, if what they had come to were good, and leave us, as they said: ﴿Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 11]. And as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieved say to those who believed: Which of the two groups is better in position and finer in assembly?﴾ [Maryam: 73].

Allah, Exalted, said in reply to that: ﴿And how many generations before them have We destroyed, who were better in appearance and in show﴾ [Maryam: 74]. And He said in reply to them when they said: ﴿Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?﴾: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾, meaning: is He not most knowing of those who are grateful to Him, by their words, their deeds and their inner selves? So He grants them success, guides them to the paths of peace, brings them out of darkness into light, and guides them to Himself on a straight path, as He, Exalted, said: ﴿And those who strive for Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways, and indeed Allah is with the doers of good﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 69]. And in the sahih hadith: "Indeed Allah does not look at your forms, nor at your colours, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds."

[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2564).]

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim narrated to us: al-Husayn narrated to us: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ikrimah, concerning His saying: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, having besides Him no protector or intercessor, that they may become righteous. And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face﴾ to His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ He said: Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah, Mut'im ibn 'Adi, al-Harith ibn Nawfal, and Qaraza ibn 'Abd 'Amr ibn Nawfal came, among the nobles of the Banu 'Abd Manaf from the people of disbelief, to Abu Talib and said: "O Abu Talib, if only your nephew Muhammad would drive away from himself our clients (mawali) and our allies (hulafa'), for they are only our slaves and our lowly ones, it would be greater in our hearts, more obedient to him among us, closer to our following him, and to our affirming him."

He said: So Abu Talib came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him what they had said to him. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "If you did that, you would see what they want and where their talk leads." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, having besides Him no protector or intercessor, that they may become righteous. And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾

He said: They were Bilal, 'Ammar ibn Yasir, Salim the client of Abu Hudhayfah, Suhayb the client of Usayd, and from the allies: Ibn Mas'ud, al-Miqdad ibn 'Amr, Mas'ud ibn al-Qari, Waqid ibn 'Abd Allah al-Handhali, 'Amr ibn 'Abd 'Amr, Dhu'sh-Shimalayn, and Marthad ibn Abi Marthad, and Abu Marthad was from Ghanm, an ally of Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, and their likes among the allies.

And it was revealed concerning the leaders of disbelief among the Quraysh, the clients and the allies: ﴿And thus We tried some of them through others, that they might say, "Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?"﴾ the verse. When it was revealed, 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, came and apologized for his statement, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And when those who believe in Our verses come to you [say, "Peace be upon you"]﴾ the verse.

* *

His saying: ﴿And when those who believe in Our verses come to you, say, "Peace be upon you."﴾ means: honor them by returning their greeting, and give them good news of Allah's vast mercy, which encompasses them. Therefore He said: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾, meaning He made it obligatory upon His noble Self, out of His bounty, kindness and generosity. ﴿That whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾. Some of the salaf (righteous predecessors) said: Everyone who disobeys Allah is ignorant.

Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman said, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrimah, concerning His saying: ﴿whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾: "The whole world is ignorance." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

﴿Then repents after that and makes amends﴾, meaning: he turns back from what he was upon of sins, gives them up, resolves not to return to them, and makes his action right in the future. ﴿Then indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: "This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us," saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah finished creating the creation, He wrote in His Book, which is with Him above the Throne: 'Indeed My mercy has overcome My wrath.'" It is recorded by the two Shaykhs in their Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). Likewise, al-A'mash narrated it from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, and Musa ibn 'Uqbah narrated it from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah. Similarly al-Layth and others narrated it from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, with the same wording.

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated, through the route of al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah has finished judging between the creatures, He will bring out a book from beneath the Throne: 'Indeed My mercy has preceded My wrath, and I am the Most Merciful of the merciful.' Then He will take a handful or two handfuls and bring out from the Fire a people who did no good, written between their eyes: 'Freed by Allah.'"

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from 'Asim ibn Sulayman, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman, concerning His saying: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾, he said: "We find in the Torah two passages: that Allah created the heavens and the earth, and created one hundred mercies (or: made one hundred mercies) before He created the creation. Then He created the creation and placed among them one mercy, and kept with Himself ninety-nine mercies. By it they show mercy to one another, by it they show compassion, by it they give to one another, by it they visit one another, by it the she-camel yearns for her young, by it the cow lows, by it the sheep bleats, by it the birds follow one another, and by it the fish follow one another in the sea. When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will gather that mercy together with what He has, and His mercy is more excellent and more vast."

This has been narrated as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) through another route: Muslim recorded it in his Sahih (no. 2753) through the route of Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah has one hundred mercies. From them is one mercy by which the creatures show mercy to one another, and ninety-nine are for the Day of Resurrection."

Many hadiths agreeing with these will come at His saying: ﴿My mercy encompasses all things﴾ [al-A'raf: 156].

Among the hadiths that also suit this noble verse is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ to Mu'adh ibn Jabal: "Do you know what the right of Allah upon the servants is?" That they worship Him and do not associate anything with Him. Then he said: "Do you know what the right of the servants upon Allah is when they do that?" That He will not punish them. It is recorded by al-Bukhari (no. 7373) and Muslim (no. 30). Imam Ahmad also narrated it through the route of Kumayl ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verses 50–54 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Say: I do not tell you that with me are the treasures of Allah﴾, meaning: I do not possess them, nor do I dispose of them. ﴿Nor do I know the unseen﴾, meaning: nor do I say that I know the unseen. That belongs only to the knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; I have access to none of it except what He makes me aware of. ﴿Nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾, meaning: I do not claim to be an angel. I am only a human being among mankind, to whom revelation comes from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He has honoured me with it and bestowed His favour upon me by it. Therefore He said: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾, meaning: I do not深 deviate from it by a hand's breadth or less.

﴿Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?﴾ meaning: are those who follow the truth and are guided to it equal to those who have strayed from it and have not submitted to it? ﴿Will you not then reflect?﴾ This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Is he who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth equal to one who is blind? Only people of understanding take heed﴾ [al-Ra'd: 19].

* *

His saying: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, having besides Him no protector and no intercessor﴾, meaning: warn, O Muhammad, by this Qur'an those ﴿who fear their Lord in awe﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 57], and those who ﴿fear their Lord and dread the evil of the reckoning﴾ [al-Ra'd: 21].

﴿Those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿They will have, on that day, besides Him, no protector and no intercessor﴾, meaning: they will have no relative and no intercessor who can save them from His punishment, should He intend it for them. ﴿That perhaps they will fear Allah﴾, meaning: warn of this Day, on which no judge exists except Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿that perhaps they will fear Him﴾, so that they act in this world with deeds by which Allah will save them from His punishment on the Day of Resurrection, and multiply for them His abundant reward.

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance﴾, meaning: do not push away from yourself those characterised by this quality; rather, make them your companions and your intimates, as He said: ﴿And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance, and let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life; and do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who follows his desire and whose affair has been [ever] in neglect﴾ [al-Kahf: 28].

* *

His saying: ﴿who call upon their Lord﴾, meaning: who worship Him and ask Him. ﴿Morning and evening﴾: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Mujahid, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: what is meant by this is the obligatory prayers.

This is like His saying: ﴿And your Lord says: Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾ [Ghafir: 60], meaning: I will accept from you.

* *

His saying: ﴿seeking His countenance﴾, meaning: they seek by that deed the noble Countenance of Allah. Thus they are sincere in what they do of acts of worship and obedience.

* *

His saying: ﴿You are not accountable for their account at all, nor are they accountable for yours at all﴾, as Nuh (peace be upon him) said in reply to those who said: ﴿Shall we believe you when the lowest people follow you?﴾ He said: ﴿And I have no knowledge of what they used to do. Their account is only upon my Lord, if you could perceive﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 112–113], meaning: their account is only with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and I am not accountable for their account at all, just as they are not accountable for my account at all.

* *

His saying: ﴿So that you would drive them away and thereby be among the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: if you were to do this in such a state.

Imam Ahmad said: Asbat, that is Ibn Muhammad, narrated to us: Ash'ath narrated to us, from Kurdus, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while with him were Khabbab, Suhayb, Bilal and 'Ammar. They said: O Muhammad, are you content with these? Then the Qur'an was revealed concerning them: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ [al-An'am: 53].

[Al-Musnad (1/420). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/21): "The narrators of Ahmad are the narrators of the Sahih, except Kurdus, who is trustworthy."]

Ibn Jarir also narrated it through the route of Ash'ath, from Kurdus, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while with him were Suhayb, Bilal, 'Ammar, Khabbab and others of the weak among the Muslims. They said: O Muhammad, are you content with these from your people? Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us? Should we be followers of these? Drive them away from you, for perhaps if you drive them away, we will follow you. So this verse was revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance﴾, and ﴿Thus We have tried some of them through others﴾, up to the end of the verse.

[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/374).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated to us: 'Amr ibn Muhammad al-'Anqazi narrated to us: Asbat ibn Nasr narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Sa'id al-Azdi, who was the reciter of the Azd, from Abu al-Kanud, from Khabbab, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾. He said: al-Aqra' ibn Habis al-Tamimi and 'Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari came and found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sitting with Suhayb, Bilal, 'Ammar and Khabbab, along with some of the weak among the believers. When they saw them around the Prophet (ﷺ), they belittled them. They came to him, spoke to him privately and said: We wish that you would set aside for us a gathering with you, by which the Arabs would recognise our merit, for the delegations of the Arabs come to you, and we are ashamed that the Arabs should see us sitting with these slaves. When we come to you, remove them from us; and when we have finished, sit with them if you wish. He said: "Yes." They said: Then write for us a document against yourself. He said: So he called for the parchment and called 'Ali to write, while we were sitting in a corner. Then Jibril descended and said: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord [morning and evening, seeking His countenance. You are not accountable for their account at all, nor are they accountable for yours at all, so that you would drive them away and thereby be among the wrongdoers]﴾. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) threw down the parchment, then called us, and we came to him.

[Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Asbat, with the same chain. Ibn Majah also narrated it in al-Sunan, no. (4127), through the route of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Qattan with the same chain, and al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/276): "This chain is sahih."]

This is a strange hadith (gharib), for this verse is Meccan, while al-Aqra' ibn Habis and 'Uyayna only embraced Islam long after the Hijrah.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh, from his father, who said: Sa'd said: This verse was revealed concerning six of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), among them Ibn Mas'ud. He said: We used to hasten to the Prophet (ﷺ), draw near to him and listen to him, and Quraysh said: These people are brought closer than us. So it was revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾.

[Al-Hakim narrated it in his al-Mustadrak through the route of Sufyan and said: "It is according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim)." Ibn Hibban also narrated it in his Sahih through the route of al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh, with the same chain.] [Al-Mustadrak (3/319).]

* *

His saying: ﴿And thus We have tried some of them through others﴾, meaning: We tested, examined and tried some of them through others, ﴿that they might say: Is it these whom Allah has favoured from among us?﴾ That is because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the beginning of his mission was mostly followed by the weak of the people, men and women, slaves and maidservants, while only a few of the nobles followed him. Just as the people of Nuh said to Nuh: ﴿And we see not following you except those who are the lowest among us, at first thought﴾ [Hud: 27], and as Heraclius, the king of the Romans, said to Abu Sufyan when he asked him those questions, saying to him: Did the weak of the people follow him, or their nobles? He said: Rather, the weak among them. He said: They are the followers of the messengers.

[The story is in Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (7), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Allah, Exalted, said in reply to that: ﴿And how many generations before them have We destroyed, who were better in appearance and in show﴾ [Maryam: 74]. And He said in reply to them when they said: ﴿Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?﴾: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾, meaning: is He not most knowing of those who are grateful to Him, by their words, their deeds and their inner selves? And in the sahih hadith: "Indeed Allah does not look at your forms, nor at your colours, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds."

[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2564).]

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim narrated to us: al-Husayn narrated to us: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ikrimah, concerning His saying: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, having besides Him no protector or intercessor, that they may become righteous. And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face﴾ to His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ He said: Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah, Mut'im ibn 'Adi, al-Harith ibn Nawfal, and Qaraza ibn 'Abd 'Amr ibn Nawfal came, among the nobles of the Banu 'Abd Manaf from the people of disbelief, to Abu Talib and said: "O Abu Talib, if only your nephew Muhammad would drive away from himself our clients (mawali) and our allies (hulafa'), for they are only our slaves and our lowly ones, it would be greater in our hearts, more obedient to him among us, closer to our following him, and to our affirming him."

He said: So Abu Talib came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him what they had said to him. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "If you did that, you would see what they want and where their talk leads." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, having besides Him no protector or intercessor, that they may become righteous. And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾

He said: They were Bilal, 'Ammar ibn Yasir, Salim the client of Abu Hudhayfah, Suhayb the client of Usayd, and from the allies: Ibn Mas'ud, al-Miqdad ibn 'Amr, Mas'ud ibn al-Qari, Waqid ibn 'Abd Allah al-Handhali, 'Amr ibn 'Abd 'Amr, Dhu'sh-Shimalayn, and Marthad ibn Abi Marthad, and Abu Marthad was from Ghanm, an ally of Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, and their likes among the allies.

When it was revealed, 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, came and apologized for his statement, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And when those who believe in Our verses come to you [say, "Peace be upon you"]﴾ the verse.

* *

His saying: ﴿And when those who believe in Our verses come to you, say, "Peace be upon you."﴾ means: honor them by returning their greeting, and give them good news of Allah's vast mercy, which encompasses them. Therefore He said: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾, meaning He made it obligatory upon His noble Self, out of His bounty, kindness and generosity. ﴿That whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾. Some of the salaf (righteous predecessors) said: Everyone who disobeys Allah is ignorant.

Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman said, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrimah, concerning His saying: ﴿whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾: "The whole world is ignorance." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

﴿Then repents after that and makes amends﴾, meaning: he turns back from what he was upon of sins, gives them up, resolves not to return to them, and makes his action right in the future. ﴿Then indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: "This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us," saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah finished creating the creation, He wrote in His Book, which is with Him above the Throne: 'Indeed My mercy has overcome My wrath.'" Likewise, al-A'mash narrated it from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, and Musa ibn 'Uqbah narrated it from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah. Similarly al-Layth and others narrated it from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, with the same wording.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from 'Asim ibn Sulayman, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman, concerning His saying: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾, he said: "We find in the Torah two passages: that Allah created the heavens and the earth, and created one hundred mercies (or: made one hundred mercies) before He created the creation. Then He created the creation and placed among them one mercy, and kept with Himself ninety-nine mercies. By it they show mercy to one another, by it they show compassion, by it they give to one another, by it they visit one another, by it the she-camel yearns for her young, by it the cow lows, by it the sheep bleats, by it the birds follow one another, and by it the fish follow one another in the sea. When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will gather that mercy together with what He has, and His mercy is more excellent and more vast."

This has been narrated as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) through another route: Muslim recorded it in his Sahih (no. 2753) through the route of Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah has one hundred mercies. From them is one mercy by which the creatures show mercy to one another, and ninety-nine are for the Day of Resurrection."

Many hadiths agreeing with these will come at His saying: ﴿My mercy encompasses all things﴾ [al-A'raf: 156].

Among the hadiths that also suit this noble verse is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ to Mu'adh ibn Jabal: "Do you know what the right of Allah upon the servants is?" That they worship Him and do not associate anything with Him. Then he said: "Do you know what the right of the servants upon Allah is when they do that?" That He will not punish them. It is recorded by al-Bukhari (no. 7373) and Muslim (no. 30). Imam Ahmad also narrated it through the route of Kumayl ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verses 50–54 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Say: I do not tell you that with me are the treasures of Allah﴾, meaning: I do not possess them, nor do I dispose of them. ﴿Nor do I know the unseen﴾, meaning: nor do I say that I know the unseen. That belongs only to the knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; I have access to none of it except what He makes me aware of. ﴿Nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾, meaning: I do not claim to be an angel. I am only a human being among mankind, to whom revelation comes from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He has honoured me with it and bestowed His favour upon me by it. Therefore He said: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾, meaning: I do not深 deviate from it by a hand's breadth or less.

﴿Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?﴾ meaning: are those who follow the truth and are guided to it equal to those who have strayed from it and have not submitted to it? ﴿Will you not then reflect?﴾ This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Is he who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth equal to one who is blind? Only people of understanding take heed﴾ [al-Ra'd: 19].

* *

His saying: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, having besides Him no protector and no intercessor﴾, meaning: warn, O Muhammad, by this Qur'an those ﴿who fear their Lord in awe﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 57], and those who ﴿fear their Lord and dread the evil of the reckoning﴾ [al-Ra'd: 21].

﴿Those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿They will have, on that day, besides Him, no protector and no intercessor﴾, meaning: they will have no relative and no intercessor who can save them from His punishment, should He intend it for them. ﴿That perhaps they will fear Allah﴾, meaning: warn of this Day, on which no judge exists except Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿that perhaps they will fear Him﴾, so that they act in this world with deeds by which Allah will save them from His punishment on the Day of Resurrection, and multiply for them His abundant reward.

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance﴾, meaning: do not push away from yourself those characterised by this quality; rather, make them your companions and your intimates, as He said: ﴿And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance, and let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life; and do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who follows his desire and whose affair has been [ever] in neglect﴾ [al-Kahf: 28].

* *

His saying: ﴿who call upon their Lord﴾, meaning: who worship Him and ask Him. ﴿Morning and evening﴾: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Mujahid, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: what is meant by this is the obligatory prayers.

This is like His saying: ﴿And your Lord says: Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾ [Ghafir: 60], meaning: I will accept from you.

* *

His saying: ﴿seeking His countenance﴾, meaning: they seek by that deed the noble Countenance of Allah. Thus they are sincere in what they do of acts of worship and obedience.

* *

His saying: ﴿You are not accountable for their account at all, nor are they accountable for yours at all﴾, as Nuh (peace be upon him) said in reply to those who said: ﴿Shall we believe you when the lowest people follow you?﴾ He said: ﴿And I have no knowledge of what they used to do. Their account is only upon my Lord, if you could perceive﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 112–113], meaning: their account is only with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and I am not accountable for their account at all, just as they are not accountable for my account at all.

* *

His saying: ﴿So that you would drive them away and thereby be among the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: if you were to do this in such a state.

Imam Ahmad said: Asbat, that is Ibn Muhammad, narrated to us: Ash'ath narrated to us, from Kurdus, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while with him were Khabbab, Suhayb, Bilal and 'Ammar. They said: O Muhammad, are you content with these? Then the Qur'an was revealed concerning them: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ [al-An'am: 53].

[Al-Musnad (1/420). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/21): "The narrators of Ahmad are the narrators of the Sahih, except Kurdus, who is trustworthy."]

Ibn Jarir also narrated it through the route of Ash'ath, from Kurdus, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while with him were Suhayb, Bilal, 'Ammar, Khabbab and others of the weak among the Muslims. They said: O Muhammad, are you content with these from your people? Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us? Should we be followers of these? Drive them away from you, for perhaps if you drive them away, we will follow you. So this verse was revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance﴾, and ﴿Thus We have tried some of them through others﴾, up to the end of the verse.

[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/374).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated to us: 'Amr ibn Muhammad al-'Anqazi narrated to us: Asbat ibn Nasr narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Sa'id al-Azdi, who was the reciter of the Azd, from Abu al-Kanud, from Khabbab, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾. He said: al-Aqra' ibn Habis al-Tamimi and 'Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari came and found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sitting with Suhayb, Bilal, 'Ammar and Khabbab, along with some of the weak among the believers. When they saw them around the Prophet (ﷺ), they belittled them. They came to him, spoke to him privately and said: We wish that you would set aside for us a gathering with you, by which the Arabs would recognise our merit, for the delegations of the Arabs come to you, and we are ashamed that the Arabs should see us sitting with these slaves. When we come to you, remove them from us; and when we have finished, sit with them if you wish. He said: "Yes." They said: Then write for us a document against yourself. He said: So he called for the parchment and called 'Ali to write, while we were sitting in a corner. Then Jibril descended and said: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord [morning and evening, seeking His countenance. You are not accountable for their account at all, nor are they accountable for yours at all, so that you would drive them away and thereby be among the wrongdoers]﴾. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) threw down the parchment, then called us, and we came to him.

[Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Asbat, with the same chain. Ibn Majah also narrated it in al-Sunan, no. (4127), through the route of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Qattan with the same chain, and al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/276): "This chain is sahih."]

This is a strange hadith (gharib), for this verse is Meccan, while al-Aqra' ibn Habis and 'Uyayna only embraced Islam long after the Hijrah.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh, from his father, who said: Sa'd said: This verse was revealed concerning six of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), among them Ibn Mas'ud. He said: We used to hasten to the Prophet (ﷺ), draw near to him and listen to him, and Quraysh said: These people are brought closer than us. So it was revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾.

[Al-Hakim narrated it in his al-Mustadrak through the route of Sufyan and said: "It is according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim)." Ibn Hibban also narrated it in his Sahih through the route of al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh, with the same chain.] [Al-Mustadrak (3/319).]

* *

His saying: ﴿And thus We have tried some of them through others﴾, meaning: We tested, examined and tried some of them through others, ﴿that they might say: Is it these whom Allah has favoured from among us?﴾ That is because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the beginning of his mission was mostly followed by the weak of the people, men and women, slaves and maidservants, while only a few of the nobles followed him. Just as the people of Nuh said to Nuh: ﴿And we see not following you except those who are the lowest among us, at first thought﴾ [Hud: 27], and as Heraclius, the king of the Romans, said to Abu Sufyan when he asked him those questions, saying to him: Did the weak of the people follow him, or their nobles? He said: Rather, the weak among them. He said: They are the followers of the messengers.

[The story is in Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (7), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him.]

The point is that the polytheists of Quraysh used to mock those of their weak who believed and would torment whomever among them they could. They used to say: ﴿Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?﴾ That is, Allah would not guide these people to good, if what they had come to were good, and leave us, as they said: ﴿Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 11]. And as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieved say to those who believed: Which of the two groups is better in position and finer in assembly?﴾ [Maryam: 73].

Allah, Exalted, said in reply to that: ﴿And how many generations before them have We destroyed, who were better in appearance and in show﴾ [Maryam: 74]. And He said in reply to them when they said: ﴿Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?﴾: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾, meaning: is He not most knowing of those who are grateful to Him, by their words, their deeds and their inner selves? So He grants them success, guides them to the paths of peace, brings them out of darkness into light, and guides them to Himself on a straight path, as He, Exalted, said: ﴿And those who strive for Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways, and indeed Allah is with the doers of good﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 69]. And in the sahih hadith: "Indeed Allah does not look at your forms, nor at your colours, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds."

[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2564).]

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim narrated to us: al-Husayn narrated to us: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ikrimah, concerning His saying: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, having besides Him no protector or intercessor, that they may become righteous. And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face﴾ to His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ He said: Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah, Mut'im ibn 'Adi, al-Harith ibn Nawfal, and Qaraza ibn 'Abd 'Amr ibn Nawfal came, among the nobles of the Banu 'Abd Manaf from the people of disbelief, to Abu Talib and said: "O Abu Talib, if only your nephew Muhammad would drive away from himself our clients (mawali) and our allies (hulafa'), for they are only our slaves and our lowly ones, it would be greater in our hearts, more obedient to him among us, closer to our following him, and to our affirming him."

He said: So Abu Talib came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him what they had said to him. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "If you did that, you would see what they want and where their talk leads." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, having besides Him no protector or intercessor, that they may become righteous. And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾

He said: They were Bilal, 'Ammar ibn Yasir, Salim the client of Abu Hudhayfah, Suhayb the client of Usayd, and from the allies: Ibn Mas'ud, al-Miqdad ibn 'Amr, Mas'ud ibn al-Qari, Waqid ibn 'Abd Allah al-Handhali, 'Amr ibn 'Abd 'Amr, Dhu'sh-Shimalayn, and Marthad ibn Abi Marthad, and Abu Marthad was from Ghanm, an ally of Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, and their likes among the allies.

And it was revealed concerning the leaders of disbelief among the Quraysh, the clients and the allies: ﴿And thus We tried some of them through others, that they might say, "Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?"﴾ the verse. When it was revealed, 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, came and apologized for his statement, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And when those who believe in Our verses come to you [say, "Peace be upon you"]﴾ the verse.

* *

His saying: ﴿And when those who believe in Our verses come to you, say, "Peace be upon you."﴾ means: honor them by returning their greeting, and give them good news of Allah's vast mercy, which encompasses them. Therefore He said: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾, meaning He made it obligatory upon His noble Self, out of His bounty, kindness and generosity. ﴿That whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾. Some of the salaf (righteous predecessors) said: Everyone who disobeys Allah is ignorant.

Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman said, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrimah, concerning His saying: ﴿whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾: "The whole world is ignorance." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

﴿Then repents after that and makes amends﴾, meaning: he turns back from what he was upon of sins, gives them up, resolves not to return to them, and makes his action right in the future. ﴿Then indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: "This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us," saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah finished creating the creation, He wrote in His Book, which is with Him above the Throne: 'Indeed My mercy has overcome My wrath.'" It is recorded by the two Shaykhs in their Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). Likewise, al-A'mash narrated it from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, and Musa ibn 'Uqbah narrated it from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah. Similarly al-Layth and others narrated it from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, with the same wording.

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated, through the route of al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah has finished judging between the creatures, He will bring out a book from beneath the Throne: 'Indeed My mercy has preceded My wrath, and I am the Most Merciful of the merciful.' Then He will take a handful or two handfuls and bring out from the Fire a people who did no good, written between their eyes: 'Freed by Allah.'"

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from 'Asim ibn Sulayman, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman, concerning His saying: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾, he said: "We find in the Torah two passages: that Allah created the heavens and the earth, and created one hundred mercies (or: made one hundred mercies) before He created the creation. Then He created the creation and placed among them one mercy, and kept with Himself ninety-nine mercies. By it they show mercy to one another, by it they show compassion, by it they give to one another, by it they visit one another, by it the she-camel yearns for her young, by it the cow lows, by it the sheep bleats, by it the birds follow one another, and by it the fish follow one another in the sea. When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will gather that mercy together with what He has, and His mercy is more excellent and more vast."

This has been narrated as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) through another route: Muslim recorded it in his Sahih (no. 2753) through the route of Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah has one hundred mercies. From them is one mercy by which the creatures show mercy to one another, and ninety-nine are for the Day of Resurrection."

Many hadiths agreeing with these will come at His saying: ﴿My mercy encompasses all things﴾ [al-A'raf: 156].

Among the hadiths that also suit this noble verse is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ to Mu'adh ibn Jabal: "Do you know what the right of Allah upon the servants is?" That they worship Him and do not associate anything with Him. Then he said: "Do you know what the right of the servants upon Allah is when they do that?" That He will not punish them. It is recorded by al-Bukhari (no. 7373) and Muslim (no. 30). Imam Ahmad also narrated it through the route of Kumayl ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verses 50–54 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Say: I do not tell you that with me are the treasures of Allah﴾, meaning: I do not possess them, nor do I dispose of them. ﴿Nor do I know the unseen﴾, meaning: nor do I say that I know the unseen. That belongs only to the knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; I have access to none of it except what He makes me aware of. ﴿Nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾, meaning: I do not claim to be an angel. I am only a human being among mankind, to whom revelation comes from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He has honoured me with it and bestowed His favour upon me by it. Therefore He said: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾, meaning: I do not深 deviate from it by a hand's breadth or less.

﴿Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?﴾ meaning: are those who follow the truth and are guided to it equal to those who have strayed from it and have not submitted to it? ﴿Will you not then reflect?﴾ This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Is he who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth equal to one who is blind? Only people of understanding take heed﴾ [al-Ra'd: 19].

* *

His saying: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, having besides Him no protector and no intercessor﴾, meaning: warn, O Muhammad, by this Qur'an those ﴿who fear their Lord in awe﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 57], and those who ﴿fear their Lord and dread the evil of the reckoning﴾ [al-Ra'd: 21].

﴿Those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿They will have, on that day, besides Him, no protector and no intercessor﴾, meaning: they will have no relative and no intercessor who can save them from His punishment, should He intend it for them. ﴿That perhaps they will fear Allah﴾, meaning: warn of this Day, on which no judge exists except Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿that perhaps they will fear Him﴾, so that they act in this world with deeds by which Allah will save them from His punishment on the Day of Resurrection, and multiply for them His abundant reward.

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance﴾, meaning: do not push away from yourself those characterised by this quality; rather, make them your companions and your intimates, as He said: ﴿And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance, and let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life; and do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who follows his desire and whose affair has been [ever] in neglect﴾ [al-Kahf: 28].

* *

His saying: ﴿who call upon their Lord﴾, meaning: who worship Him and ask Him. ﴿Morning and evening﴾: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Mujahid, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: what is meant by this is the obligatory prayers.

This is like His saying: ﴿And your Lord says: Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾ [Ghafir: 60], meaning: I will accept from you.

* *

* *

His saying: ﴿You are not accountable for their account at all, nor are they accountable for yours at all﴾, as Nuh (peace be upon him) said in reply to those who said: ﴿Shall we believe you when the lowest people follow you?﴾ He said: ﴿And I have no knowledge of what they used to do. Their account is only upon my Lord, if you could perceive﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 112–113], meaning: their account is only with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and I am not accountable for their account at all, just as they are not accountable for my account at all.

* *

His saying: ﴿So that you would drive them away and thereby be among the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: if you were to do this in such a state.

Imam Ahmad said: Asbat, that is Ibn Muhammad, narrated to us: Ash'ath narrated to us, from Kurdus, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while with him were Khabbab, Suhayb, Bilal and 'Ammar. They said: O Muhammad, are you content with these from your people? Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us? Should we be followers of these? Drive them away from you, for perhaps if you drive them away, we will follow you. So this verse was revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance﴾, and ﴿Thus We have tried some of them through others﴾, up to the end of the verse.

[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/374).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated to us: 'Amr ibn Muhammad al-'Anqazi narrated to us: Asbat ibn Nasr narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Sa'id al-Azdi, who was the reciter of the Azd, from Abu al-Kanud, from Khabbab, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾. When they saw them around the Prophet (ﷺ), they belittled them. When we come to you, remove them from us; and when we have finished, sit with them if you wish. He said: "Yes." They said: Then write for us a document against yourself. He said: So he called for the parchment and called 'Ali to write, while we were sitting in a corner. Then Jibril descended and said: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord [morning and evening, seeking His countenance. You are not accountable for their account at all, nor are they accountable for yours at all, so that you would drive them away and thereby be among the wrongdoers]﴾. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) threw down the parchment, then called us, and we came to him.

[Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Asbat, with the same chain. Ibn Majah also narrated it in al-Sunan, no. (4127), through the route of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Qattan with the same chain, and al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/276): "This chain is sahih."]
