[Al-Hakim narrated it in his al-Mustadrak through the route of Sufyan and said: "It is according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim)." Ibn Hibban also narrated it in his Sahih through the route of al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh, with the same chain.] [Al-Mustadrak (3/319).]

* *

His saying: ﴿And thus We have tried some of them through others﴾, meaning: We tested, examined and tried some of them through others, ﴿that they might say: Is it these whom Allah has favoured from among us?﴾ That is because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the beginning of his mission was mostly followed by the weak of the people, men and women, slaves and maidservants, while only a few of the nobles followed him. Just as the people of Nuh said to Nuh: ﴿And we see not following you except those who are the lowest among us, at first thought﴾ [Hud: 27], and as Heraclius, the king of the Romans, said to Abu Sufyan when he asked him those questions, saying to him: Did the weak of the people follow him, or their nobles? He said: Rather, the weak among them. He said: They are the followers of the messengers.

[The story is in Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (7), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him.]

The point is that the polytheists of Quraysh used to mock those of their weak who believed and would torment whomever among them they could. They used to say: ﴿Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?﴾ That is, Allah would not guide these people to good, if what they had come to were good, and leave us, as they said: ﴿Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 11]. And as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieved say to those who believed: Which of the two groups is better in position and finer in assembly?﴾ [Maryam: 73].

Allah, Exalted, said in reply to that: ﴿And how many generations before them have We destroyed, who were better in appearance and in show﴾ [Maryam: 74]. And He said in reply to them when they said: ﴿Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?﴾: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾, meaning: is He not most knowing of those who are grateful to Him, by their words, their deeds and their inner selves? So He grants them success, guides them to the paths of peace, brings them out of darkness into light, and guides them to Himself on a straight path, as He, Exalted, said: ﴿And those who strive for Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways, and indeed Allah is with the doers of good﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 69]. And in the sahih hadith: "Indeed Allah does not look at your forms, nor at your colours, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds."

[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2564).]

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim narrated to us: al-Husayn narrated to us: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ikrimah, concerning His saying: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, having besides Him no protector or intercessor, that they may become righteous. And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face﴾ to His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ He said: Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah, Mut'im ibn 'Adi, al-Harith ibn Nawfal, and Qaraza ibn 'Abd 'Amr ibn Nawfal came, among the nobles of the Banu 'Abd Manaf from the people of disbelief, to Abu Talib and said: "O Abu Talib, if only your nephew Muhammad would drive away from himself our clients (mawali) and our allies (hulafa'), for they are only our slaves and our lowly ones, it would be greater in our hearts, more obedient to him among us, closer to our following him, and to our affirming him."

He said: So Abu Talib came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him what they had said to him. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "If you did that, you would see what they want and where their talk leads." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, having besides Him no protector or intercessor, that they may become righteous. And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾

He said: They were Bilal, 'Ammar ibn Yasir, Salim the client of Abu Hudhayfah, Suhayb the client of Usayd, and from the allies: Ibn Mas'ud, al-Miqdad ibn 'Amr, Mas'ud ibn al-Qari, Waqid ibn 'Abd Allah al-Handhali, 'Amr ibn 'Abd 'Amr, Dhu'sh-Shimalayn, and Marthad ibn Abi Marthad, and Abu Marthad was from Ghanm, an ally of Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, and their likes among the allies.

And it was revealed concerning the leaders of disbelief among the Quraysh, the clients and the allies: ﴿And thus We tried some of them through others, that they might say, "Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?"﴾ the verse. When it was revealed, 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, came and apologized for his statement, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And when those who believe in Our verses come to you [say, "Peace be upon you"]﴾ the verse.

* *

His saying: ﴿And when those who believe in Our verses come to you, say, "Peace be upon you."﴾ means: honor them by returning their greeting, and give them good news of Allah's vast mercy, which encompasses them. Therefore He said: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾, meaning He made it obligatory upon His noble Self, out of His bounty, kindness and generosity. ﴿That whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾. Some of the salaf (righteous predecessors) said: Everyone who disobeys Allah is ignorant.

Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman said, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrimah, concerning His saying: ﴿whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾: "The whole world is ignorance." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

﴿Then repents after that and makes amends﴾, meaning: he turns back from what he was upon of sins, gives them up, resolves not to return to them, and makes his action right in the future. ﴿Then indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: "This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us," saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah finished creating the creation, He wrote in His Book, which is with Him above the Throne: 'Indeed My mercy has overcome My wrath.'" It is recorded by the two Shaykhs in their Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). Likewise, al-A'mash narrated it from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, and Musa ibn 'Uqbah narrated it from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah. Similarly al-Layth and others narrated it from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, with the same wording.

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated, through the route of al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah has finished judging between the creatures, He will bring out a book from beneath the Throne: 'Indeed My mercy has preceded My wrath, and I am the Most Merciful of the merciful.' Then He will take a handful or two handfuls and bring out from the Fire a people who did no good, written between their eyes: 'Freed by Allah.'"

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from 'Asim ibn Sulayman, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman, concerning His saying: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾, he said: "We find in the Torah two passages: that Allah created the heavens and the earth, and created one hundred mercies (or: made one hundred mercies) before He created the creation. Then He created the creation and placed among them one mercy, and kept with Himself ninety-nine mercies. By it they show mercy to one another, by it they show compassion, by it they give to one another, by it they visit one another, by it the she-camel yearns for her young, by it the cow lows, by it the sheep bleats, by it the birds follow one another, and by it the fish follow one another in the sea. When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will gather that mercy together with what He has, and His mercy is more excellent and more vast."

This has been narrated as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) through another route: Muslim recorded it in his Sahih (no. 2753) through the route of Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah has one hundred mercies. From them is one mercy by which the creatures show mercy to one another, and ninety-nine are for the Day of Resurrection."

Many hadiths agreeing with these will come at His saying: ﴿My mercy encompasses all things﴾ [al-A'raf: 156].

Among the hadiths that also suit this noble verse is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ to Mu'adh ibn Jabal: "Do you know what the right of Allah upon the servants is?" That they worship Him and do not associate anything with Him. Then he said: "Do you know what the right of the servants upon Allah is when they do that?" That He will not punish them. It is recorded by al-Bukhari (no. 7373) and Muslim (no. 30). Imam Ahmad also narrated it through the route of Kumayl ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him].

Allah the Exalted says: Just as We have explained the proofs and evidences previously mentioned for the path of guidance and righteousness, and censured disputation and obstinacy, ﴿Thus do We detail the verses﴾, meaning those which those addressed need to have explained, ﴿and that the way of the criminals may become clear﴾, meaning that the way of the criminals who oppose the Messengers may be manifest. It was also read: "and that the way of the criminals may become clear" (wa-liyastabīna sabīlu l-mujrimīn), meaning: that the way of the criminals may become clear, O Muhammad, or O addressee.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Say: "Indeed, I am upon clear evidence from my Lord"﴾, meaning: upon insight into the law of Allah which He has revealed to me, ﴿but you have denied it﴾, meaning: the truth that has come to me from Allah. ﴿What you seek to hasten is not with me﴾, meaning: the punishment. ﴿The decision belongs only to Allah﴾, meaning: the matter of that rests only with Allah. If He wills, He will hasten for you what you have asked for of it, and if He wills, He will give you respite and a term, for He has in that great wisdom. Therefore He said: ﴿The decision belongs only to Allah. He relates the truth, and He is the best of the deciders﴾, meaning: He is the best of those who decide matters and the best of judges among His servants.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Say: "If I had what you seek to hasten, the matter would have been decided between me and you"﴾, meaning: if the outcome of what you seek to hasten were in my hands, I would have inflicted upon you what you deserve of it. ﴿And Allah knows best the wrongdoers.﴾

If it is asked: what is the reconciliation between this verse and what is established in the two Sahihs, by way of Ibn Wahb, from Yunus, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, that she said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "O Messenger of Allah, has there come upon you a day harder than the day of Uhud?" So I departed, deeply distressed, on my face, and I did not come to myself except at Qarn al-Tha'alib. I raised my head and behold, a cloud had shaded me, and I looked and in it was Jibril, peace be upon him, who called to me and said: 'Indeed Allah has heard the words of your people to you and their reply to you, and He has sent to you the angel of the mountains, that you may command him with whatever you wish concerning them.'" He said: "Then the angel of the mountains called to me, greeted me, and said: 'O Muhammad, indeed Allah has heard the words of your people to you, and your Lord has sent me to you, that you may command me with your command. What do you wish? If you wish, I will close the two Akhshabayn upon them.'" * *

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And He knows what is in the land and the sea﴾, meaning: His noble knowledge encompasses all existing things, their land and their sea; nothing of that is hidden from Him, nor an atom's weight on earth or in the heavens. How well al-Sarsari said:

"Nothing is hidden from Him, the ant, whether it appears to the eyes or hides."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And not a leaf falls but He knows it﴾, meaning: He knows the movements even of inanimate things, so what is your assumption about living beings, especially the accountable among them, jinn and humans, as He said: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal﴾ [Ghafir: 19].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, from Hassan al-Namari, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And not a leaf falls but He knows it﴾, he said: There is no tree on land or sea but that an angel is assigned to it, recording what falls from it.

* *

On every corner of the earth is a seal of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and on every seal is an angel whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends to it each day from Him, saying: "Keep safe what is with you."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Miswar al-Zuhri narrated to us: Malik ibn Su'ayr narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, who said: There is no tree on earth nor a place where a needle is pierced but that over it is an assigned angel who brings to Allah its knowledge: its moisture when it is moist, and its dryness when it is dry.

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 6, verses 60–62:

He, exalted is He, informs that He takes (yatawaffa) His servants in their sleep at night, and this is the lesser taking (al-tawaffi al-asghar, the minor death, that is, sleep). As He said: ﴿When God said, "O Jesus, I will take you and raise you up to Me and purify you from those who disbelieve"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 55]. And He said: ﴿God takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and sends the others back until an appointed term﴾ [al-Zumar: 42]. In this verse He mentions the two takings: the greater and the lesser. Likewise, in this context, He mentions the rulings concerning the lesser taking and then the greater. He said: ﴿It is He who takes you at night, and knows what you have committed by day﴾, meaning: and He knows what deeds you have earned by day. This is a parenthetical clause (jumlah mu'taridah) which indicates the comprehensiveness of His knowledge of His creation in their night and their day, in their state of rest and in their state of movement. As He said: ﴿Whether one of you conceals speech or speaks aloud, whether one hides by night or goes forth by day﴾ [al-Ra'd: 10]. And as He said: ﴿And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein﴾, meaning in the night, ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ [al-Qasas: 73], meaning in the day. As He said: ﴿And We made the night as a covering, and We made the day for livelihood﴾ [al-Naba': 10–11]. For this reason He said here: ﴿It is He who takes you at night and knows what you have committed by day﴾, meaning what you have earned by day, ﴿then He raises you up therein﴾, meaning in the day. This was said by Mujahid, Qatadah, and al-Suddi.

Ibn Jurayj related from 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir: that is, in the sleep.

The first view is more apparent. Ibn Mardawayh related with his chain from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "With every person is an angel. When he sleeps, it takes his soul and it is returned to him. If God permits the seizing of his spirit, it seizes it; otherwise it is returned to him." This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿It is He who takes you at night﴾.[[Abu al-Shaykh related it, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (3/280), and there is a break (inqita') in its chain between al-Dahhak and Ibn 'Abbas.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿that a term appointed may be fulfilled﴾, it means the term of each one of the people. ﴿Then to Him is your return﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Then He will inform you﴾, meaning He will tell you ﴿of what you used to do﴾, meaning He will recompense you for it: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil.[[In the manuscript A: "فينبئكم", which is an error.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants﴾, meaning He is the One who has subdued everything, and everything submits to His majesty, greatness, and magnificence.

﴿And He sends over you guardians﴾, meaning of the angels who guard the human body, as He said: ﴿For him are angels following one another, before him and behind him, guarding him by the command of God﴾ [al-Ra'd: 11]. And guardians who record his deeds and count them, as He said: ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording, who know what you do﴾ [al-Infitar: 10–12]. And He said: ﴿One sits on the right and one on the left. Not a word does he utter but that there is with him an observer prepared﴾ [Qaf: 17–18].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿until, when death comes to one of you﴾, meaning when he is at the point of death and his term has come, ﴿Our messengers take him﴾, meaning angels appointed for that.

Ibn 'Abbas and others said: The Angel of Death has assistants from among the angels who bring the spirit out of the body. Then the Angel of Death seizes it when it reaches the throat (al-hulqum). The related hadiths, which bear witness to the authenticity of what was related from Ibn 'Abbas and others, will come at His saying: ﴿God keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾ [Ibrahim: 27].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and they do not neglect﴾, meaning in preserving the spirit of the deceased; rather they preserve it and bring it down wherever God, mighty and majestic, wills. If he was among the righteous, it is in 'Illiyyin; and if he was among the wicked, it is in Sijjin, we seek refuge in God from that.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then they are returned to God, their true Master﴾. Ibn Jarir said: ﴿Then they are returned﴾ means the angels, ﴿to God, their true Master﴾.

We mention here the hadith which Imam Ahmad related from Abu Hurayrah concerning the ascent of the angels with the spirit from heaven to heaven until it reaches the heaven in which God, mighty and majestic, is. He said: Husayn ibn Muhammad related to us, Ibn Abi Dhi'b related to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed, the dead person is attended by the angels. If he is a righteous man, they say: 'Come out, O good soul, which was in a good body; come out praised, and rejoice in rest and fragrance and a Lord not angry.' It is continually said to it until it comes out. Then it is ascended to the heaven, and it is requested to be opened, and it is said: 'Who is this?' It is said: 'So-and-so.' It is said: 'Welcome to the good soul which was in the good body; enter praised, and rejoice in rest and fragrance and a Lord not angry.' It is continually said to it until it reaches the heaven in which God, mighty and majestic, is. And if he is an evil man, they say: 'Come out, O evil soul, which was in an evil body; come out blameworthy, and rejoice in boiling water and dark pus and other kinds of similar torment.' It is continually said to it until it comes out. Then it is ascended to the heaven, and it is requested to be opened, and it is said: 'Who is this?' It is said: 'So-and-so.' It is said: 'No welcome to the evil soul which was in the evil body; return blameworthy, for the gates of heaven will not be opened for you.' It is sent down from the heaven and then it goes to the grave. The righteous man sits up and is asked the same as was mentioned in the first hadith, and the evil man sits up and is asked the same as was mentioned in the first hadith [[In manuscript A: "الثاني" (the second)]]."

This is a gharib (rare/unusual) hadith.[[Musnad (2/364–365).]]

It is possible that what is meant by His saying: ﴿Then they are returned to God﴾ is all creation returning to God on the Day of Resurrection, and He will judge among them with His justice, as He said: ﴿Say: Indeed, the former and the latter are gathered to the appointed time of a known day﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 49–50]. And He said: ﴿And We gathered them, and We left none of them behind﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf: 47–49]. For this reason He said: ﴿their true Master. Unquestionably, His is the judgment, and He is the swiftest of reckoners﴾.

As for His saying: ﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants﴾, meaning He is the One who has subdued everything, and everything submits to His majesty, greatness, and magnificence.

﴿And He sends over you guardians﴾, meaning of the angels who guard the human body, as He said: ﴿For him are angels following one another, before him and behind him, guarding him by the command of God﴾ [al-Ra'd: 11]. And guardians who record his deeds and count them, as He said: ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording, who know what you do﴾ [al-Infitar: 10–12]. And He said: ﴿One sits on the right and one on the left. Not a word does he utter but that there is with him an observer prepared﴾ [Qaf: 17–18].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿until, when death comes to one of you﴾, meaning when he is at the point of death and his term has come, ﴿Our messengers take him﴾, meaning angels appointed for that.

Ibn 'Abbas and others said: The Angel of Death has assistants from among the angels who bring the spirit out of the body. Then the Angel of Death seizes it when it reaches the throat (al-hulqum). The related hadiths, which bear witness to the authenticity of what was related from Ibn 'Abbas and others, will come at His saying: ﴿God keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾ [Ibrahim: 27].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and they do not neglect﴾, meaning in preserving the spirit of the deceased; rather they preserve it and bring it down wherever God, mighty and majestic, wills. If he was among the righteous, it is in 'Illiyyin; and if he was among the wicked, it is in Sijjin, we seek refuge in God from that.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then they are returned to God, their true Master﴾. Ibn Jarir said: ﴿Then they are returned﴾ means the angels, ﴿to God, their true Master﴾.

We mention here the hadith which Imam Ahmad related from Abu Hurayrah concerning the ascent of the angels with the spirit from heaven to heaven until it reaches the heaven in which God, mighty and majestic, is. He said: Husayn ibn Muhammad related to us, Ibn Abi Dhi'b related to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed, the dead person is attended by the angels. If he is a righteous man, they say: 'Come out, O good soul, which was in a good body; come out praised, and rejoice in rest and fragrance and a Lord not angry.' It is continually said to it until it comes out. Then it is ascended to the heaven, and it is requested to be opened, and it is said: 'Who is this?' It is said: 'So-and-so.' It is said: 'Welcome to the good soul which was in the good body; enter praised, and rejoice in rest and fragrance and a Lord not angry.' It is continually said to it until it reaches the heaven in which God, mighty and majestic, is. And if he is an evil man, they say: 'Come out, O evil soul, which was in an evil body; come out blameworthy, and rejoice in boiling water and dark pus and other kinds of similar torment.' It is continually said to it until it comes out. Then it is ascended to the heaven, and it is requested to be opened, and it is said: 'Who is this?' It is said: 'So-and-so.' It is said: 'No welcome to the evil soul which was in the evil body; return blameworthy, for the gates of heaven will not be opened for you.' It is sent down from the heaven and then it goes to the grave. The righteous man sits up and is asked the same as was mentioned in the first hadith, and the evil man sits up and is asked the same as was mentioned in the first hadith [[In manuscript A: "الثاني" (the second)]]."

This is a gharib (rare/unusual) hadith.[[Musnad (2/364–365).]]

It is possible that what is meant by His saying: ﴿Then they are returned to God﴾ is all creation returning to God on the Day of Resurrection, and He will judge among them with His justice, as He said: ﴿Say: Indeed, the former and the latter are gathered to the appointed time of a known day﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 49–50]. And He said: ﴿And We gathered them, and We left none of them behind﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf: 47–49]. For this reason He said: ﴿their true Master. Unquestionably, His is the judgment, and He is the swiftest of reckoners﴾.

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 6, verses 60–62:

He, exalted is He, informs that He takes (yatawaffa) His servants in their sleep at night, and this is the lesser taking (al-tawaffi al-asghar, the minor death, that is, sleep). As He said: ﴿When God said, "O Jesus, I will take you and raise you up to Me and purify you from those who disbelieve"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 55]. And He said: ﴿God takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and sends the others back until an appointed term﴾ [al-Zumar: 42]. In this verse He mentions the two takings: the greater and the lesser. Likewise, in this context, He mentions the rulings concerning the lesser taking and then the greater. He said: ﴿It is He who takes you at night, and knows what you have committed by day﴾, meaning: and He knows what deeds you have earned by day. This is a parenthetical clause (jumlah mu'taridah) which indicates the comprehensiveness of His knowledge of His creation in their night and their day, in their state of rest and in their state of movement. As He said: ﴿Whether one of you conceals speech or speaks aloud, whether one hides by night or goes forth by day﴾ [al-Ra'd: 10]. And as He said: ﴿And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein﴾, meaning in the night, ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ [al-Qasas: 73], meaning in the day. As He said: ﴿And We made the night as a covering, and We made the day for livelihood﴾ [al-Naba': 10–11]. For this reason He said here: ﴿It is He who takes you at night and knows what you have committed by day﴾, meaning what you have earned by day, ﴿then He raises you up therein﴾, meaning in the day. This was said by Mujahid, Qatadah, and al-Suddi.

Ibn Jurayj related from 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir: that is, in the sleep.

The first view is more apparent. Ibn Mardawayh related with his chain from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "With every person is an angel. When he sleeps, it takes his soul and it is returned to him. If God permits the seizing of his spirit, it seizes it; otherwise it is returned to him." This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿It is He who takes you at night﴾.[[Abu al-Shaykh related it, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (3/280), and there is a break (inqita') in its chain between al-Dahhak and Ibn 'Abbas.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿that a term appointed may be fulfilled﴾, it means the term of each one of the people. ﴿Then to Him is your return﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Then He will inform you﴾, meaning He will tell you ﴿of what you used to do﴾, meaning He will recompense you for it: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil.[[In the manuscript A: "فينبئكم", which is an error.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants﴾, meaning He is the One who has subdued everything, and everything submits to His majesty, greatness, and magnificence.

﴿And He sends over you guardians﴾, meaning of the angels who guard the human body, as He said: ﴿For him are angels following one another, before him and behind him, guarding him by the command of God﴾ [al-Ra'd: 11]. * *

If he was among the righteous, it is in 'Illiyyin; and if he was among the wicked, it is in Sijjin, we seek refuge in God from that.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then they are returned to God, their true Master﴾. Ibn Jarir said: ﴿Then they are returned﴾ means the angels, ﴿to God, their true Master﴾.

We mention here the hadith which Imam Ahmad related from Abu Hurayrah concerning the ascent of the angels with the spirit from heaven to heaven until it reaches the heaven in which God, mighty and majestic, is. He said: Husayn ibn Muhammad related to us, Ibn Abi Dhi'b related to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed, the dead person is attended by the angels. If he is a righteous man, they say: 'Come out, O good soul, which was in a good body; come out praised, and rejoice in rest and fragrance and a Lord not angry.' It is continually said to it until it comes out. Then it is ascended to the heaven, and it is requested to be opened, and it is said: 'Who is this?' It is said: 'So-and-so.' It is said: 'Welcome to the good soul which was in the good body; enter praised, and rejoice in rest and fragrance and a Lord not angry.' It is continually said to it until it reaches the heaven in which God, mighty and majestic, is. And if he is an evil man, they say: 'Come out, O evil soul, which was in an evil body; come out blameworthy, and rejoice in boiling water and dark pus and other kinds of similar torment.' It is continually said to it until it comes out. Then it is ascended to the heaven, and it is requested to be opened, and it is said: 'Who is this?' It is said: 'So-and-so.' It is said: 'No welcome to the evil soul which was in the evil body; return blameworthy, for the gates of heaven will not be opened for you.' It is sent down from the heaven and then it goes to the grave. The righteous man sits up and is asked the same as was mentioned in the first hadith, and the evil man sits up and is asked the same as was mentioned in the first hadith [[In manuscript A: "الثاني" (the second)]]."

This is a gharib (rare/unusual) hadith.[[Musnad (2/364–365).]]

And He said: ﴿And We gathered them, and We left none of them behind﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf: 47–49]. For this reason He said: ﴿their true Master. Unquestionably, His is the judgment, and He is the swiftest of reckoners﴾.

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Allah, the Exalted, says, bestowing favor upon His servants in that He rescues from them those who are in distress, ﴿from the darknesses of the land and the sea﴾, that is, the bewildered ones who find themselves in the desert wastes and in the deep waters of the sea when the violent wind blows. Then they single out Him alone in supplication, having no partner, as He says: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those whom you invoke vanish except Him. But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away; and man is ever ungrateful﴾ [al-Isra' 17:67]. And He says: ﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea, until when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice therein, there comes upon them a stormy wind and the waves come at them from every place, and they assume that they are encompassed. They supplicate Allah, sincere to Him in religion: "If You should save us from this, we will surely be among the thankful." But when He saves them, at once they commit injustice upon the earth without right﴾ [Yunus 10:22]. And He says: ﴿Is He who guides you in the darknesses of the land and sea, and who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy, is there a god with Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him﴾ [al-Naml 27:63].

And He said in this noble verse: ﴿Say, "Who rescues you from the darknesses of the land and sea, which you call upon in humility and secretly?"﴾, that is, openly and privately. ﴿"If He should rescue us from this"﴾, that is, from this distress, ﴿"we will surely be among the thankful."﴾, that is, after it. Allah [the Exalted] said: ﴿Say, "Allah rescues you from it and from every distress; then you [still] associate others with Him"﴾, that is, after that, ﴿associate﴾, that is, you call upon other gods along with Him in times of ease.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet"﴾: when He said, ﴿Then you associate others with Him﴾, He followed it with this, ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet"﴾, that is, after rescuing you. As He said in Surah al-Isra': ﴿Your Lord is He who drives for you the ships upon the sea that you may seek of His bounty. Indeed He is ever Merciful to you. And when harm touches you at sea, those whom you invoke vanish except Him. But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away; and man is ever ungrateful. Then do you feel secure that He will not cause a side of the land to swallow you or send upon you a storm of stones? Then you will not find for yourselves a protector. Or do you feel secure that He will not return you to it another time and send against you a violent wind and drown you for what you disbelieved? Then you will not find for yourselves against Us any pursuer﴾ [al-Isra' 17:66–69].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Muslim ibn Ibrahim, from Harun al-A'war, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman, from al-Hasan regarding His saying: ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet"﴾, that he said: "This is for the polytheists."

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet"﴾: "It is for the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ, but He pardoned them."

Here we will mention the ahadith and reports related to this, and in Allah is the seeking of help, upon Him is reliance, and in Him is trust.

Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said regarding the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet, or to confuse you with partisanship and make you taste the violence of one another. Look how We diversify the signs that perhaps they will understand"﴾. Yalbisakum: yukhlitakum (mix you), from al-iltibas (confusion). Yalbisu: yakhlitu (they mix). Shiya'an: firqan (sects).

Abu al-Nu'man narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you"﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I seek refuge in Your Face." ﴿Or from beneath your feet﴾, he said: "I seek refuge in Your Face." ﴿Or to confuse you with partisanship and make you taste the violence of one another﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "This is easier" or "This is lighter."

He also narrated it in the "Kitab al-Tawhid," from Qutaybah, from Hammad, with the same chain. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (4628), (7406)]

Al-Nasa'i also narrated it in the "Tafsir," from Qutaybah, Muhammad ibn al-Nadr ibn Musawir, and Yahya ibn Habib ibn Arabi, all four from Hammad ibn Zayd, with the same.

Al-Humaydi narrated it in his Musnad, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Amr ibn Dinar, who heard Jabir, from the Prophet ﷺ, with the same.

Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih, from Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, from Abu Khaythamah, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, with the same.

Ibn Jarir narrated it in his tafsir from Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Qurashi, Sa'id ibn al-Rabi', and Sufyan ibn WakI', all from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, with the same.

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Adam ibn Abi Iyas, Yahya ibn Abd al-Hamid, and Asim ibn Ali, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, with the same.

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it from Hammad ibn Zayd and Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, both from Amr ibn Dinar, with the same. [Al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11164); Musnad al-Humaydi (2/530); Musnad Abi Ya'la (3/362); Tafsir al-Tabari (11/422)]

Another route: The Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said in his tafsir: Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Muqaddam ibn Dawud narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: When this was revealed: ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you"﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I seek refuge in Allah from that." ﴿Or from beneath your feet﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I seek refuge in Allah from that." ﴿Or to confuse you with partisanship﴾, he said: "This is easier," and had he sought refuge for it, He would have granted it. [In its chain is Abd Allah ibn Lahi'ah, who became confused in memory.]

Related to this noble verse are many ahadith:

The first: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said in his Musnad: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Abu Bakr, that is Ibn Abi Maryam, narrated to us, from Rashid, that is Ibn Sa'd al-Muqri'i, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about this verse: ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet"﴾, and he said: "Indeed, it will occur, but its interpretation has not yet come."

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi, from al-Hasan ibn Arafah, from Isma'il ibn Ayyash, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam, with the same. Then he said: This is a very gharib hadith. [Musnad (1/170); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3066).]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ya'la, that is Ibn Ubayd, narrated to us, Uthman ibn Hakim narrated to us, from Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from his father, who said: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until we passed by the mosque of Banu Mu'awiyah. He entered and prayed two rak'ahs, and we prayed with him, and he conversed with his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, at length. Then he said: "I asked my Lord three things. I asked Him not to destroy my Ummah by drowning, and He granted it to me. I asked Him not to destroy my Ummah by famine, and He granted it to me. I asked Him not to make their violence among themselves, and He refused me."

Muslim alone narrated it, in the "Kitab al-Fitan," from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Numayr, both from Abd Allah ibn Numayr; and from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Abi Umar, from Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah, both from Uthman ibn Hakim, with the same. [Musnad (1/175); Sahih Muslim no. (2890).]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: I read to Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Malik, from Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Jabir ibn Atik, from Jabir ibn Atik, that he said: Abd Allah ibn Umar came to us at Banu Mu'awiyah, a village of the Ansar, and said to me: "Do you know where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed in this mosque of yours?" I said: "Yes." And I pointed to a part of it. He said: "Do you know what the three things were that he supplicated for in it?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Tell me of them." I said: He supplicated that enemies from outside them would not overcome them, and that He would not destroy them by famine; and He granted them both. He supplicated that their violence would not be among themselves, and that was refused him. He said: "You have spoken truly. The killing will continue until the Day of Resurrection." [Musnad (5/445); al-Haythami in al-Majma' (7/221) said: "its narrators are trustworthy."]

It is not in any of the Six Books, but its chain is good and strong, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

Another hadith: Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Hakim ibn Hakim ibn Abbad, from Khusayf, from Ali ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman informed me, saying: I went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to the harra of Banu Mu'awiyah. He prayed eight rak'ahs and prolonged them. Then he turned to me and said: "Did I detain you?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Indeed I asked Allah three things. He gave me two and refused me one. I asked Him not to let an enemy from outside them dominate my Ummah, and He granted it. I asked Him not to destroy them by drowning, and He granted it. I asked Him not to make their violence among themselves, and He refused me."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Ishaq. [Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (10/318) narrated it through Abd Allah ibn Numayr from Muhammad ibn Ishaq.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ubaydah ibn Humayd narrated to us, Sulayman al-A'mash narrated to me, from Raja' al-Ansari, from Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seeking him, and it was said to me: "He went out just before." So I did not pass anyone except that he said: "He passed just before," until I passed and found him standing in prayer. I came and stood behind him, and he prolonged the prayer. When he finished his prayer I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have prayed a very long prayer." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed I prayed a prayer of desire and fear. I asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic, three things, and He gave me two and refused me one. I asked Him not to destroy my Ummah by drowning, and He granted it to me. I asked Him not to let an enemy that is not from them dominate them, and He granted it to me. I asked Him not to make their violence among themselves, and He returned it to me."

Ibn Majah narrated it in "al-Fitan," from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Numayr and Ali ibn Muhammad, both from Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, with the same. [Musnad (5/240); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3951).] Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Abu Awanah, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, from the Prophet ﷺ, with the same or similar.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Harun ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us, Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj [in A: "Bakr"], that al-Dahhak ibn Abdullah al-Qurashi narrated to him, from Anas ibn Malik, that he said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey pray the forenoon prayer (Subhat al-Duha) eight rak'ahs. When he finished, he said: 'I prayed a prayer of hope and fear. I asked my Lord for three things and He gave me two and withheld one from me. I asked Him not to destroy my Ummah by famine, and He did so. I asked Him not to let their enemy overcome them, and He did so. I asked Him not to cause them to split into factions (shi'a), but He refused me.'"

Narrated by al-Nasa'i in the Book of Prayer, from Muhammad ibn Salama, from Ibn Wahb, with the same chain.[[Al-Musnad (2/146).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamza informed us, he said: al-Zuhri said: Abdullah ibn Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Khabbab, from his father Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, client of Banu Zuhra, who had witnessed Badr with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) [in M: "I visited"], that he said: "I watched the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a night when he prayed all of it, until at dawn the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished his prayer. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you have prayed tonight a prayer the like of which I have never seen you pray.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed, it was a prayer of hope and fear. I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, for three qualities in it. He gave me two and withheld one from me. I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, not to destroy us with what He destroyed the nations before us with, and He gave it to me. I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, not to let an enemy other than us overcome us, and He gave it to me. I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, not to make us split into factions, and He withheld it from me.'"

Al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamza, with the same chain, and by another route.[[Al-Musnad (5/108) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/216).]] Ibn Hibban in his Sahih narrated it with both of its chains, from Salih ibn Kaysan. Al-Tirmidhi in "al-Fitan" narrated it from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Rashid. Both of them (Salih and al-Nu'man) narrated it from al-Zuhri, with the same chain.[[Al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra as in Tuhfat al-Ashraf (3/115), Sahih Ibn Hibban (9/180) (al-Ihsan), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2175).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih" (good and authentic).

Another hadith: Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said in his Tafsir: Ziyad ibn Ubayd Allah al-Muzani narrated to me, Marwan ibn Mu'awiya al-Fazari narrated to us, Abu Malik narrated to us, Nafi' ibn Khalid al-Khuza'i narrated to me, from his father, that the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed a light prayer, complete in its bowing and prostration, and said: "It was a prayer of hope and fear. I asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic, three things in it, and He gave me two and withheld one from me. I asked Allah not to afflict you with a punishment that befell those before you, and He gave it to me. I asked Allah not to empower over you an enemy who would plunder your territory, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to make you split into factions and make some of you taste the violence of others, but He withheld it from me." Abu Malik said: I said to him: "Did your father hear this from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "Yes, I heard him narrate it to the people, that he heard it from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/433). It was also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (4/192) and al-Bazzar in his Musnad no. (3289) (Kashf al-Astar), through Marwan ibn Mu'awiya with the same chain.]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Ma'mar said: Ayyub informed me, from Abu Qilaba, from Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani, from Abu Asma al-Rahbi, from Shaddad ibn Aws, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah gathered the earth for me until I saw its east and its west, and the dominion of my Ummah will reach what was gathered for me of it. I have been given the two treasures, the white and the red. I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, not to destroy my Ummah by a general famine, and not to empower over them an enemy who would destroy them entirely, and not to make them split into factions, and not to make some of them taste the violence of others." He said: "O Muhammad, when I decree a decree, it cannot be turned back. I have granted you for your Ummah that I will not destroy them with a general famine, and that I will not empower over them an enemy from others than them who would destroy them entirely, until some of them destroy others, some kill others, and some take others captive." And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I fear for my Ummah only the misguiding leaders. When the sword is placed among my Ummah, it will not be lifted from them until the Day of Resurrection."[[Al-Musnad (4/123). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/221): "The men of Ahmad are the men of the Sahih."]]

It is not in any of the al-Kutub al-Sittah (the Six Canonical Books). Its chain is good and strong. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Zayd, Abbad ibn Mansur, and Qatada, all three from Ayyub, from Abu Qilaba, from Abu Asma, from Thawban, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in a similar wording.[[Sahih Muslim no. (2889) narrated it from the route of Hammad ibn Zayd, and from the route of Mu'adh ibn Hisham, from his father, from Qatada, from Abu Qilaba, without mentioning Ayyub.]] And Allah knows best [in A: "And Allah knows best"].

Another hadith: al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Abdullah ibn Isma'il ibn Ibrahim al-Hashimi and Maymun ibn Ishaq ibn al-Hasan al-Hanafi narrated to us, they said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ja'i, from Nafi' ibn Khalid al-Khuza'i, from his father, who said, and his father was one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and one of the People of the Tree: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed while the people were around him, he prayed a light prayer, complete in its bowing and prostration. One day he sat and prolonged his sitting, until some of us signaled to one another: 'Be quiet, he is receiving revelation.' When he finished, some of the people said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, you prolonged your sitting until some of us signaled to one another: he is receiving revelation to you.' He said: 'No, but it was a prayer of hope and fear. I asked Allah in it for three things, and He gave me two and withheld one from me. I asked Allah not to punish you with a punishment with which He punished those before you, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to empower over my Ummah an enemy who would plunder them, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to make you split into factions and not to make some of you taste the violence of others, but He withheld it from me.'" He said: I said to him: "Did your father hear it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "Yes, I heard him say: he heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), [counting] on my fingers, ten fingers."[[Also narrated by al-Bazzar in his Musnad no. (3289) (Kashf al-Astar) and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (4/192), through Abu Malik al-Ash'ja'i, from Nafi', from his father, with the same chain.]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yunus, that is Ibn Muhammad al-Mu'addib, narrated to us, Layth, that is Ibn Sa'd, narrated to us, from Abu Wahb al-Khawlani, from a man whose name he mentioned, from Abu Basra al-Ghifari, a Companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, for four things, and He gave me three and withheld one from me. I asked Allah not to unite my Ummah upon misguidance, and He gave it to me. I asked Allah not to let an enemy from other than them overcome them, and He gave it to me. I asked Allah not to destroy them by years of famine as He destroyed the nations before them, and He gave it to me. And I asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic, not to make them split into factions and not to make some of them taste the violence of others, but He withheld it from me."[[Al-Musnad (6/396). Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/280) through al-Layth with the same chain. Note: In the Musnad it appears as "Abu Wahb al-Khawlani," while in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani it appears as "Abu Hani' al-Khawlani," and the latter is the correct one, as mentioned by al-Mizzi in Tahdhib al-Kamal (7/401) and Ibn Abd al-Barr in al-Istighna (2/976).]]

It is not narrated by anyone from the authors of the al-Kutub al-Sittah.

Another hadith: al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us, Minjab ibn al-Harith narrated to us, Abu Hudhayfa al-Tha'labi narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Ilaqa, from Jabir ibn Samura al-Sawa'i, from Ali [may Allah be pleased with him] [addition from A]; that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I asked my Lord for three qualities, and He gave me two and withheld one from me. I said: 'O Lord, do not destroy my Ummah by hunger.' He said: 'This is yours.' I said: 'O Lord, do not empower over them an enemy from other than them,' meaning the people of polytheism, 'who would annihilate them.' He said: 'That is yours.' I said: 'O Lord, do not make their violence among themselves.' " He said: "So He withheld this one from me."[[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (1/107). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/222): "In it is Abu Hudhayfa al-Tha'labi, whom I do not know, and the rest of its men are trustworthy."]]

Another hadith: al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Asim, Abu al-Darda al-Marwazi narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Kaysan narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I called upon my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to lift four things from my Ummah. He lifted two of them from them, and refused me to lift two of them. I called upon my Lord to lift stoning from the sky and drowning from the earth, and not to make them split into factions and not to make some of them taste the violence of others. So He lifted from them stoning from the sky and drowning from the earth, and Allah refused to lift two: killing and al-Haraj (chaos, mutual slaughter)."

Another route from Ibn Abbas also: Ibn Mardawayh said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd [in A: "Yazid"] narrated to me, al-Walid ibn Aban narrated to me, Ja'far ibn Munir narrated to us, Abu Badr Shuja' ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Amr ibn Qays narrated to us, from a man, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Say, He is the One able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet, or to confuse you into factions and make you taste the violence of one another﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) stood, performed ablution, then said: "O Allah, do not send upon my Ummah a punishment from above them, nor from beneath their feet, nor confuse them into factions, nor make some of them taste the violence of others." He said: Then Jibril came to him and said: "O Muhammad, Allah has granted protection to your Ummah from being sent upon them a punishment from above them or from beneath their feet."[[Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/374) through Abu al-Darda al-Marwazi, and in its chain are men I do not know.]]

Another hadith: Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Bazzar narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Musa narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi narrated to us, Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu al-Minhal, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "I asked my Lord for my Ummah four qualities, and He gave me three and withheld one from me. I asked Him that my Ummah would not disbelieve entirely, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to punish them with what He punished the nations before them, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to let an enemy from other than them overcome them, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to make their violence among themselves, but He withheld it from me."

Al-Tabarani narrated it, through Ibn Abi Hatim, from Abu Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan, from Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi, with a similar wording.[[Al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat no. (4336) (Majma' al-Bahrayn), through al-Qatay'i from Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi with the same chain. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/222): "Its men are trustworthy."]]

Another route: Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, Kathir ibn Zayd al-Laythi al-Madani narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Rabah, a freedman of the family of Abu Dhubab, narrated to me, that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I asked my Lord for three things, and He gave me two and denied me one. I asked Him that He not let an enemy from other than them dominate my Ummah, and He gave me that. I asked Him that He not destroy them by famine, and He gave me that. I asked Him that He not cause them to be divided into factions (shiya') and that He not let some of them inflict violence upon others, but He denied me that."

Then Ibn Mardawayh narrated it with its chain from Sa'd ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with similar wording. Al-Bazzar narrated it through the route of Umar ibn Salamah, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with similar wording. [Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (3290), Kashf al-Astar.]

Another report: Sufyan al-Thawri said, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "Four [punishments] are for this Ummah: two have passed, and two remain: ﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment from above you﴾ — he said: stoning. ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾ — he said: sinking into the earth. ﴿or to confuse you with factions and make you taste the violence of one another﴾." Sufyan said: meaning stoning and sinking into the earth.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b: ﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet or to confuse you with factions and make you taste the violence of one another﴾. He said: They are four characteristics, two of which came after the death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) by twenty-five years: they were confused into factions and some of them tasted the violence of others. Two remain which must befall them: stoning and sinking into the earth.

Ahmad narrated it from Waki', from Abu Ja'far. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Mundhir ibn Shadhan narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abu al-Ashhab narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment [from above you or from beneath your feet or to confuse you with factions]﴾ — the verse — he said: "Its punishment was withheld until its sin was committed, and when its sin was committed, its punishment was released."

Likewise said Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Malik, Mujahid, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd regarding His words: ﴿a punishment from above you﴾, meaning stoning, and ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾, meaning sinking into the earth. This is the choice of Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Yunus, from Ibn Wahb, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam regarding His words: ﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet﴾, he said: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) used to cry out while in the gathering — or upon the pulpit — saying: "O people, it has indeed descended upon you. Allah says: ﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment from above you [or from beneath your feet]﴾. If a punishment came to you from the sky, it would leave none of you alive; ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾: if the earth swallowed you up, it would destroy you and leave none of you alive; ﴿or to confuse you with factions and make you taste the violence of one another﴾. Behold, the worst of the three has descended upon you."

Second opinion: Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, I heard Khallad ibn Sulayman say: I heard Amir ibn Abd al-Rahman say: Ibn Abbas used to say regarding this verse, ﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment from above you﴾: as for the punishment from above you, it is evil rulers; ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾: evil servants.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿a punishment from above you﴾ means your rulers; ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾ means your slaves and your lowest-ranking people.

Ibn Abi Hatim related something similar from Abu Sinan and Umayr ibn Hani'.

Ibn Jarir said: Although this view has a valid basis, the first is more apparent and stronger.

What Ibn Jarir said is correct, may Allah have mercy on him, and what supports its soundness is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Are you secure from the One in heaven that He will not cause the earth to swallow you, and then it shakes? Or are you secure from the One in heaven that He will not send against you a storm of stones? Then you will know how was My warning. And previously denied those before them, so how was My reproach﴾ [al-Mulk: 16–18]. And in the hadith: "There will surely occur in this Ummah a hurling of stones, sinking into the earth, and transformation (maskh)." [Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (2/163) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with him.] This is mentioned along with its counterparts among the signs of the Hour, its portents, and the appearance of signs before the Day of Resurrection, and it will come in its appropriate place, Allah willing.

* *

His words: ﴿or to confuse you with factions﴾ mean: to make you mingled, divided into factions (shiya') differing from one another. Al-Walibi related from Ibn Abbas: it means the desires (ahwa'); and Mujahid and others said likewise.

It has been reported in hadith, narrated through various routes from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "This Ummah will split into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire except one."

* *

His words: ﴿and make you taste the violence of one another﴾. Ibn Abbas and others said: it means He empowers some of you over others, with punishment and killing.

* *

His words: ﴿See how We vary the signs﴾, meaning: We clarify them, make them evident and explain them, ﴿that they may understand﴾, meaning: that they may comprehend and reflect upon Allah's signs, proofs and evidences.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: When the verse ﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment from above you [or from beneath your feet]﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not return after me as disbelievers, striking one another's necks with swords." They said: "We testify that there is no god but Allah, and that you are the Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." Some people said: "This will never happen, that some of us kill others while we are Muslims." So there was revealed: ﴿See how We vary the signs that they may understand. But your people have denied it, while it is the truth. Say: I am not a guardian over you. For every news is a fixed time, and you will come to know﴾.

Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir. [Tafsir al-Tabari (11/430).]

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Allah, the Exalted, says, bestowing favor upon His servants in that He rescues from them those who are in distress, ﴿from the darknesses of the land and the sea﴾, that is, the bewildered ones who find themselves in the desert wastes and in the deep waters of the sea when the violent wind blows. Then they single out Him alone in supplication, having no partner, as He says: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those whom you invoke vanish except Him. But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away; and man is ever ungrateful﴾ [al-Isra' 17:67]. And He says: ﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea, until when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice therein, there comes upon them a stormy wind and the waves come at them from every place, and they assume that they are encompassed. They supplicate Allah, sincere to Him in religion: "If You should save us from this, we will surely be among the thankful." But when He saves them, at once they commit injustice upon the earth without right﴾ [Yunus 10:22]. And He says: ﴿Is He who guides you in the darknesses of the land and sea, and who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy, is there a god with Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him﴾ [al-Naml 27:63].

And He said in this noble verse: ﴿Say, "Who rescues you from the darknesses of the land and sea, which you call upon in humility and secretly?"﴾, that is, openly and privately. ﴿"If He should rescue us from this"﴾, that is, from this distress, ﴿"we will surely be among the thankful."﴾, that is, after it. Allah [the Exalted] said: ﴿Say, "Allah rescues you from it and from every distress; then you [still] associate others with Him"﴾, that is, after that, ﴿associate﴾, that is, you call upon other gods along with Him in times of ease.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet"﴾: when He said, ﴿Then you associate others with Him﴾, He followed it with this, ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet"﴾, that is, after rescuing you. As He said in Surah al-Isra': ﴿Your Lord is He who drives for you the ships upon the sea that you may seek of His bounty. Indeed He is ever Merciful to you. And when harm touches you at sea, those whom you invoke vanish except Him. But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away; and man is ever ungrateful. Then do you feel secure that He will not cause a side of the land to swallow you or send upon you a storm of stones? Then you will not find for yourselves a protector. Or do you feel secure that He will not return you to it another time and send against you a violent wind and drown you for what you disbelieved? Then you will not find for yourselves against Us any pursuer﴾ [al-Isra' 17:66–69].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Muslim ibn Ibrahim, from Harun al-A'war, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman, from al-Hasan regarding His saying: ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet"﴾, that he said: "This is for the polytheists."

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet"﴾: "It is for the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ, but He pardoned them."

Here we will mention the ahadith and reports related to this, and in Allah is the seeking of help, upon Him is reliance, and in Him is trust.

Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said regarding the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet, or to confuse you with partisanship and make you taste the violence of one another. Look how We diversify the signs that perhaps they will understand"﴾. Yalbisakum: yukhlitakum (mix you), from al-iltibas (confusion). Yalbisu: yakhlitu (they mix). Shiya'an: firqan (sects).

Abu al-Nu'man narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you"﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I seek refuge in Your Face." ﴿Or from beneath your feet﴾, he said: "I seek refuge in Your Face." ﴿Or to confuse you with partisanship and make you taste the violence of one another﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "This is easier" or "This is lighter."

He also narrated it in the "Kitab al-Tawhid," from Qutaybah, from Hammad, with the same chain. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (4628), (7406)]

Al-Nasa'i also narrated it in the "Tafsir," from Qutaybah, Muhammad ibn al-Nadr ibn Musawir, and Yahya ibn Habib ibn Arabi, all four from Hammad ibn Zayd, with the same.

Al-Humaydi narrated it in his Musnad, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Amr ibn Dinar, who heard Jabir, from the Prophet ﷺ, with the same.

Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih, from Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, from Abu Khaythamah, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, with the same.

Ibn Jarir narrated it in his tafsir from Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Qurashi, Sa'id ibn al-Rabi', and Sufyan ibn WakI', all from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, with the same.

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Adam ibn Abi Iyas, Yahya ibn Abd al-Hamid, and Asim ibn Ali, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, with the same.

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it from Hammad ibn Zayd and Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, both from Amr ibn Dinar, with the same. [Al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11164); Musnad al-Humaydi (2/530); Musnad Abi Ya'la (3/362); Tafsir al-Tabari (11/422)]

Another route: The Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said in his tafsir: Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Muqaddam ibn Dawud narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: When this was revealed: ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you"﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I seek refuge in Allah from that." ﴿Or from beneath your feet﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I seek refuge in Allah from that." ﴿Or to confuse you with partisanship﴾, he said: "This is easier," and had he sought refuge for it, He would have granted it. [In its chain is Abd Allah ibn Lahi'ah, who became confused in memory.]

Related to this noble verse are many ahadith:

The first: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said in his Musnad: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Abu Bakr, that is Ibn Abi Maryam, narrated to us, from Rashid, that is Ibn Sa'd al-Muqri'i, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about this verse: ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet"﴾, and he said: "Indeed, it will occur, but its interpretation has not yet come."

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi, from al-Hasan ibn Arafah, from Isma'il ibn Ayyash, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam, with the same. Then he said: This is a very gharib hadith. [Musnad (1/170); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3066).]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ya'la, that is Ibn Ubayd, narrated to us, Uthman ibn Hakim narrated to us, from Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from his father, who said: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until we passed by the mosque of Banu Mu'awiyah. He entered and prayed two rak'ahs, and we prayed with him, and he conversed with his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, at length. Then he said: "I asked my Lord three things. I asked Him not to destroy my Ummah by drowning, and He granted it to me. I asked Him not to destroy my Ummah by famine, and He granted it to me. I asked Him not to make their violence among themselves, and He refused me."

Muslim alone narrated it, in the "Kitab al-Fitan," from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Numayr, both from Abd Allah ibn Numayr; and from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Abi Umar, from Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah, both from Uthman ibn Hakim, with the same. [Musnad (1/175); Sahih Muslim no. (2890).]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: I read to Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Malik, from Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Jabir ibn Atik, from Jabir ibn Atik, that he said: Abd Allah ibn Umar came to us at Banu Mu'awiyah, a village of the Ansar, and said to me: "Do you know where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed in this mosque of yours?" I said: "Yes." And I pointed to a part of it. He said: "Do you know what the three things were that he supplicated for in it?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Tell me of them." I said: He supplicated that enemies from outside them would not overcome them, and that He would not destroy them by famine; and He granted them both. He supplicated that their violence would not be among themselves, and that was refused him. He said: "You have spoken truly. The killing will continue until the Day of Resurrection." [Musnad (5/445); al-Haythami in al-Majma' (7/221) said: "its narrators are trustworthy."]

It is not in any of the Six Books, but its chain is good and strong, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

Another hadith: Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Hakim ibn Hakim ibn Abbad, from Khusayf, from Ali ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman informed me, saying: I went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to the harra of Banu Mu'awiyah. He prayed eight rak'ahs and prolonged them. Then he turned to me and said: "Did I detain you?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Indeed I asked Allah three things. He gave me two and refused me one. I asked Him not to let an enemy from outside them dominate my Ummah, and He granted it. I asked Him not to destroy them by drowning, and He granted it. I asked Him not to make their violence among themselves, and He refused me."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Ishaq. [Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (10/318) narrated it through Abd Allah ibn Numayr from Muhammad ibn Ishaq.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ubaydah ibn Humayd narrated to us, Sulayman al-A'mash narrated to me, from Raja' al-Ansari, from Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seeking him, and it was said to me: "He went out just before." So I did not pass anyone except that he said: "He passed just before," until I passed and found him standing in prayer. I came and stood behind him, and he prolonged the prayer. When he finished his prayer I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have prayed a very long prayer." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed I prayed a prayer of desire and fear. I asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic, three things, and He gave me two and refused me one. I asked Him not to destroy my Ummah by drowning, and He granted it to me. I asked Him not to let an enemy that is not from them dominate them, and He granted it to me. I asked Him not to make their violence among themselves, and He returned it to me."

Ibn Majah narrated it in "al-Fitan," from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Numayr and Ali ibn Muhammad, both from Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, with the same. [Musnad (5/240); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3951).] Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Abu Awanah, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, from the Prophet ﷺ, with the same or similar.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Harun ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us, Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj [in A: "Bakr"], that al-Dahhak ibn Abdullah al-Qurashi narrated to him, from Anas ibn Malik, that he said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey pray the forenoon prayer (Subhat al-Duha) eight rak'ahs. When he finished, he said: 'I prayed a prayer of hope and fear. I asked my Lord for three things and He gave me two and withheld one from me. I asked Him not to destroy my Ummah by famine, and He did so. I asked Him not to let their enemy overcome them, and He did so. I asked Him not to cause them to split into factions (shi'a), but He refused me.'"

Narrated by al-Nasa'i in the Book of Prayer, from Muhammad ibn Salama, from Ibn Wahb, with the same chain.[[Al-Musnad (2/146).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamza informed us, he said: al-Zuhri said: Abdullah ibn Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Khabbab, from his father Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, client of Banu Zuhra, who had witnessed Badr with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) [in M: "I visited"], that he said: "I watched the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a night when he prayed all of it, until at dawn the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished his prayer. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you have prayed tonight a prayer the like of which I have never seen you pray.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed, it was a prayer of hope and fear. I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, for three qualities in it. He gave me two and withheld one from me. I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, not to destroy us with what He destroyed the nations before us with, and He gave it to me. I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, not to let an enemy other than us overcome us, and He gave it to me. I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, not to make us split into factions, and He withheld it from me.'"

Al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamza, with the same chain, and by another route.[[Al-Musnad (5/108) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/216).]] Ibn Hibban in his Sahih narrated it with both of its chains, from Salih ibn Kaysan. Al-Tirmidhi in "al-Fitan" narrated it from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Rashid. Both of them (Salih and al-Nu'man) narrated it from al-Zuhri, with the same chain.[[Al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra as in Tuhfat al-Ashraf (3/115), Sahih Ibn Hibban (9/180) (al-Ihsan), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2175).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih" (good and authentic).

Another hadith: Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said in his Tafsir: Ziyad ibn Ubayd Allah al-Muzani narrated to me, Marwan ibn Mu'awiya al-Fazari narrated to us, Abu Malik narrated to us, Nafi' ibn Khalid al-Khuza'i narrated to me, from his father, that the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed a light prayer, complete in its bowing and prostration, and said: "It was a prayer of hope and fear. I asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic, three things in it, and He gave me two and withheld one from me. I asked Allah not to afflict you with a punishment that befell those before you, and He gave it to me. I asked Allah not to empower over you an enemy who would plunder your territory, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to make you split into factions and make some of you taste the violence of others, but He withheld it from me." Abu Malik said: I said to him: "Did your father hear this from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "Yes, I heard him narrate it to the people, that he heard it from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/433). It was also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (4/192) and al-Bazzar in his Musnad no. (3289) (Kashf al-Astar), through Marwan ibn Mu'awiya with the same chain.]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Ma'mar said: Ayyub informed me, from Abu Qilaba, from Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani, from Abu Asma al-Rahbi, from Shaddad ibn Aws, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah gathered the earth for me until I saw its east and its west, and the dominion of my Ummah will reach what was gathered for me of it. I have been given the two treasures, the white and the red. I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, not to destroy my Ummah by a general famine, and not to empower over them an enemy who would destroy them entirely, and not to make them split into factions, and not to make some of them taste the violence of others." He said: "O Muhammad, when I decree a decree, it cannot be turned back. I have granted you for your Ummah that I will not destroy them with a general famine, and that I will not empower over them an enemy from others than them who would destroy them entirely, until some of them destroy others, some kill others, and some take others captive." And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I fear for my Ummah only the misguiding leaders. When the sword is placed among my Ummah, it will not be lifted from them until the Day of Resurrection."[[Al-Musnad (4/123). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/221): "The men of Ahmad are the men of the Sahih."]]

It is not in any of the al-Kutub al-Sittah (the Six Canonical Books). Its chain is good and strong. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Zayd, Abbad ibn Mansur, and Qatada, all three from Ayyub, from Abu Qilaba, from Abu Asma, from Thawban, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in a similar wording.[[Sahih Muslim no. (2889) narrated it from the route of Hammad ibn Zayd, and from the route of Mu'adh ibn Hisham, from his father, from Qatada, from Abu Qilaba, without mentioning Ayyub.]] And Allah knows best [in A: "And Allah knows best"].

Another hadith: al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Abdullah ibn Isma'il ibn Ibrahim al-Hashimi and Maymun ibn Ishaq ibn al-Hasan al-Hanafi narrated to us, they said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ja'i, from Nafi' ibn Khalid al-Khuza'i, from his father, who said, and his father was one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and one of the People of the Tree: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed while the people were around him, he prayed a light prayer, complete in its bowing and prostration. One day he sat and prolonged his sitting, until some of us signaled to one another: 'Be quiet, he is receiving revelation.' When he finished, some of the people said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, you prolonged your sitting until some of us signaled to one another: he is receiving revelation to you.' He said: 'No, but it was a prayer of hope and fear. I asked Allah in it for three things, and He gave me two and withheld one from me. I asked Allah not to punish you with a punishment with which He punished those before you, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to empower over my Ummah an enemy who would plunder them, and He gave it to me.
