I asked Him not to make you split into factions and not to make some of you taste the violence of others, but He withheld it from me.'" He said: I said to him: "Did your father hear it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "Yes, I heard him say: he heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), [counting] on my fingers, ten fingers."[[Also narrated by al-Bazzar in his Musnad no. (3289) (Kashf al-Astar) and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (4/192), through Abu Malik al-Ash'ja'i, from Nafi', from his father, with the same chain.]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yunus, that is Ibn Muhammad al-Mu'addib, narrated to us, Layth, that is Ibn Sa'd, narrated to us, from Abu Wahb al-Khawlani, from a man whose name he mentioned, from Abu Basra al-Ghifari, a Companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, for four things, and He gave me three and withheld one from me. I asked Allah not to unite my Ummah upon misguidance, and He gave it to me. I asked Allah not to let an enemy from other than them overcome them, and He gave it to me. I asked Allah not to destroy them by years of famine as He destroyed the nations before them, and He gave it to me. And I asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic, not to make them split into factions and not to make some of them taste the violence of others, but He withheld it from me."[[Al-Musnad (6/396). Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/280) through al-Layth with the same chain. Note: In the Musnad it appears as "Abu Wahb al-Khawlani," while in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani it appears as "Abu Hani' al-Khawlani," and the latter is the correct one, as mentioned by al-Mizzi in Tahdhib al-Kamal (7/401) and Ibn Abd al-Barr in al-Istighna (2/976).]]

It is not narrated by anyone from the authors of the al-Kutub al-Sittah.

Another hadith: al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us, Minjab ibn al-Harith narrated to us, Abu Hudhayfa al-Tha'labi narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Ilaqa, from Jabir ibn Samura al-Sawa'i, from Ali [may Allah be pleased with him] [addition from A]; that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I asked my Lord for three qualities, and He gave me two and withheld one from me. I said: 'O Lord, do not destroy my Ummah by hunger.' He said: 'This is yours.' I said: 'O Lord, do not empower over them an enemy from other than them,' meaning the people of polytheism, 'who would annihilate them.' He said: 'That is yours.' I said: 'O Lord, do not make their violence among themselves.' " He said: "So He withheld this one from me."[[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (1/107). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/222): "In it is Abu Hudhayfa al-Tha'labi, whom I do not know, and the rest of its men are trustworthy."]]

Another hadith: al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Asim, Abu al-Darda al-Marwazi narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Kaysan narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I called upon my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to lift four things from my Ummah. He lifted two of them from them, and refused me to lift two of them. I called upon my Lord to lift stoning from the sky and drowning from the earth, and not to make them split into factions and not to make some of them taste the violence of others. So He lifted from them stoning from the sky and drowning from the earth, and Allah refused to lift two: killing and al-Haraj (chaos, mutual slaughter)."

Another route from Ibn Abbas also: Ibn Mardawayh said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd [in A: "Yazid"] narrated to me, al-Walid ibn Aban narrated to me, Ja'far ibn Munir narrated to us, Abu Badr Shuja' ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Amr ibn Qays narrated to us, from a man, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Say, He is the One able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet, or to confuse you into factions and make you taste the violence of one another﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) stood, performed ablution, then said: "O Allah, do not send upon my Ummah a punishment from above them, nor from beneath their feet, nor confuse them into factions, nor make some of them taste the violence of others." He said: Then Jibril came to him and said: "O Muhammad, Allah has granted protection to your Ummah from being sent upon them a punishment from above them or from beneath their feet."[[Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/374) through Abu al-Darda al-Marwazi, and in its chain are men I do not know.]]

Another hadith: Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Bazzar narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Musa narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi narrated to us, Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu al-Minhal, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "I asked my Lord for my Ummah four qualities, and He gave me three and withheld one from me. I asked Him that my Ummah would not disbelieve entirely, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to punish them with what He punished the nations before them, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to let an enemy from other than them overcome them, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to make their violence among themselves, but He withheld it from me."

Al-Tabarani narrated it, through Ibn Abi Hatim, from Abu Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan, from Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi, with a similar wording.[[Al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat no. (4336) (Majma' al-Bahrayn), through al-Qatay'i from Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi with the same chain. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/222): "Its men are trustworthy."]]

Another route: Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, Kathir ibn Zayd al-Laythi al-Madani narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Rabah, a freedman of the family of Abu Dhubab, narrated to me, that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I asked my Lord for three things, and He gave me two and denied me one. I asked Him that He not let an enemy from other than them dominate my Ummah, and He gave me that. I asked Him that He not destroy them by famine, and He gave me that. I asked Him that He not cause them to be divided into factions (shiya') and that He not let some of them inflict violence upon others, but He denied me that."

Then Ibn Mardawayh narrated it with its chain from Sa'd ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with similar wording. Al-Bazzar narrated it through the route of Umar ibn Salamah, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with similar wording. [Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (3290), Kashf al-Astar.]

Another report: Sufyan al-Thawri said, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "Four [punishments] are for this Ummah: two have passed, and two remain: ﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment from above you﴾ — he said: stoning. ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾ — he said: sinking into the earth. ﴿or to confuse you with factions and make you taste the violence of one another﴾." Sufyan said: meaning stoning and sinking into the earth.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b: ﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet or to confuse you with factions and make you taste the violence of one another﴾. He said: They are four characteristics, two of which came after the death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) by twenty-five years: they were confused into factions and some of them tasted the violence of others. Two remain which must befall them: stoning and sinking into the earth.

Ahmad narrated it from Waki', from Abu Ja'far. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Mundhir ibn Shadhan narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abu al-Ashhab narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment [from above you or from beneath your feet or to confuse you with factions]﴾ — the verse — he said: "Its punishment was withheld until its sin was committed, and when its sin was committed, its punishment was released."

Likewise said Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Malik, Mujahid, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd regarding His words: ﴿a punishment from above you﴾, meaning stoning, and ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾, meaning sinking into the earth. This is the choice of Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Yunus, from Ibn Wahb, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam regarding His words: ﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet﴾, he said: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) used to cry out while in the gathering — or upon the pulpit — saying: "O people, it has indeed descended upon you. Allah says: ﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment from above you [or from beneath your feet]﴾. If a punishment came to you from the sky, it would leave none of you alive; ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾: if the earth swallowed you up, it would destroy you and leave none of you alive; ﴿or to confuse you with factions and make you taste the violence of one another﴾. Behold, the worst of the three has descended upon you."

Second opinion: Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, I heard Khallad ibn Sulayman say: I heard Amir ibn Abd al-Rahman say: Ibn Abbas used to say regarding this verse, ﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment from above you﴾: as for the punishment from above you, it is evil rulers; ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾: evil servants.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿a punishment from above you﴾ means your rulers; ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾ means your slaves and your lowest-ranking people.

Ibn Abi Hatim related something similar from Abu Sinan and Umayr ibn Hani'.

Ibn Jarir said: Although this view has a valid basis, the first is more apparent and stronger.

What Ibn Jarir said is correct, may Allah have mercy on him, and what supports its soundness is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Are you secure from the One in heaven that He will not cause the earth to swallow you, and then it shakes? Or are you secure from the One in heaven that He will not send against you a storm of stones? Then you will know how was My warning. And previously denied those before them, so how was My reproach﴾ [al-Mulk: 16–18]. And in the hadith: "There will surely occur in this Ummah a hurling of stones, sinking into the earth, and transformation (maskh)." [Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (2/163) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with him.] This is mentioned along with its counterparts among the signs of the Hour, its portents, and the appearance of signs before the Day of Resurrection, and it will come in its appropriate place, Allah willing.

* *

His words: ﴿or to confuse you with factions﴾ mean: to make you mingled, divided into factions (shiya') differing from one another. Al-Walibi related from Ibn Abbas: it means the desires (ahwa'); and Mujahid and others said likewise.

It has been reported in hadith, narrated through various routes from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "This Ummah will split into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire except one."

* *

His words: ﴿and make you taste the violence of one another﴾. Ibn Abbas and others said: it means He empowers some of you over others, with punishment and killing.

* *

His words: ﴿See how We vary the signs﴾, meaning: We clarify them, make them evident and explain them, ﴿that they may understand﴾, meaning: that they may comprehend and reflect upon Allah's signs, proofs and evidences.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: When the verse ﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment from above you [or from beneath your feet]﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not return after me as disbelievers, striking one another's necks with swords." They said: "We testify that there is no god but Allah, and that you are the Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." Some people said: "This will never happen, that some of us kill others while we are Muslims." So there was revealed: ﴿See how We vary the signs that they may understand. But your people have denied it, while it is the truth. Say: I am not a guardian over you. For every news is a fixed time, and you will come to know﴾.

Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir. [Tafsir al-Tabari (11/430).]

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Allah, the Exalted, says, bestowing favor upon His servants in that He rescues from them those who are in distress, ﴿from the darknesses of the land and the sea﴾, that is, the bewildered ones who find themselves in the desert wastes and in the deep waters of the sea when the violent wind blows. Then they single out Him alone in supplication, having no partner, as He says: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those whom you invoke vanish except Him. But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away; and man is ever ungrateful﴾ [al-Isra' 17:67]. And He says: ﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea, until when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice therein, there comes upon them a stormy wind and the waves come at them from every place, and they assume that they are encompassed. They supplicate Allah, sincere to Him in religion: "If You should save us from this, we will surely be among the thankful." But when He saves them, at once they commit injustice upon the earth without right﴾ [Yunus 10:22]. And He says: ﴿Is He who guides you in the darknesses of the land and sea, and who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy, is there a god with Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him﴾ [al-Naml 27:63].

And He said in this noble verse: ﴿Say, "Who rescues you from the darknesses of the land and sea, which you call upon in humility and secretly?"﴾, that is, openly and privately. ﴿"If He should rescue us from this"﴾, that is, from this distress, ﴿"we will surely be among the thankful."﴾, that is, after it. Allah [the Exalted] said: ﴿Say, "Allah rescues you from it and from every distress; then you [still] associate others with Him"﴾, that is, after that, ﴿associate﴾, that is, you call upon other gods along with Him in times of ease.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet"﴾: when He said, ﴿Then you associate others with Him﴾, He followed it with this, ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet"﴾, that is, after rescuing you. As He said in Surah al-Isra': ﴿Your Lord is He who drives for you the ships upon the sea that you may seek of His bounty. Indeed He is ever Merciful to you. And when harm touches you at sea, those whom you invoke vanish except Him. But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away; and man is ever ungrateful. Then do you feel secure that He will not cause a side of the land to swallow you or send upon you a storm of stones? Then you will not find for yourselves a protector. Or do you feel secure that He will not return you to it another time and send against you a violent wind and drown you for what you disbelieved? Then you will not find for yourselves against Us any pursuer﴾ [al-Isra' 17:66–69].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Muslim ibn Ibrahim, from Harun al-A'war, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman, from al-Hasan regarding His saying: ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet"﴾, that he said: "This is for the polytheists."

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet"﴾: "It is for the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ, but He pardoned them."

Here we will mention the ahadith and reports related to this, and in Allah is the seeking of help, upon Him is reliance, and in Him is trust.

Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said regarding the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet, or to confuse you with partisanship and make you taste the violence of one another. Look how We diversify the signs that perhaps they will understand"﴾. Yalbisakum: yukhlitakum (mix you), from al-iltibas (confusion). Yalbisu: yakhlitu (they mix). Shiya'an: firqan (sects).

Abu al-Nu'man narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you"﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I seek refuge in Your Face." ﴿Or from beneath your feet﴾, he said: "I seek refuge in Your Face." ﴿Or to confuse you with partisanship and make you taste the violence of one another﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "This is easier" or "This is lighter."

He also narrated it in the "Kitab al-Tawhid," from Qutaybah, from Hammad, with the same chain. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (4628), (7406)]

Al-Nasa'i also narrated it in the "Tafsir," from Qutaybah, Muhammad ibn al-Nadr ibn Musawir, and Yahya ibn Habib ibn Arabi, all four from Hammad ibn Zayd, with the same.

Al-Humaydi narrated it in his Musnad, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Amr ibn Dinar, who heard Jabir, from the Prophet ﷺ, with the same.

Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih, from Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, from Abu Khaythamah, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, with the same.

Ibn Jarir narrated it in his tafsir from Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Qurashi, Sa'id ibn al-Rabi', and Sufyan ibn WakI', all from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, with the same.

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Adam ibn Abi Iyas, Yahya ibn Abd al-Hamid, and Asim ibn Ali, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, with the same.

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it from Hammad ibn Zayd and Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, both from Amr ibn Dinar, with the same. [Al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11164); Musnad al-Humaydi (2/530); Musnad Abi Ya'la (3/362); Tafsir al-Tabari (11/422)]

Another route: The Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said in his tafsir: Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Muqaddam ibn Dawud narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: When this was revealed: ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you"﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I seek refuge in Allah from that." ﴿Or from beneath your feet﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I seek refuge in Allah from that." ﴿Or to confuse you with partisanship﴾, he said: "This is easier," and had he sought refuge for it, He would have granted it. [In its chain is Abd Allah ibn Lahi'ah, who became confused in memory.]

Related to this noble verse are many ahadith:

The first: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said in his Musnad: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Abu Bakr, that is Ibn Abi Maryam, narrated to us, from Rashid, that is Ibn Sa'd al-Muqri'i, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about this verse: ﴿Say, "He is Able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet"﴾, and he said: "Indeed, it will occur, but its interpretation has not yet come."

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi, from al-Hasan ibn Arafah, from Isma'il ibn Ayyash, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam, with the same. Then he said: This is a very gharib hadith. [Musnad (1/170); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3066).]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ya'la, that is Ibn Ubayd, narrated to us, Uthman ibn Hakim narrated to us, from Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from his father, who said: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until we passed by the mosque of Banu Mu'awiyah. He entered and prayed two rak'ahs, and we prayed with him, and he conversed with his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, at length. Then he said: "I asked my Lord three things. I asked Him not to destroy my Ummah by drowning, and He granted it to me. I asked Him not to destroy my Ummah by famine, and He granted it to me. I asked Him not to make their violence among themselves, and He refused me."

Muslim alone narrated it, in the "Kitab al-Fitan," from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Numayr, both from Abd Allah ibn Numayr; and from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Abi Umar, from Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah, both from Uthman ibn Hakim, with the same. [Musnad (1/175); Sahih Muslim no. (2890).]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: I read to Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Malik, from Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Jabir ibn Atik, from Jabir ibn Atik, that he said: Abd Allah ibn Umar came to us at Banu Mu'awiyah, a village of the Ansar, and said to me: "Do you know where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed in this mosque of yours?" I said: "Yes." And I pointed to a part of it. He said: "Do you know what the three things were that he supplicated for in it?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Tell me of them." I said: He supplicated that enemies from outside them would not overcome them, and that He would not destroy them by famine; and He granted them both. He supplicated that their violence would not be among themselves, and that was refused him. He said: "You have spoken truly. The killing will continue until the Day of Resurrection." [Musnad (5/445); al-Haythami in al-Majma' (7/221) said: "its narrators are trustworthy."]

It is not in any of the Six Books, but its chain is good and strong, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

Another hadith: Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Hakim ibn Hakim ibn Abbad, from Khusayf, from Ali ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman informed me, saying: I went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to the harra of Banu Mu'awiyah. He prayed eight rak'ahs and prolonged them. Then he turned to me and said: "Did I detain you?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Indeed I asked Allah three things. He gave me two and refused me one. I asked Him not to let an enemy from outside them dominate my Ummah, and He granted it. I asked Him not to destroy them by drowning, and He granted it. I asked Him not to make their violence among themselves, and He refused me."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Ishaq. [Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (10/318) narrated it through Abd Allah ibn Numayr from Muhammad ibn Ishaq.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ubaydah ibn Humayd narrated to us, Sulayman al-A'mash narrated to me, from Raja' al-Ansari, from Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seeking him, and it was said to me: "He went out just before." So I did not pass anyone except that he said: "He passed just before," until I passed and found him standing in prayer. I came and stood behind him, and he prolonged the prayer. When he finished his prayer I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have prayed a very long prayer." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed I prayed a prayer of desire and fear. I asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic, three things, and He gave me two and refused me one. I asked Him not to destroy my Ummah by drowning, and He granted it to me. I asked Him not to let an enemy that is not from them dominate them, and He granted it to me. I asked Him not to make their violence among themselves, and He returned it to me."

Ibn Majah narrated it in "al-Fitan," from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Numayr and Ali ibn Muhammad, both from Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, with the same. [Musnad (5/240); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3951).] Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Abu Awanah, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, from the Prophet ﷺ, with the same or similar.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Harun ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us, Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj [in A: "Bakr"], that al-Dahhak ibn Abdullah al-Qurashi narrated to him, from Anas ibn Malik, that he said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey pray the forenoon prayer (Subhat al-Duha) eight rak'ahs. When he finished, he said: 'I prayed a prayer of hope and fear. I asked my Lord for three things and He gave me two and withheld one from me. I asked Him not to destroy my Ummah by famine, and He did so. I asked Him not to let their enemy overcome them, and He did so. I asked Him not to cause them to split into factions (shi'a), but He refused me.'"

Narrated by al-Nasa'i in the Book of Prayer, from Muhammad ibn Salama, from Ibn Wahb, with the same chain.[[Al-Musnad (2/146).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamza informed us, he said: al-Zuhri said: Abdullah ibn Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Khabbab, from his father Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, client of Banu Zuhra, who had witnessed Badr with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) [in M: "I visited"], that he said: "I watched the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a night when he prayed all of it, until at dawn the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished his prayer. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you have prayed tonight a prayer the like of which I have never seen you pray.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed, it was a prayer of hope and fear. I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, for three qualities in it. He gave me two and withheld one from me. I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, not to destroy us with what He destroyed the nations before us with, and He gave it to me. I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, not to let an enemy other than us overcome us, and He gave it to me. I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, not to make us split into factions, and He withheld it from me.'"

Al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamza, with the same chain, and by another route.[[Al-Musnad (5/108) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/216).]] Ibn Hibban in his Sahih narrated it with both of its chains, from Salih ibn Kaysan. Al-Tirmidhi in "al-Fitan" narrated it from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Rashid. Both of them (Salih and al-Nu'man) narrated it from al-Zuhri, with the same chain.[[Al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra as in Tuhfat al-Ashraf (3/115), Sahih Ibn Hibban (9/180) (al-Ihsan), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2175).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih" (good and authentic).

Another hadith: Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said in his Tafsir: Ziyad ibn Ubayd Allah al-Muzani narrated to me, Marwan ibn Mu'awiya al-Fazari narrated to us, Abu Malik narrated to us, Nafi' ibn Khalid al-Khuza'i narrated to me, from his father, that the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed a light prayer, complete in its bowing and prostration, and said: "It was a prayer of hope and fear. I asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic, three things in it, and He gave me two and withheld one from me. I asked Allah not to afflict you with a punishment that befell those before you, and He gave it to me. I asked Allah not to empower over you an enemy who would plunder your territory, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to make you split into factions and make some of you taste the violence of others, but He withheld it from me." Abu Malik said: I said to him: "Did your father hear this from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "Yes, I heard him narrate it to the people, that he heard it from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/433). It was also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (4/192) and al-Bazzar in his Musnad no. (3289) (Kashf al-Astar), through Marwan ibn Mu'awiya with the same chain.]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Ma'mar said: Ayyub informed me, from Abu Qilaba, from Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani, from Abu Asma al-Rahbi, from Shaddad ibn Aws, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah gathered the earth for me until I saw its east and its west, and the dominion of my Ummah will reach what was gathered for me of it. I have been given the two treasures, the white and the red. I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, not to destroy my Ummah by a general famine, and not to empower over them an enemy who would destroy them entirely, and not to make them split into factions, and not to make some of them taste the violence of others." He said: "O Muhammad, when I decree a decree, it cannot be turned back. I have granted you for your Ummah that I will not destroy them with a general famine, and that I will not empower over them an enemy from others than them who would destroy them entirely, until some of them destroy others, some kill others, and some take others captive." And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I fear for my Ummah only the misguiding leaders. When the sword is placed among my Ummah, it will not be lifted from them until the Day of Resurrection."[[Al-Musnad (4/123). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/221): "The men of Ahmad are the men of the Sahih."]]

It is not in any of the al-Kutub al-Sittah (the Six Canonical Books). Its chain is good and strong. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Zayd, Abbad ibn Mansur, and Qatada, all three from Ayyub, from Abu Qilaba, from Abu Asma, from Thawban, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in a similar wording.[[Sahih Muslim no. (2889) narrated it from the route of Hammad ibn Zayd, and from the route of Mu'adh ibn Hisham, from his father, from Qatada, from Abu Qilaba, without mentioning Ayyub.]] And Allah knows best [in A: "And Allah knows best"].

Another hadith: al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Abdullah ibn Isma'il ibn Ibrahim al-Hashimi and Maymun ibn Ishaq ibn al-Hasan al-Hanafi narrated to us, they said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ja'i, from Nafi' ibn Khalid al-Khuza'i, from his father, who said, and his father was one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and one of the People of the Tree: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed while the people were around him, he prayed a light prayer, complete in its bowing and prostration. One day he sat and prolonged his sitting, until some of us signaled to one another: 'Be quiet, he is receiving revelation.' When he finished, some of the people said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, you prolonged your sitting until some of us signaled to one another: he is receiving revelation to you.' He said: 'No, but it was a prayer of hope and fear. I asked Allah in it for three things, and He gave me two and withheld one from me. I asked Allah not to punish you with a punishment with which He punished those before you, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to empower over my Ummah an enemy who would plunder them, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to make you split into factions and not to make some of you taste the violence of others, but He withheld it from me.'" He said: I said to him: "Did your father hear it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "Yes, I heard him say: he heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), [counting] on my fingers, ten fingers."[[Also narrated by al-Bazzar in his Musnad no. (3289) (Kashf al-Astar) and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (4/192), through Abu Malik al-Ash'ja'i, from Nafi', from his father, with the same chain.]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yunus, that is Ibn Muhammad al-Mu'addib, narrated to us, Layth, that is Ibn Sa'd, narrated to us, from Abu Wahb al-Khawlani, from a man whose name he mentioned, from Abu Basra al-Ghifari, a Companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, for four things, and He gave me three and withheld one from me. I asked Allah not to unite my Ummah upon misguidance, and He gave it to me. I asked Allah not to let an enemy from other than them overcome them, and He gave it to me. I asked Allah not to destroy them by years of famine as He destroyed the nations before them, and He gave it to me. And I asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic, not to make them split into factions and not to make some of them taste the violence of others, but He withheld it from me."[[Al-Musnad (6/396). Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/280) through al-Layth with the same chain. Note: In the Musnad it appears as "Abu Wahb al-Khawlani," while in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani it appears as "Abu Hani' al-Khawlani," and the latter is the correct one, as mentioned by al-Mizzi in Tahdhib al-Kamal (7/401) and Ibn Abd al-Barr in al-Istighna (2/976).]]

It is not narrated by anyone from the authors of the al-Kutub al-Sittah.

Another hadith: al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us, Minjab ibn al-Harith narrated to us, Abu Hudhayfa al-Tha'labi narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Ilaqa, from Jabir ibn Samura al-Sawa'i, from Ali [may Allah be pleased with him] [addition from A]; that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I asked my Lord for three qualities, and He gave me two and withheld one from me. I said: 'O Lord, do not destroy my Ummah by hunger.' He said: 'This is yours.' I said: 'O Lord, do not empower over them an enemy from other than them,' meaning the people of polytheism, 'who would annihilate them.' He said: 'That is yours.' I said: 'O Lord, do not make their violence among themselves.' " He said: "So He withheld this one from me."[[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (1/107). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/222): "In it is Abu Hudhayfa al-Tha'labi, whom I do not know, and the rest of its men are trustworthy."]]

Another hadith: al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Asim, Abu al-Darda al-Marwazi narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Kaysan narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I called upon my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to lift four things from my Ummah. He lifted two of them from them, and refused me to lift two of them. I called upon my Lord to lift stoning from the sky and drowning from the earth, and not to make them split into factions and not to make some of them taste the violence of others. So He lifted from them stoning from the sky and drowning from the earth, and Allah refused to lift two: killing and al-Haraj (chaos, mutual slaughter)."

Another route from Ibn Abbas also: Ibn Mardawayh said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd [in A: "Yazid"] narrated to me, al-Walid ibn Aban narrated to me, Ja'far ibn Munir narrated to us, Abu Badr Shuja' ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Amr ibn Qays narrated to us, from a man, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Say, He is the One able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet, or to confuse you into factions and make you taste the violence of one another﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) stood, performed ablution, then said: "O Allah, do not send upon my Ummah a punishment from above them, nor from beneath their feet, nor confuse them into factions, nor make some of them taste the violence of others." He said: Then Jibril came to him and said: "O Muhammad, Allah has granted protection to your Ummah from being sent upon them a punishment from above them or from beneath their feet."[[Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/374) through Abu al-Darda al-Marwazi, and in its chain are men I do not know.]]

Another hadith: Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Bazzar narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Musa narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi narrated to us, Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu al-Minhal, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "I asked my Lord for my Ummah four qualities, and He gave me three and withheld one from me. I asked Him that my Ummah would not disbelieve entirely, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to punish them with what He punished the nations before them, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to let an enemy from other than them overcome them, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to make their violence among themselves, but He withheld it from me."

Al-Tabarani narrated it, through Ibn Abi Hatim, from Abu Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan, from Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi, with a similar wording.[[Al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat no. (4336) (Majma' al-Bahrayn), through al-Qatay'i from Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi with the same chain. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/222): "Its men are trustworthy."]]

Another route: Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, Kathir ibn Zayd al-Laythi al-Madani narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Rabah, a freedman of the family of Abu Dhubab, narrated to me, that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I asked my Lord for three things, and He gave me two and denied me one. I asked Him that He not let an enemy from other than them dominate my Ummah, and He gave me that. I asked Him that He not destroy them by famine, and He gave me that. I asked Him that He not cause them to be divided into factions (shiya') and that He not let some of them inflict violence upon others, but He denied me that."

Then Ibn Mardawayh narrated it with its chain from Sa'd ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with similar wording. Al-Bazzar narrated it through the route of Umar ibn Salamah, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with similar wording. [Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (3290), Kashf al-Astar.]

Another report: Sufyan al-Thawri said, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "Four [punishments] are for this Ummah: two have passed, and two remain: ﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment from above you﴾ — he said: stoning. ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾ — he said: sinking into the earth. ﴿or to confuse you with factions and make you taste the violence of one another﴾." Sufyan said: meaning stoning and sinking into the earth.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b: ﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet or to confuse you with factions and make you taste the violence of one another﴾. He said: They are four characteristics, two of which came after the death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) by twenty-five years: they were confused into factions and some of them tasted the violence of others. Two remain which must befall them: stoning and sinking into the earth.

Ahmad narrated it from Waki', from Abu Ja'far. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Mundhir ibn Shadhan narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abu al-Ashhab narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment [from above you or from beneath your feet or to confuse you with factions]﴾ — the verse — he said: "Its punishment was withheld until its sin was committed, and when its sin was committed, its punishment was released."

Likewise said Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Malik, Mujahid, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd regarding His words: ﴿a punishment from above you﴾, meaning stoning, and ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾, meaning sinking into the earth. This is the choice of Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Yunus, from Ibn Wahb, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam regarding His words: ﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet﴾, he said: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) used to cry out while in the gathering — or upon the pulpit — saying: "O people, it has indeed descended upon you. Allah says: ﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment from above you [or from beneath your feet]﴾. If a punishment came to you from the sky, it would leave none of you alive; ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾: if the earth swallowed you up, it would destroy you and leave none of you alive; ﴿or to confuse you with factions and make you taste the violence of one another﴾. Behold, the worst of the three has descended upon you."

Second opinion: Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, I heard Khallad ibn Sulayman say: I heard Amir ibn Abd al-Rahman say: Ibn Abbas used to say regarding this verse, ﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment from above you﴾: as for the punishment from above you, it is evil rulers; ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾: evil servants.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿a punishment from above you﴾ means your rulers; ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾ means your slaves and your lowest-ranking people.

Ibn Abi Hatim related something similar from Abu Sinan and Umayr ibn Hani'.

Ibn Jarir said: Although this view has a valid basis, the first is more apparent and stronger.

What Ibn Jarir said is correct, may Allah have mercy on him, and what supports its soundness is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Are you secure from the One in heaven that He will not cause the earth to swallow you, and then it shakes? Or are you secure from the One in heaven that He will not send against you a storm of stones? Then you will know how was My warning. And previously denied those before them, so how was My reproach﴾ [al-Mulk: 16–18]. And in the hadith: "There will surely occur in this Ummah a hurling of stones, sinking into the earth, and transformation (maskh)." [Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (2/163) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with him.] This is mentioned along with its counterparts among the signs of the Hour, its portents, and the appearance of signs before the Day of Resurrection, and it will come in its appropriate place, Allah willing.

* *

His words: ﴿or to confuse you with factions﴾ mean: to make you mingled, divided into factions (shiya') differing from one another. Al-Walibi related from Ibn Abbas: it means the desires (ahwa'); and Mujahid and others said likewise.

It has been reported in hadith, narrated through various routes from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "This Ummah will split into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire except one."

* *

His words: ﴿and make you taste the violence of one another﴾. Ibn Abbas and others said: it means He empowers some of you over others, with punishment and killing.

* *

His words: ﴿See how We vary the signs﴾, meaning: We clarify them, make them evident and explain them, ﴿that they may understand﴾, meaning: that they may comprehend and reflect upon Allah's signs, proofs and evidences.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: When the verse ﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment from above you [or from beneath your feet]﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not return after me as disbelievers, striking one another's necks with swords." They said: "We testify that there is no god but Allah, and that you are the Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." Some people said: "This will never happen, that some of us kill others while we are Muslims." So there was revealed: ﴿See how We vary the signs that they may understand. But your people have denied it, while it is the truth. Say: I am not a guardian over you. For every news is a fixed time, and you will come to know﴾.

Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir. [Tafsir al-Tabari (11/430).]

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And your people denied it﴾, that is, the Qur'an which you have brought them, with its guidance and clarification, ﴿your people﴾ meaning the Quraysh, ﴿while it is the truth﴾, that is, the truth beyond which there is no other truth. ﴿Say, "I am not over you a guardian"﴾, that is, I am not a keeper over you, nor am I entrusted with you, like His saying: ﴿And say, "The truth is from your Lord, so whoever wills let him believe, and whoever wills let him disbelieve"﴾ [Al-Kahf: 29]. Therefore He said: ﴿And remind by it﴾, meaning: remind the people with this Qur'an, and warn them of Allah's vengeance and His painful punishment on the Day of Resurrection.

His saying: ﴿lest a soul be delivered up for what it has earned﴾, meaning: lest it be delivered up. Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas, and Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan and al-Suddi said: "tubsala" means "tuslam" (handed over).

Al-Walibi reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "tafdahah" (disgraced). Qatadah said: "tuhbas" (detained). Murrah and Ibn Zayd said: "tu'akhadh" (seized to account). Al-Kalbi said: "tujazza" (recompensed). [In manuscripts M and A: "tujzi" (recompensed).]

All these expressions are close in meaning, and their sum is: being handed over to ruin, being held back from good, and being held in pledge, unable to attain what is sought. As He said: ﴿Every soul, for what it has earned, is held in pledge, except the companions of the right﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 38-39].

* *

His saying: ﴿It will have no protector or intercessor besides Allah﴾, meaning: there will be no relative, and no one who will intercede for it, as He said: ﴿before a Day comes in which there is no trading, nor friendship, nor intercession. And the disbelievers — they are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 254].

* *

His saying: ﴿And if it should offer every ransom, it will not be accepted from it﴾, meaning: even if it gave every kind of compensation offered, it would not be accepted from it, as He said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers — never will be accepted from any of them the earth filled with gold, even if he should ransom himself by it. For those there will be a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers [in manuscript H: "the verse"]﴾ [Al 'Imran: 91]. And so He said here: ﴿Those are they who have been delivered up for what they earned. For them is a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.﴾

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verses 71–73 (part 1 of 3):

Al-Suddi said: The polytheists said to the believers, "Follow our way and abandon the religion of Muhammad." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed: ﴿Say: Shall we call upon other than Allah that which neither benefits us nor harms us, and be turned back on our heels﴾, meaning, into disbelief, ﴿after Allah has guided us?﴾ Then our situation would be like that of the one whom ﴿the devils have enticed in the earth, bewildered﴾ [[Addition from MS A.]], meaning: your situation, if you disbelieve after faith, is like that of a man who was with a group on the road. He lost the way, and the devils bewildered him and enticed him in the earth, while his companions were on the road. They kept calling him to them, saying, "Come to us, for we are on the road," but he refused to come to them. That is the example of one who follows them after knowing Muhammad ﷺ, and Muhammad is the one who calls to the path, and the path is Islam. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

Qatadah said: ﴿The devils have enticed him in the earth﴾ means they led him astray in the earth. That is, ﴿enticed him﴾ [[In MS M: "his course enticed him."]], like His saying: ﴿hearts yearning toward them﴾ [Ibrahim: 37].

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Say: Shall we call upon other than Allah that which neither benefits us nor harms us﴾, the verse. He said: This is a parable Allah struck for the idols and for those who call to them. The callers who call to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, are like a man who strayed from the road, wandering and lost, when a caller called to him, "O so-and-so, son of so-and-so, come to the road!" He has companions who also call him, "O so-and-so, come to the road!" If he follows the first caller, he is taken until he is thrown into destruction. But if he answers the one who calls him to guidance, he is guided to the road. This is the caller who calls in the wilderness, of the ghouls. He means: the example of one who worships these gods other than Allah is that he thinks he is in something until death comes to him, and he meets destruction and regret. His saying: ﴿like one whom the devils have enticed in the earth﴾ refers to the "ghouls" who call him by his name and the name of his father and grandfather, so he follows them while thinking he is in something. In the morning he finds that they have cast him into destruction, and perhaps they devour him, or they lead him into a desert wasteland where he dies of thirst. This is the example of one who answers the idols that are worshipped besides Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid regarding ﴿like one whom the devils have enticed in the earth, bewildered﴾: He said, a bewildered man whose companions call him to the road. That is like one who goes astray after having been guided.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿like one whom the devils have enticed in the earth, bewildered﴾: He is one who does not respond to the guidance of Allah. He is a man who obeyed the Satan, worked in the earth by disobedience, deviated from the truth, and strayed from it. He has companions who call him to guidance, and they claim that what they command him is guidance. Allah says this about their human allies: [Allah says,] ﴿Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the guidance﴾, and misguidance is what the jinn call to. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Then he said: This implies that his companions call him to misguidance while claiming it is guidance. He said: This contradicts the apparent meaning of the verse, for Allah informed that his companions call him to guidance, so it is not permissible for it to be misguidance when Allah has stated that it is guidance.

What Ibn Jarir said is correct. The context of the verse implies that this one whom the devils have enticed in the earth, bewildered, is in a state of accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: in a state of his bewilderment, his misguidance, and his ignorance of the right way, while he has companions travelling on the right path who kept calling him to them and to going with them on the best course. The sense of the speech is: he refuses them and does not turn to them. Had Allah willed, He would have guided him and returned him to the road. For this reason He said: ﴿Say: Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the guidance﴾.

As He said: ﴿And whomever Allah guides, there is no misleader for him﴾ [Az-Zumar: 37], and He said: ﴿If you are eager for their guidance, indeed Allah does not guide those who mislead, and they will have no helpers﴾ [An-Nahl: 37]. And His saying: ﴿and we are commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾ means: we devote the worship to Him alone, with no partner.

﴿And to establish prayer and fear Him﴾, meaning: we are commanded to establish prayer and to fear Him in all circumstances. ﴿And it is He to whom you will be gathered﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in truth﴾, meaning: with justice. So He is their Creator and their Owner, and the Manager of them and of whatever is in them.

* *

His saying: ﴿And the day He says, "Be," and it is﴾ means: the Day of Resurrection, when Allah says "Be" and it is, by His command, in the blink of an eye, or it is closer.

﴿And the day﴾ is in the accusative either by conjunction with His saying ﴿and fear Him﴾, meaning: and fear the day He says "Be" and it is. Or by conjunction with His saying ﴿created the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: and He created on the day He says "Be" and it is. So He mentions the beginning of creation and its return, and this is appropriate. Or it is in the accusative by an implied verb, meaning: and remember the day He says "Be" and it is.

* *

His saying: ﴿His word is the truth, and to Him belongs the dominion﴾ consists of two clauses in the genitive position, as they are two descriptions of the Lord of the worlds.

* *

His saying: ﴿The day the Horn is blown﴾ may be a substitute for His saying ﴿And the day He says "Be" and it is﴾, or it may be an adverbial complement of His saying ﴿and to Him belongs the dominion the day the Horn is blown﴾, like His saying: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is for Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ghafir: 16], and His saying: ﴿The dominion that Day belongs truly to the Most Merciful, and it will be a difficult day for the disbelievers﴾ [Al-Furqan: 26], and what is similar to that.

The commentators differed regarding His saying: ﴿the day the Horn is blown﴾. Some of them said: what is meant by "al-Sur" here is the plural of "sūrah" (form), meaning: the day He blows into them and they come to life.

Ibn Jarir said: as it is said "sūr" for the wall of the city, which is the plural of "sūrah." But the correct view is that what is meant by "al-Sur" is the "qarn" (horn) into which Israfil, peace be upon him, blows. Ibn Jarir said: What is correct in our view is what the reports have widely transmitted from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "Indeed Israfil has taken the Sur into his mouth and bowed his forehead, waiting for when he will be commanded, and then he will blow." [Tafsir al-Tabari (11/463).]

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il narrated to us, Sulayman al-Taymi narrated to us, from Aslam al-Ijli, from Bishr ibn Shaghaf, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: A Bedouin said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the Sur?" He said: "A horn that is blown into." [Al-Musnad (2/192).]

We have also related the long hadith about the Sur through the route of the memorizer (al-Hafiz) Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani in his book "al-Tiwalat." He said: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Misri al-Ayli narrated to us, Abu Asim al-Nabil narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Rafi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated to us while he was among a group of his companions, and he said: "When Allah had finished creating the heavens and the earth, He created the Sur and gave it to Israfil. He places it on his mouth, fixing his gaze on the Throne, waiting for when he will be commanded." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the Sur?" He said: "The horn." I said: "What is it like?" He said: "Great. By the One who sent me with the truth, the circumference of its circle is like the breadth of the heavens and the earth. It is blown three blasts: the first blast is the blast of terror, the second is the blast of swooning, and the third is the blast of rising for the Lord of the worlds. Allah, Exalted is He, commands Israfil with the first blast, and he says, 'Blow.' He blows the blast of terror, and the people of the heavens and the people of the earth are terrified, except whom Allah wills. He commands him, and he prolongs it, extends it, and does not pause. This is like the saying of Allah: ﴿And they await but a single blast, with no respite﴾ [Sad: 15]. Then Allah sets the mountains in motion, and they pass like clouds, and become a mirage."

Then the earth quakes with its inhabitants in a great quaking, and it becomes like a ship tossed in the sea, struck by the waves, overturned with its people, like a lamp hung from the Throne, shaken by the winds. This is what Allah means in His saying: ﴿On the day the quaking quakes, followed by the sequel, hearts that Day will be trembling﴾ [An-Nazi'at: 6–8]. People sway upon its back, nursing mothers are distracted, pregnant women miscarry, children turn gray, and the devils flee in terror, until they reach the horizons, but the angels meet them and strike their faces, so they return. The people turn their backs fleeing, having no protector from the command of Allah. Some of them call out to others. This is what Allah, Exalted is He, means: ﴿The Day of Calling Out﴾ [Ghafir: 32].

While they are in that state, the earth splits from one side to the other. They see a great thing they have never seen before, and they are seized by such distress and terror that only Allah knows. Then they look up to the sky, and it has become like molten brass. Then it splits open and its stars scatter, and its sun and moon are eclipsed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The dead know nothing of that." Abu Hurayrah said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are those whom Allah excepts when He says: ﴿So whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, except whom Allah wills﴾ [An-Naml: 87]?" He said: "Those are the martyrs. Terror only reaches the living, and they are alive with their Lord, provided for. Allah protects them from the terror of that Day and keeps them safe from it. It is the punishment of Allah that He sends upon the worst of His creation." He said: This is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, means: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing. On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget what she nursed, and every pregnant one will deliver her load, and you will see people intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe﴾ [Al-Hajj: 1, 2]. They will remain in that punishment for as long as Allah wills, except that it will be prolonged.

Then Allah commands Israfil (Isrāfīl) to blow the blast of the swoon (nafkhat al-ṣaʿq), and he blows the blast of the swoon, so that those in the heavens and [those in] the earth swoon, except whomever Allah wills. Then they have died away. The Angel of Death comes to the Mighty, the Majestic, and says: "O Lord, the people of the heavens and the earth have died, except whom You willed." Allah, and He knows best who remains, says: "Who remains?" He says: "O Lord, You remain, the Living who does not die, and the bearers of the Throne remain, and Jibril and Mika'il remain, and I remain." Allah, the Mighty, the Majestic, says: "Let Jibril and Mika'il die." Allah makes the Throne speak, and it says: "O Lord, Jibril and Mika'il are dying!!" He says: "Be silent, for I have decreed death upon everyone beneath My Throne," and the two of them die.

Then the Angel of Death comes to the Mighty [the Majestic] and says: "O Lord, Jibril and Mika'il have died." Allah says, and He knows best who remains: "Who remains?" He says: "You remain, the Living who does not die, and the bearers of Your Throne remain, and I remain." Allah says: "Let the bearers of My Throne die." They die. Allah commands the Throne, and it seizes the Trumpet (al-Ṣūr) from Israfil. Then the Angel of Death comes and says: "O Lord, the bearers of Your Throne have died." Allah, and He knows best who remains, says: "Who remains?" He says: "O Lord, You remain, the Living who does not die, and I remain." Allah says: "You are a creature from among My creatures. I created you for what I saw, so die." He dies.

When none remains except Allah, the One, the Subduer, the Unique (al-Aḥad) [the Eternal Refuge (al-Ṣamad)], who did not beget and was not begotten, He was the Last as He was the First. He folds up the heavens and the earth as a scribe folds the scroll for the books [in manuscript A: "the book"], then He spreads them out again. Then He grasps them three times, and then He says: "I am the Compeller, I am the Compeller, I am the Compeller," three times. Then He cries out with His voice: "Whose is the dominion today?" three times. No one answers Him. Then He says to Himself: "For Allah, the One, the Subduer" (Ghāfir 16). Allah says: "On the Day the earth will be changed into other than the earth, and the heavens" (Ibrāhīm 48). He spreads them out and flattens them, then stretches them out like the stretching of the leather of Ukaz (al-adīm al-ʿukāẓī, a famous leather from the market of ʿUkāẓ), "in which you will see no crookedness or curvature" (Ṭā-Hā 107).

Then Allah drives the creation with one driving cry, and behold, they are on this changed earth, just as they were in the first earth. Whoever was in its belly is in its belly, and whoever was on its surface is on its surface. Then Allah sends down upon them water from beneath the Throne, then Allah commands the sky to rain, and it rains for forty days, until the water is twelve cubits above them. Then Allah commands the bodies to grow, and they grow like the growth of the ṭarāthīth [a kind of mushroom/plant] (or: like the growth of herbs), until their bodies are complete and they are as they were. Allah, the Mighty, the Majestic, says: "Let the bearers of My Throne live," and they live. Allah commands Israfil, and he takes the Trumpet, places it at his mouth, and then says: "Let Jibril and Mika'il live," and the two of them live. Then He calls the spirits (al-arwāḥ), and they are brought, glowing: the spirits of the Muslims glow with light, and the spirits of the disbelievers with darkness. He gathers them all together, then He places them in the Trumpet.

Then Allah commands Israfil to blow the blast of resurrection, and he blows the blast of resurrection. The spirits come out as if they were bees, filling what is between the heaven and the earth. Allah says: "By My might and My majesty, every spirit will return to its body." The spirits enter the earth towards the bodies, and they enter through the nostrils, then they move through the bodies as poison moves through the one who has been stung. Then the earth splits open over you [in manuscript A: "over them"], and I am the first one the earth splits open for. You come out hastening to your Lord, rushing (tansilūn) [in manuscript A: "they come out from it hastening to their Lord, walking"], "hastening towards the caller; the disbelievers will say: This is a difficult day" (al-Qamar 8), barefoot, naked, uncircumcised (ghurlan). You stand in one station, its duration seventy years. You are not looked at, and no judgment is passed between you. You weep until the tears run out, then you shed blood, and you sweat until the sweat bridles you or reaches the chins. You say: "Who will intercede for us with our Lord so that He judges between us?" They say: "Who is more deserving of this than your father Adam? Allah created him with His hand, breathed into him from His spirit, and spoke to him directly." So they come to Adam and request this from him, but he refuses and says: "I am not the one for this." They go through the prophets, prophet by prophet, and each time they come to a prophet, he refuses them.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Until they come to me. I will go to the place of prostration (al-faḥṣ) and fall down in prostration." Abu Hurayrah said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is al-faḥṣ?" He said: "In front of the Throne. Until Allah sends to me an angel who takes hold of my arm and raises me, and says to me: 'O Muhammad.' I say: 'Yes, my Lord.' Allah, the Mighty, the Majestic, says, and He knows best: 'What is your matter?' I say: 'O my Lord, You promised me the intercession, so intercede for me among Your creation, and judge between them.' Allah says: 'I have granted you intercession. I will come to you to judge between you.'"

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Then I return and stand with the people. While we are standing, we hear a tremendous sound from the sky, which frightens us. Then the people of the first heaven descend, twice the number of those on earth from among the jinn and mankind. When they draw near the earth, the earth becomes illuminated with their light, and they take their ranks, and we say to them: 'Is our Lord among you?' They say: 'No, but He is coming.'

Then the people of the second heaven descend, twice the number of the angels who descended, and twice the number of those in it from among the jinn and mankind. When they draw near the earth, the earth is illuminated with their light, and they take their ranks, and we say to them: 'Is our Lord among you?' They say: 'No, but He is coming.'

Then they descend in proportion to that multiplication, until the Mighty, the Majestic, descends in shadows of clouds and angels. On that day, eight [who are four today] will carry His Throne, their feet upon the lowest boundary of the earth, while the earth and the heavens reach their waists, and the Throne is upon their shoulders. They have a rumbling in their glorification, saying: 'Glory be to the Lord of the Throne and the Sovereignty. Glory be to the Lord of dominion and the kingdom. Glory be to the Living who does not die. Glory be to the One who causes creatures to die and does not die. Holy, Holy, Holy, Most Holy, Glory be to our Lord, the Most High, Lord of the angels and the Spirit. Glory be to our Lord, the Most High, who causes creatures to die and does not die.' Then Allah places His Footstool (kursiyy) wherever He wills in His earth. Then He calls out with His voice: 'O assembly of jinn and mankind, I have been silent towards you since I created you until this day of yours. I hear your speech and see your deeds. So listen to Me, for these are your deeds and your records being read to you. Whoever finds good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame none but himself.'

Then Allah commands Jahannam, and a bright neck emerges from it, and then He says: "Did I not command you, O children of Adam, not to worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy. And that you should worship Me; this is the straight path. And he had already misled from among you a great multitude. Did you not then use reason? This is Jahannam which you were promised" (Yā-Sīn 60–64). [Or: "by it you used to deny," a doubt from Abu ʿĀṣim.] "And separate yourselves today, O criminals" (Yā-Sīn 59). So Allah separates the people, and the nations kneel. Allah, the Exalted, says: "And you will see every nation kneeling; every nation will be called to its record. Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do" (al-Jāthiyah 28). Then Allah, the Mighty, the Majestic, judges among His creatures, except the two weighty ones, the jinn and mankind. He judges among the wild beasts and the cattle, to the extent that He judges for the hornless ewe against the horned one. When He finishes from that, and no claim remains for one against another, Allah says to them: "Be dust." At that moment the disbeliever says: "Would that I were dust" (al-Naba' 40).

Then Allah, the Mighty, the Majestic, judges among the servants. The first thing He judges concerning is blood. Every slain person who was killed in the way of Allah, the Mighty, the Majestic, comes, and Allah commands every slain person, and he carries his head, with his veins gushing, and says: "O Lord, for what did this one kill me?" He says, and He knows best: "For what did you kill him?" He says: "I killed them so that might would belong to You." Allah says to him: "You have spoken the truth." Then Allah makes his face like the light of the sun, and then the angels pass by him into Paradise.

Every person who was killed for other than that also comes, carrying his head with his veins gushing, and says: "O Lord, for what did this one kill me?" He says, and He knows best: "Why did you kill them?" He says: "O Lord, I killed them so that might would belong to You and to me." He says: "You are ruined." Then no soul that was killed remains without being requited for it, and no wrong that was done remains without being taken for it, and it is in the will of Allah: if He wills, He punishes him, and if He wills, He has mercy on him.

Then Allah, the Exalted, judges among whoever remains of His creation, until no wrong remains for anyone against anyone without Allah taking it for the wronged from the wrongdoer, to the extent that one is made to pay for milk mixed with water, and then sells it, so that the milk is separated from the water.

When Allah finishes from that, a caller calls out, making all creatures hear: "Let every people join their gods and what they used to worship besides Allah." No one who worshipped besides Allah remains without his gods being displayed before him, and on that day an angel from among the angels will be made in the form of ʿUzayr, and an angel from among the angels will be made in the form of ʿĪsā son of Maryam. Then the Jews follow this, and the Christians follow that, then their gods lead them to the Fire. This is what He says, the Exalted: "If these were gods, they would not have entered it, and all of them will abide in it forever" (al-Anbiyāʾ 99).

When only the believers remain, and the hypocrites are among them, God comes to them in whatever form He wills, and says: "O people, the people have departed, so join your deities and what you used to worship." They say: "By God, we have no deity except God, and we did not worship anything other than Him." So He turns away from them. Then He comes to them in a form they recognise, and He says: "O people, the people have departed, so join your deities and what you used to worship." They say: "By God, we have no deity except God, and we did not worship anything other than Him." Then He uncovers His shin for them, and manifests to them some of His greatness, so they recognise that He is their Lord. They fall down prostrate on their faces, and every hypocrite falls on his back, and God makes their spines like the bones of cattle. Then God permits them to rise. God then lays the Path (al-Sirat) over the middle of Hell, sharp like the edge of a blade (or: like the edge of a sword), with hooks, grappling irons and thorns like the thorns of the sa'dan plant, over a slippery bridge. They pass across it as swiftly as the blink of an eye, or a flash of lightning, or the wind, or the best of horses, or the best of riding camels, or the best of men. Some are saved and unharmed, some are saved but scratched, and some are thrown headlong into Hell.

When the people of Paradise have reached Paradise, they say: "Who will intercede for us with our Lord, so that we may enter Paradise?" They say: "Who is more worthy of this than your father Adam, peace be upon him, whom God created with His own hand, into whom He breathed of His spirit, and to whom He spoke directly?" So they come to Adam and ask him for this. He mentions a sin and says: "I am not the one for this. Rather, go to Noah, for he was the first of God's messengers." Noah is approached and asked for this. He mentions a sin and says: "I am not the one for this," and says: "Go to Abraham, for God took him as a friend." Abraham is approached and asked for this. He mentions a sin and says: "I am not the one for this," and says: "Go to Moses, for God brought him near as a confidant, spoke to him, and sent down the Torah to him." Moses is approached and asked for this. He mentions a sin and says: "I am not the one for this. Rather, go to the Spirit of God and His Word, Jesus son of Mary."

Jesus son of Mary is approached and asked for this, and he says: "I am not the one for you. Rather, go to Muhammad."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "They will come to me, and I have three intercessions with my Lord [which He promised me]. So I will set out and come to Paradise, and I will take hold of the ring of its door and ask for it to be opened, and it will be opened for me, and I will be greeted and welcomed. When I enter Paradise and see my Lord, I will fall down prostrate. God will then permit me, through His praise and glorification, with something He has permitted to none of His creation. Then He will say: 'Raise your head, O Muhammad, intercede and your intercession will be accepted, ask and you will be given.' When I raise my head, God says, and He knows best: 'What is your matter?' I say: 'O Lord, You promised me intercession, so intercede for me on behalf of the people of Paradise.' They then enter Paradise. God says: 'I have interceded for you, and I have permitted them to enter Paradise.'"

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to say: "By the One in whose hand my soul is, you are not more knowing in this world of your wives and dwellings than the people of Paradise are of their wives and dwellings. Each man among them will enter upon seventy-two wives: seventy whom God, mighty and majestic, creates, and two human women of the children of Adam, who have a virtue over those whom God created, because of their worship of God in this world. He enters upon the first of them in a chamber of ruby, on a throne of gold encrusted with pearls, on which are seventy mattresses of silk and brocade. Then he places his hand between her shoulders, and looks at his hand through her chest, and through her garments, skin and flesh; and he looks at the marrow of her shin as you look at the thread in a ruby tube. Her liver is a mirror for him, and his liver is a mirror for her. While he is with her, neither tiring of her nor she of him, each time he comes to her he finds her a virgin, his member never slackens, and she never complains of her private part. While he is thus, he is called: 'We know that you do not tire and are not made to tire, but there is no ejaculation and no death, except that you have other wives besides her.' He then comes out and goes to them one by one, and each time he goes to one of them she says: 'By God, I see nothing in Paradise more beautiful than you, and nothing in Paradise is dearer to me than you.'"

When the people of the Fire fall into the Fire, a group of God's creation, whom their deeds have destroyed, fall into it. Among them is one whom the Fire seizes by the feet, and it does not go beyond that; among them is one whom it seizes up to the middle of his shins; among them is one whom it seizes up to his knees; among them is one whom it seizes up to his waist; among them is one whom it seizes in his entire body, except his face, which God has forbidden to it." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I will say: 'O Lord, [what about] those of my community who fell into the Fire?' He says: 'Bring out whomever you recognise.' Those are brought out until none of them remains. Then God permits intercession, and no prophet or martyr remains but interceded. God says: 'Bring out whomever you find in his heart the weight of a dinar of faith.' Those are brought out until none of them remains. Then God intercedes and says: 'Bring out whomever you find in his heart two-thirds of a dinar of faith.' Then He says: 'a third of a dinar.' Then He says: 'a quarter of a dinar.' Then He says: 'a qirat.' Then He says: 'a grain of mustard seed.' Those are brought out until none of them remains, and until no one remains in the Fire who has ever done any good for God, and no one remains who has an intercession except that he interceded. Even Iblis stretches up, because of what he sees of God's mercy, hoping that he too may be interceded for. Then He says: 'I remain, and I am the Most Merciful of the merciful.' He then puts His hand into Hell and brings out from it a multitude that none but He can count, as if they were charcoal. They are cast into a river called the River of Life, and they sprout like a seed sprouts in the silt of a flood: what faces the sun of them turns yellowish-green, and what is in the shade of them turns yellowish. They sprout like the growth of the taraathith plant, until they become like grains of dust. On their necks is written: 'The people of Hell are the freed ones of the Most Merciful.' The people of Paradise recognise them by that writing, though they never did any good for God. They remain in Paradise for as long as God wills, and that writing remains on their necks. Then they say: 'Our Lord, erase this writing from us,' and God, mighty and majestic, erases it from them."

This is a very [well-known] [[Addition from manuscript M and A.]] hadith, and it is extremely strange (gharib), and some of its parts have corroborating reports in scattered hadiths. [[Al-Tabarani's al-Ahadith al-Tiwal, no. 36. Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Ayli has contradicted it: Abu al-Shaykh al-Isbahani in al-Azamah, no. 387, narrated it through Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th wa al-Nushur, no. 669, through Abu Qilabah al-Raqashi. Both Ishaq and Abu Qilabah narrate it from Abu Asim al-Dahhak, from Isma'il ibn Rafi', from Muhammad ibn Abi Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayrah. It has also been transmitted by another route centred on Isma'il ibn Rafi' al-Madani, whom the imams have weakened, and al-Daraqutni abandoned him. Ibn 'Adi said: "All his hadiths are open to question."]] There is some strangeness in some of its wording. It is transmitted solely by Isma'il ibn Rafi', the storyteller (qass) of the people of Madinah. Opinions about him differ: some have declared him reliable, and some have declared him weak. Several imams, such as Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Abu Hatim al-Razi and Amr ibn Ali al-Fallas, explicitly stated that his hadith is strange, and some said he is abandoned (matruk). Ibn 'Adi said: "All his hadiths are open to question, but he is recorded among the weak narrators."

I say: Its chain of narration has been reported in many different ways, and I have devoted a separate volume to them. As for its text, it is extremely strange. It is said that he gathered it from many hadiths and made it into one continuous narration, and for this reason he was criticised. I heard our shaykh, the hafiz Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, say: "He saw a work by al-Walid ibn Muslim in which he had gathered all the corroborating reports for some of the individual elements of this hadith." And God knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verses 71–73 (part 1 of 3):

Al-Suddi said: The polytheists said to the believers, "Follow our way and abandon the religion of Muhammad." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed: ﴿Say: Shall we call upon other than Allah that which neither benefits us nor harms us, and be turned back on our heels﴾, meaning, into disbelief, ﴿after Allah has guided us?﴾ Then our situation would be like that of the one whom ﴿the devils have enticed in the earth, bewildered﴾ [[Addition from MS A.]], meaning: your situation, if you disbelieve after faith, is like that of a man who was with a group on the road. He lost the way, and the devils bewildered him and enticed him in the earth, while his companions were on the road. They kept calling him to them, saying, "Come to us, for we are on the road," but he refused to come to them. That is the example of one who follows them after knowing Muhammad ﷺ, and Muhammad is the one who calls to the path, and the path is Islam. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

Qatadah said: ﴿The devils have enticed him in the earth﴾ means they led him astray in the earth. That is, ﴿enticed him﴾ [[In MS M: "his course enticed him."]], like His saying: ﴿hearts yearning toward them﴾ [Ibrahim: 37].

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Say: Shall we call upon other than Allah that which neither benefits us nor harms us﴾, the verse. He said: This is a parable Allah struck for the idols and for those who call to them. The callers who call to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, are like a man who strayed from the road, wandering and lost, when a caller called to him, "O so-and-so, son of so-and-so, come to the road!" He has companions who also call him, "O so-and-so, come to the road!" If he follows the first caller, he is taken until he is thrown into destruction. But if he answers the one who calls him to guidance, he is guided to the road. This is the caller who calls in the wilderness, of the ghouls. He means: the example of one who worships these gods other than Allah is that he thinks he is in something until death comes to him, and he meets destruction and regret. His saying: ﴿like one whom the devils have enticed in the earth﴾ refers to the "ghouls" who call him by his name and the name of his father and grandfather, so he follows them while thinking he is in something.
