Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verses 74–79 (part 1 of 2):

Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "The name of Abraham's father was not Azar; his name was Tarih." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

He also said: Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn Abi 'Asim al-Nabil narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Abu 'Asim Shabib narrated to us, 'Ikrimah narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar﴾. He meant by Azar: the idol. Abraham's father's name was Tarih, his mother's name was Mathani, his wife's name was Sarah, and the mother of Isma'il was Hajar, who was Abraham's concubine.

Likewise said more than one of the genealogists ('ulama' al-nasab): his name was Tarih. Mujahid and al-Suddi said: Azar is the name of an idol.

I say: It seems that Azar became his name because he served that idol, and Allah knows best. [[In manuscript A: "wallahu a'lam" (and Allah knows best).]] Ibn Jarir said: Others said: "It is an insult and a defect in their speech, and its meaning is: crooked (mu'waj)," but he did not attribute it to a chain of narrators, nor did he report it from anyone.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman: I heard my father reading ﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar﴾, and he said: "It has reached me that it means 'crooked,' and that it is the harshest word Abraham, peace be upon him, ever uttered."

Then Ibn Jarir said: "The correct view is that the name of his father was Azar." Then he raised an objection against himself, namely the opinion of the genealogists that his name was Tarih, and then answered that a person may have two names, as many people do, or that one of them may be a title (laqab). [[Ahmad Shakir (may Allah have mercy on him), in a study at the end of al-Jawaliqi's book "al-Mu'arrab," wrote in its conclusion: "The decisive proof against the interpretations they claimed for the word 'Azar,' and against what they called readings, which takes the word out of being a proper name for the father of Abraham, is the sound and explicit hadith in al-Bukhari, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: 'Abraham will meet his father Azar on the Day of Resurrection, and on Azar's face there will be dust and darkness. Abraham will say to him: Did I not tell you: do not disobey me? His father will say: Today I will not disobey you... to the end of the hadith.' In al-Bukhari (4/139 of the Sultaniyyah edition), Fath al-Bari (6/276 of the Bulaq edition), and Sharh al-'Ayni (15/243, 244 of the Munirriyyah edition), this text shows that it is his proper name, and it does not admit interpretation or distortion."]] This that he said is good and strong, and Allah knows best.

The reciters differed in the pronunciation of His saying: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar﴾. Ibn Jarir related from al-Hasan al-Basri and Abu Yazid al-Madani that they used to read: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father, "O Azar, do you take idols as gods?"﴾, meaning: O Azar, do you take idols as gods?

The majority (al-Jumhur) read it with a fatha (فَتْحٌ), either because it is a non-Arabic proper name that does not take nunation (ghayr munsarif), and it is then a substitute (badal) for ﴿his father﴾, or an explanatory apposition ('atf bayan), and this is more likely.

And according to the view of the one who made it a descriptive (na't) that also does not take nunation, like "ahmar" and "aswad."

As for the one who claimed that it is in the accusative because it is governed by ﴿do you take idols﴾, with the meaning: "O father, do you make Azar idols as gods?", this is a far-fetched view in the language, because what follows the interrogative particle does not govern what comes before it, since the interrogative has precedence at the beginning of the sentence. Ibn Jarir and others established this, and it is well known in the rules of Arabic grammar.

The point is that Abraham, peace be upon him, admonished his father about worshipping idols, rebuked him for them, and forbade him, but he did not desist, as He said: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar, "Do you take idols as gods? Indeed I see you and your people in clear error."﴾ That is: do you make a god of an idol that you worship besides Allah? ﴿Indeed I see you and your people﴾, that is: those who follow your path, ﴿in clear error﴾, that is: bewildered, not guided as to where they are going, but in confusion and ignorance, and your affair is manifestly in ignorance and error, clear to everyone of sound intellect.

He, the Exalted, also said: ﴿And mention in the Book Abraham. Indeed he was a man of truth and a prophet. When he said to his father, "O my father, why do you worship that which neither hears nor sees and does not avail you at all? O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge what has not come to you, so follow me; I will guide you to an even path. O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed Satan has ever been to the Most Merciful disobedient. O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will touch you, so you would be a companion to Satan." He said, "Do you reject my gods, O Abraham? If you do not cease, I will surely stone you, so leave me for a long time." He said, "Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed He is ever gracious to me. And I will leave you and what you invoke other than Allah, and I will invoke my Lord; perhaps I will not be in invoking my Lord unblessed."﴾ [Maryam: 41–48]. So Abraham, peace be upon him, kept asking forgiveness for his father throughout his life. When his father died upon polytheism and Abraham became clear about that, he gave up asking forgiveness for him and disassociated himself from him, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And the request for forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy to Allah, he disowned him. Indeed Abraham was compassionate and forbearing.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 114].

It is established in the Sahih that Abraham will meet his father Azar on the Day of Resurrection, and his father will say to him: "O my son, today I will not disobey you." Abraham will say: "O my Lord, did You not promise me that You would not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected? And what disgrace is greater than that of my farthest father?" It will be said: "O Abraham, look behind you." Then he will see a dhikh (a smeared, filthy creature), which will be seized by its legs and thrown into the Fire. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3350).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And thus We showed Abraham the realm of the heavens and the earth﴾: that is, We made clear to him the aspect of proof in his looking at their creation, for the oneness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in His dominion and creation, and that there is no god but Him and no lord besides Him. It is like His saying: ﴿Say, "Look at what is in the heavens and the earth"﴾ [Yunus: 101], and He said: ﴿Have they not looked into the realm of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-A'raf: 185], and He said: ﴿Have they not looked at what is before them and behind them of the sky and the earth? The seven earths were opened for him, and he looked at what is in them." Another added: "He began to look at the servants committing sins, and he would curse them. (6700), through the route of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him.]] But their chains are not sound, and Allah knows best. When he began to curse the people of sins, Allah said: "Indeed you are not able to bear this." So He returned him to how he was before that. It is possible that He uncovered his sight so that he saw that directly, and it is possible that it was through his insight until he witnessed it with his heart, verified it and recognized it, and knew the great wisdoms and decisive proofs in it. Likewise, Imam Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi narrated, and al-Tirmidhi declared it sound, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Added from A.]] in the hadith of the dream: "My Lord came to me in the best form and said: 'O Muhammad, about what do the exalted assembly dispute?' I said: 'I do not know, O my Lord.' So He placed His palm between my shoulders, until I found the coolness of His fingertips between my breasts, and everything was made clear to me and I knew..." and he mentioned the hadith. [[Al-Musnad (5/243) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3235). Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith. I asked Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) about this hadith and he said: 'This is a hasan sahih hadith.'"]]

His saying: ﴿and that he might be among the certain [in faith]﴾. It has been said: the "wa" (و) is extra, its meaning being: "Thus We showed Abraham the realm of the heavens and the earth, so that he might be among the certain," like His saying: ﴿[Thus] We detail the verses, and that the way of the criminals may become clear﴾ [al-An'am: 55].

It has also been said: rather, it is on its original [meaning], that is: We showed him that so that he might be a knower and certain.

"Lamps, not like the stars that lead them, nor like the setting ones that vanish."

And it is said: "Where did you set (afalta) from us?" meaning: "Where did you go absent from us?"

He said: ﴿He said, "I do not love those that set."﴾ Qatadah said: He knew that his Lord is eternal and does not cease. ﴿Then when he saw the moon rising﴾, that is: ascending, ﴿he said, "This is my lord." O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge what has not come to you, so follow me; I will guide you to an even path. O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed Satan has ever been to the Most Merciful disobedient. O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will touch you, so you would be a companion to Satan." He said, "Do you reject my gods, O Abraham? If you do not cease, I will surely stone you, so leave me for a long time." He said, "Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed He is ever gracious to me. And I will leave you and what you invoke other than Allah, and I will invoke my Lord; perhaps I will not be in invoking my Lord unblessed."﴾ [Maryam: 41–48]. So Abraham, peace be upon him, kept asking forgiveness for his father throughout his life. When his father died upon polytheism and Abraham became clear about that, he gave up asking forgiveness for him and disassociated himself from him, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And the request for forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy to Allah, he disowned him. Indeed Abraham was compassionate and forbearing.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 114].

It is established in the Sahih that Abraham will meet his father Azar on the Day of Resurrection, and his father will say to him: "O my son, today I will not disobey you." Abraham will say: "O my Lord, did You not promise me that You would not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected? And what disgrace is greater than that of my farthest father?" It will be said: "O Abraham, look behind you." Then he will see a dhikh (a smeared, filthy creature), which will be seized by its legs and thrown into the Fire. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3350).]]

His saying: ﴿And thus We showed Abraham the realm of the heavens and the earth﴾: that is, We made clear to him the aspect of proof in his looking at their creation, for the oneness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in His dominion and creation, and that there is no god but Him and no lord besides Him. When he began to curse the people of sins, Allah said: "Indeed you are not able to bear this." So He returned him to how he was before that. It is possible that He uncovered his sight so that he saw that directly, and it is possible that it was through his insight until he witnessed it with his heart, verified it and recognized it, and knew the great wisdoms and decisive proofs in it. Likewise, Imam Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi narrated, and al-Tirmidhi declared it sound, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Added from A.]] in the hadith of the dream: "My Lord came to me in the best form and said: 'O Muhammad, about what do the exalted assembly dispute?' I said: 'I do not know, O my Lord.' [[Al-Musnad (5/243) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3235). Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith. * *

His saying: ﴿and that he might be among the certain [in faith]﴾. It has been said: the "wa" (و) is extra, its meaning being: "Thus We showed Abraham the realm of the heavens and the earth, so that he might be among the certain," like His saying: ﴿[Thus] We detail the verses, and that the way of the criminals may become clear﴾ [al-An'am: 55].

It has also been said: rather, it is on its original [meaning], that is: We showed him that so that he might be a knower and certain.

* *

His saying: ﴿So when the night covered him﴾, that is: it enveloped him and concealed him, ﴿he saw a star﴾, that is: a planet, ﴿he said, "This is my lord." But when it set﴾, that is: it disappeared. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: "al-Uful" means departing. Ibn Jarir said: It is said: the star afala, yafulu, and ya'fil, ufulan and ufulan (أَفَلَ يَأْفُلُ وَيَأْفِلُ أُفُولًا وَأُفُولًا) when it disappeared. From this is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

"Lamps, not like the stars that lead them, nor like the setting ones that vanish."

And it is said: "Where did you set (afalta) from us?" meaning: "Where did you go absent from us?"

He said: ﴿He said, "I do not love those that set."﴾ Qatadah said: He knew that his Lord is eternal and does not cease. ﴿Then when he saw the moon rising﴾, that is: ascending, ﴿he said, "This is my lord." But when it set, he said, "If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the people who are astray."﴾ ﴿Then when he saw the sun rising, he said, "This is my lord; this is greater."﴾ That is: this shining one rising is my lord. ﴿This is greater﴾, that is: greater in body than the star and the moon, and more radiant. ﴿But when it set﴾, that is: it disappeared, ﴿he said, "O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate with Allah. Indeed I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with Allah."﴾ That is: I have made my religion sincere and devoted my worship exclusively ﴿to He who created the heavens and the earth﴾, that is: who created them and originated them without a prior pattern. ﴿Inclining﴾, that is: while I am inclining, turning away from polytheism toward monotheism. For this reason He said: ﴿And I am not of those who associate others with Allah.﴾

The commentators differed about this station: was it a station of reflection (nazar) or of debate (munazarah)? Ibn Jarir related through the route of 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, what indicates that it was a station of reflection, and Ibn Jarir preferred this, citing His saying: ﴿If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the people who are astray.﴾

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: He said that when he came out of the cave (sarab) in which his mother had given birth to him, when she feared for him from Nimrod ibn Kan'an, because it had been reported to him that a child would be born whose hands would bring an end to his kingdom, so he ordered the killing of the boys at that time. When Abraham's mother became pregnant with him, and her delivery drew near, she took him to a cave outside the town, gave birth to Abraham there, and left him there. He mentioned matters of extraordinary occurrences, as other commentators from the early and later generations also mentioned them.

The commentary, in its own words, holds that Abraham, peace be upon him, in this station was debating his people and showing them the falsehood of what they were upon, worshipping the hayakil (temples; here, the celestial bodies) and the idols. In the first station, with his father, he showed their error in worshipping the earthly idols, which are in the form of the heavenly angels, so that they would intercede for them with the Great Creator. They regard themselves as too lowly to worship Him directly, so they approach Him through worship of His angels, that these might intercede for them with Him regarding provision, victory, and other things they need. In this station he showed their error and misguidance in worshipping the hayakil, namely the seven wandering planets that move about: the Moon, Mercury, Venus, the Sun, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. The brightest and most radiant of them in their view are the Sun, then the Moon, then Venus. First he showed that Venus is not fit for divinity, because it is subjected and ordained to a specific course from which it does not deviate right or left, and it does not possess any control over itself. Rather, it is a body among the bodies, which Allah created luminous for the great wisdoms He has in that. It rises from the East, then travels between it and the West until it sets from sight there, then appears the following night in the same manner. Such a thing is not fit for divinity.

Then he moved on to the Moon and showed regarding it the same as he showed regarding the star.

Then he moved on to the Sun in the same way. When divinity was negated from these three bodies, which are the brightest things that eyes fall upon, and this was established by a decisive proof, [Abraham] said: ﴿O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate with Allah.﴾ That is: I am free from worshipping them and from allying with them. So if they are gods, then plot against me with them all, then give me no respite. ﴿Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, as a hanif (upright monotheist), and I am not of those who associate others with Allah.﴾ That is: I only worship the Creator of these things, their Originator, their Subjugator, their Determiner, their Manager, in whose hand is the dominion of everything, the Creator of everything, its Lord, its Sovereign, and its God. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne. He causes the night to cover the day, pursuing it rapidly, and [He created] the sun and the moon and the stars, subjected by His command. Unquestionably, to Him belong creation and command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ [Al-A'raf: 54]. And how is it permissible that Abraham [the Friend (al-Khalil)] [addition from manuscript A] should be debating in this station, when it is he about whom Allah said: ﴿And We had certainly given Abraham his sound judgment before, and We were of him well-Knowing. When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted?"﴾ and the verses that follow [Al-Anbiya: 51, 52]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah, hanif, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah. He was grateful for His favors. He chose him and guided him to a straight path. And We gave him good in this world, and indeed he, in the Hereafter, is among the righteous. Then We revealed to you, "Follow the religion of Abraham, hanif, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah."﴾ [An-Nahl: 120-123]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a correct religion, the way of Abraham, hanif, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah."﴾ [Al-An'am: 161].

It is established in the two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn, Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every child is born upon the fitrah (innate natural disposition towards faith)." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1385) and Sahih Muslim no. (2658).] In Sahih Muslim, from Iyad ibn Hammad, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah said: Indeed, I created My servants as hunafa (upright monotheists)." [Sahih Muslim no. (2865).] And Allah said in His Mighty Book: ﴿The fitrah of Allah upon which He has created mankind; there is no change in the creation of Allah.﴾ [Ar-Rum: 30]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And [mention] when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves, [saying], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified."﴾ [Al-A'raf: 172]. Its meaning, according to one of the two opinions, is like His saying: ﴿The fitrah of Allah upon which He has created mankind﴾ as will come with its explanation.

So if this is the case regarding all of creation, how could Abraham the Friend, whom Allah made ﴿a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah, hanif, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah﴾ [An-Nahl: 120], be debating in this station?! Rather, he is, after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), without doubt or hesitation, the most deserving of people of the sound fitrah and the upright disposition. Among the things that support that he was debating his people about the shirk they were engaged in, and not inquiring (into the matter), is the saying of the Exalted:

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verses 74–79 (part 1 of 2):

Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "The name of Abraham's father was not Azar; his name was Tarih." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

He also said: Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn Abi 'Asim al-Nabil narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Abu 'Asim Shabib narrated to us, 'Ikrimah narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar﴾. He meant by Azar: the idol. Abraham's father's name was Tarih, his mother's name was Mathani, his wife's name was Sarah, and the mother of Isma'il was Hajar, who was Abraham's concubine.

Likewise said more than one of the genealogists ('ulama' al-nasab): his name was Tarih. Mujahid and al-Suddi said: Azar is the name of an idol.

I say: It seems that Azar became his name because he served that idol, and Allah knows best. [[In manuscript A: "wallahu a'lam" (and Allah knows best).]] Ibn Jarir said: Others said: "It is an insult and a defect in their speech, and its meaning is: crooked (mu'waj)," but he did not attribute it to a chain of narrators, nor did he report it from anyone.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman: I heard my father reading ﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar﴾, and he said: "It has reached me that it means 'crooked,' and that it is the harshest word Abraham, peace be upon him, ever uttered."

Then Ibn Jarir said: "The correct view is that the name of his father was Azar." Then he raised an objection against himself, namely the opinion of the genealogists that his name was Tarih, and then answered that a person may have two names, as many people do, or that one of them may be a title (laqab). [[Ahmad Shakir (may Allah have mercy on him), in a study at the end of al-Jawaliqi's book "al-Mu'arrab," wrote in its conclusion: "The decisive proof against the interpretations they claimed for the word 'Azar,' and against what they called readings, which takes the word out of being a proper name for the father of Abraham, is the sound and explicit hadith in al-Bukhari, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: 'Abraham will meet his father Azar on the Day of Resurrection, and on Azar's face there will be dust and darkness. Abraham will say to him: Did I not tell you: do not disobey me? His father will say: Today I will not disobey you... to the end of the hadith.' In al-Bukhari (4/139 of the Sultaniyyah edition), Fath al-Bari (6/276 of the Bulaq edition), and Sharh al-'Ayni (15/243, 244 of the Munirriyyah edition), this text shows that it is his proper name, and it does not admit interpretation or distortion."]] This that he said is good and strong, and Allah knows best.

The reciters differed in the pronunciation of His saying: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar﴾. Ibn Jarir related from al-Hasan al-Basri and Abu Yazid al-Madani that they used to read: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father, "O Azar, do you take idols as gods?"﴾, meaning: O Azar, do you take idols as gods?

The majority (al-Jumhur) read it with a fatha (فَتْحٌ), either because it is a non-Arabic proper name that does not take nunation (ghayr munsarif), and it is then a substitute (badal) for ﴿his father﴾, or an explanatory apposition ('atf bayan), and this is more likely.

And according to the view of the one who made it a descriptive (na't) that also does not take nunation, like "ahmar" and "aswad."

As for the one who claimed that it is in the accusative because it is governed by ﴿do you take idols﴾, with the meaning: "O father, do you make Azar idols as gods?", this is a far-fetched view in the language, because what follows the interrogative particle does not govern what comes before it, since the interrogative has precedence at the beginning of the sentence. Ibn Jarir and others established this, and it is well known in the rules of Arabic grammar.

The point is that Abraham, peace be upon him, admonished his father about worshipping idols, rebuked him for them, and forbade him, but he did not desist, as He said: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar, "Do you take idols as gods? Indeed I see you and your people in clear error."﴾ That is: do you make a god of an idol that you worship besides Allah? ﴿Indeed I see you and your people﴾, that is: those who follow your path, ﴿in clear error﴾, that is: bewildered, not guided as to where they are going, but in confusion and ignorance, and your affair is manifestly in ignorance and error, clear to everyone of sound intellect.

He, the Exalted, also said: ﴿And mention in the Book Abraham. Indeed he was a man of truth and a prophet. When he said to his father, "O my father, why do you worship that which neither hears nor sees and does not avail you at all? O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge what has not come to you, so follow me; I will guide you to an even path. O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed Satan has ever been to the Most Merciful disobedient. O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will touch you, so you would be a companion to Satan." When divinity was negated from these three bodies, which are the brightest things that eyes fall upon, and this was established by a decisive proof, [Abraham] said: ﴿O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate with Allah.﴾ That is: I am free from worshipping them and from allying with them. So if they are gods, then plot against me with them all, then give me no respite. ﴿Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, as a hanif (upright monotheist), and I am not of those who associate others with Allah.﴾ That is: I only worship the Creator of these things, their Originator, their Subjugator, their Determiner, their Manager, in whose hand is the dominion of everything, the Creator of everything, its Lord, its Sovereign, and its God. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne. He causes the night to cover the day, pursuing it rapidly, and [He created] the sun and the moon and the stars, subjected by His command. Unquestionably, to Him belong creation and command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ [Al-A'raf: 54]. And how is it permissible that Abraham [the Friend (al-Khalil)] [addition from manuscript A] should be debating in this station, when it is he about whom Allah said: ﴿And We had certainly given Abraham his sound judgment before, and We were of him well-Knowing. When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted?"﴾ and the verses that follow [Al-Anbiya: 51, 52]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah, hanif, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah. He was grateful for His favors. He chose him and guided him to a straight path. And We gave him good in this world, and indeed he, in the Hereafter, is among the righteous. Then We revealed to you, "Follow the religion of Abraham, hanif, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah."﴾ [An-Nahl: 120-123]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a correct religion, the way of Abraham, hanif, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah."﴾ [Al-An'am: 161].

It is established in the two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn, Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every child is born upon the fitrah (innate natural disposition towards faith)." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1385) and Sahih Muslim no. (2658).] In Sahih Muslim, from Iyad ibn Hammad, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah said: Indeed, I created My servants as hunafa (upright monotheists)." [Sahih Muslim no. (2865).] And Allah said in His Mighty Book: ﴿The fitrah of Allah upon which He has created mankind; there is no change in the creation of Allah.﴾ [Ar-Rum: 30]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And [mention] when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves, [saying], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified."﴾ [Al-A'raf: 172]. Its meaning, according to one of the two opinions, is like His saying: ﴿The fitrah of Allah upon which He has created mankind﴾ as will come with its explanation.

So if this is the case regarding all of creation, how could Abraham the Friend, whom Allah made ﴿a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah, hanif, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah﴾ [An-Nahl: 120], be debating in this station?! Rather, he is, after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), without doubt or hesitation, the most deserving of people of the sound fitrah and the upright disposition. Among the things that support that he was debating his people about the shirk they were engaged in, and not inquiring (into the matter), is the saying of the Exalted:

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verses 74–79 (part 1 of 2):

Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "The name of Abraham's father was not Azar; his name was Tarih." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

He also said: Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn Abi 'Asim al-Nabil narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Abu 'Asim Shabib narrated to us, 'Ikrimah narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar﴾. He meant by Azar: the idol. Abraham's father's name was Tarih, his mother's name was Mathani, his wife's name was Sarah, and the mother of Isma'il was Hajar, who was Abraham's concubine.

Likewise said more than one of the genealogists ('ulama' al-nasab): his name was Tarih. Mujahid and al-Suddi said: Azar is the name of an idol.

I say: It seems that Azar became his name because he served that idol, and Allah knows best. [[In manuscript A: "wallahu a'lam" (and Allah knows best).]] Ibn Jarir said: Others said: "It is an insult and a defect in their speech, and its meaning is: crooked (mu'waj)," but he did not attribute it to a chain of narrators, nor did he report it from anyone.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman: I heard my father reading ﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar﴾, and he said: "It has reached me that it means 'crooked,' and that it is the harshest word Abraham, peace be upon him, ever uttered."

Then Ibn Jarir said: "The correct view is that the name of his father was Azar." Then he raised an objection against himself, namely the opinion of the genealogists that his name was Tarih, and then answered that a person may have two names, as many people do, or that one of them may be a title (laqab). [[Ahmad Shakir (may Allah have mercy on him), in a study at the end of al-Jawaliqi's book "al-Mu'arrab," wrote in its conclusion: "The decisive proof against the interpretations they claimed for the word 'Azar,' and against what they called readings, which takes the word out of being a proper name for the father of Abraham, is the sound and explicit hadith in al-Bukhari, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: 'Abraham will meet his father Azar on the Day of Resurrection, and on Azar's face there will be dust and darkness. Abraham will say to him: Did I not tell you: do not disobey me? His father will say: Today I will not disobey you... to the end of the hadith.' In al-Bukhari (4/139 of the Sultaniyyah edition), Fath al-Bari (6/276 of the Bulaq edition), and Sharh al-'Ayni (15/243, 244 of the Munirriyyah edition), this text shows that it is his proper name, and it does not admit interpretation or distortion."]] This that he said is good and strong, and Allah knows best.

The reciters differed in the pronunciation of His saying: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar﴾. Ibn Jarir related from al-Hasan al-Basri and Abu Yazid al-Madani that they used to read: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father, "O Azar, do you take idols as gods?"﴾, meaning: O Azar, do you take idols as gods?

The majority (al-Jumhur) read it with a fatha (فَتْحٌ), either because it is a non-Arabic proper name that does not take nunation (ghayr munsarif), and it is then a substitute (badal) for ﴿his father﴾, or an explanatory apposition ('atf bayan), and this is more likely.

And according to the view of the one who made it a descriptive (na't) that also does not take nunation, like "ahmar" and "aswad."

As for the one who claimed that it is in the accusative because it is governed by ﴿do you take idols﴾, with the meaning: "O father, do you make Azar idols as gods?", this is a far-fetched view in the language, because what follows the interrogative particle does not govern what comes before it, since the interrogative has precedence at the beginning of the sentence. Ibn Jarir and others established this, and it is well known in the rules of Arabic grammar.

The point is that Abraham, peace be upon him, admonished his father about worshipping idols, rebuked him for them, and forbade him, but he did not desist, as He said: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar, "Do you take idols as gods? Indeed I see you and your people in clear error."﴾ That is: do you make a god of an idol that you worship besides Allah? ﴿Indeed I see you and your people﴾, that is: those who follow your path, ﴿in clear error﴾, that is: bewildered, not guided as to where they are going, but in confusion and ignorance, and your affair is manifestly in ignorance and error, clear to everyone of sound intellect.

He, the Exalted, also said: ﴿And mention in the Book Abraham. Indeed he was a man of truth and a prophet. When he said to his father, "O my father, why do you worship that which neither hears nor sees and does not avail you at all? O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge what has not come to you, so follow me; I will guide you to an even path. O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed Satan has ever been to the Most Merciful disobedient. O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will touch you, so you would be a companion to Satan." He said, "Do you reject my gods, O Abraham? If you do not cease, I will surely stone you, so leave me for a long time." He said, "Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed He is ever gracious to me. And I will leave you and what you invoke other than Allah, and I will invoke my Lord; perhaps I will not be in invoking my Lord unblessed."﴾ [Maryam: 41–48]. So Abraham, peace be upon him, kept asking forgiveness for his father throughout his life. When his father died upon polytheism and Abraham became clear about that, he gave up asking forgiveness for him and disassociated himself from him, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And the request for forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy to Allah, he disowned him. Indeed Abraham was compassionate and forbearing.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 114].

It is established in the Sahih that Abraham will meet his father Azar on the Day of Resurrection, and his father will say to him: "O my son, today I will not disobey you." Abraham will say: "O my Lord, did You not promise me that You would not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected? And what disgrace is greater than that of my farthest father?" It will be said: "O Abraham, look behind you." Then he will see a dhikh (a smeared, filthy creature), which will be seized by its legs and thrown into the Fire. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3350).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And thus We showed Abraham the realm of the heavens and the earth﴾: that is, We made clear to him the aspect of proof in his looking at their creation, for the oneness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in His dominion and creation, and that there is no god but Him and no lord besides Him. It is like His saying: ﴿Say, "Look at what is in the heavens and the earth"﴾ [Yunus: 101], and He said: ﴿Have they not looked into the realm of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-A'raf: 185], and He said: ﴿Have they not looked at what is before them and behind them of the sky and the earth? If We willed, We could cause the earth to swallow them or let fall upon them fragments from the sky. Indeed in that is a sign for every servant who turns back [to Allah].﴾ [Saba': 9].

As for what Ibn Jarir and others related from Mujahid, 'Ata', Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi, and others, they said, and the wording is Mujahid's: "The heavens were opened for him, and he looked at what is in them until his sight reached the Throne. The seven earths were opened for him, and he looked at what is in them." Another added: "He began to look at the servants committing sins, and he would curse them. Allah said to him: 'I am more merciful to My servants than you are; perhaps they will repent and return.'" Ibn Mardawayh narrated in this regard two marfu' hadiths, from Mu'adh and 'Ali [ibn Abi Talib]. [[The hadith of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib was mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (3/302). As for the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Jabal, al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. (6700), through the route of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him.]] But their chains are not sound, and Allah knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through the route of al-'Awfi, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And thus We showed Abraham the realm of the heavens and the earth, and that he might be among the certain [in faith]﴾: that He, the Exalted, made the matter clear to him, its secret and its open aspects, so nothing of the deeds of creatures was hidden from him. When he began to curse the people of sins, Allah said: "Indeed you are not able to bear this." So He returned him to how he was before that. It is possible that He uncovered his sight so that he saw that directly, and it is possible that it was through his insight until he witnessed it with his heart, verified it and recognized it, and knew the great wisdoms and decisive proofs in it. Likewise, Imam Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi narrated, and al-Tirmidhi declared it sound, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Added from A.]] in the hadith of the dream: "My Lord came to me in the best form and said: 'O Muhammad, about what do the exalted assembly dispute?' I said: 'I do not know, O my Lord.' So He placed His palm between my shoulders, until I found the coolness of His fingertips between my breasts, and everything was made clear to me and I knew..." and he mentioned the hadith. [[Al-Musnad (5/243) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3235). Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith. I asked Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) about this hadith and he said: 'This is a hasan sahih hadith.'"]]

* *

His saying: ﴿and that he might be among the certain [in faith]﴾. It has been said: the "wa" (و) is extra, its meaning being: "Thus We showed Abraham the realm of the heavens and the earth, so that he might be among the certain," like His saying: ﴿[Thus] We detail the verses, and that the way of the criminals may become clear﴾ [al-An'am: 55].

It has also been said: rather, it is on its original [meaning], that is: We showed him that so that he might be a knower and certain.

* *

His saying: ﴿So when the night covered him﴾, that is: it enveloped him and concealed him, ﴿he saw a star﴾, that is: a planet, ﴿he said, "This is my lord." But when it set﴾, that is: it disappeared. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: "al-Uful" means departing. Ibn Jarir said: It is said: the star afala, yafulu, and ya'fil, ufulan and ufulan (أَفَلَ يَأْفُلُ وَيَأْفِلُ أُفُولًا وَأُفُولًا) when it disappeared. From this is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

"Lamps, not like the stars that lead them, nor like the setting ones that vanish."

And it is said: "Where did you set (afalta) from us?" meaning: "Where did you go absent from us?"

He said: ﴿He said, "I do not love those that set."﴾ Qatadah said: He knew that his Lord is eternal and does not cease. ﴿Then when he saw the moon rising﴾, that is: ascending, ﴿he said, "This is my lord." But when it set, he said, "If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the people who are astray."﴾ ﴿Then when he saw the sun rising, he said, "This is my lord; this is greater."﴾ That is: this shining one rising is my lord. ﴿This is greater﴾, that is: greater in body than the star and the moon, and more radiant. ﴿But when it set﴾, that is: it disappeared, ﴿he said, "O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate with Allah. Indeed I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with Allah."﴾ That is: I have made my religion sincere and devoted my worship exclusively ﴿to He who created the heavens and the earth﴾, that is: who created them and originated them without a prior pattern. ﴿Inclining﴾, that is: while I am inclining, turning away from polytheism toward monotheism. For this reason He said: ﴿And I am not of those who associate others with Allah.﴾

The commentators differed about this station: was it a station of reflection (nazar) or of debate (munazarah)? Ibn Jarir related through the route of 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, what indicates that it was a station of reflection, and Ibn Jarir preferred this, citing His saying: ﴿If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the people who are astray.﴾

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: He said that when he came out of the cave (sarab) in which his mother had given birth to him, when she feared for him from Nimrod ibn Kan'an, because it had been reported to him that a child would be born whose hands would bring an end to his kingdom, so he ordered the killing of the boys at that time. When Abraham's mother became pregnant with him, and her delivery drew near, she took him to a cave outside the town, gave birth to Abraham there, and left him there. He mentioned matters of extraordinary occurrences, as other commentators from the early and later generations also mentioned them.

The commentary, in its own words, holds that Abraham, peace be upon him, in this station was debating his people and showing them the falsehood of what they were upon, worshipping the hayakil (temples; here, the celestial bodies) and the idols. In the first station, with his father, he showed their error in worshipping the earthly idols, which are in the form of the heavenly angels, so that they would intercede for them with the Great Creator. They regard themselves as too lowly to worship Him directly, so they approach Him through worship of His angels, that these might intercede for them with Him regarding provision, victory, and other things they need. In this station he showed their error and misguidance in worshipping the hayakil, namely the seven wandering planets that move about: the Moon, Mercury, Venus, the Sun, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. The brightest and most radiant of them in their view are the Sun, then the Moon, then Venus. First he showed that Venus is not fit for divinity, because it is subjected and ordained to a specific course from which it does not deviate right or left, and it does not possess any control over itself. Rather, it is a body among the bodies, which Allah created luminous for the great wisdoms He has in that. It rises from the East, then travels between it and the West until it sets from sight there, then appears the following night in the same manner. Such a thing is not fit for divinity.

Then he moved on to the Moon and showed regarding it the same as he showed regarding the star.

Then he moved on to the Sun in the same way. When divinity was negated from these three bodies, which are the brightest things that eyes fall upon, and this was established by a decisive proof, [Abraham] said: ﴿O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate with Allah.﴾ That is: I am free from worshipping them and from allying with them. So if they are gods, then plot against me with them all, then give me no respite. ﴿Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, as a hanif (upright monotheist), and I am not of those who associate others with Allah.﴾ That is: I only worship the Creator of these things, their Originator, their Subjugator, their Determiner, their Manager, in whose hand is the dominion of everything, the Creator of everything, its Lord, its Sovereign, and its God. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne. He causes the night to cover the day, pursuing it rapidly, and [He created] the sun and the moon and the stars, subjected by His command. Unquestionably, to Him belong creation and command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ [Al-A'raf: 54]. And how is it permissible that Abraham [the Friend (al-Khalil)] [addition from manuscript A] should be debating in this station, when it is he about whom Allah said: ﴿And We had certainly given Abraham his sound judgment before, and We were of him well-Knowing. When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted?"﴾ and the verses that follow [Al-Anbiya: 51, 52]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah, hanif, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah. He was grateful for His favors. He chose him and guided him to a straight path. And We gave him good in this world, and indeed he, in the Hereafter, is among the righteous. Then We revealed to you, "Follow the religion of Abraham, hanif, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah."﴾ [An-Nahl: 120-123]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a correct religion, the way of Abraham, hanif, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah."﴾ [Al-An'am: 161].

It is established in the two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn, Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every child is born upon the fitrah (innate natural disposition towards faith)." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1385) and Sahih Muslim no. (2658).] In Sahih Muslim, from Iyad ibn Hammad, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah said: Indeed, I created My servants as hunafa (upright monotheists)." [Sahih Muslim no. (2865).] And Allah said in His Mighty Book: ﴿The fitrah of Allah upon which He has created mankind; there is no change in the creation of Allah.﴾ [Ar-Rum: 30]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And [mention] when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves, [saying], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified."﴾ [Al-A'raf: 172]. Its meaning, according to one of the two opinions, is like His saying: ﴿The fitrah of Allah upon which He has created mankind﴾ as will come with its explanation.

So if this is the case regarding all of creation, how could Abraham the Friend, whom Allah made ﴿a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah, hanif, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah﴾ [An-Nahl: 120], be debating in this station?! Rather, he is, after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), without doubt or hesitation, the most deserving of people of the sound fitrah and the upright disposition. Among the things that support that he was debating his people about the shirk they were engaged in, and not inquiring (into the matter), is the saying of the Exalted:

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him: Allah the Exalted says: His people argued with him concerning what he held of Tawhid (the oneness of Allah), and they disputed with him using specious arguments. He said: ﴿He said: "Do you argue with me about Allah, when He has guided me?"﴾ That is: "Do you dispute with me about the matter of Allah, that there is no god but Him, when He has given me insight and guided me to the truth, and I stand upon clear proof from Him? So how should I turn to your corrupt sayings and your false doubts?!"

* *

And His saying: ﴿And I do not fear those you associate with Him, unless my Lord wills something.﴾ That is: among the proofs of the falsehood of your position is that these deities you worship do not affect anything, and I do not fear them or care for them. If they had any power, then ﴿plot against me, all of you together﴾ [[Addition from manuscript M.]] ﴿and give me no respite.﴾ Rather, hasten to do that against me.

* *

And His saying: ﴿unless my Lord wills something﴾ is an exception of a disconnected type (istithna' munqati'): that is, none harms or benefits except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge.﴾ That is, His knowledge encompasses all things, so nothing is hidden from Him.

﴿Will you not then take heed?﴾ That is, concerning what I have explained to you, so that you consider that these deities are false, and refrain from worshipping them? This argument is similar to what the Prophet of Allah Hud (peace be upon him) argued with his people, 'Ad, as Allah relates in His Book, where He says: ﴿They said: "O Hud, you have brought us no clear proof, and we will not abandon our gods on your word, nor will we believe in you. We say only that some of our gods have struck you with evil." He said: "I call Allah to witness, and bear witness yourselves that I am free from what you associate, besides Him. So plot against me all together, then give me no respite. Indeed I have placed my trust in Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock. Indeed my Lord is on a straight path."﴾ [Hud: 53–56] [[Addition from manuscripts M and A; in H: "the verse".]]

* *

And His saying: ﴿And how should I fear what you associate, when you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority?﴾ That is: how should I fear these idols that you worship besides Allah? ﴿and you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority?﴾ Ibn 'Abbas and many of the early scholars (al-Salaf) said: "That is, no proof." This is like His saying: ﴿Or do they have partners who have prescribed for them in religion what Allah has not permitted?﴾ [al-Shura: 21], and His saying: ﴿They are only names you have named, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority.﴾ [al-Najm: 23]

* *

And His saying: ﴿So which of the two parties has more right to security, if you know?﴾ That is: which of the two groups is more correct? The one that worships the One in whose hand is harm and benefit, or the one that worships, without any evidence, what neither harms nor benefits? Which of the two has more right to security from the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection? Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing—for them is security, and they are rightly guided.﴾ That is: these are the ones who devoted worship purely to Allah alone, without any partner, and did not associate anything with Him. They are the ones who will be secure on the Day of Resurrection, and the ones who are guided in this world and the Hereafter.

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Sulayman, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, from 'Abd Allah who said: When the verse ﴿and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing﴾ was revealed, his companions said: "And which of us has not wronged himself?" Then it was revealed: ﴿Indeed, associating others with Allah is a tremendous wrong.﴾ [Luqman: 13] [[Sahih al-Bukhari, number (4629).]]

And Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, from 'Abd Allah who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing﴾, it weighed heavily upon the people [[in M: "the Muslims".]] and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of us does not wrong himself?" He said: "It is not what you mean! Did you not hear what the righteous servant said: ﴿O my son, do not associate anything with Allah; indeed, associating others with Allah is a tremendous wrong.﴾ It is only shirk." [[Al-Musnad (1/378).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Waki' and Ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, from 'Abd Allah who said: When ﴿and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing﴾ was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They said: "And which of us has not wronged himself?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is not as you think. Luqman only said to his son: ﴿O my son, do not associate anything with Allah; indeed, associating others with Allah is a tremendous wrong.﴾" [[In M: "Luqman" added.]] [[Also narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, number (6937), by the route of Waki' with similar wording.]] And 'Umar ibn Shabbah al-Numayri narrated to us, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, from 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning His saying: ﴿and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing﴾, he said: "With shirk."

He said: It has been related from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, 'Umar, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Salman, Hudhayfah, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar, 'Amr ibn Shurahbil, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Nakha'i, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and al-Suddi something similar to this.
