He said: "I affirm it." Then his camel's leg went into a jerboa's hole, and the camel fell, and the man fell, landing on his head, and died. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Bring the man to me." So 'Ammar ibn Yasir and Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman leapt up to him and sat him up, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, the man has died!" He turned away from them, and then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Did you not see my turning away from the man? I saw two angels pushing into his mouth fruits of Paradise, so I knew that he died hungry." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is one of those of whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing﴾ [[In M and A: "...for them is security, and they are rightly guided."]] Then he said: "Take care of your brother." So we carried him to the water, washed him, applied perfume, shrouded him, and carried him to the grave. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and sat on the edge of the grave and said: "Dig the lahd (niche) and do not dig the shaqq (trench), for the lahd is for us and the shaqq is for others." [[Al-Musnad (4/359). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/42): "In its chain is Abu Janab, who is a mudallis (concealer of sources) and has narrated with 'an'anah."]]

Then Ahmad narrated it from Aswad ibn 'Amir, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far al-Farra', from Thabit, from Zadhan, from Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah, mentioning something similar, and in it he said: "This is one who did a little deed and was rewarded greatly." [[Al-Musnad (4/359). Thabit did follow Abu Janab, but there is disagreement on it: al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/319) by the route of 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, from Thabit, from Abu al-Buqdhan, from Zadhan, from Jarir.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Yusuf ibn Musa al-Qattan narrated to us, Mihran ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us [[in A: "'Abd Allah".]], from his father, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey, when a Bedouin confronted him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Him who sent you with the truth, I have left my land, my wealth and my property to be guided by your guidance and to take from your speech. I have not reached you until I have no food except what grows from the earth. So present Islam to me." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) presented it to him, and he accepted. We crowded around him, and the Bedouin's camel's foot entered a jerboa's hole, so the Bedouin fell and his neck broke. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He spoke the truth, by Him who sent me with the truth. He left his land, his wealth and his property seeking to be guided by my guidance and to take from my speech, and he did not reach me until he had no food except what grows from the earth. Did you hear of one who did a little deed and was rewarded greatly? This is one of them! Did you hear of those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing—for them is security, and they are rightly guided? Indeed, this is one of them." [[Narrated also by al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (3/309).]]

[And Ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Mu'alla—who had settled in al-Rayy—: Ziyad ibn Khaythamah narrated to us, from Abu Dawud, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is given and is grateful, and is denied and is patient, and wrongs and seeks forgiveness, and is wronged and forgives," and he fell silent. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about him?" He said: ﴿Those are the ones for whom is security, and they are rightly guided.﴾] [[Addition from M and A.]]

* *

And His saying: ﴿And that was Our argument, which We gave to Ibrahim against his people.﴾ That is: We directed his argument against his people.

Mujahid and others said: This refers to his saying: ﴿And how should I fear what you associate, when you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority? So which of the two parties has more right to security, if you know?﴾ [[Addition from M and A; in H: "the verse".]] Allah confirmed him, and judged him to have security and guidance, saying: ﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing—for them is security, and they are rightly guided.﴾ Then after all of that He said: ﴿And that was Our argument, which We gave to Ibrahim against his people. We raise in degrees whom We will.﴾

It is recited with the idafah (construct, "degrees of") and without the idafah, as in Surat Yusuf, and both are close in meaning.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed your Lord is Wise and Knowing.﴾ That is: Wise in His actions and sayings, ﴿Knowing﴾, that is, of whom He guides and whom He misguides, even if proofs and evidences are established against him, as He said: ﴿Indeed, those against whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe. Even if every sign came to them, until they see the painful punishment.﴾ [Yunus: 96–97]. For this reason He said here:

﴿Indeed your Lord is Wise and Knowing.﴾

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him: Allah the Exalted says: His people argued with him concerning what he held of Tawhid (the oneness of Allah), and they disputed with him using specious arguments. He said: ﴿He said: "Do you argue with me about Allah, when He has guided me?"﴾ That is: "Do you dispute with me about the matter of Allah, that there is no god but Him, when He has given me insight and guided me to the truth, and I stand upon clear proof from Him? So how should I turn to your corrupt sayings and your false doubts?!"

* *

And His saying: ﴿And I do not fear those you associate with Him, unless my Lord wills something.﴾ That is: among the proofs of the falsehood of your position is that these deities you worship do not affect anything, and I do not fear them or care for them. If they had any power, then ﴿plot against me, all of you together﴾ [[Addition from manuscript M.]] ﴿and give me no respite.﴾ Rather, hasten to do that against me.

* *

And His saying: ﴿unless my Lord wills something﴾ is an exception of a disconnected type (istithna' munqati'): that is, none harms or benefits except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge.﴾ That is, His knowledge encompasses all things, so nothing is hidden from Him.

﴿Will you not then take heed?﴾ That is, concerning what I have explained to you, so that you consider that these deities are false, and refrain from worshipping them? This argument is similar to what the Prophet of Allah Hud (peace be upon him) argued with his people, 'Ad, as Allah relates in His Book, where He says: ﴿They said: "O Hud, you have brought us no clear proof, and we will not abandon our gods on your word, nor will we believe in you. We say only that some of our gods have struck you with evil." He said: "I call Allah to witness, and bear witness yourselves that I am free from what you associate, besides Him. So plot against me all together, then give me no respite. Indeed I have placed my trust in Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock. Indeed my Lord is on a straight path."﴾ [Hud: 53–56] [[Addition from manuscripts M and A; in H: "the verse".]]

* *

And His saying: ﴿And how should I fear what you associate, when you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority?﴾ That is: how should I fear these idols that you worship besides Allah? ﴿and you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority?﴾ Ibn 'Abbas and many of the early scholars (al-Salaf) said: "That is, no proof." This is like His saying: ﴿Or do they have partners who have prescribed for them in religion what Allah has not permitted?﴾ [al-Shura: 21], and His saying: ﴿They are only names you have named, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority.﴾ [al-Najm: 23]

* *

And His saying: ﴿So which of the two parties has more right to security, if you know?﴾ That is: which of the two groups is more correct? The one that worships the One in whose hand is harm and benefit, or the one that worships, without any evidence, what neither harms nor benefits? Which of the two has more right to security from the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection? Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing—for them is security, and they are rightly guided.﴾ That is: these are the ones who devoted worship purely to Allah alone, without any partner, and did not associate anything with Him. They are the ones who will be secure on the Day of Resurrection, and the ones who are guided in this world and the Hereafter.

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Sulayman, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, from 'Abd Allah who said: When the verse ﴿and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing﴾ was revealed, his companions said: "And which of us has not wronged himself?" Then it was revealed: ﴿Indeed, associating others with Allah is a tremendous wrong.﴾ [Luqman: 13] [[Sahih al-Bukhari, number (4629).]]

And Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, from 'Abd Allah who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing﴾, it weighed heavily upon the people [[in M: "the Muslims".]] and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of us does not wrong himself?" He said: "It is not what you mean! Did you not hear what the righteous servant said: ﴿O my son, do not associate anything with Allah; indeed, associating others with Allah is a tremendous wrong.﴾ It is only shirk." [[Al-Musnad (1/378).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Waki' and Ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, from 'Abd Allah who said: When ﴿and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing﴾ was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They said: "And which of us has not wronged himself?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is not as you think. Luqman only said to his son: ﴿O my son, do not associate anything with Allah; indeed, associating others with Allah is a tremendous wrong.﴾" [[In M: "Luqman" added.]] [[Also narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, number (6937), by the route of Waki' with similar wording.]] And 'Umar ibn Shabbah al-Numayri narrated to us, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, from 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning His saying: ﴿and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing﴾, he said: "With shirk."

He said: It has been related from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, 'Umar, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Salman, Hudhayfah, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar, 'Amr ibn Shurahbil, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Nakha'i, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and al-Suddi something similar to this.

Ibn Mardawayh said: al-Shafi'i narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Shaddad al-Mis'ami narrated to us, Abu 'Asim narrated to us, Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, from 'Abd Allah who said: When ﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It was said to me: 'You are among them.'" [[In its chain is Muhammad ibn Shaddad al-Mis'ami. Al-Daraqutni said: "His narrations are not written down," and said at another time: "Weak," and al-Barqani declared him weak.]]

And Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Abu Janab narrated to us, from Zadhan, from Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When we emerged from Madinah, a rider came toward us at a fast pace. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It seems this rider intends you." The man reached us, greeted us, and we returned his greeting. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "From where have you come?" He said: "From my family, my children and my tribe." He said: "Where are you heading?" He said: "I want the Messenger of Allah." He said: "Then you have found him." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, teach me what faith is." He said: "That you testify that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; that you establish the prayer, pay the zakat, fast Ramadan, and perform Hajj to the House." He said: "I affirm it." Then his camel's leg went into a jerboa's hole, and the camel fell, and the man fell, landing on his head, and died. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Bring the man to me." So 'Ammar ibn Yasir and Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman leapt up to him and sat him up, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, the man has died!" He turned away from them, and then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Did you not see my turning away from the man? I saw two angels pushing into his mouth fruits of Paradise, so I knew that he died hungry." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is one of those of whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing﴾ [[In M and A: "...for them is security, and they are rightly guided."]] Then he said: "Take care of your brother." So we carried him to the water, washed him, applied perfume, shrouded him, and carried him to the grave. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and sat on the edge of the grave and said: "Dig the lahd (niche) and do not dig the shaqq (trench), for the lahd is for us and the shaqq is for others." [[Al-Musnad (4/359). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/42): "In its chain is Abu Janab, who is a mudallis (concealer of sources) and has narrated with 'an'anah."]]

Then Ahmad narrated it from Aswad ibn 'Amir, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far al-Farra', from Thabit, from Zadhan, from Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah, mentioning something similar, and in it he said: "This is one who did a little deed and was rewarded greatly." [[Al-Musnad (4/359). Thabit did follow Abu Janab, but there is disagreement on it: al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/319) by the route of 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, from Thabit, from Abu al-Buqdhan, from Zadhan, from Jarir.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Yusuf ibn Musa al-Qattan narrated to us, Mihran ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us [[in A: "'Abd Allah".]], from his father, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey, when a Bedouin confronted him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Him who sent you with the truth, I have left my land, my wealth and my property to be guided by your guidance and to take from your speech. I have not reached you until I have no food except what grows from the earth. So present Islam to me." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) presented it to him, and he accepted. We crowded around him, and the Bedouin's camel's foot entered a jerboa's hole, so the Bedouin fell and his neck broke. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He spoke the truth, by Him who sent me with the truth. He left his land, his wealth and his property seeking to be guided by my guidance and to take from my speech, and he did not reach me until he had no food except what grows from the earth. Did you hear of one who did a little deed and was rewarded greatly? This is one of them! Did you hear of those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing—for them is security, and they are rightly guided? Indeed, this is one of them." [[Narrated also by al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (3/309).]]

[And Ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Mu'alla—who had settled in al-Rayy—: Ziyad ibn Khaythamah narrated to us, from Abu Dawud, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is given and is grateful, and is denied and is patient, and wrongs and seeks forgiveness, and is wronged and forgives," and he fell silent. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about him?" He said: ﴿Those are the ones for whom is security, and they are rightly guided.﴾] [[Addition from M and A.]]

* *

And His saying: ﴿And that was Our argument, which We gave to Ibrahim against his people.﴾ That is: We directed his argument against his people.

Mujahid and others said: This refers to his saying: ﴿And how should I fear what you associate, when you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority? So which of the two parties has more right to security, if you know?﴾ [[Addition from M and A; in H: "the verse".]] Allah confirmed him, and judged him to have security and guidance, saying: ﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing—for them is security, and they are rightly guided.﴾ Then after all of that He said: ﴿And that was Our argument, which We gave to Ibrahim against his people. We raise in degrees whom We will.﴾

It is recited with the idafah (construct, "degrees of") and without the idafah, as in Surat Yusuf, and both are close in meaning.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed your Lord is Wise and Knowing.﴾ That is: Wise in His actions and sayings, ﴿Knowing﴾, that is, of whom He guides and whom He misguides, even if proofs and evidences are established against him, as He said: ﴿Indeed, those against whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe. Even if every sign came to them, until they see the painful punishment.﴾ [Yunus: 96–97]. For this reason He said here:

﴿Indeed your Lord is Wise and Knowing.﴾

He said Allah granted Abraham Isaac after he had reached old age, when he and his wife Sarah had despaired of having a child. The angels came to him as they were heading to the people of Lot, and they gave them the good news of Isaac. The woman wondered at this and said: ﴿Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and this, my husband, is an old man? Indeed, this is an astonishing thing.﴾ They said: ﴿Do you wonder at the decree of Allah? The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O people of the house. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Glorious.﴾ [Hud: 72, 73]. They gave the good news to him as well, while he was still alive, of his prophethood and that he would have offspring and descendants, as He said: ﴿And We gave him the good news of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous.﴾ [al-Saffat: 112]. This is more complete in the good news and greater in blessing. He also said: ﴿So We gave her good news of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob.﴾ [Hud: 71]. That is, this child will have a child during your lifetime, so that you will be comforted by him just as you were comforted by his father. The joy of a grandchild is intense because it ensures the continuation of lineage and descendants. Since the child of an old man and an old woman might be thought to be unable to have offspring because of their weakness, the good news was given about him and his son by the name "Jacob," which contains the derivation of "lineage" (ʿaqib) and "offspring" (dhurriyyah). This was a recompense to Abraham, peace be upon him, for having withdrawn from his people, abandoned them, moved away from them, and emigrated from their lands, going to worship Allah in the earth. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, compensated him for his people and kin with righteous children from his own loins who followed his religion, so that his eye would be comforted by them, as He said: ﴿So when he had withdrawn from them and what they worshipped other than Allah, We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and each We made a prophet.﴾ [Maryam: 49]. Here He said: ﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob; each We guided.﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿And Noah, We guided before﴾ means: before him (Abraham). We guided him as We guided him (Abraham), and We gave him righteous offspring. Each of them has a great distinction. As for Noah, peace be upon him, when Allah drowned the people of the earth except those who believed in him, and they were those who accompanied him in the ark, Allah made his descendants the ones who remained. So all people are from the descendants of Noah. Likewise, the Friend (khalil), Abraham, peace be upon him: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not send any prophet after him except from his descendants, as He said: ﴿And We placed in his descendants prophethood and the Scripture﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-ʿAnkabut: 27]. He also said: ﴿And We sent Noah and Abraham and placed in their descendants prophethood and the Scripture﴾ [al-Hadid: 26]. He also said: ﴿Those are the ones upon whom Allah bestowed favor among the prophets of the descendants of Adam, and of those whom We carried with Noah, and of the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and of those whom We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell down in prostration and weeping.﴾ [Maryam: 58].

* *

His saying in this noble verse: ﴿And from his descendants﴾ means: and We guided from his descendants ﴿David and Solomon﴾, and so on to the end of the verse. The return of the pronoun to Noah is apparent, because he is the nearest of those mentioned, and this is the choice of Ibn Jarir, with no difficulty in it. Its return to Abraham, because the discourse was about him, is also acceptable, but Lot creates a difficulty for this view, since he is not from Abraham's descendants; rather, he is the son of Abraham's brother Haran, son of Azar. Unless it is said that he is included in the "descendants" by way of taghlib (predominance, where one term covers another in a single sense), as in His saying: ﴿Or were you witnesses when death approached Jacob, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac, one God, and to Him we are Muslims."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 133]. Ishmael was Jacob's paternal uncle, and he is included among the "fathers" by taghlib.

[And as He said: ﴿So all the angels prostrated, all of them entirely, except Iblis﴾ [al-Hijr: 30, 31]. Iblis was included in the command to the angels to prostrate, and he was blamed for disobeying, because he had made himself similar to them, so he was treated as they were and was included with them by taghlib, although he was from the jinn, whose nature is fire, while the angels are of light.] [addition from M and A.]

Mentioning Jesus, peace be upon him, among the descendants of Abraham or Noah, according to the other view, is evidence that the children of daughters are included among the descendants of men, because Jesus, peace be upon him, is traced to Abraham, peace be upon him, through his mother Mary, peace be upon her, since he had no father.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Sahl ibn Yahya al-ʿAskari narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Salih narrated to us, ʿAli ibn ʿAbis [in A: "ʿAbbas"] narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAta al-Makki, from Abu Harb ibn Abi al-Aswad, who said: al-Hajjaj sent for Yahya ibn Yaʿmur and said: "It has reached me that you claim that al-Hasan and al-Husayn are descendants of the Prophet ﷺ. You will find it in the Book of Allah, but I have read it from beginning to end and have not found it." He said: "Do you not recite Surat al-Anʿam: ﴿And from his descendants, David and Solomon﴾ until he reached ﴿and Yahya and Jesus﴾?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Is not Jesus from the descendants of Abraham, and he has no father?" He said: "You are right."

Therefore, when a man bequeaths to his descendants, or endows for his descendants, or gives gifts to them, the children of daughters enter among them. But when a man gives to his sons or endows for them, it is specific to his children of his own loins and the children of his sons. They cited the words of the Arab poet:

"Our sons are the sons of our sons, and our daughters' sons are the sons of other men."

[Ibn ʿAqil cited it in his commentary on Ibn Malik's Alfiyya, no. 51. In his version, "al-abaʿid" appears instead of "al-ajanib."]

Others said: The sons of daughters are also included in it, because it is established in Sahih al-Bukhari that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to al-Hasan ibn ʿAli: "This son of mine is a master, and perhaps Allah will reconcile through him between two great groups of the Muslims." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2704, from the hadith of Abu Bakrah, may Allah be pleased with him.] He called him "son," which shows that he is included among the sons.

Others said: This is a figurative usage (tajawwuz).

* *

His saying: ﴿And from their fathers, their descendants, and their brothers﴾ mentions their ancestors, their offspring, and their contemporaries, and that guidance and choosing included them all. Therefore He said: ﴿And We chose them and guided them to a straight path.﴾

Then He said: ﴿That is the guidance of Allah; He guides whom He wills of His servants.﴾ That is, this was attained by them only through Allah's success (tawfiq) and His guidance to them. ﴿But if they had associated others with Him, what they had been doing would have been worthless to them.﴾ This is an emphasis on the matter of shirk, a stern warning about its gravity, and a magnification of its seriousness, as He said: ﴿And it has already been revealed to you and to those before you: If you should associate others with Allah, your work will surely be nullified.﴾ [al-Zumar: 65] up to the end of the verse. This is a conditional statement, and a conditional does not imply that the condition occurs, as in His saying: ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first of the worshippers.﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 81], and His saying: ﴿Had We intended to take a diversion, We would have taken it from Our presence, if We were ever to do so.﴾ [al-Anbiya: 17], and His saying: ﴿Had Allah intended to take a son, He would have chosen from what He creates whatever He willed. Exalted is He; He is Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ [al-Zumar: 4].

* *

His saying: ﴿Those are the ones to whom We gave the Scripture, judgment, and prophethood.﴾ That is, We bestowed these favors on them as a mercy to the servants through them, and as kindness from Us to creation. ﴿But if these people disbelieve in them﴾ means: in the prophethood. It is also possible that the pronoun refers to these three things: the Scripture, the judgment, and the prophethood.

* *

His saying: ﴿these people﴾ means: the people of Makkah. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and al-Suddi. ﴿Then We have entrusted them to a people who are not disbelievers in them.﴾ That is: if those who disbelieve in these favors among the Quraysh and others among all the people of the earth, Arab and non-Arab, followers of religions and of scripture, disbelieve in them, then We have entrusted them to ﴿other﴾ people, meaning the Emigrants (Muhajirun), the Helpers (Ansar), and their followers until the Day of Resurrection, ﴿who are not disbelievers in them﴾. That is, they do not deny any part of them and do not reject even a single letter of them, but believe in all of them, the clear and the allegorical. May Allah make us among them by His grace, generosity, and kindness.

Then Allah, exalted, addressed His servant and Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, saying: ﴿Those﴾ means: the mentioned prophets together with those who were attributed to them of fathers, descendants, and brothers, who were of the same class (ashbah). ﴿Are the ones whom Allah guided.﴾ That is: they are the people of guidance, not others. ﴿So follow their guidance.﴾ That is: follow and adhere to it. Since this is a command to the Messenger ﷺ, his community follows him in what he legislates for them and commands them to do.

His saying: ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any wage for it.﴾ That is: I do not seek from you any payment (ajr) for my conveying of this Qur'an to you, nor do I want anything from you. ﴿It is nothing but a reminder to the worlds.﴾ That is: they may be reminded by it and guided from blindness to guidance, from error to right direction, and from disbelief to faith.

He said Allah granted Abraham Isaac after he had reached old age, when he and his wife Sarah had despaired of having a child. The angels came to him as they were heading to the people of Lot, and they gave them the good news of Isaac. The woman wondered at this and said: ﴿Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and this, my husband, is an old man? Indeed, this is an astonishing thing.﴾ They said: ﴿Do you wonder at the decree of Allah? The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O people of the house. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Glorious.﴾ [Hud: 72, 73]. They gave the good news to him as well, while he was still alive, of his prophethood and that he would have offspring and descendants, as He said: ﴿And We gave him the good news of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous.﴾ [al-Saffat: 112]. This is more complete in the good news and greater in blessing. He also said: ﴿So We gave her good news of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob.﴾ [Hud: 71]. That is, this child will have a child during your lifetime, so that you will be comforted by him just as you were comforted by his father. The joy of a grandchild is intense because it ensures the continuation of lineage and descendants. Since the child of an old man and an old woman might be thought to be unable to have offspring because of their weakness, the good news was given about him and his son by the name "Jacob," which contains the derivation of "lineage" (ʿaqib) and "offspring" (dhurriyyah). This was a recompense to Abraham, peace be upon him, for having withdrawn from his people, abandoned them, moved away from them, and emigrated from their lands, going to worship Allah in the earth. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, compensated him for his people and kin with righteous children from his own loins who followed his religion, so that his eye would be comforted by them, as He said: ﴿So when he had withdrawn from them and what they worshipped other than Allah, We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and each We made a prophet.﴾ [Maryam: 49]. Here He said: ﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob; each We guided.﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿And Noah, We guided before﴾ means: before him (Abraham). We guided him as We guided him (Abraham), and We gave him righteous offspring. Each of them has a great distinction. As for Noah, peace be upon him, when Allah drowned the people of the earth except those who believed in him, and they were those who accompanied him in the ark, Allah made his descendants the ones who remained. So all people are from the descendants of Noah. Likewise, the Friend (khalil), Abraham, peace be upon him: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not send any prophet after him except from his descendants, as He said: ﴿And We placed in his descendants prophethood and the Scripture﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-ʿAnkabut: 27]. He also said: ﴿And We sent Noah and Abraham and placed in their descendants prophethood and the Scripture﴾ [al-Hadid: 26]. He also said: ﴿Those are the ones upon whom Allah bestowed favor among the prophets of the descendants of Adam, and of those whom We carried with Noah, and of the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and of those whom We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell down in prostration and weeping.﴾ [Maryam: 58].

* *

His saying in this noble verse: ﴿And from his descendants﴾ means: and We guided from his descendants ﴿David and Solomon﴾, and so on to the end of the verse. The return of the pronoun to Noah is apparent, because he is the nearest of those mentioned, and this is the choice of Ibn Jarir, with no difficulty in it. Its return to Abraham, because the discourse was about him, is also acceptable, but Lot creates a difficulty for this view, since he is not from Abraham's descendants; rather, he is the son of Abraham's brother Haran, son of Azar. Unless it is said that he is included in the "descendants" by way of taghlib (predominance, where one term covers another in a single sense), as in His saying: ﴿Or were you witnesses when death approached Jacob, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac, one God, and to Him we are Muslims."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 133]. Ishmael was Jacob's paternal uncle, and he is included among the "fathers" by taghlib.

[And as He said: ﴿So all the angels prostrated, all of them entirely, except Iblis﴾ [al-Hijr: 30, 31]. Iblis was included in the command to the angels to prostrate, and he was blamed for disobeying, because he had made himself similar to them, so he was treated as they were and was included with them by taghlib, although he was from the jinn, whose nature is fire, while the angels are of light.] [addition from M and A.]

Mentioning Jesus, peace be upon him, among the descendants of Abraham or Noah, according to the other view, is evidence that the children of daughters are included among the descendants of men, because Jesus, peace be upon him, is traced to Abraham, peace be upon him, through his mother Mary, peace be upon her, since he had no father.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Sahl ibn Yahya al-ʿAskari narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Salih narrated to us, ʿAli ibn ʿAbis [in A: "ʿAbbas"] narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAta al-Makki, from Abu Harb ibn Abi al-Aswad, who said: al-Hajjaj sent for Yahya ibn Yaʿmur and said: "It has reached me that you claim that al-Hasan and al-Husayn are descendants of the Prophet ﷺ. You will find it in the Book of Allah, but I have read it from beginning to end and have not found it." He said: "Do you not recite Surat al-Anʿam: ﴿And from his descendants, David and Solomon﴾ until he reached ﴿and Yahya and Jesus﴾?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Is not Jesus from the descendants of Abraham, and he has no father?" He said: "You are right."

Therefore, when a man bequeaths to his descendants, or endows for his descendants, or gives gifts to them, the children of daughters enter among them. But when a man gives to his sons or endows for them, it is specific to his children of his own loins and the children of his sons. They cited the words of the Arab poet:

"Our sons are the sons of our sons, and our daughters' sons are the sons of other men."

[Ibn ʿAqil cited it in his commentary on Ibn Malik's Alfiyya, no. 51. In his version, "al-abaʿid" appears instead of "al-ajanib."]

Others said: The sons of daughters are also included in it, because it is established in Sahih al-Bukhari that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to al-Hasan ibn ʿAli: "This son of mine is a master, and perhaps Allah will reconcile through him between two great groups of the Muslims." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2704, from the hadith of Abu Bakrah, may Allah be pleased with him.] He called him "son," which shows that he is included among the sons.

Others said: This is a figurative usage (tajawwuz).

* *

His saying: ﴿And from their fathers, their descendants, and their brothers﴾ mentions their ancestors, their offspring, and their contemporaries, and that guidance and choosing included them all. Therefore He said: ﴿And We chose them and guided them to a straight path.﴾

Then He said: ﴿That is the guidance of Allah; He guides whom He wills of His servants.﴾ That is, this was attained by them only through Allah's success (tawfiq) and His guidance to them. ﴿But if they had associated others with Him, what they had been doing would have been worthless to them.﴾ This is an emphasis on the matter of shirk, a stern warning about its gravity, and a magnification of its seriousness, as He said: ﴿And it has already been revealed to you and to those before you: If you should associate others with Allah, your work will surely be nullified.﴾ [al-Zumar: 65] up to the end of the verse. This is a conditional statement, and a conditional does not imply that the condition occurs, as in His saying: ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first of the worshippers.﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 81], and His saying: ﴿Had We intended to take a diversion, We would have taken it from Our presence, if We were ever to do so.﴾ [al-Anbiya: 17], and His saying: ﴿Had Allah intended to take a son, He would have chosen from what He creates whatever He willed. Exalted is He; He is Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ [al-Zumar: 4].

* *

His saying: ﴿Those are the ones to whom We gave the Scripture, judgment, and prophethood.﴾ That is, We bestowed these favors on them as a mercy to the servants through them, and as kindness from Us to creation. ﴿But if these people disbelieve in them﴾ means: in the prophethood. It is also possible that the pronoun refers to these three things: the Scripture, the judgment, and the prophethood.

* *

His saying: ﴿these people﴾ means: the people of Makkah. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and al-Suddi. ﴿Then We have entrusted them to a people who are not disbelievers in them.﴾ That is: if those who disbelieve in these favors among the Quraysh and others among all the people of the earth, Arab and non-Arab, followers of religions and of scripture, disbelieve in them, then We have entrusted them to ﴿other﴾ people, meaning the Emigrants (Muhajirun), the Helpers (Ansar), and their followers until the Day of Resurrection, ﴿who are not disbelievers in them﴾. That is, they do not deny any part of them and do not reject even a single letter of them, but believe in all of them, the clear and the allegorical. May Allah make us among them by His grace, generosity, and kindness.

Then Allah, exalted, addressed His servant and Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, saying: ﴿Those﴾ means: the mentioned prophets together with those who were attributed to them of fathers, descendants, and brothers, who were of the same class (ashbah). ﴿Are the ones whom Allah guided.﴾ That is: they are the people of guidance, not others. ﴿So follow their guidance.﴾ That is: follow and adhere to it. Since this is a command to the Messenger ﷺ, his community follows him in what he legislates for them and commands them to do.

Al-Bukhari said regarding this verse: Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Hisham informed us that Ibn Jurayj informed them, saying: Sulayman al-Ahwal informed me that Mujahid informed him that he asked Ibn ʿAbbas: "Is there a prostration in (Surat Sad)?" He said: "Yes," then he recited ﴿And We gave him Isaac﴾ up to His saying: ﴿So follow their guidance﴾, then said: "He is among them." Yazid ibn Harun, Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd, and Sahl ibn Yusuf added, from al-ʿAwwam, from Mujahid, who said: "I said to Ibn ʿAbbas..." and he said: "Your Prophet ﷺ is among those whom he was commanded to follow." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4632.]

* *

His saying: ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any wage for it.﴾ That is: I do not seek from you any payment (ajr) for my conveying of this Qur'an to you, nor do I want anything from you. ﴿It is nothing but a reminder to the worlds.﴾ That is: they may be reminded by it and guided from blindness to guidance, from error to right direction, and from disbelief to faith.

He, the Exalted, says: "They did not magnify Allah with the magnification due to Him, when they denied His messengers sent to them." Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and 'Abdullah ibn Kathir said: it was revealed concerning the Quraysh. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) preferred this view. It was also said that it was revealed concerning a group of the Jews; and it was said that it concerned Finhas, a man among them; and it was said that it concerned Malik ibn al-Sayf.

﴿They said: "Allah has not sent down anything to a human being."﴾ The first view is the more apparent, because the verse is Meccan, and the Jews did not deny that books were sent down from heaven. The Quraysh, and the Arabs in general, found it strange that a messenger should be sent from among mankind, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Is it a wonder for the people that We revealed to a man from among them: "Warn the people, and give good news to those who believe that they have a sure standing with their Lord"?﴾ [Yunus: 2]. He also said: ﴿Nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them, except that they said: "Has Allah sent a human being as a messenger?" Say: "If there were angels walking securely on the earth, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger."﴾ [al-Isra: 94–95]. Here He said: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure when they said: "Allah has not sent down anything to a human being."﴾ Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: "Who sent down the Book which Musa brought, as a light and guidance for the people?"﴾ That is: say, O Muhammad, to these who deny that any book was sent down from Allah, in reply to their general negation, by affirming a particular affirmative proposition: ﴿Who sent down the Book which Musa brought?﴾ meaning the Torah, which you all know, and everyone knows, that Allah sent down to Musa son of 'Imran as a light and guidance for the people, that is, so that they might be illuminated by it in resolving difficulties, and be guided by it out of the darkness of doubts.

* *

His saying: ﴿You make it into scrolls, showing them and concealing much﴾ [[Ibn al-Jawzi said in Zad al-Masir (3/84): "Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read: 'yaj'alunahu fi qarativs yubdunaha' and 'yukhfun' with the letter ya' in them; Nafi', 'Asim, Ibn 'Amir, Hamzah and al-Kisai read with ta' in them." It appears that the Hafiz Ibn Kathir relied on the first reading.]] That is, they make it (the hamalah, i.e. its carriers, in one manuscript "jumlatuha") into scrolls, meaning pieces, which they write out from the original Book that is in their hands, altering in it what they alter, changing and interpreting it, and saying: ﴿This is from Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 79], that is, in His revealed Book, while it is not from Allah. Therefore He said: ﴿You make it into scrolls, showing them and concealing much.﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿And you were taught what you did not know, neither you nor your fathers﴾ That is: and (it was) He who sent down the Qur'an, in which Allah taught you the news of what came before and the account of what is to come, which you did not know, neither you nor your fathers.

Qatadah said: these are the polytheists of the Arabs. Mujahid said: this is addressed to the Muslims.

* *

His saying: ﴿Say: "Allah."﴾ 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn 'Abbas: that is, say: "Allah sent it down." What Ibn 'Abbas said is the definite meaning of this expression, not what some later scholars said, that the meaning of ﴿Say: "Allah"﴾ is that there is no address to them except this word, the word "Allah."

What this speaker said would amount to a command with a single word without any construction, and the use of a single word does not, in the language of the Arabs, convey a meaning on which it is good to remain silent.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then leave them in their plunging, playing﴾ That is: then leave them in their ignorance and error, playing, until the certainty comes to them from Allah. ﴿Then they will know﴾ whether the final outcome is theirs, or whether it belongs to the righteous servants of Allah.

* *

His saying: ﴿And this is a Book﴾ meaning the Qur'an, ﴿which We have sent down, blessed, confirming what is before it, and that you may warn the Mother of the Cities﴾ meaning Makkah, ﴿and those around it﴾ from the tribes of the Arabs and from all the other groups of the children of Adam, Arab and non-Arab. As He said in another verse: ﴿Say, O mankind, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you all﴾ [al-A'raf: 158]; and He said: ﴿That I may warn you by it, and whoever it reaches﴾ [al-An'am: 19]; and He said: ﴿And whoever among the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his appointed place﴾ [Hud: 17]; and He said: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant, that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [al-Furqan: 1]; and He said: ﴿And say to those who were given the Book and to the unlettered: "Have you submitted?" If they submit, then they are guided; but if they turn away, then upon you is only the conveying, and Allah is Seeing of the servants﴾ [Al 'Imran: 20].

It is established in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been given five things which none before me was given," and he mentioned among them: "A prophet was sent only to his own people, but I have been sent to all people." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (335) and Sahih Muslim, no. (521).]]

Therefore He said: ﴿Those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it﴾ That is: everyone who believes in Allah and the Last Day believes in this blessed Book which We have sent down to you, O Muhammad, which is the Qur'an. ﴿And they are upon their prayer, guarding﴾ That is: they perform what has been enjoined upon them of the prayers at their appointed times.

He, the Exalted, says: "They did not magnify Allah with the magnification due to Him, when they denied His messengers sent to them." Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and 'Abdullah ibn Kathir said: it was revealed concerning the Quraysh. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) preferred this view. It was also said that it was revealed concerning a group of the Jews; and it was said that it concerned Finhas, a man among them; and it was said that it concerned Malik ibn al-Sayf.

﴿They said: "Allah has not sent down anything to a human being."﴾ The first view is the more apparent, because the verse is Meccan, and the Jews did not deny that books were sent down from heaven. The Quraysh, and the Arabs in general, found it strange that a messenger should be sent from among mankind, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Is it a wonder for the people that We revealed to a man from among them: "Warn the people, and give good news to those who believe that they have a sure standing with their Lord"?﴾ [Yunus: 2]. He also said: ﴿Nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them, except that they said: "Has Allah sent a human being as a messenger?" Say: "If there were angels walking securely on the earth, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger."﴾ [al-Isra: 94–95]. Here He said: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure when they said: "Allah has not sent down anything to a human being."﴾ Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: "Who sent down the Book which Musa brought, as a light and guidance for the people?"﴾ That is: say, O Muhammad, to these who deny that any book was sent down from Allah, in reply to their general negation, by affirming a particular affirmative proposition: ﴿Who sent down the Book which Musa brought?﴾ meaning the Torah, which you all know, and everyone knows, that Allah sent down to Musa son of 'Imran as a light and guidance for the people, that is, so that they might be illuminated by it in resolving difficulties, and be guided by it out of the darkness of doubts.

* *

His saying: ﴿You make it into scrolls, showing them and concealing much﴾ [[Ibn al-Jawzi said in Zad al-Masir (3/84): "Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read: 'yaj'alunahu fi qarativs yubdunaha' and 'yukhfun' with the letter ya' in them; Nafi', 'Asim, Ibn 'Amir, Hamzah and al-Kisai read with ta' in them." It appears that the Hafiz Ibn Kathir relied on the first reading.]] That is, they make it (the hamalah, i.e. its carriers, in one manuscript "jumlatuha") into scrolls, meaning pieces, which they write out from the original Book that is in their hands, altering in it what they alter, changing and interpreting it, and saying: ﴿This is from Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 79], that is, in His revealed Book, while it is not from Allah. Therefore He said: ﴿You make it into scrolls, showing them and concealing much.﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿And you were taught what you did not know, neither you nor your fathers﴾ That is: and (it was) He who sent down the Qur'an, in which Allah taught you the news of what came before and the account of what is to come, which you did not know, neither you nor your fathers.

Qatadah said: these are the polytheists of the Arabs. Mujahid said: this is addressed to the Muslims.

* *

His saying: ﴿Say: "Allah."﴾ 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn 'Abbas: that is, say: "Allah sent it down." What Ibn 'Abbas said is the definite meaning of this expression, not what some later scholars said, that the meaning of ﴿Say: "Allah"﴾ is that there is no address to them except this word, the word "Allah."

What this speaker said would amount to a command with a single word without any construction, and the use of a single word does not, in the language of the Arabs, convey a meaning on which it is good to remain silent.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then leave them in their plunging, playing﴾ That is: then leave them in their ignorance and error, playing, until the certainty comes to them from Allah. ﴿Then they will know﴾ whether the final outcome is theirs, or whether it belongs to the righteous servants of Allah.

* *

His saying: ﴿And this is a Book﴾ meaning the Qur'an, ﴿which We have sent down, blessed, confirming what is before it, and that you may warn the Mother of the Cities﴾ meaning Makkah, ﴿and those around it﴾ from the tribes of the Arabs and from all the other groups of the children of Adam, Arab and non-Arab. As He said in another verse: ﴿Say, O mankind, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you all﴾ [al-A'raf: 158]; and He said: ﴿That I may warn you by it, and whoever it reaches﴾ [al-An'am: 19]; and He said: ﴿And whoever among the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his appointed place﴾ [Hud: 17]; and He said: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant, that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [al-Furqan: 1]; and He said: ﴿And say to those who were given the Book and to the unlettered: "Have you submitted?" If they submit, then they are guided; but if they turn away, then upon you is only the conveying, and Allah is Seeing of the servants﴾ [Al 'Imran: 20].

It is established in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been given five things which none before me was given," and he mentioned among them: "A prophet was sent only to his own people, but I have been sent to all people." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (335) and Sahih Muslim, no. (521).]]

Therefore He said: ﴿Those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it﴾ That is: everyone who believes in Allah and the Last Day believes in this blessed Book which We have sent down to you, O Muhammad, which is the Qur'an. ﴿And they are upon their prayer, guarding﴾ That is: they perform what has been enjoined upon them of the prayers at their appointed times.

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah be exalted: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah﴾, meaning: none is more unjust than one who lies about Allah, by ascribing to Him a partner or a son, or by claiming that Allah sent him to mankind when He had not sent him. For this reason He said: ﴿or says, "It has been revealed to me," when nothing has been revealed to him﴾.

ʿIkrimah and Qatadah said: it was revealed concerning Musaylimah the Liar [may Allah curse him] [[Addition from A.]].

﴿Or who says, "I will send down the like of what Allah has sent down"﴾, meaning: one who claims that he can match what has come from Allah as revelation, by fabricating words of his own, as He said: ﴿When Our verses are recited to them, they say, "We have heard. If we willed, we could say the like of this. This is nothing but the tales of the ancients"﴾ [al-Anfal: 31]. Allah said: ﴿If only you could see when the wrongdoers are in the agonies of death﴾, meaning: in its pangs, its throes and its distress, ﴿while the angels extend their hands﴾, meaning: to strike them, as He said: ﴿If you extend your hand against me to kill me, I shall not extend my hand against you to kill you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 28], up to the end of the verse, and He said: ﴿and they would extend against you their hands and their tongues with evil﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 2] up to the end of the verse.

Ad-Dahhak and Abu Salih said: ﴿extending their hands﴾ means with punishment. As He said [may He be exalted] [[Addition from M.]]: ﴿If only you could see when those who disbelieved are taken by the angels, who strike their faces and their backs﴾ [al-Anfal: 50]. For this reason He said: ﴿while the angels extend their hands﴾, meaning: striking them until their souls come out of their bodies. For this reason they say to them: ﴿Expel your souls﴾. When the disbeliever is at the point of death, the angels give him the good news of punishment, torment, shackles, chains, the Blazing Fire and boiling water, and the wrath of the Most Merciful. His soul then scatters through his body and refuses and resists coming out, so the angels strike them until their souls come out of their bodies, saying to them: ﴿Expel your souls. Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say about Allah other than the truth, and you used to be arrogant toward His verses﴾ [[Addition from M, A; in H: "the verse".]], meaning: today you will be humiliated to the utmost degree, just as you used to lie about Allah and be arrogant toward following His verses and submitting to His messengers.

Numerous hadiths (mutawatir, meaning widely transmitted, reports) have come concerning how the believer and the disbeliever die, and they are established under His saying: ﴿Allah makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾ [Ibrahim: 27].

Ibn Mardawayh mentioned here a very lengthy hadith, traced back to the Prophet (marfu'), through a strange chain, from ad-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas. Allah knows best [[Mentioned by as-Suyuti in ad-Durr al-Manthur (3/318), and he said: its chain is weak.]].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And you have come to Us alone, as We created you the first time﴾, meaning: it will be said to them on this day of their return: as He said, ﴿And they will be presented before your Lord in rows: "You have come to Us as We created you the first time"﴾ [al-Kahf: 48]. That is, as We originated you, We restore you. You used to deny this and consider it far-fetched. This is the Day of Resurrection.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And you have left behind what We bestowed upon you﴾, meaning: of the bounties and wealth that you acquired in the worldly abode, ﴿behind your backs﴾. It is established in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The son of Adam says, 'My wealth, my wealth.' Do you have any of your wealth except what you have eaten and consumed, or what you have worn and worn out, or what you have given in charity and sent forward? As for anything other than that, it will perish and you will leave it for the people."

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: the son of Adam will be brought on the Day of Resurrection like a stalk. Allah, may He be mighty and majestic, will say to him: "Where is what you gathered?" He will say: "My Lord, I gathered it and left it at its fullest." He will say: "Then where is what you sent forward for yourself?" He will not see that he sent forward anything. Then he recited this verse: ﴿And you have come to Us alone, as We created you the first time, and you have left behind what We bestowed upon you behind your backs﴾. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed were partners in regard to you﴾, this is a rebuke and reproach for them concerning the rivals, idols and images they took in the worldly abode, thinking that these would benefit them in their livelihood and in their return, if there is indeed a return. When the Day of Resurrection comes, the means will be severed, error will be dispelled, and what they used to invent will vanish from them. The Lord, mighty and majestic, will call out to them before all creation: ﴿Where are your partners whom you used to claim?﴾ [al-An'am: 22]. It will also be said to them: ﴿Where is what you used to worship besides Allah? Can they help you or help themselves?﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 92–93]. For this reason He said here: ﴿And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed were partners in regard to you﴾, meaning: in worship, that they have a share in deserving worship from you.

Then He said: ﴿Certainly, your bonds have been severed among you﴾. Thus Allah will show them their deeds as regrets for them, and they will not emerge from the Fire﴾ [al-Baqarah: 166–167]. He also said: ﴿And when the Horn is blown, there will be no kinship among them that Day, nor will they ask of one another﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 101]. He said: ﴿And it will be said, "Call upon your partners," so they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them﴾ [al-Qasas: 64] up to the end of the verse. He said [may He be exalted]: ﴿And on the Day We gather them all, then We will say to those who associated others with Allah...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and what they used to invent will be lost from them﴾ [al-An'am: 22–24]. The verses on this are very numerous.

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah be exalted: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah﴾, meaning: none is more unjust than one who lies about Allah, by ascribing to Him a partner or a son, or by claiming that Allah sent him to mankind when He had not sent him. For this reason He said: ﴿or says, "It has been revealed to me," when nothing has been revealed to him﴾.

ʿIkrimah and Qatadah said: it was revealed concerning Musaylimah the Liar [may Allah curse him] [[Addition from A.]].

﴿Or who says, "I will send down the like of what Allah has sent down"﴾, meaning: one who claims that he can match what has come from Allah as revelation, by fabricating words of his own, as He said: ﴿When Our verses are recited to them, they say, "We have heard. If we willed, we could say the like of this. This is nothing but the tales of the ancients"﴾ [al-Anfal: 31]. Allah said: ﴿If only you could see when the wrongdoers are in the agonies of death﴾, meaning: in its pangs, its throes and its distress, ﴿while the angels extend their hands﴾, meaning: to strike them, as He said: ﴿If you extend your hand against me to kill me, I shall not extend my hand against you to kill you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 28], up to the end of the verse, and He said: ﴿and they would extend against you their hands and their tongues with evil﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 2] up to the end of the verse.

Ad-Dahhak and Abu Salih said: ﴿extending their hands﴾ means with punishment. As He said [may He be exalted] [[Addition from M.]]: ﴿If only you could see when those who disbelieved are taken by the angels, who strike their faces and their backs﴾ [al-Anfal: 50]. For this reason He said: ﴿while the angels extend their hands﴾, meaning: striking them until their souls come out of their bodies. For this reason they say to them: ﴿Expel your souls﴾. When the disbeliever is at the point of death, the angels give him the good news of punishment, torment, shackles, chains, the Blazing Fire and boiling water, and the wrath of the Most Merciful. His soul then scatters through his body and refuses and resists coming out, so the angels strike them until their souls come out of their bodies, saying to them: ﴿Expel your souls. Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say about Allah other than the truth, and you used to be arrogant toward His verses﴾ [[Addition from M, A; in H: "the verse".]], meaning: today you will be humiliated to the utmost degree, just as you used to lie about Allah and be arrogant toward following His verses and submitting to His messengers.

Numerous hadiths (mutawatir, meaning widely transmitted, reports) have come concerning how the believer and the disbeliever die, and they are established under His saying: ﴿Allah makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾ [Ibrahim: 27].

Ibn Mardawayh mentioned here a very lengthy hadith, traced back to the Prophet (marfu'), through a strange chain, from ad-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas. Allah knows best [[Mentioned by as-Suyuti in ad-Durr al-Manthur (3/318), and he said: its chain is weak.]].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And you have come to Us alone, as We created you the first time﴾, meaning: it will be said to them on this day of their return: as He said, ﴿And they will be presented before your Lord in rows: "You have come to Us as We created you the first time"﴾ [al-Kahf: 48]. That is, as We originated you, We restore you. You used to deny this and consider it far-fetched. This is the Day of Resurrection.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And you have left behind what We bestowed upon you﴾, meaning: of the bounties and wealth that you acquired in the worldly abode, ﴿behind your backs﴾. It is established in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The son of Adam says, 'My wealth, my wealth.' Do you have any of your wealth except what you have eaten and consumed, or what you have worn and worn out, or what you have given in charity and sent forward? As for anything other than that, it will perish and you will leave it for the people."

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: the son of Adam will be brought on the Day of Resurrection like a stalk. Allah, may He be mighty and majestic, will say to him: "Where is what you gathered?" He will say: "My Lord, I gathered it and left it at its fullest." He will say: "Then where is what you sent forward for yourself?" He will not see that he sent forward anything. Then he recited this verse: ﴿And you have come to Us alone, as We created you the first time, and you have left behind what We bestowed upon you behind your backs﴾. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed were partners in regard to you﴾, this is a rebuke and reproach for them concerning the rivals, idols and images they took in the worldly abode, thinking that these would benefit them in their livelihood and in their return, if there is indeed a return. When the Day of Resurrection comes, the means will be severed, error will be dispelled, and what they used to invent will vanish from them. The Lord, mighty and majestic, will call out to them before all creation: ﴿Where are your partners whom you used to claim?﴾ [al-An'am: 22]. It will also be said to them: ﴿Where is what you used to worship besides Allah? Can they help you or help themselves?﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 92–93]. For this reason He said here: ﴿And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed were partners in regard to you﴾, meaning: in worship, that they have a share in deserving worship from you.

Then He said: ﴿Certainly, your bonds have been severed among you﴾. The verses on this are very numerous.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on Surah 6, verses 95–97:

He informs, exalted is He, that He is the Splitter of the grain and the date-stone (fāliq al-ḥabb wa'l-nawā), meaning: He splits them in the soil so that the crops grow in their varied kinds of grains, and the fruits grow from the date-stones in their varied shapes, colours and tastes. For this reason He explained ﴿the Splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾ with His saying ﴿He brings forth the living from the dead﴾, meaning: He brings forth the living plant from the grain and the date-stone, which is like the dead inanimate matter, as He said: ﴿And a sign for them is the dead earth. We give it life and bring forth from it grain, and from it they eat. And We made therein gardens of palm trees and grapes, and We caused springs to gush forth therein, that they may eat of its fruit, and their hands did not make it. Will they not then be grateful? Glory be to Him who created all the pairs, of what the earth produces, and of themselves, and of what they do not know﴾ [Yā-Sīn: 33–36].

* *

His saying ﴿and the One who brings forth the dead from the living﴾ is coordinated (ma'ṭūf) upon ﴿the Splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾; then He explained it, then He coordinated upon it His saying: ﴿and the One who brings forth the dead from the living﴾.

The scholars have expressed this with phrases that are all close in meaning and convey the same sense. Some say: He brings forth the chick from the egg and the egg from the chick. Others say: He brings forth the righteous child from the disbeliever, and the disbeliever from the righteous, and other such expressions that the verse encompasses and includes.

Then He said: ﴿That is Allah﴾, meaning: the doer of these things is Allah alone, without partner. ﴿So how are you turned away?﴾, meaning: how are you diverted from the truth and turned aside from it toward falsehood, so that you worship others alongside Allah?

* *

His saying ﴿He is the Splitter of the dawn, and has made the night for rest﴾ means: the Creator of light and darkness, as He said at the beginning of the surah: ﴿and made the darknesses and the light﴾. He, glorified is He, splits the darkness of the night to reveal the brightness of morning, so existence is illuminated, the horizon becomes bright, the darkness vanishes, the night departs with its beginnings and the shadow of its canopy, and the day arrives with its light and its radiance, as He said: ﴿He causes the night to cover the day, seeking it swiftly﴾ [al-A'rāf: 54]. Thus He showed His power to create opposing and differing things, which indicate the perfection of His greatness and the immensity of His dominion. He mentioned that He is the Splitter of the dawn and paired it with His saying: ﴿and made the night for rest﴾, meaning: still and dark, in which things are at rest, as He said: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā: 1–2], and He said: ﴿By the night when it covers, and by the day when it shines forth﴾ [al-Layl: 1–2], and He said: ﴿By the day when it reveals it, and by the night when it covers it﴾ [al-Shams: 3–4].

Ṣuhayb al-Rūmī (may Allah be pleased with him) said to his wife, when she reproached him for staying up late much of the night: "Indeed Allah has made the night for rest, except for Ṣuhayb. Indeed Ṣuhayb, when he remembers Paradise, his longing lengthens, and when he remembers the Fire, his sleep flies away." Narrated by Ibn Abī Ḥātim.

* *

His saying ﴿And the sun and the moon, as a reckoning﴾ means: they both run by a precise, measured calculation, which does not change or fluctuate. Rather, each of them has stations which it traverses in summer and winter, and from this results the variation of night and day in length and shortness, as He said: ﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light, and determined for it stations, that you might know the number of years and the reckoning﴾ [Yūnus: 5], and as He said: ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day; each is floating in an orbit﴾ [Yā-Sīn: 40], and He said: ﴿And the sun and the moon and the stars are subjected by His command﴾ [al-A'rāf: 54].

* *

His saying ﴿That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾ means: all of this proceeds by the decree of the Almighty, whom none can resist or oppose, the All-Knowing of everything, so that not even the weight of an atom in the earth or in the heaven escapes His knowledge. Often when Allah, exalted is He, mentions the creation of night, day, the sun and the moon, He concludes the statement with might and knowledge, as He mentions in this verse, and as in His saying: ﴿And a sign for them is the night: We strip from it the day, and behold, they are in darkness. And the sun runs on to a resting place for it; that is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [Yā-Sīn: 37–38].

When He mentioned the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is in them at the beginning of the surah Ḥā Mīm al-Sajda, He said: ﴿And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and as a guard. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 12].

* *

His saying ﴿And it is He who has placed for you the stars, that you may be guided by them in the darknesses of the land and the sea﴾: some of the early scholars (salaf) said: whoever believes that these stars have any purpose other than three has erred and lied against Allah. Allah made them an adornment for the sky, missiles against the devils, and a means by which one is guided in the darknesses of land and sea.

* *

His saying ﴿We have detailed the signs﴾ means: We have made them clear and explained them ﴿for a people who know﴾, meaning: who understand, recognise the truth, and avoid falsehood.

Allah says: ﴿And it is He who produced you from a single soul﴾, meaning Adam, peace be upon him, as He said: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women﴾ [An-Nisa: 1].

* *

Regarding His saying ﴿then a place of stability﴾, the scholars differed over its meaning. From Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, Qays ibn Abi Hazim, Mujahid, 'Ata', Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and 'Ata' al-Khurasani: ﴿then a place of stability﴾ means in the wombs, and they said (or most of them said): ﴿and a place of storage﴾ means in the loins.

From Ibn Mas'ud and a group, the reverse of this is related. Also from Ibn Mas'ud and a group: ﴿a place of stability﴾ is in this world, and ﴿a place of storage﴾ is where one dies. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿a place of stability﴾ is in the wombs and on the surface of the earth, and where one dies. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: the place of stability is that in which one has died, so that his deeds have settled with him. From Ibn Mas'ud: the place of storage is in the Hereafter.

The first opinion is the most apparent, and Allah knows best.

* *

Regarding His saying ﴿We have detailed the signs for a people who understand﴾, meaning: who comprehend and grasp the words of Allah and their meaning.

* *

Regarding His saying ﴿And it is He who sends down water from the sky﴾, meaning by measure, blessed, as provision for the servants and relief for creation, a mercy from Allah to His creatures. ﴿Then We produce by it the growth of all things﴾, as He said: ﴿And We made from water every living thing﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 30]. ﴿Then We bring forth from it green (vegetation)﴾, meaning crops and green trees. Then after that He creates in it the grain and the fruit; therefore He said: ﴿We bring forth from it grain arranged in layers﴾, meaning one part piled upon another, like ears of grain and the like. ﴿And from the palm trees, from its spathe, clusters hanging low﴾, meaning qinwan is the plural of qinw, which are the bunches of ripe dates, ﴿hanging low﴾, meaning near to the reach. As 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah al-Walibi related from Ibn Abbas: ﴿qinwan daniyah﴾, by the hanging low clusters he meant the short palm trees whose bunches cling to the ground. Related by Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Jarir said: The people of the Hijaz say qinwan, while the Qays say qunwan, and Imru' al-Qays said:

"Its upper parts were cut off and its roots were uprooted, and a red cluster of unripe dates bent down."

He said: and the Tamim say qinyan with a ya', and it is the plural of qinw, just as sinwan is the plural of sinw.

* *

Regarding His saying ﴿And gardens of grapevines﴾, meaning: and We bring forth from it gardens of grapevines. These two kinds are the most noble among the people of the Hijaz, and perhaps they are the finest of fruits in this world, as Allah has bestowed favour upon His servants through them, in His saying: ﴿And from the fruits of the date palm and grapevines you take from them intoxicant and good provision﴾ [An-Nahl: 67]. That was before the prohibition of wine.

And He said: ﴿And We made in it gardens of date palms and grapevines﴾ [Ya-Sin: 34].

* *

Regarding His saying ﴿And the olive and the pomegranate, similar and dissimilar﴾, Qatadah and others said: they resemble one another in their leaves, close in form, one to another, and differ in their fruits in shape, taste and nature.

* *

Regarding His saying ﴿Look at its fruit when it bears fruit and at its ripening﴾, meaning its maturity. This was said by al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, al-Suddi, Qatadah and others. That is: reflect on the power of its Creator, from non-existence to existence, after it was firewood it became grapes, dates and other things, of the colours, shapes, tastes and fragrances that Allah, exalted is He, created, as He said: ﴿And on the earth are adjoining tracts, and gardens of grapevines, and crops, and palm trees, some with multiple trunks and some with single trunks, irrigated with one water, yet We make some of them exceed others in fruit. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 4]. Therefore He said here: ﴿Indeed in that are signs﴾, meaning proofs of the perfection of the power, wisdom and mercy of the Creator of these things, ﴿for a people who believe﴾, meaning who affirm Him and follow His messengers.

Allah says: ﴿And it is He who produced you from a single soul﴾, meaning Adam, peace be upon him, as He said: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women﴾ [An-Nisa: 1].

* *

Regarding His saying ﴿then a place of stability﴾, the scholars differed over its meaning. From Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, Qays ibn Abi Hazim, Mujahid, 'Ata', Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and 'Ata' al-Khurasani: ﴿then a place of stability﴾ means in the wombs, and they said (or most of them said): ﴿and a place of storage﴾ means in the loins.

From Ibn Mas'ud and a group, the reverse of this is related. Also from Ibn Mas'ud and a group: ﴿a place of stability﴾ is in this world, and ﴿a place of storage﴾ is where one dies. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿a place of stability﴾ is in the wombs and on the surface of the earth, and where one dies. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: the place of stability is that in which one has died, so that his deeds have settled with him. From Ibn Mas'ud: the place of storage is in the Hereafter.

The first opinion is the most apparent, and Allah knows best.

* *

Regarding His saying ﴿We have detailed the signs for a people who understand﴾, meaning: who comprehend and grasp the words of Allah and their meaning.

* *
