This is a refutation of the polytheists who worshipped others besides Allah, and who associated with Allah in worship by worshipping the jinn, making them partners of Allah in worship. Exalted is Allah above their shirk and their disbelief.

If it is said: how were the jinn worshipped, when they [the polytheists] were only worshipping idols? The answer: they only worshipped the idols out of obedience to the jinn and their commanding them to do so, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female deities, and they invoke none but a rebellious Satan. Allah has cursed him, and he said: "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion. And I will mislead them, and I will arouse in them desires, and I will order them so they will slit the ears of cattle, and I will order them so they will change the creation of Allah." And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah has certainly suffered a clear loss. He promises them and arouses desires in them, but Satan promises them only delusion﴾ [An-Nisa: 117-120]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Then do you take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me, while they are enemies to you? Wretched is the exchange for the wrongdoers [a substitute].﴾ [Al-Kahf: 50]. And Ibrahim said to his father: ﴿O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed, Satan has been disobedient to the Most Merciful﴾ [Maryam: 44]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy. And that you worship Me; this is the straight path﴾ [Ya-Sin: 60-61]. And the angels will say on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Exalted are You! You are our Protector, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them﴾ [Saba: 41]. For this reason, He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they made the jinn partners with Allah, though He created them﴾, meaning: while He had created them. He alone is the Creator, with no partner, so how can anything be worshipped along with Him? As Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: ﴿Do you worship what you carve? While Allah created you and what you make﴾ [As-Saffat: 95-96].

The meaning of the verse: He, glorified and exalted, is the sole Originator of creation; therefore He alone must be singled out for worship, with no partner.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they attribute to Him sons and daughters without knowledge﴾ draws attention to the error of those who went astray in describing Him, exalted is He, as having a son, as the Jews claim concerning Uzair, and as those among the Christians claim concerning the Messiah, and as the Arab polytheists said concerning the angels: that they are daughters of Allah. Exalted is Allah far above what they say, a great exaltation.

The meaning of His saying ﴿wakharaqu﴾ (and they fabricated) is: they invented, forged, lied and fabricated, as the scholars of the early generations said. ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿wakharaqu﴾ means: they conjectured falsely.

Al-ʿAwfi narrated from him: ﴿And they attribute to Him sons and daughters without knowledge﴾, he said: they made for Him sons and daughters. Mujahid said: ﴿And they attribute to Him sons and daughters﴾, he said: they lied. Likewise said al-Hasan. Al-Dahhak said: they fabricated; al-Suddi said: they cut off.

Ibn Jarir said: the meaning of the speech, then, is: and they made the jinn partners with Allah in their worship of Him, while He alone created them, without partner or helper. ﴿And they attributed to Him sons and daughters﴾, meaning: they fabricated lies about Allah, inventing for Him sons and daughters without knowledge of the reality of what they say, but out of ignorance of Allah and His greatness, and that it is not fitting, if He is God, that He should have sons, daughters or a consort, nor that anyone should share in His creation as a partner.

For this reason He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Glorified and exalted is He above what they describe﴾, meaning: He is sanctified, free from, and magnified above what these ignorant and misguided people describe of children, equals, peers and partners.

﴿The Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾: that is, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, their Creator and their Producer, who brought them into being without any prior model, as Mujahid and al-Suddi said. From this word the innovation (bid'ah) is so called, because there is no precedent for it in what came before.

﴿How can He have a child when He has no companion?﴾ That is, how could He have a child when He has no wife? A child comes into being only from two mutually compatible things, and Allah has no compatibility with anything of His creation and nothing of His creation resembles Him, because He is the Creator of everything. So He has neither a companion nor a child. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." You have indeed brought forth a monstrous thing. The heavens are almost torn apart from it, the earth is split open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son. It is not befitting the Most Merciful that He should take a son. There is none in the heavens and the earth but comes to the Most Merciful as a servant. He has counted them and enumerated them with exact counting. And each of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone﴾ [Maryam: 88-95].

﴿And He created all things, and He is Knowing of all things﴾: Here Allah the Exalted makes clear that He is the One who created everything and that He has knowledge of everything. How then could He have a companion from among His creation who is compatible with Him? He is the One who has no equal, so how could He have a child? Exalted is Allah above that, far exalted.

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾, meaning: the One who created everything, who has no offspring and no consort, ﴿there is no god except Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him﴾, so worship Him alone, with no partner. Acknowledge His oneness, that there is no god but Him, that He has no son and no father, and no consort, no like and no equal. ﴿And He is Disposer of all things﴾, meaning: the Guardian and Watcher who manages everything other than Himself, provides for them, and protects them by night and by day.

* *

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿No vision can grasp Him﴾, the scholars of the early generations have several statements about it.

The first: it means that He cannot be grasped by vision in this world, though they will see Him in the Hereafter, as the reports have been transmitted by mass narration (tawatur) from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) through multiple chains that are established in the Sahih collections, the Musnads and the Sunan. Masruq narrated from Aisha that she said: "Whoever claims that Muhammad saw his Lord has lied. [In another narration: against Allah.] For Allah says: ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision.﴾"

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, from Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq. Others narrated it from Masruq as well, and it is established in the Sahih and elsewhere from Aisha through more than one route.[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (4612), Muslim in his Sahih, no. (177), and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (3068), through al-Sha'bi, from Masruq.]]

Ibn Abbas differed with her: from him there is an unrestricted affirmation of vision, and also a report that he saw Him with his heart twice. The matter is discussed at the beginning of Surat al-Najm, Allah willing.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Muslim mentioned to us, Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi related to us, Yahya ibn Ma'in related to us, saying: I heard Isma'il ibn Ulayyah say concerning the saying of Allah, ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision﴾: "This is in this world." He said: My father mentioned, from Hisham ibn Ubayd Allah, that he said something similar.

Others said: ﴿No vision can grasp Him﴾ means all vision. This is specified by what is established regarding the believers seeing Him in the Hereafter.

Others, from the Mu'tazilah, following what they understood from the verse, said: He is not seen in this world or in the Hereafter. They opposed the people of the Sunnah and the community in this, along with their ignorance of what the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger indicate. As for the Book, there is His saying: ﴿Faces that day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 22-23], and His saying about the disbelievers: ﴿No indeed; they will be veiled from their Lord that day﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 15].

Imam al-Shafi'i said: This indicates that the believers will not be veiled from Him, blessed and exalted is He.

As for the Sunnah, reports have been transmitted by mass narration from Abu Sa'id, Abu Hurairah, Anas, Jarir, Suhayb, Bilal and many other Companions from the Prophet (ﷺ) that the believers will see Allah in the Hereafter, on the plains of judgment and in the gardens of Paradise. May Allah make us among them by His bounty and generosity. Amin.

It was also said: what is meant by His saying ﴿No vision can grasp Him﴾ is that no intellects can grasp Him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from al-Fallas, from Ibn Mahdi, from Abu al-Husayn Yahya ibn al-Husayn, the reciter of the people of Makkah, that he said this. This is very strange and contrary to the apparent meaning of the verse, and it seems he took "idrak" to mean "ru'yah" (seeing). And Allah knows best.

Others said: there is no contradiction between affirming vision and negating idrak (grasping), for idrak is more specific than ru'yah, and negating the more specific does not necessitate negating the more general. Then these scholars differed about what the negated idrak is. It was said: it is knowing the reality (haqiqah), for no one knows this except Him, even if the believers see Him, just as one who sees the moon does not grasp its reality, its essence and its nature. The Mighty is more deserving of this, and to Him belongs the highest likeness.

Others said: what is meant by idrak is ihatah (encompassing). They said: the absence of encompassment does not necessitate the absence of seeing, just as the absence of encompassing knowledge does not necessitate the absence of knowledge. Allah says: ﴿and they cannot encompass Him in knowledge﴾ [Ta-Ha: 110]. In Sahih Muslim: "I cannot count praise of You; You are as You have praised Yourself" [Sahih Muslim, no. (486), from the hadith of Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her]. Yet this does not necessitate the absence of praise, and likewise here.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision﴾: he said: No one's sight encompasses the King.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah related to us, Amr ibn Hammad ibn Talhah al-Qannad related to us, Asbat related to us, from Simak, from Ikrimah, that he was asked: ﴿No vision can grasp Him﴾? He said: "Do you not see the sky?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you see all of it?"

Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah narrated from Qatadah: ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision﴾: He is greater than that vision can grasp Him.

Ibn Jarir said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam related to us, Khalid ibn Abd al-Rahman related to us, Abu Arfajah related to us, from Ata al-Awfi concerning His saying ﴿Faces that day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾: he said: They look at Allah; their sight does not encompass Him because of His greatness, while His sight encompasses them. That is His saying: ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision.﴾

A hadith has been reported concerning the interpretation of this verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it here, saying:

Abu Zur'ah related to us, Minjab ibn al-Harith al-Sahmi [in M: al-Tamimi] related to us, Bishr ibn Imarah related to us, from Abu Rawq, from Ata al-Awfi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning His saying: ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision﴾, he said: "If the jinn, mankind, the devils and the angels, from the time they were created until they perish, were lined up in a single row, they would never encompass Allah."

Strange; it is not known except through this route, and none of the authors of the Six Books narrated it. [Ibn Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (2/10) through Sufyan ibn Bishr, from Bishr ibn Imarah, and its chain is weak.] And Allah knows best.

Others said concerning His saying ﴿No vision can grasp Him﴾, based on what al-Tirmidhi narrated in his Jami', Ibn Abi Asim in his book al-Sunnah, Ibn Abi Hatim in his Tafsir, Ibn Mardawayh also, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of al-Hakam ibn Aban, who said: I heard Ikrimah say: I heard Ibn Abbas say: "Muhammad saw his Lord, blessed and exalted is He." I said: Does Allah not say: ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision﴾ and so on? He said to me: "May your mother be bereaved! That is His light, which is His light. When He manifests Himself with His light, nothing can grasp Him." In another narration: "Nothing can stand before Him."

Al-Hakim said: Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3279); al-Sunnah of Ibn Abi Asim, no. (437); al-Mustadrak (2/306). Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib." Ibn Abi Asim said: "There is discussion about it."]

Corresponding in meaning to this report is what is established in the two Sahihs from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah does not sleep, and it is not fitting for Him to sleep. He lowers the scale and raises it. The deeds of the night are raised to Him before the deeds of the day, and the deeds of the day before the deeds of the night. His veil is light, or fire; if He were to uncover it, the glories of His Face would burn away whatever of His creation His sight reaches." [Sahih Muslim, no. (179). I have not found it in Sahih al-Bukhari after searching; even al-Hafiz al-Mizzi did not mention it in Tuhfat al-Ashraf from al-Bukhari's narration.]

In the earlier scriptures: when Musa asked for vision, Allah said to him: "O Musa, no living thing sees Me except that it dies, and no dry thing except that it crumbles." That is, it collapses. And He, Exalted, said: ﴿When his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble to dust, and Musa fell down unconscious. When he recovered, he said: Glory be to You, I have turned to You in repentance, and I am the first of the believers﴾ [al-A'raf: 143]. Negating this particular grasping does not negate seeing on the Day of Resurrection, when He manifests Himself to His believing servants as He wills. As for His majesty and greatness as He truly is, exalted, sanctified and far above all deficiency, ﴿no vision can grasp Him﴾. For this reason Mother of the Believers Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, affirmed seeing in the Hereafter and negated it in this world, citing this verse: ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision.﴾ So what she negated is grasping in the sense of seeing His greatness and majesty as He is, for that is impossible for humans, for angels, and for anything else.[[See Sharh al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah (1/214) of Ibn Abi al-'Izz al-Hanafi for an extensive discussion of vision.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿But He grasps all vision﴾, meaning: He encompasses them and knows them as they truly are, because He created them, as He says: ﴿Should not He who created know? And He is the Subtle, the Acquainted﴾ [al-Mulk: 14].

It may be that by "vision" He means those who see, as al-Suddi said concerning His saying: ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision﴾: nothing sees Him, while He sees all creation.

Abu al-'Aliyah said concerning His saying ﴿And He is the Subtle, the Acquainted﴾: Subtle in extracting them, Acquainted with their place. And Allah knows best.

This is like His saying, relating the words of Luqman in his advice to his son: ﴿O my son, indeed if it is the weight of a mustard seed and should be within a rock or in the heavens or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth. Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted﴾ [Luqman: 16].

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾, meaning: the One who created everything, who has no offspring and no consort, ﴿there is no god except Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him﴾, so worship Him alone, with no partner. Acknowledge His oneness, that there is no god but Him, that He has no son and no father, and no consort, no like and no equal. ﴿And He is Disposer of all things﴾, meaning: the Guardian and Watcher who manages everything other than Himself, provides for them, and protects them by night and by day.

Allah says: ﴿and they cannot encompass Him in knowledge﴾ [Ta-Ha: 110]. In Sahih Muslim: "I cannot count praise of You; You are as You have praised Yourself" [Sahih Muslim, no. (486), from the hadith of Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her]. Yet this does not necessitate the absence of praise, and likewise here.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision﴾: he said: No one's sight encompasses the King.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah related to us, Amr ibn Hammad ibn Talhah al-Qannad related to us, Asbat related to us, from Simak, from Ikrimah, that he was asked: ﴿No vision can grasp Him﴾? He said: "Do you not see the sky?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you see all of it?"

Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah narrated from Qatadah: ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision﴾: He is greater than that vision can grasp Him.

Ibn Jarir said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam related to us, Khalid ibn Abd al-Rahman related to us, Abu Arfajah related to us, from Ata al-Awfi concerning His saying ﴿Faces that day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾: he said: They look at Allah; their sight does not encompass Him because of His greatness, while His sight encompasses them. That is His saying: ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision.﴾

A hadith has been reported concerning the interpretation of this verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it here, saying:

Abu Zur'ah related to us, Minjab ibn al-Harith al-Sahmi [in M: al-Tamimi] related to us, Bishr ibn Imarah related to us, from Abu Rawq, from Ata al-Awfi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning His saying: ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision﴾, he said: "If the jinn, mankind, the devils and the angels, from the time they were created until they perish, were lined up in a single row, they would never encompass Allah."

Strange; it is not known except through this route, and none of the authors of the Six Books narrated it. [Ibn Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (2/10) through Sufyan ibn Bishr, from Bishr ibn Imarah, and its chain is weak.] And Allah knows best.

Others said concerning His saying ﴿No vision can grasp Him﴾, based on what al-Tirmidhi narrated in his Jami', Ibn Abi Asim in his book al-Sunnah, Ibn Abi Hatim in his Tafsir, Ibn Mardawayh also, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of al-Hakam ibn Aban, who said: I heard Ikrimah say: I heard Ibn Abbas say: "Muhammad saw his Lord, blessed and exalted is He." I said: Does Allah not say: ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision﴾ and so on? He said to me: "May your mother be bereaved! That is His light, which is His light. When He manifests Himself with His light, nothing can grasp Him." In another narration: "Nothing can stand before Him."

Al-Hakim said: Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3279); al-Sunnah of Ibn Abi Asim, no. (437); al-Mustadrak (2/306). Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib." Ibn Abi Asim said: "There is discussion about it."]

Corresponding in meaning to this report is what is established in the two Sahihs from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah does not sleep, and it is not fitting for Him to sleep. He lowers the scale and raises it. The deeds of the night are raised to Him before the deeds of the day, and the deeds of the day before the deeds of the night. His veil is light, or fire; if He were to uncover it, the glories of His Face would burn away whatever of His creation His sight reaches." [Sahih Muslim, no. (179). I have not found it in Sahih al-Bukhari after searching; even al-Hafiz al-Mizzi did not mention it in Tuhfat al-Ashraf from al-Bukhari's narration.]

In the earlier scriptures: when Musa asked for vision, Allah said to him: "O Musa, no living thing sees Me except that it dies, and no dry thing except that it crumbles." That is, it collapses. And He, Exalted, said: ﴿When his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble to dust, and Musa fell down unconscious. When he recovered, he said: Glory be to You, I have turned to You in repentance, and I am the first of the believers﴾ [al-A'raf: 143]. Negating this particular grasping does not negate seeing on the Day of Resurrection, when He manifests Himself to His believing servants as He wills. As for His majesty and greatness as He truly is, exalted, sanctified and far above all deficiency, ﴿no vision can grasp Him﴾. For this reason Mother of the Believers Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, affirmed seeing in the Hereafter and negated it in this world, citing this verse: ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision.﴾ So what she negated is grasping in the sense of seeing His greatness and majesty as He is, for that is impossible for humans, for angels, and for anything else.[[See Sharh al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah (1/214) of Ibn Abi al-'Izz al-Hanafi for an extensive discussion of vision.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿But He grasps all vision﴾, meaning: He encompasses them and knows them as they truly are, because He created them, as He says: ﴿Should not He who created know? And He is the Subtle, the Acquainted﴾ [al-Mulk: 14].

It may be that by "vision" He means those who see, as al-Suddi said concerning His saying: ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision﴾: nothing sees Him, while He sees all creation.

Abu al-'Aliyah said concerning His saying ﴿And He is the Subtle, the Acquainted﴾: Subtle in extracting them, Acquainted with their place. And Allah knows best.

This is like His saying, relating the words of Luqman in his advice to his son: ﴿O my son, indeed if it is the weight of a mustard seed and should be within a rock or in the heavens or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth. Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted﴾ [Luqman: 16].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verse 104–105:

Al-Basa'ir (insights, proofs): these are the clear proofs and arguments contained in the Qur'an and what the Messenger (ﷺ) brought. ﴿Whoever sees, it is for his own self﴾, like His saying: ﴿Whoever is guided, is only guided for his own self, and whoever goes astray, only goes astray to its detriment﴾ [al-Isra: 15]. Therefore He said: ﴿And whoever is blind, it is against himself﴾, when He mentioned the insights, He said:

﴿And whoever is blind, it is against himself﴾, meaning: the burden of that returns only upon him, like His saying: ﴿For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blind, but it is the hearts within the breasts that are blind﴾ [al-Hajj: 46].

﴿And I am not a guardian over you﴾, meaning: not a watcher or a keeper. Rather, I am only a conveyor (of the message), and Allah guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills.

* *

His saying: ﴿And thus We detail the verses﴾, meaning: just as We have explained the verses in this surah, concerning the clarification of monotheism and that there is no god but Him, thus do We make the verses clear, explain them and manifest them in every setting, due to the ignorance of the ignorant, and so that the polytheists and the disbelieving deniers may say: "You have studied (darasta), O Muhammad, with those before you from the People of the Book, and you have recited to them and learned from them."

Thus said Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, and others.

Al-Tabarani said: Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Amr ibn Kaysan, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas read: ﴿darasta﴾ as "you recited (talawta), you disputed (khasamta), you argued (jadalta)" [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (11/137). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/22): "its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat)"].

This is as He, the Exalted, said, informing of their lying and obstinacy: ﴿And those who disbelieve say: "This is nothing but a fabrication he has invented, and others have helped him with it." Indeed, they have produced an injustice and a falsehood. And they say: "Tales of the ancients, which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening"﴾ [al-Furqan: 4, 5]. And He, the Exalted, said, informing of their leader and his lying: ﴿Indeed, he thought and calculated. So may he be destroyed, how he calculated! Then may he be destroyed, how he calculated! Then he looked. Then he frowned and scowled. Then he turned away and was arrogant. And he said, "This is nothing but magic transmitted. This is but the speech of a human being"﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 18–25].

* *

His saying: ﴿And that We may make it clear to a people who know﴾, meaning: and that We may make it clear to a people who know the truth so they follow it, and falsehood so they avoid it. For Allah, the Exalted, there is perfect wisdom in misguiding those, and in clarifying the truth for these. As He, the Exalted, said: ﴿He misleads many by it and guides many by it, and He misleads by it none except the defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Baqarah: 26]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿That He may make what Satan throws in a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease and whose hearts are hardened, and indeed the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension﴾ [al-Hajj: 53]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We have not made the companions of the Fire except angels, and We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve, that those who were given the Scripture may be certain and those who believe may increase in faith, and those who were given the Scripture and the believers will not doubt, and that those in whose hearts is disease and the disbelievers may say, "What does Allah intend by this as an example?" Thus does Allah leave astray whom He wills and guide whom He wills. And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 31].

And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is healing and mercy for the believers, and it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss﴾ [al-Isra: 82]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say, "It is for those who believe a guidance and healing. And those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is blindness for them. Those are being called from a distant place"﴾ [Fussilat: 44], and other verses indicating that He, the Exalted, sent down the Qur'an as guidance for the God-fearing, and that He misleads by it whom He wills and guides by it whom He wills. Therefore He said here: ﴿And thus We detail the verses, and that they may say, "You have studied," and that We may make it clear to a people who know﴾. Some of them read: ﴿and that they may say, "You have studied (darasta)"﴾.

Al-Tamimi said, from Ibn Abbas: "darasta" means: you recited and learned. Likewise said Mujahid, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam.

Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, that al-Hasan said: "wa liyaqulu darasat", meaning: it has grown old and been effaced. Abd al-Razzaq also said: Ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Amr ibn Dinar, who said: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr say: "Indeed, our children read here 'darasat' (with a feminine ending), but it is only 'darasta'."

Shu'bah said: Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani narrated to us, who said regarding the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "darasat" without an alif, with a fatha on the sin and a pause on the ta.

Ibn Jarir said: its meaning is: it has been effaced and has grown old, i.e., this which you recite to us has passed by us long ago, and its time has become long.

Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah said, from Qatadah, that he read it: "durisat", meaning: it was recited and taught.

Ma'mar said, from Qatadah: "durisat": it was recited. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is "darasa".

Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam said: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun, who said: it is in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Ibn Mas'ud: "wa liyaqulu daras." He said: they mean the Prophet (ﷺ), that he had studied (qara'a).

This is unusual (gharib), for there is narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b something contrary to this. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn al-Layth narrated to us, Abu Salamah narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abi Bazzah al-Makki narrated to us, Wahb ibn Zam'ah narrated to us, from his father, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught me: ﴿wa liyaqulu darasta﴾.

Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Wahb ibn Zam'ah, and said: meaning with the sin sukun and the ta fatha. Then he said: its chain is sahih, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it.

Allah says, commanding His Messenger ﷺ and whoever follows his way: ﴿Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾, meaning: take him as your model, follow his footsteps, and act upon it, for what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth about which there is no doubt, because there is no god but Him.

﴿And turn away from the polytheists﴾, meaning: pardon them, overlook (their wrongs), and bear with their harm, until Allah grants you victory, helps you, and makes you prevail over them.

And know that Allah has a wisdom in their being led astray, for if He willed, He would have guided all people together [and if Allah had willed, He would have united them upon guidance].

﴿And if Allah had willed, they would not have associated others with Him﴾, meaning: rather, to Him belongs the will and the wisdom in what He wills and chooses. He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We have not made you a guardian over them﴾, meaning: a keeper who preserves their deeds and their words. ﴿Nor are you a manager over them﴾, meaning: one appointed to take charge of their provisions and affairs. ﴿Your duty is only to convey (the message)﴾, as Allah says: ﴿So remind, for you are only a reminder. You are not over them a controller﴾ [Al-Ghashiyah: 21, 22], and He says: ﴿Upon you is only the conveyance (of the message), and upon Us is the account﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 40].

You are not over them a controller﴾ [Al-Ghashiyah: 21, 22], and He says: ﴿Upon you is only the conveyance (of the message), and upon Us is the account﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 40].

Allah, the Exalted, says, forbidding His Messenger (ﷺ) and the believers from reviling the gods of the polytheists. Even though there may be a benefit in it, it would lead to a greater harm, namely the polytheists responding by reviling the God of the believers, who is Allah, there is no god but Him.

As ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding this verse: They said, "O Muhammad, either you stop reviling our gods, or we will revile your Lord." So Allah forbade them to revile their idols, ﴿lest they revile Allah in enmity without knowledge﴾.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq said, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah: The Muslims used to revile the idols of the disbelievers, and the disbelievers would then revile Allah in enmity without knowledge. So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not revile those whom they invoke besides Allah﴾.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi that he said in the tafsir (exegesis) of this verse: When the death of Abu Talib approached, the Quraysh said, "Come, let us go in to this man and ask him to forbid his nephew from us, for we are ashamed to kill him after his death, lest the Arabs say, 'He used to protect them, and when he died they killed him.'" So Abu Sufyan, Abu Jahl, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Umayyah and Ubayy, the two sons of Khalaf, ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt, ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs, and al-Aswad ibn al-Bakhtari set out. [In manuscript M: "ʿAbd Yaghuth."] They sent a man from among them called "al-Muttalib," and said, "Ask permission for us to enter upon Abu Talib." He went to Abu Talib and said, "These are the elders of your people who wish to enter upon you." So he permitted them to enter upon him. They entered and said, "O Abu Talib, you are our senior and our master, and Muhammad has harmed us and harmed our gods. We want you to call him and forbid him from mentioning our gods, and we will leave him and his God alone." So he called him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) came. Abu Talib said to him, "These are your people and the sons of your paternal uncle." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "What do you want?" They said, "We want you to leave us and our gods, and we will leave you and your God." Abu Talib said to him, "Your people have treated you fairly, so accept from them." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Tell me, if I give you this, will you give me one word which, if you say it, you will rule the Arabs by it, and the non-Arabs (ʿajam) will submit to you by it, and they will pay you the tribute (kharaj)?" Abu Jahl said, "By your father, we will give you that and ten times as much." He said, "What is it?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Say: There is no god but Allah." But they refused and recoiled. Abu Talib said, "O my nephew, say something else, for your people have been alarmed by it." He said, "O uncle, I will not say anything else, even if they bring the sun and place it in my hand; even if they brought the sun and placed it in my hand, I would not say anything other than it." He intended by this to despair them. They became angry and said, "You must desist from reviling our gods, or we will revile you and revile whoever commands you." So this is His statement: ﴿so that they revile Allah in enmity without knowledge﴾. [Tafsir al-Tabari (12/34).]

From this category, which is abandoning a benefit for the sake of a greater harm, is what has come in the Sahih: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Cursed is one who reviles his parents." They said, "O Messenger of Allah, how can a man revile his parents?" He said, "He reviles the father of a man, so he reviles his father, and he reviles his mother, so he reviles his mother." Or as he said, peace be upon him. [Related by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (90), from the hadith of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs, may Allah be pleased with him.]

* *

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿Thus We have made attractive to every nation its deeds﴾ means: Just as We made attractive to these people the love of their idols, their defense of them, and their support for them, so too We made attractive to every nation of the past their deeds in which they were engaged in error. And to Allah belongs the conclusive proof and the perfect wisdom in what He wills and chooses. ﴿Then to their Lord is their return﴾ means: their final return and their destination, ﴿and He will inform them of what they used to do﴾ means: He will recompense them for their deeds; if it was good, then good, and if it was evil, then evil.

The commentary is on surah 6, verses 109–110.

Allah, the Exalted, says, reporting about the polytheists: they swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths, that is, they swore solemn oaths, ﴿If a sign comes to them﴾, that is, a miracle or an extraordinary event, ﴿they will surely believe in it﴾, that is, they will surely affirm it. ﴿Say: Indeed, the signs are with Allah﴾, that is, say, O Muhammad, to those who ask you for signs out of obstinacy, disbelief and stubbornness, not seeking guidance or right direction: the matter of these signs returns only to Allah. If He wills, He answers you, and if He wills, He leaves you, as He said. Ibn Jarir said:

Hannad narrated to us: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us: Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke with the Quraysh, and they said: "O Muhammad, you tell us that Musa had a staff with which he struck the rock, and twelve springs gushed forth from it, and you tell us that 'Isa used to give life to the dead, and you tell us that Thamud had a she-camel. So bring us some signs so that we may believe you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What do you wish that I bring you?" They said: "Make the Safa into gold for us." He said to them: "If I do so, will you believe me?" They said: "Yes, by Allah, if you do it, we will all follow you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up and began to supplicate, and Jibril, upon him be peace, came to him and said: "For you is what you wish: if you wish, Safa will become gold; but if a sign is sent and they do not believe after it, He will surely punish them. And if you wish, leave them until those among them who repent do so." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rather, let those among them who repent repent." Then Allah revealed: ﴿And they swore by Allah﴾ up to His saying ﴿they are ignorant﴾.

This report is mursal (its chain lacks a companion), but it has supporting reports through other routes. Allah, the Exalted, also says: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending signs except that the former peoples denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her with it. And We do not send signs except as a warning﴾ [al-Isra': 59].

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And what will make you aware that when it comes they will not believe﴾. It has been said: the addressees of ﴿And what will make you aware﴾ are the polytheists, and Mujahid held this view, as if he is saying to them: "And what will make you know of the truthfulness of these oaths you swear?" On this view, the reading "innaha idha ja'at la yu'minun" with a kasra on "innaha" is an independent statement about them, denying that they will believe when the signs they asked for come. Some readers read it: "annaha idha ja'at la tu'minun" with a ta' at the beginning (the second person form).

It has also been said: the addressees of His saying ﴿And what will make you aware﴾ are the believers, that is: "And what will make you know, O believers?" On this view, it is permissible to read ﴿annaha﴾ with a kasra as in the first view, or with a fatha, as an object of "yush'irukum". On this view, the "la" in ﴿annaha idha ja'at la yu'minun﴾ is an extra particle (silah), as in His saying: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?﴾ [al-A'raf: 12], and His saying ﴿And it is forbidden for a town which We have destroyed that they should return﴾ [al-Anbiya': 95]. That is: what prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you, and it is forbidden that they return. Its implied meaning in this verse is: "And what will make you know, O believers, who wish this for them out of eagerness for their faith, that when the signs come to them, they will believe?"

Some of them said: "annaha" means "la'allaha" (perhaps).

Ibn Jarir said: They mentioned that this is so in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b. He said: It has been reported from the Arabs by transmission: "Go to the market, perhaps (annaka) you will buy something for us," meaning: perhaps you will buy.

He said: It has also been said that the verse of 'Adi ibn Zayd al-'Ibadi is of this kind:

"O blamer, what will make you know that my death
is at an hour in the day or in the forenoon of tomorrow?"

Ibn Jarir chose this view and cited as evidence verses from the poetry of the Arabs. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights away, as they did not believe in it the first time﴾. Al-'Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas regarding this verse: When the polytheists denied what Allah had sent down, their hearts did not remain firm upon anything, and they were turned away from every matter.

Mujahid said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights away as they did not believe in it the first time﴾, and We prevent between them and faith, even if every sign came to them, so they would not believe, just as We prevented between them and faith the first time.

Ikrimah and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said likewise.

Ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: Allah informed of what the servants will say before they say it, and of their deeds before they do them. He said: ﴿And none informs you like the One who is All-Aware﴾ [Fatir: 14]. And He said: ﴿Lest a soul should say, "Alas, my regret over what I neglected concerning Allah, and I was indeed among the mockers." Or say, "If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous." Or say, when it sees the punishment, "If only I had another return, I would be among the good-doers"﴾ [az-Zumar: 56–58]. So He informed, glorified be He, that if they were returned they would not be able to be guided, and He said: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾ [al-An'am: 28]. And He said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights away as they did not believe in it the first time﴾. He said: If they were returned to the world, guidance would be prevented between them, just as We prevented it between them the first time while they were in the world.

His saying: ﴿And We leave them﴾, that is, We leave them ﴿in their transgression﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and al-Suddi said: in their disbelief. Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas and Qatadah said: in their misguidance.

﴿Wandering blindly (ya'mahun)﴾. Al-A'mash said: playing. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi', Abu Malik and others said: in their disbelief they hesitate and waver.

The commentary is on surah 6, verses 109–110.

God, exalted is He, says: Even if We had answered the request of those who swore by God with their most emphatic oaths, [saying], ﴿If a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it,﴾ and sent down the angels to them, meaning to inform them of the message from God, confirming the messengers, as they asked when they said: ﴿Or you bring God and the angels before us as a group,﴾ [al-Isra: 92] ﴿They said, "We will not believe until we are given what the messengers of God were given,"﴾ [al-An'am: 124] and ﴿Those who do not expect to meet Us say, "Why have the angels not been sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?" Indeed, they have become arrogant within themselves and have transgressed with great transgression.﴾ [al-Furqan: 21]

﴿And the dead spoke to them﴾, meaning they informed them of the truth of what the messengers brought them, ﴿and We gathered against them every thing face to face (qubulan)﴾. Some read "qibalan" with a kasra on the qaf and a fatha on the ba', from al-muqabalah (facing) and al-mu'ayanah (direct observation). Others read "qubulan" with a damma on both letters. It is said that its meaning is also from al-muqabalah and al-mu'ayanah, as related by Ali ibn Abi Talhah and al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Qatadah and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam also said this.

Mujahid said: "Qubulan" means in groups, one group after another, meaning every nation would be presented to them after another nation, and they would inform them of the truthfulness of the messengers in what they brought them. ﴿They would not have believed unless God willed﴾, meaning guidance belongs to Him, not to them. Rather, He guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills. He is the Doer of what He intends, and He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned, due to His knowledge, wisdom, authority, dominance, and victory. This verse is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those against whom the word of your Lord has been fulfilled will not believe. Even if every sign came to them, until they see the painful punishment.﴾ [Yunus: 96-97]

Allah says: Just as We made for you, O Muhammad, enemies who oppose you and oppose you [in م، أ: "and oppose you stubbornly"], so too We made for every prophet before you enemies. So let that not weaken you, as Allah says: ﴿And if they deny you, then messengers before you were denied﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 184], and Allah says: ﴿And messengers were denied before you, but they were patient over what they were denied and harmed, until Our help came to them﴾ [al-An'am: 34], and Allah says: ﴿Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you. Indeed your Lord is the possessor of forgiveness and painful punishment﴾ [Fussilat: 43], and Allah says: ﴿And thus We made for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals [and your Lord is sufficient as a guide and helper]﴾ [al-Furqan: 43].

Waraqah ibn Nawfal said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): [Indeed] no one has come with the like of what you have come with except that he was opposed. [Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (3), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (160), from the hadith of 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]

* *

His saying: ﴿shayatin al-ins wal-jinn﴾ is a substitute (badal) for ﴿enemy﴾, meaning: they have enemies from the devils of mankind and of the jinn, and from these and those, may Allah disfigure and curse them.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying [Exalted is He] ﴿shayatin al-ins wal-jinn﴾, he said: Among the jinn there are devils, and among mankind there are devils, who inspire one another. Qatadah said: It has reached me that Abu Dharr was once praying, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Seek refuge, O Abu Dharr, from the devils of mankind and the jinn." He said: "Are there indeed devils among mankind?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Yes."

This is disconnected (munqati') between Qatadah and Abu Dharr. [Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/209).] It has also been narrated by another route from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him. Ibn Jarir said:

Al-Muthanna narrated to us, Abu Salih narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ayyub and others from the shaykhs, from Ibn 'A'idh, from Abu Dharr, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in a gathering in which he had sat for a long time. He said: "O Abu Dharr, have you prayed?" I said: "No, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Stand and pray two rak'ahs." He said: Then I came and sat with him, and he said: "O Abu Dharr, have you sought refuge in Allah from the devils of the jinn and mankind?" I said: "No, O Messenger of Allah. Are there devils among mankind?" He said: "Yes, they are worse than the devils of the jinn."

This also has a break in its chain [Tafsir al-Tabari (12/53)]. It has been narrated connected (muttasil), as Imam Ahmad said:

Waki' narrated to us, al-Mas'udi narrated to us, Abu 'Umar al-Dimashqi informed me, from 'Ubayd ibn al-Khashkhash, from Abu Dharr, who said: I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was in the mosque, so I sat, and he said: "O Abu Dharr, have you prayed?" I said: "No." He said: "Stand and pray." He said: So I stood and prayed, then I sat, and he said: "O Abu Dharr, seek refuge in Allah from the evil of the devils of mankind and the jinn." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, do mankind have devils?" He said: "Yes." And he mentioned the complete long hadith.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh also narrated it in his Tafsir, from the hadith of Ja'far ibn 'Awn, Ya'la ibn 'Ubayd, and 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, all three from al-Mas'udi, with the same chain [Al-Musnad (5/178); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/160): "In it is al-Mas'udi, who is trustworthy but became confused."]. Another route from Abu Dharr: Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, al-Hajjaj narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, a man from the people of Damascus narrated to me, from 'Awf ibn Malik, from Abu Dharr, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Dharr, have you sought refuge in Allah from the evil of the devils of mankind and the jinn?" He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, do mankind have devils?" He said: "Yes" [Tafsir al-Tabari (12/53)].

Another route for the hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Awf al-Himsi narrated to us, Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, Mu'an ibn Rifa'ah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah [may Allah be pleased with him], who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Dharr, have you sought refuge from the devils of the jinn and mankind?" He said: O Messenger of Allah, do mankind have devils? He said: "Yes, devils of mankind and the jinn, who inspire one another with ornamented speech as deception" [Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (5/265) through Abu al-Mughirah, at length. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/159): "Its focus is 'Ali ibn Zayd, and he is weak."].

These are the routes of this hadith, and their collection gives it strength and soundness, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir narrated: Ibn Waki' narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, from Sharik, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, from 'Ikrimah: ﴿shayatin al-ins wal-jinn﴾, he said: There are no devils among mankind, but the devils of the jinn inspire the devils of mankind, and the devils of mankind inspire the devils of the jinn.

He said: Al-Harith narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from 'Ikrimah regarding His saying: ﴿inspire one another with ornamented speech as deception﴾, he said: For the human there is a devil, and for the jinn there is a devil, so the devil of mankind meets the devil of the jinn, and they inspire one another with ornamented speech as deception.

Asbat said, from al-Suddi, from 'Ikrimah regarding His saying: ﴿inspire one another﴾, in explaining this verse: As for the devils of mankind, they are the devils who mislead mankind, and the devils of the jinn who mislead the jinn meet, and each says to his companion: "I have misled my companion with such-and-such, so mislead you your companion with such-and-such," and so they teach one another.

From this Ibn Jarir understood that what is meant by "devils of mankind" according to 'Ikrimah and al-Suddi is the devils from the jinn who mislead people, not that the devils of mankind are meant. There is no doubt that this is clear from the words of 'Ikrimah; as for the words of al-Suddi, they are not like this in meaning, and it is open to interpretation. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Ibn 'Abbas through the narration of al-Dahhak from him, who said: Indeed the jinn have devils who mislead them just as the devils of mankind mislead them. He said: The devils of mankind and the devils of the jinn meet, and this one says to that one: "Mislead him with such-and-such, mislead him with such-and-such." This is His saying: ﴿inspire one another with ornamented speech as deception﴾.

In any case, the correct view is what preceded from the hadith of Abu Dharr: indeed there are devils among mankind, and the devil of every thing is what rebels against it. For this reason it came in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Dharr, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The black dog is a devil" [Sahih Muslim no. (510)]. Its meaning, and Allah knows best, is: a devil among dogs.

Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said regarding the tafsir of this verse: The disbelieving jinn are devils who inspire the disbelieving devils of mankind with ornamented speech as deception.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from 'Ikrimah, who said: I came to al-Mukhtar, and he honoured me and lodged me, to the point that he almost looked after my lodging at night. He said to me: "Go out to the people and speak to them." So I went out, and a man came and said: "What do you say about revelation?" I said: "Revelation is of two kinds." Allah says: ﴿by what We revealed to you, this Qur'an﴾ [Yusuf: 3], and Allah says: ﴿devils of mankind and the jinn who inspire one another with ornamented speech as deception﴾. He said: They intended to seize me, so I said: "What is this for you? I am your mufti and your guest." So they left me.

'Ikrimah was only alluding to al-Mukhtar, Ibn Abi 'Ubayd, may Allah disfigure him, who claimed that revelation came to him. His sister Safiyyah was married to 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, and she was among the righteous women. When 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar was informed that al-Mukhtar claimed that revelation came to him, he said: "He spoke the truth," and Allah says: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies﴾ [al-An'am: 121]. And His saying: ﴿inspire one another with ornamented speech as deception﴾ means: some of them cast to others the embellished, adorned speech, which is the decorated kind that deceives its hearer among the ignorant regarding its matter.

﴿And if your Lord had willed, they would not have done it﴾, meaning: all of that is by the decree of Allah, His determination, His will, and His wish, that there should be for every prophet an enemy from among these.

﴿So leave them﴾, meaning: leave them, ﴿and what they fabricate﴾, meaning: what they lie about. That is: leave their harm, and rely upon Allah regarding their enmity, for Allah is sufficient for you and will help you against them.

* *

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it﴾, meaning: and that they may lean toward it. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas. ﴿the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter﴾ meaning: their hearts, their minds, and their hearing.

Al-Suddi said: the hearts of the disbelievers. ﴿and that they may be pleased with it﴾, meaning: that they may love it and desire it. Only those who do not believe in the Hereafter respond to this, as Allah says: ﴿Indeed you and what you worship. You cannot lead astray against Him, except one who is destined for the Blazing Fire﴾ [al-Saffat: 161–163], and Allah says: ﴿Indeed you are in a contradictory saying. Turned away from it is whoever is turned away﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 8–9].

Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: ﴿and that they may do what they are doing﴾.

Qatadah said: It has reached me that Abu Dharr was once praying, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Seek refuge, O Abu Dharr, from the devils of mankind and the jinn." He said: "Are there indeed devils among mankind?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Yes."

This is disconnected (munqati') between Qatadah and Abu Dharr. [Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/209).] It has also been narrated by another route from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him. Ibn Jarir said:

Al-Muthanna narrated to us, Abu Salih narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ayyub and others from the shaykhs, from Ibn 'A'idh, from Abu Dharr, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in a gathering in which he had sat for a long time. He said: "O Abu Dharr, have you prayed?" I said: "No, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Stand and pray two rak'ahs." He said: Then I came and sat with him, and he said: "O Abu Dharr, have you sought refuge in Allah from the devils of the jinn and mankind?" I said: "No, O Messenger of Allah. Are there devils among mankind?" He said: "Yes, they are worse than the devils of the jinn."

This also has a break in its chain [Tafsir al-Tabari (12/53)]. It has been narrated connected (muttasil), as Imam Ahmad said:

Waki' narrated to us, al-Mas'udi narrated to us, Abu 'Umar al-Dimashqi informed me, from 'Ubayd ibn al-Khashkhash, from Abu Dharr, who said: I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was in the mosque, so I sat, and he said: "O Abu Dharr, have you prayed?" I said: "No." He said: "Stand and pray." He said: So I stood and prayed, then I sat, and he said: "O Abu Dharr, seek refuge in Allah from the evil of the devils of mankind and the jinn." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, do mankind have devils?" He said: "Yes." And he mentioned the complete long hadith.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh also narrated it in his Tafsir, from the hadith of Ja'far ibn 'Awn, Ya'la ibn 'Ubayd, and 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, all three from al-Mas'udi, with the same chain [Al-Musnad (5/178); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/160): "In it is al-Mas'udi, who is trustworthy but became confused."]. Another route from Abu Dharr: Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, al-Hajjaj narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, a man from the people of Damascus narrated to me, from 'Awf ibn Malik, from Abu Dharr, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Dharr, have you sought refuge in Allah from the evil of the devils of mankind and the jinn?" He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, do mankind have devils?" He said: "Yes" [Tafsir al-Tabari (12/53)].

Another route for the hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Awf al-Himsi narrated to us, Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, Mu'an ibn Rifa'ah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah [may Allah be pleased with him], who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Dharr, have you sought refuge from the devils of the jinn and mankind?" He said: O Messenger of Allah, do mankind have devils? He said: "Yes, devils of mankind and the jinn, who inspire one another with ornamented speech as deception" [Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (5/265) through Abu al-Mughirah, at length. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/159): "Its focus is 'Ali ibn Zayd, and he is weak."].

These are the routes of this hadith, and their collection gives it strength and soundness, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir narrated: Ibn Waki' narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, from Sharik, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, from 'Ikrimah: ﴿shayatin al-ins wal-jinn﴾, he said: There are no devils among mankind, but the devils of the jinn inspire the devils of mankind, and the devils of mankind inspire the devils of the jinn.

He said: Al-Harith narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from 'Ikrimah regarding His saying: ﴿inspire one another with ornamented speech as deception﴾, he said: For the human there is a devil, and for the jinn there is a devil, so the devil of mankind meets the devil of the jinn, and they inspire one another with ornamented speech as deception.

Asbat said, from al-Suddi, from 'Ikrimah regarding His saying: ﴿inspire one another﴾, in explaining this verse: As for the devils of mankind, they are the devils who mislead mankind, and the devils of the jinn who mislead the jinn meet, and each says to his companion: "I have misled my companion with such-and-such, so mislead you your companion with such-and-such," and so they teach one another.

From this Ibn Jarir understood that what is meant by "devils of mankind" according to 'Ikrimah and al-Suddi is the devils from the jinn who mislead people, not that the devils of mankind are meant. There is no doubt that this is clear from the words of 'Ikrimah; as for the words of al-Suddi, they are not like this in meaning, and it is open to interpretation. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Ibn 'Abbas through the narration of al-Dahhak from him, who said: Indeed the jinn have devils who mislead them just as the devils of mankind mislead them. He said: The devils of mankind and the devils of the jinn meet, and this one says to that one: "Mislead him with such-and-such, mislead him with such-and-such." This is His saying: ﴿inspire one another with ornamented speech as deception﴾.

In any case, the correct view is what preceded from the hadith of Abu Dharr: indeed there are devils among mankind, and the devil of every thing is what rebels against it. For this reason it came in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Dharr, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The black dog is a devil" [Sahih Muslim no. (510)]. Its meaning, and Allah knows best, is: a devil among dogs.

Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said regarding the tafsir of this verse: The disbelieving jinn are devils who inspire the disbelieving devils of mankind with ornamented speech as deception.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from 'Ikrimah, who said: I came to al-Mukhtar, and he honoured me and lodged me, to the point that he almost looked after my lodging at night. He said to me: "Go out to the people and speak to them." So I went out, and a man came and said: "What do you say about revelation?" I said: "Revelation is of two kinds." Allah says: ﴿by what We revealed to you, this Qur'an﴾ [Yusuf: 3], and Allah says: ﴿devils of mankind and the jinn who inspire one another with ornamented speech as deception﴾. He said: They intended to seize me, so I said: "What is this for you? I am your mufti and your guest." So they left me.

'Ikrimah was only alluding to al-Mukhtar, Ibn Abi 'Ubayd, may Allah disfigure him, who claimed that revelation came to him. His sister Safiyyah was married to 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, and she was among the righteous women. When 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar was informed that al-Mukhtar claimed that revelation came to him, he said: "He spoke the truth," and Allah says: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies﴾ [al-An'am: 121]. And His saying: ﴿inspire one another with ornamented speech as deception﴾ means: some of them cast to others the embellished, adorned speech, which is the decorated kind that deceives its hearer among the ignorant regarding its matter.

﴿And if your Lord had willed, they would not have done it﴾, meaning: all of that is by the decree of Allah, His determination, His will, and His wish, that there should be for every prophet an enemy from among these.

﴿So leave them﴾, meaning: leave them, ﴿and what they fabricate﴾, meaning: what they lie about. That is: leave their harm, and rely upon Allah regarding their enmity, for Allah is sufficient for you and will help you against them.

* *

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it﴾, meaning: and that they may lean toward it. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas. ﴿the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter﴾ meaning: their hearts, their minds, and their hearing.

Al-Suddi said: the hearts of the disbelievers. ﴿and that they may be pleased with it﴾, meaning: that they may love it and desire it. Only those who do not believe in the Hereafter respond to this, as Allah says: ﴿Indeed you and what you worship. You cannot lead astray against Him, except one who is destined for the Blazing Fire﴾ [al-Saffat: 161–163], and Allah says: ﴿Indeed you are in a contradictory saying. Turned away from it is whoever is turned away﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 8–9].

Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: ﴿and that they may do what they are doing﴾.

Allah says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say to these polytheists who worship other than Him: ﴿Shall I seek other than Allah as a judge (ḥakam) between me and you?﴾ That is, between me and you. ﴿While it is He who has sent down to you the Book, detailed (mufaṣṣalan)﴾ That is, explained clearly. ﴿And those to whom We have given the Book﴾ That is, the Jews and the Christians, ﴿know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth﴾ That is, by what they have of the good tidings concerning you in the books of the earlier prophets. ﴿So do not be among the doubters﴾ Like His saying: ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you, then ask those who recite the Book before you. The truth has certainly come to you from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾ [Yunus: 94]. This is a conditional statement, and a conditional does not imply that its condition has occurred. For this reason it has come from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "I do not doubt and I do not ask."

* *

And His saying: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice﴾ Qatadah said: "In truth regarding what He said, and in justice regarding what He judged."

He means: truthful in reports and just in commands. Everything He informs of is true, with no doubt or uncertainty about it. Everything He commands is the justice beyond which there is no justice. Everything He forbids is falsehood, for He forbids only what is corrupt, as He said: ﴿He commands them what is right and forbids them what is wrong, and makes lawful for them the good things and prohibits for them the evil things﴾ [Al-A'raf: 157] to the end of the verse.

﴿None can alter His words﴾ That is, no one can overturn His judgment, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing﴾ of the statements of His servants, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of their movements and their stillnesses, who recompenses every doer for his deed.

Allah says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say to these polytheists who worship other than Him: ﴿Shall I seek other than Allah as a judge (ḥakam) between me and you?﴾ That is, between me and you. ﴿While it is He who has sent down to you the Book, detailed (mufaṣṣalan)﴾ That is, explained clearly. ﴿And those to whom We have given the Book﴾ That is, the Jews and the Christians, ﴿know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth﴾ That is, by what they have of the good tidings concerning you in the books of the earlier prophets. ﴿So do not be among the doubters﴾ Like His saying: ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you, then ask those who recite the Book before you. The truth has certainly come to you from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾ [Yunus: 94]. This is a conditional statement, and a conditional does not imply that its condition has occurred. For this reason it has come from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "I do not doubt and I do not ask."

And His saying: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice﴾ Qatadah said: "In truth regarding what He said, and in justice regarding what He judged."

He means: truthful in reports and just in commands. Everything He informs of is true, with no doubt or uncertainty about it. Everything He commands is the justice beyond which there is no justice. Everything He forbids is falsehood, for He forbids only what is corrupt, as He said: ﴿He commands them what is right and forbids them what is wrong, and makes lawful for them the good things and prohibits for them the evil things﴾ [Al-A'raf: 157] to the end of the verse.

﴿None can alter His words﴾ That is, no one can overturn His judgment, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing﴾ of the statements of His servants, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of their movements and their stillnesses, who recompenses every doer for his deed.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says: Allah, exalted is He, informs us about the state of most of the people of the earth among the children of Adam, that they are in error, as He said: ﴿And certainly most of the earlier generations went astray before them﴾ [al-Saffat: 71], and He said: ﴿And most of mankind will not believe, even if you should strive eagerly﴾ [Yusuf: 103]. They, in their error, are not upon certainty regarding their affair; rather, they are only in false assumptions and vain conjecture: ﴿They follow not except assumption, and they are not but guessing﴾. Indeed, al-kharş (guessing, estimation) is al-hazr (estimating by conjecture), and from it comes kharş al-nakhl (estimating the dates on palm trees), which is estimating the quantity of dates on them. Likewise, all of this is by the decree of Allah and His will. And ﴿He is most knowing of who strays from His way﴾, so He facilitates that for him, and ﴿He is most knowing of the guided﴾, so He facilitates that for them, and each is facilitated for what he was created for.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says: Allah, exalted is He, informs us about the state of most of the people of the earth among the children of Adam, that they are in error, as He said: ﴿And certainly most of the earlier generations went astray before them﴾ [al-Saffat: 71], and He said: ﴿And most of mankind will not believe, even if you should strive eagerly﴾ [Yusuf: 103]. They, in their error, are not upon certainty regarding their affair; rather, they are only in false assumptions and vain conjecture: ﴿They follow not except assumption, and they are not but guessing﴾. Indeed, al-kharş (guessing, estimation) is al-hazr (estimating by conjecture), and from it comes kharş al-nakhl (estimating the dates on palm trees), which is estimating the quantity of dates on them. Likewise, all of this is by the decree of Allah and His will. And ﴿He is most knowing of who strays from His way﴾, so He facilitates that for him, and ﴿He is most knowing of the guided﴾, so He facilitates that for them, and each is facilitated for what he was created for.

This (verse) is a permission from Allah (Exalted) to His believing servants to eat of the slaughtered animals over which His name has been mentioned. Its implication is that what over which Allah's name has not been mentioned is not permitted, just as the polytheist unbelievers (the unbelievers of Quraysh) used to make lawful for themselves eating carrion and eating what was slaughtered on the stone altars (nusub) and other things.

Then He encouraged eating of what over which Allah's name has been mentioned, saying: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned while He has already detailed for you what He has forbidden to you?﴾ That is: He has already made clear to you what He has forbidden to you and explained it.

Some of them recited ﴿fassala﴾ with the doubled letter (tashdid), and others recited it without it (takhfif), and both carry the meaning of clarification and explicitness.

﴿Except what you are compelled to﴾ That is: except in a state of necessity, for then what you find is permitted to you.

Then Allah (Exalted) explained the ignorance of the polytheists in their corrupt opinions, regarding their making lawful carrion and what was over which other than Allah's name was mentioned. He said: ﴿And indeed, many [of them] lead [others] astray by their desires without knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of the transgressors.﴾ That is: He is most knowing of their transgression, their lying, and their fabrication.
