Mujahid said: "And leave the outward and the inward of sin" (﴿وَذَرُوا ظَاهِرَ الإثْمِ وَبَاطِنَهُ﴾): his disobedience, in secret and in public. In another narration from him: it is what one intends while doing it.

Qatadah said: "And leave the outward and the inward of sin" means its little and its much, its secret and its public.

As-Suddi said: Its outward is fornication with prostitutes who display their banners (al-baghaya dhawat ar-rayat), and its inward is fornication with mistresses, female friends and secret lovers (al-khalilah, as-sadaiq, al-akhdan).

Ikrimah said: Its outward is marrying women who are within the prohibited degrees (dhat al-mahram).

The correct view is that the verse is general in all of this, and it is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: My Lord has only forbidden the indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden, and sin and transgression without right, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority﴾ [al-A'raf: 33]. Therefore He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who earn sin will be recompensed for what they used to commit﴾, meaning: whether it is apparent or hidden, Allah will surely recompense them for it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan ibn Arafah narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Muawiyah ibn Salih, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from his father, from an-Nawwas ibn Sam'an, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about sin (al-ithm), and he said: "Sin is that which troubles your breast, and you dislike that people should see it."

[Muslim narrated it in his Sahih, no. (2553), through the route of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi with this chain.]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verse 121 (part 1 of 2):

Those who hold that an animal slaughtered without the name of Allah being mentioned over it is not lawful, even if the slaughterer is a Muslim, have cited this noble verse as evidence. The imams, may Allah have mercy on them, differed on this question in three opinions.

Some said: this slaughtered animal is not lawful in this condition, whether the one who omitted the basmalah did so deliberately or through forgetfulness. This is narrated from Ibn Umar, Nafi' his freed slave, 'Amir al-Sha'bi, and Muhammad ibn Sirin. It is also a narration from Imam Malik, and a narration from Ahmad ibn Hanbal, which a group of his earlier and later companions upheld. It is the choice of Abu Thawr and Dawud al-Zahiri. Abu al-Futuh Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Ta'i [[In A: "al-Zahiri".]], one of the later Shafi'is, also chose this in his book "al-Arba'in". They argued for this position with this verse, and with His saying in the verse on hunting: ﴿So eat of what they catch for you, and mention the name of Allah over it﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 4]. Then He emphasised this in this verse with His saying: ﴿And indeed, it is a grave sin (fisq)﴾. The pronoun is said to refer to eating, and it is said to refer to slaughter for other than Allah. They also cited the hadiths that command mentioning the name of Allah at slaughter and at hunting, such as the two hadiths of 'Adi ibn Hatim and Abu Tha'labah: "When you send your trained dog and mention the name of Allah over it, then eat what it catches for you." Both are in the two Sahihs. They also cited the hadith of Rafi' ibn Khadij: "Whatever draws blood and over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, eat it." This too is in both Sahihs. They also cited the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the jinn: "For you is every bone over which the name of Allah has been mentioned." Muslim narrated it. They also cited the hadith of Jundab ibn Sufyan al-Bajali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever slaughters before praying, let him slaughter another in its place; and whoever has not slaughtered until we have prayed, let him slaughter in the name of Allah." Both al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it. And from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that some people said: "O Messenger of Allah, some people bring us meat and we do not know whether the name of Allah was mentioned over it or not?" He said: "Mention the name of Allah over it yourselves and eat." She said: "They were recent in their acceptance of disbelief." Al-Bukhari narrated it. The point of the argument is that they understood the basmalah to be necessary, and they feared it had not been done by those people because of their recent conversion, so he commanded them to take precaution by mentioning the name at the time of eating, so that it would stand in place of the omission at slaughter if it had not been done, and he commanded them to apply the rulings of the Muslims in the correct manner. And Allah knows best.

The second opinion on this question: the basmalah is not a condition; rather it is recommended, so if it is omitted deliberately or out of forgetfulness, it does no harm. This is the school of Imam al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, and all his companions, and a narration from Imam Ahmad, transmitted from him by Hanbal. It is also a narration from Imam Malik, and Ashhab ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, one of his companions, stated this explicitly. It is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Hurayrah, and 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah. And Allah knows best.

Al-Shafi'i interpreted the noble verse: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed it is a grave sin﴾ as referring to what is slaughtered for other than Allah, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿or a sin (fisq) over which the name of other than Allah has been invoked﴾ [al-An'am: 145].

Ibn Juraij said, from 'Ata': ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾ — he said: it forbids the animals slaughtered by the Quraysh for idols, and it forbids the slaughter of the Magians. The path that Imam al-Shafi'i followed is strong. Some later scholars tried to strengthen it by making the "wa" in His saying ﴿and indeed it is a grave sin﴾ a circumstantial (ḥāliyyah) particle, meaning: do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned while it is a sin, and it is not a sin unless it has been invoked over for other than Allah. Then he claimed that this is the only correct reading, and that the "wa" cannot be a coordinating conjunction, because that would require coordinating a declarative nominal sentence with an imperative verbal sentence. This is refuted by His saying: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies﴾, where the "wa" is a coordinating conjunction without any problem. If the "wa" which he claimed to be circumstantial were correct as he said, it would be impossible to coordinate this clause upon it; and if it is coordinated upon the imperative clause, the same objection he raised against others applies to it. And if the "wa" is not circumstantial, his whole argument collapses from its foundation. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Yahya ibn al-Mughirah told us, Jarir informed us, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾, that he said: it is carrion (al-maytah).

Then he narrated it from Abu Zur'ah, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Ibn Lahi'ah, from 'Ata' — and he is Ibn al-Sa'ib — with the same.

This position has also been supported by what Abu Dawud narrated in al-Marasil, from the hadith of Thawr ibn Yazid, from al-Salt al-Sadusi — freed slave of Suwayd ibn Manjuf [[In M and A: "Maymun".]], one of the Successors whom Abu Hatim ibn Hibban mentioned in the book "al-Thiqat" — who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The slaughter of a Muslim is lawful, whether the name of Allah is mentioned or not, for indeed if he mentions it, he mentions nothing but the name of Allah." [[al-Marasil no. (378); al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (9/240) through Abu Dawud with the same chain. Ibn al-Qattan said, as in Nasb al-Rayah (4/183): "Its flaw, besides the irsal, is that nothing is known of al-Salt al-Sadusi's condition, nor is he known for anything other than this, and only Thawr ibn Yazid narrated from him."]]

This mursal report is strengthened by what al-Daraqutni narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "If a Muslim slaughters and does not mention the name of Allah, let him eat, for the Muslim has in him a name of the names of Allah." [[Sunan al-Daraqutni (4/295). It was also narrated as marfu', but al-Bayhaqi preferred its being mawquf, and Ibn al-Sakan authenticated it.]]

Al-Bayhaqi also argued with the hadith of 'A'ishah mentioned earlier, that some people said: "O Messenger of Allah, some people who are recent in their acceptance of the Jahiliyyah bring us meat and we do not know whether they mentioned the name of Allah over it or not?" He said: "Mention the name yourselves and eat." He said: If the presence of the basmalah were a condition, he would not have granted them permission except with certainty that it had been done. And Allah knows best.

The third opinion on this question: if he leaves out the basmalah over the slaughtered animal through forgetfulness, it does no harm; but if he leaves it out deliberately, it is not lawful.

This is the well-known position of Imam Malik and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and Abu Hanifah and his companions, and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, hold this view. It is also reported from 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, 'Ata', Tawus, al-Hasan al-Basri, Abu Malik, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, and Rabi'ah ibn Abi 'Abd al-Rahman.

Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Marghinani, in his book "al-Hidayah", reported a consensus, prior to al-Shafi'i, on the prohibition of an animal over which the basmalah was deliberately omitted. For this reason Abu Yusuf and the scholars said: if a judge ruled for the permissibility of selling it, the ruling would not be enforced, because it contradicts the consensus.

What he said is very strange, and the reports of disagreement from those before al-Shafi'i have already been mentioned. And Allah knows best.

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Whoever prohibits the slaughter of one who forgets has left the position of the whole body of scholars and opposed the established report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on this matter. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (12/53).]]

This refers to what al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi narrated: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz informed us, Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm told us, Abu Umayyah al-Tarsusi told us, Muhammad ibn Yazid told us, Ma'qil ibn 'Ubayd Allah told us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The Muslim is sufficed by his name. If he forgets to say the name when slaughtering, let him mention the name of Allah and eat it." [[al-Sunan al-Kubra (9/240).]]

The raising of this hadith to the Prophet (ﷺ) is an error, in which Ma'qil ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Jazari erred. Although he is among the narrators of Muslim, Sa'id ibn Mansur and 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr al-Humaydi both narrated it from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Amr, from Abu al-Sha'tha', from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, as his own statement. They added "Abu al-Sha'tha'" to its chain and stopped it at Ibn 'Abbas. And Allah knows best. This is the more authentic version, as al-Bayhaqi and other memorisers of hadith stated explicitly.

Ibn Jarir and others have reported from al-Sha'bi and Muhammad ibn Sirin that both disliked the slaughter over which the basmalah was forgotten. The early scholars often use "disliked" to mean "prohibited." However, it is a rule of Ibn Jarir that he does not regard the view of one or two as opposing the majority, and so he counts it as consensus. This should be noted. And Allah is the Granter of success.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakic told us, Abu Usamah told us, from Jahir ibn Yazid, who said: al-Hasan was asked. A man asked him: "I came with birds of some kind; some of them had been slaughtered with the name of Allah mentioned over them, and some had been slaughtered without the name of Allah being mentioned over them through forgetfulness, and the birds became mixed together." Al-Hasan said: "Eat it, eat it." He said: I also asked Muhammad ibn Sirin, and he said: Allah says ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾.

This position was also supported by the hadith narrated through several chains in Ibn Majah, from Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Hurayrah, Abu Dharr, 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed Allah has removed from my nation mistake, forgetfulness, and what they have been compelled to do." [[Ibn Majah narrated it in al-Sunan no. (2045) through al-Awza'i from 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him. Ibn Majah narrated it no. (2044) through Qatadah from Zurarah ibn Abi Awfa from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. Ibn Majah narrated it no. (2043) through Abu Bakr al-Hudhali from Shahr ibn Hawshab from Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, may Allah be pleased with him. al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/130): "Its chain is weak." al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/356) through Ibn Lahi'ah from Musa ibn Wardan from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, may Allah be pleased with him. As for the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, I have not found it, though it has come from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, narrated by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (6/352).]] But this is open to scrutiny, and Allah knows best.

Al-Hafiz Abu Ahmad ibn 'Adi narrated, through the hadith of Marwan ibn Salim al-Qurqusani, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about a man among us who slaughters and forgets to say the name?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The name of Allah is upon every Muslim." [[al-Kamil li-Ibn 'Adi (6/385).]]

But the chain of this report is weak, for Marwan ibn Salim al-Qurqusani, Abu 'Abd Allah al-Shami, is weak; several of the imams have spoken against him. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 6, verse 121 (part 2 of 2):

I have devoted a separate treatment to this question, in which I mentioned the positions (*madhahib*) of the Imams, their sources (*ma'akhidh*) and their evidences (*adilla*), the manner of their inferences (*wujuh al-dalalat*), and the points of contradiction (*munaqadat*) and opposition (*mu'aradat*) between them. [[The preferred view on this question, and Allah knows best, is that of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, that saying the name of Allah (*tasmiyah*) is obligatory in every case, so that an animal slaughtered without it is not lawful to eat, whether the omission was deliberate or forgetful. He said: "This is the most apparent of the opinions, for the Book and the Sunnah have made lawfulness conditional on the mention of the name of Allah in more than one place." See his words in *Majmu' al-Fatawa* (35/239).]] And Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir said: The scholars have differed regarding this verse: has any part of its ruling been abrogated (*nusikh*) or not? Some of them said: nothing of it has been abrogated, and it is *muhkam* (firm, unabrogated) in what it intends. This is the view of the majority of the scholars.

It is narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri and Ikrimah what Ibn Humayd related to us: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, who both said: Allah said: ﴿So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs﴾, and He said: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed it is defiantly disobedient (*fisq*)﴾. Then it was abrogated, and He made an exception, saying: ﴿The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 5].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was read to al-Abbas ibn al-Walid ibn Mazid: Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb narrated to us: al-Nu'man, that is Ibn al-Mundhir, informed me, from Makhul, who said: Allah revealed in the Qur'an: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾. Then the Lord abrogated it and had mercy upon the Muslims, saying: ﴿This day the good things have been made lawful for you, and the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you﴾. Thereby He abrogated it, and made the food of the People of the Book lawful.

Then Ibn Jarir said: The correct view is that there is no contradiction between the lawfulness of the food of the People of the Book and the prohibition of what over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned.

What he said is sound. Whoever among the early generations (*salaf*) used the term "abrogation" here, he meant specification (*takhsis*).

* *

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: A man said to Ibn Umar: "Al-Mukhtar claims that revelation (*wahy*) comes to him?" He said: "He spoke the truth," and he recited this verse: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies﴾.

My father narrated to us: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us: Ikrimah ibn Ammar narrated to us, from Abu Zumayl, who said: I was sitting with Ibn Abbas when al-Mukhtar ibn Abi Ubayd came for Hajj. A man came to him and said: "O Ibn Abbas, Abu Ishaq claims that revelation came to him last night?" Ibn Abbas said: "He spoke the truth." So I recoiled and said: "Ibn Abbas says he spoke the truth!" Ibn Abbas said: "There are two revelations: the revelation of Allah, and the revelation of the devil. The revelation of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, comes to Muhammad (ﷺ), and the revelation of the devil comes to his allies." Then he recited: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies﴾.

It has already been reported from Ikrimah, regarding His saying: ﴿Some of them inspire others with decorated speech as deception﴾, something similar to this.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿to dispute with you﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us: Imran ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The Jews disputed with the Prophet (ﷺ), saying: "We eat what we kill, but we do not eat what Allah kills?" So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed it is defiantly disobedient﴾.

This is how he narrated it, as a *mursal* (a report in which the companion is omitted from the chain). Abu Dawud narrated it connected (*muttasil*), saying: Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Imran ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Jews came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "We eat what we kill, but we do not eat what Allah kills?" So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned [and indeed it is defiantly disobedient]﴾.

Likewise Ibn Jarir narrated it from Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la and Sufyan ibn WakI', both from Imran ibn Uyaynah, with the same chain. [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2819), and Tafsir al-Tabari (12/82).]]

Al-Bazzar also narrated it, from Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi, from Imran ibn Uyaynah, with the same chain. This report is open to scrutiny (*nazar*) on three grounds:

First: the Jews do not hold that carrion is permissible, so that they would dispute about it.

Second: the verse is from al-An'am, and it is Meccan.

Third: this hadith was narrated by al-Tirmidhi, from Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi, from Ziyad ibn Abd Allah al-Bakka'i, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it with the wording: "Some people came to the Prophet (ﷺ)," and he mentioned it, and said: "Hasan gharib. It is reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr as a *mursal*." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3069).]]

Al-Tabarani said: Ali ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us: Zayd ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us: Musa ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us: al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾ was revealed, Persia sent to the Quraysh: "Dispute with Muhammad and say to him: 'What you slaughter with your hand with a knife is lawful, but what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, kills with a sword of gold, that is, carrion, is unlawful.'" Then this verse was revealed: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you﴾. He said: "The devils are from Persia, and their allies are from the Quraysh." [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (11/241).]]

Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us: Israil informed us: Sammak narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies﴾, that they say: "What Allah slaughters, do not eat it; and what you slaughter, eat it." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾.

Ibn Majah and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it, from Amr ibn Abd Allah, from Waki', from Israil, with the same chain. [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2818), and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3173).]] This is a sound chain (*isnad sahih*).

Ibn Jarir narrated it through multiple routes from Ibn Abbas, and there is no mention of the Jews in them. This is the preserved version (*al-mahfuz*). [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (12/78).]] And Allah knows best.

Ibn Jurayj said: Amr ibn Dinar said, from Ikrimah: The idolaters of the Quraysh corresponded with Persia against the Romans, and Persia corresponded with them. Persia wrote to the idolaters of the Quraysh: "Muhammad and his companions claim that they follow the command of Allah. What Allah slaughters with a knife of gold, Muhammad and his companions do not eat, that is, carrion; but what they slaughter themselves, they eat." The idolaters conveyed this to the companions of Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and something of it troubled some of the Muslims. So Allah revealed: ﴿And indeed it is defiantly disobedient, and indeed the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you, and if you obey them, indeed you are polytheists [mushrikun]﴾. And this was revealed: ﴿Some of them inspire others with decorated speech as deception﴾.

Al-Suddi said regarding the interpretation of this verse: The polytheists said to the believers: "How do you claim that you follow the pleasure of Allah, when what Allah slaughters you do not eat, and what you slaughter, you eat?" So Allah said: ﴿And if you obey them﴾, eating carrion, ﴿indeed you are polytheists﴾.

Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and many other scholars of the early generations (*salaf*), may Allah have mercy on them, said the same.

* *

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if you obey them, indeed you are polytheists﴾. That is: in that you have turned away from the command and law of Allah to the word of another, and given precedence to it over His, this is *shirk* (associating partners with Allah), as He, Exalted, said: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah, and [also] the Messiah, son of Mary, and they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no deity except Him; exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾ [al-Tawbah: 31]. [[The bracketed portion is from manuscripts M and A; in H it reads "the verse".]]

Al-Tirmidhi narrated in its explanation, from Adi ibn Hatim, that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, they did not worship them." He (ﷺ) said: "Rather, they made lawful for them what was unlawful and made unlawful for them what was lawful, and they followed them; that is their worship of them." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3095), by way of Abd al-Salam ibn Harb, from Ghutayf ibn A'yan, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from Adi ibn Hatim (may Allah be pleased with him). Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it except from the narration of Abd al-Salam ibn Harb, and Ghutayf ibn A'yan is not well known in hadith."]]

This is a parable God set forth for the believer who was dead, that is, in misguidance, ruined and bewildered; then God gave him life, that is, He gave life to his heart through faith, guided him to it, and enabled him to follow His messengers. ﴿And We made for him a light by which he walks among the people﴾, that is, by which he is guided on how to proceed and how to conduct himself. The light is the Qur'an, as related by al-'Awfi and Ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Suddi said it is Islam. And all of these are sound.

﴿Like one whose likeness is in the darknesses﴾ [the reading in one copy: "in the darknesses, not coming out of them"], that is, in ignorance, desires and scattered misguidances, ﴿not coming out of them﴾, that is, he is not guided to any exit or escape from what he is in. [In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: "Indeed Allah created His creation in darkness, then sprinkled upon them of His light; whoever is struck by that light is guided, and whoever misses it goes astray."] As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah is the Protector of those who believe; He brings them out of the darknesses into the light. And those who disbelieve – their protectors are the taghut; they bring them out of the light into the darknesses. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever﴾ [al-Baqarah: 257]. And as He the Exalted said: ﴿Is one who walks prone on his face better guided, or one who walks upright on a straight path?﴾ [al-Mulk: 22]. And He the Exalted said: ﴿The example of the two parties is like the blind and the deaf and the seeing and the hearing. Are they equal in comparison? Then will you not remember?﴾ [Hud: 24]. And He the Exalted said: ﴿And not equal are the blind and the seeing, nor the darknesses and the light, nor the shade and the scorching heat, nor are the living and the dead alike. Indeed, Allah causes to hear whom He wills, but you cannot make hear those who are in the graves. You are not but a warner﴾ [Fatir: 19–23]. The verses on this are many. The connection in citing the two parables here, with light and darknesses, is what preceded at the beginning of the surah: ﴿and made the darknesses and the light﴾ [al-An'am: 1].

Some have claimed that the intended meaning of this parable is two specific men: it was said that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab is the one who was dead and whom Allah gave life, and made for him a light by which he walks among the people. It was also said: 'Ammar ibn Yasir. As for the one who is in the darknesses, not coming out of them: Abu Jahl 'Amr ibn Hisham, may Allah curse him. The correct view is that the verse is general, encompassing every believer and disbeliever.

* *

His saying the Exalted: ﴿Thus was made attractive to the disbelievers what they used to do﴾, that is, We made appealing to them what they were in of ignorance and misguidance, by decree from Allah and a far-reaching wisdom. There is no god but Him [and no lord besides Him] [addition from M; in A: "alone, with no partner"].

And (Allah) the Exalted says: Just as We placed in your town, O Muhammad, great criminals, leaders and callers to disbelief and to turning away from the way of Allah, and to opposing and being hostile to you, so too were the Messengers before you tested in this way, and then the final outcome was theirs. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals. And sufficient is your Lord as a guide and a helper﴾ [al-Furqan: 31]. And He the Exalted said: ﴿And when We intend to destroy a town, We command its affluent ones, and they defiantly commit sin therein. Then the word becomes due against it, and We destroy it with complete destruction﴾ [al-Isra: 16]. It has been said that its meaning is: We commanded them to obey, but they disobeyed, so We destroyed them. And it has been said: We commanded them with a decree of destiny, as He said here: ﴿that they may plot therein﴾.

Ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿its great criminals﴾: "We empowered its wicked ones, so they disobeyed therein. When they did that, We destroyed them with punishment."

Mujahid and Qatadah said regarding ﴿its great criminals﴾: "Its leaders."

I say: This is like His saying: ﴿And We did not send a warner into any town but its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with." And they said, "We have more wealth and children, and we will not be punished."﴾ [Saba: 34-35]. And He the Exalted said: ﴿And similarly, We did not send before you a warner into any town but its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps."﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 23].

The intended meaning of "plotting" here is their calling people to misguidance through adorned speech and deeds, as He the Exalted said, informing about the people of Nuh: ﴿And they plotted a great plot﴾ [Nuh: 22]. And He the Exalted said: ﴿If only you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, returning word to one another. Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Were it not for you, we would have been believers." Those who were arrogant will say to those who were oppressed, "Did we avert you from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals." And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Rather, it was the plotting of night and day when you commanded us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals to Him." And they will conceal regret when they see the punishment, and We will put shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved. Will they be recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾ [Saba: 31-33].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, who said: "Every plotting (makr) in the Qur'an is (an) action (amal)."

* *

His saying: ﴿And they do not plot except against themselves, and they do not perceive﴾. That is: the harmful consequence of their plotting and of misguiding those whom they misguided returns only upon themselves, as He the Exalted said: ﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens and burdens along with their burdens﴾ [al-Ankabut: 13], and He said: ﴿And from the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge. Unquestionably, evil is what they bear﴾ [an-Nahl: 25].

* *

His saying: ﴿And when a sign comes to them, they say, "We will never believe until we are given like what was given to the messengers of Allah."﴾ That is: when a sign, clear proof and decisive argument comes to them, they say: ﴿We will never believe until we are given like what was given to the messengers of Allah﴾, meaning: until the angels come to us from Allah with the message, as they come to the messengers. Like His saying, Glorified and Exalted is He: ﴿And those who do not expect to meet Us say, "Why were not the angels sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?" Indeed, they have become arrogant within themselves and have transgressed with great insolence﴾ [al-Furqan: 21].

* *

His saying: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾. That is: He knows best where to place His message and who among His creation is suitable for it, as He the Exalted said: ﴿And they say, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of importance from one of the two cities?" Is it they who would apportion the mercy of your Lord?﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 31-32] up to the end of the verse. They meant: "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great, important man, honored in their eyes?" ﴿From one of the two cities﴾ means Makkah and at-Ta'if. That is because they, may Allah disfigure them, used to belittle the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, out of envy, spite, obstinacy and arrogance. As He the Exalted said, informing about them: ﴿And when those who disbelieve see you, they take you only for ridicule: "Is this the one who mentions your gods?" while they are, at the mention of the Most Merciful, disbelievers﴾ [al-Anbiya: 36]. And He the Exalted said: ﴿And when they see you, they take you only for ridicule: "Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?"﴾ [al-Furqan: 41]. And He the Exalted said: ﴿And messengers before you were certainly ridiculed, but those who ridiculed them were enveloped by what they used to mock﴾ [al-An'am: 10]. And this while they acknowledged his virtue, his honor, his lineage, the purity of his household, his upbringing and his origin, to the extent that they used to call him among themselves, before he was given revelation, "al-Amin" (the trustworthy). The leader of the disbelievers, Abu Sufyan, acknowledged this when Heraclius, king of the Romans, asked him: "How is his lineage among you?" He said: "He is of noble lineage among us." He said: "Did you used to accuse him of lying before he said what he said?" He said: "No." The lengthy hadith through which the king of the Romans deduced, from the purity of his attributes, peace be upon him, his truthfulness, his prophethood and the soundness of what he brought.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Mus'ab narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, from Shaddad Abu Ammar, from Wathilah ibn al-Asqa', may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah chose Isma'il from among the sons of Ibrahim, and He chose from the sons of Isma'il the Banu Kinanah, and He chose from the Banu Kinanah the Quraysh, and He chose from the Quraysh the Banu Hashim, and He chose me from the Banu Hashim."

Muslim alone narrated it from the hadith of al-Awza'i, who is Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr, the imam of the people of ash-Sham, with a similar wording [al-Musnad (4/107) and Sahih Muslim, no. 2276].

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was sent from the best of the generations of the children of Adam, generation after generation, until I was sent from the generation in which I was." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3557].

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal, from al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wada'ah, who said: al-Abbas said: "Some of what the people were saying reached him (ﷺ), so he ascended the pulpit and said: 'Who am I?'" They said: "You are the Messenger of Allah." He said: "I am Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib. Indeed Allah created the creation and placed me in the best of His creation, and He made them into two groups and placed me in the best group. He created the tribes and placed me in the best tribe. He made them into households and placed me in the best of their households. So I am the best of you in household and the best of you in person." [al-Musnad (1/210)]. He spoke the truth, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

Also in the hadith narrated from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Jibril said to me: 'I turned the earth, its easts and its wests, and I did not find a man better than Muhammad. And I turned the earth, its easts and its wests, and I did not find any father's children better than the Banu Hashim.'" Al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi narrated it [Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (1/176), through the route of Musa ibn Ubaydah, from Amr ibn Abdullah, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Aishah with it. It was also narrated by at-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. 3511, Majma' al-Bahrayn, through the route of Musa ibn Ubaydah ar-Rabadhi with it. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/217): "In it is Musa ibn Ubaydah ar-Rabadhi, and he is weak."].

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Bakr narrated to us, Asim narrated to us, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud [may Allah be pleased with him], who said: "Indeed Allah looked into the hearts of the servants and found the heart of Muhammad (ﷺ) to be the best of the hearts of the servants, so He chose it for Himself and sent him with His message. Then He looked into the hearts of the servants after the heart of Muhammad (ﷺ), and found the hearts of his companions to be the best of the hearts of the servants, so He made them the ministers of His Prophet, fighting for his religion. So what the Muslims see as good is good with Allah, and what they see as evil is evil with Allah." [al-Musnad (1/379)].

And Ahmad said: Shuja' ibn al-Walid narrated to us, who said: Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan mentioned, from his father, from Salman, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "O Salman, do not hate me, lest you leave your religion." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how could I hate you when Allah guided us through you?" He said: "You hate the Arabs, so you hate me." [al-Musnad (5/440); at-Tirmidhi, no. 3927; al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (4/86); and at-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (6/238), through the route of Shuja' ibn al-Walid from Qabus with it. At-Tirmidhi said: "A hasan gharib hadith, which we only know from the hadith of Abu Badr Shuja' ibn al-Walid. I heard Muhammad ibn Isma'il say: Abu Zabyan did not meet Salman; Salman died before Ali."].

Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned in the tafsir of this verse: It was mentioned from Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Jawaz, who narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Husayn, who said: A man saw Ibn Abbas entering from the gate of the mosque, and when he looked at him, he was startled. He said: "Who is this?" They said: "Ibn Abbas, the cousin of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." He said: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾.

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Those who committed crimes will be struck with humiliation before Allah and severe punishment for what they used to plot﴾. This is a severe threat from Allah and a strong warning for whoever is arrogant toward following His messengers and submitting to them in what they brought. He will surely be struck on the Day of Resurrection before Allah with ﴿humiliation (sagar)﴾, which is permanent abasement. Because they were arrogant, that brought them humiliation, as He the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell humbled﴾ [Ghafir: 60], meaning: abased, humiliated, despised.

* *

His saying: ﴿And a severe punishment for what they used to plot﴾. Since plotting is usually hidden, being a subtle scheming and deception, they were repaid with severe punishment as a fitting recompense, ﴿and your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf: 49]. As He the Exalted said: ﴿The Day when secrets are tested﴾ [at-Tariq: 9], meaning: the hidden things, the concealed things and the inner thoughts will be made manifest. And it has come in the two Sahihs, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "On the Day of Resurrection, a banner will be raised for every treacherous person at his backside, and it will be said: 'This is the treachery of so-and-so, son of so-and-so.'" [Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 7111, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 1735, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him].

The wisdom in this is that since treachery is hidden, not known to people, on the Day of Resurrection it becomes a manifest sign upon its doer for what he did.

And (Allah) the Exalted says: Just as We placed in your town, O Muhammad, great criminals, leaders and callers to disbelief and to turning away from the way of Allah, and to opposing and being hostile to you, so too were the Messengers before you tested in this way, and then the final outcome was theirs. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals. And sufficient is your Lord as a guide and a helper﴾ [al-Furqan: 31]. And He the Exalted said: ﴿And when We intend to destroy a town, We command its affluent ones, and they defiantly commit sin therein. Then the word becomes due against it, and We destroy it with complete destruction﴾ [al-Isra: 16]. It has been said that its meaning is: We commanded them to obey, but they disobeyed, so We destroyed them. And it has been said: We commanded them with a decree of destiny, as He said here: ﴿that they may plot therein﴾.

Ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿its great criminals﴾: "We empowered its wicked ones, so they disobeyed therein. When they did that, We destroyed them with punishment."

Mujahid and Qatadah said regarding ﴿its great criminals﴾: "Its leaders."

I say: This is like His saying: ﴿And We did not send a warner into any town but its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with." And they said, "We have more wealth and children, and we will not be punished."﴾ [Saba: 34-35]. And He the Exalted said: ﴿And similarly, We did not send before you a warner into any town but its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps."﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 23].

The intended meaning of "plotting" here is their calling people to misguidance through adorned speech and deeds, as He the Exalted said, informing about the people of Nuh: ﴿And they plotted a great plot﴾ [Nuh: 22]. And He the Exalted said: ﴿If only you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, returning word to one another. Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Were it not for you, we would have been believers." Those who were arrogant will say to those who were oppressed, "Did we avert you from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals." And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Rather, it was the plotting of night and day when you commanded us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals to Him." And they will conceal regret when they see the punishment, and We will put shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved. Will they be recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾ [Saba: 31-33].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, who said: "Every plotting (makr) in the Qur'an is (an) action (amal)."

* *

His saying: ﴿And they do not plot except against themselves, and they do not perceive﴾. That is: the harmful consequence of their plotting and of misguiding those whom they misguided returns only upon themselves, as He the Exalted said: ﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens and burdens along with their burdens﴾ [al-Ankabut: 13], and He said: ﴿And from the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge. Unquestionably, evil is what they bear﴾ [an-Nahl: 25].

* *

His saying: ﴿And when a sign comes to them, they say, "We will never believe until we are given like what was given to the messengers of Allah."﴾ That is: when a sign, clear proof and decisive argument comes to them, they say: ﴿We will never believe until we are given like what was given to the messengers of Allah﴾, meaning: until the angels come to us from Allah with the message, as they come to the messengers. Like His saying, Glorified and Exalted is He: ﴿And those who do not expect to meet Us say, "Why were not the angels sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?" Indeed, they have become arrogant within themselves and have transgressed with great insolence﴾ [al-Furqan: 21].

* *

His saying: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾. That is: He knows best where to place His message and who among His creation is suitable for it, as He the Exalted said: ﴿And they say, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of importance from one of the two cities?" Is it they who would apportion the mercy of your Lord?﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 31-32] up to the end of the verse. They meant: "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great, important man, honored in their eyes?" ﴿From one of the two cities﴾ means Makkah and at-Ta'if. That is because they, may Allah disfigure them, used to belittle the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, out of envy, spite, obstinacy and arrogance. As He the Exalted said, informing about them: ﴿And when those who disbelieve see you, they take you only for ridicule: "Is this the one who mentions your gods?" while they are, at the mention of the Most Merciful, disbelievers﴾ [al-Anbiya: 36]. And He the Exalted said: ﴿And when they see you, they take you only for ridicule: "Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?"﴾ [al-Furqan: 41]. And He the Exalted said: ﴿And messengers before you were certainly ridiculed, but those who ridiculed them were enveloped by what they used to mock﴾ [al-An'am: 10]. And this while they acknowledged his virtue, his honor, his lineage, the purity of his household, his upbringing and his origin, to the extent that they used to call him among themselves, before he was given revelation, "al-Amin" (the trustworthy). The leader of the disbelievers, Abu Sufyan, acknowledged this when Heraclius, king of the Romans, asked him: "How is his lineage among you?" He said: "He is of noble lineage among us." He said: "Did you used to accuse him of lying before he said what he said?" He said: "No." The lengthy hadith through which the king of the Romans deduced, from the purity of his attributes, peace be upon him, his truthfulness, his prophethood and the soundness of what he brought.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Mus'ab narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, from Shaddad Abu Ammar, from Wathilah ibn al-Asqa', may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah chose Isma'il from among the sons of Ibrahim, and He chose from the sons of Isma'il the Banu Kinanah, and He chose from the Banu Kinanah the Quraysh, and He chose from the Quraysh the Banu Hashim, and He chose me from the Banu Hashim."

Muslim alone narrated it from the hadith of al-Awza'i, who is Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr, the imam of the people of ash-Sham, with a similar wording [al-Musnad (4/107) and Sahih Muslim, no. 2276].

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was sent from the best of the generations of the children of Adam, generation after generation, until I was sent from the generation in which I was." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3557].

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal, from al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wada'ah, who said: al-Abbas said: "Some of what the people were saying reached him (ﷺ), so he ascended the pulpit and said: 'Who am I?'" They said: "You are the Messenger of Allah." He said: "I am Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib. Indeed Allah created the creation and placed me in the best of His creation, and He made them into two groups and placed me in the best group. He created the tribes and placed me in the best tribe. He made them into households and placed me in the best of their households. So I am the best of you in household and the best of you in person." [al-Musnad (1/210)]. He spoke the truth, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

Also in the hadith narrated from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Jibril said to me: 'I turned the earth, its easts and its wests, and I did not find a man better than Muhammad. And I turned the earth, its easts and its wests, and I did not find any father's children better than the Banu Hashim.'" Al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi narrated it [Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (1/176), through the route of Musa ibn Ubaydah, from Amr ibn Abdullah, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Aishah with it. It was also narrated by at-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. 3511, Majma' al-Bahrayn, through the route of Musa ibn Ubaydah ar-Rabadhi with it. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/217): "In it is Musa ibn Ubaydah ar-Rabadhi, and he is weak."].

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Bakr narrated to us, Asim narrated to us, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud [may Allah be pleased with him], who said: "Indeed Allah looked into the hearts of the servants and found the heart of Muhammad (ﷺ) to be the best of the hearts of the servants, so He chose it for Himself and sent him with His message. Then He looked into the hearts of the servants after the heart of Muhammad (ﷺ), and found the hearts of his companions to be the best of the hearts of the servants, so He made them the ministers of His Prophet, fighting for his religion. So what the Muslims see as good is good with Allah, and what they see as evil is evil with Allah." [al-Musnad (1/379)].

And Ahmad said: Shuja' ibn al-Walid narrated to us, who said: Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan mentioned, from his father, from Salman, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "O Salman, do not hate me, lest you leave your religion." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how could I hate you when Allah guided us through you?" He said: "You hate the Arabs, so you hate me." [al-Musnad (5/440); at-Tirmidhi, no. 3927; al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (4/86); and at-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (6/238), through the route of Shuja' ibn al-Walid from Qabus with it. At-Tirmidhi said: "A hasan gharib hadith, which we only know from the hadith of Abu Badr Shuja' ibn al-Walid. I heard Muhammad ibn Isma'il say: Abu Zabyan did not meet Salman; Salman died before Ali."].

Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned in the tafsir of this verse: It was mentioned from Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Jawaz, who narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Husayn, who said: A man saw Ibn Abbas entering from the gate of the mosque, and when he looked at him, he was startled. He said: "Who is this?" They said: "Ibn Abbas, the cousin of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." He said: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾.

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Those who committed crimes will be struck with humiliation before Allah and severe punishment for what they used to plot﴾. This is a severe threat from Allah and a strong warning for whoever is arrogant toward following His messengers and submitting to them in what they brought. He will surely be struck on the Day of Resurrection before Allah with ﴿humiliation (sagar)﴾, which is permanent abasement. Because they were arrogant, that brought them humiliation, as He the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell humbled﴾ [Ghafir: 60], meaning: abased, humiliated, despised.

* *

His saying: ﴿And a severe punishment for what they used to plot﴾. Since plotting is usually hidden, being a subtle scheming and deception, they were repaid with severe punishment as a fitting recompense, ﴿and your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf: 49]. As He the Exalted said: ﴿The Day when secrets are tested﴾ [at-Tariq: 9], meaning: the hidden things, the concealed things and the inner thoughts will be made manifest. And it has come in the two Sahihs, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "On the Day of Resurrection, a banner will be raised for every treacherous person at his backside, and it will be said: 'This is the treachery of so-and-so, son of so-and-so.'" [Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 7111, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 1735, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him].

The wisdom in this is that since treachery is hidden, not known to people, on the Day of Resurrection it becomes a manifest sign upon its doer for what he did.

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast for Islam﴾, meaning: He makes it easy for him, invigorates him, and facilitates that for him. This is a sign of good, like His saying: ﴿Is one whose breast Allah has expanded for Islam, so that he is upon a light from his Lord...? [Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah. Those are in manifest error.]﴾ [Az-Zumar: 22]. And He, the Exalted, says: ﴿But Allah has endeared to you the faith and made it pleasing in your hearts, and He has made hateful to you disbelief, defiance, and disobedience. Those are the rightly guided﴾ [Al-Hujurat: 7].

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast for Islam﴾ means: He widens his heart for monotheism (tawhid) and belief in Him. Abu Malik and others said likewise, and it is apparent.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Al-Thawri informed us, from 'Amr ibn Qays, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu Ja'far, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was asked: "Which of the believers is the most intelligent (akyas)?" He said: "The one who remembers death the most and prepares for what comes after it the best." He said: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about this verse: ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast for Islam﴾, and they said: "How does He expand his breast, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "A light is cast into it, and it opens and expands." They said: "Is there a sign by which one may recognize that?" He said: "Turning in repentance to the abode of eternity, withdrawing from the abode of delusion, and preparing for death before the encounter with death."

Ibn Jarir said: Hannad narrated to us, Qabisah narrated to us, from Sufyan (al-Thawri), from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from a man known as Abu Ja'far who lived in al-Mada'in, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about His saying: ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast for Islam﴾, and he mentioned something similar to what preceded.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn al-Furat al-Qazzaz, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu Ja'far, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When faith enters the heart, the heart opens and expands." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there a sign of that?" He said: "Yes: turning in repentance to the abode of eternity, withdrawing from the abode of delusion, and preparing for death before death."

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Sawwar ibn 'Abd Allah al-'Anbari: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, I heard my father narrate from 'Abd Allah ibn Murrah, from Abu Ja'far, and he mentioned it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Qays, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Miswar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse: ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast for Islam﴾. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is this expansion?" He said: "A light cast into the heart." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there a sign by which it is known?" He said: "Yes." They said: "And what is it?" He said: "Turning in repentance to the abode of eternity, withdrawing from the abode of delusion, and preparing for death before death."

Ibn Jarir also said: Hilal ibn al-'Ala' narrated to me, Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Waqid narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahim, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu 'Ubaydah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When light enters the heart, it opens and expands." They said: "Is there a sign by which it may be recognized?" He said: "Turning in repentance to the abode of eternity, withdrawing from the abode of delusion, and preparing for death before meeting death."

Ibn Jarir also narrated it from another route, from Ibn Mas'ud, connected and traced to the Prophet, saying: Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to me, Mahbub ibn al-Hasan al-Hashimi narrated to us, from Yunus, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Utbah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast for Islam﴾. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how is the breast expanded?" He said: "He enters Paradise and it opens up." They said: "And is there a sign for that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Withdrawing from the abode of delusion, turning in repentance to the abode of eternity, and preparing for death before death comes."

These are routes for this hadith, some mursal and some connected, which strengthen one another, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿And whomever He wills to leave astray, He makes his breast constricted, tight﴾ [[Addition from ms. A: "as if he were climbing into the sky"]]. It is recited with a fatha on the dad and a sukun on the ya', while most readers recite ﴿ḍayyiqan﴾ with a shadda on the ya' and a kasra, and both are dialects, like hayn and hayyin. Some read ﴿ḥaraj﴾ with a fatha on the ha' and a kasra on the ra', said to mean "sinful" (athim), and this was said by al-Suddi. It was also said that it has the meaning of the other reading, ﴿ḥarajan﴾ with a fatha on both the ha' and the ra', which is the one that does not allow any of the guidance to expand within it, and nothing that would benefit him of faith reaches it or penetrates it.

'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, asked a Bedouin man from the desert dwellers of Mudlij: "What is al-harajah?" He said: "It is a tree among trees that no grazing animal or wild animal or anything can reach." 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Likewise is the heart of the hypocrite: no good reaches it."

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: Allah makes Islam constricted for him, while Islam is wide. This is when He says: ﴿And He has not placed upon you any hardship (haraj) in the religion﴾ [Al-Hajj: 78], meaning: He has not placed upon you any constriction in Islam.

Mujahid and al-Suddi said: ﴿ḍayyiqan ḥarajan﴾ means doubting. 'Ata' al-Khurasani said: ﴿ḍayyiqan ḥarajan﴾ means there is no outlet for good in it. Ibn al-Mubarak narrated from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿ḍayyiqan ḥarajan﴾ means "there is no god but Allah" is such that he cannot enter it, as if he were climbing into the sky from the intensity of that upon him. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: He makes his breast ﴿ḍayyiqan ḥarajan﴾; he said: he finds no path in it except ascending.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿as if he were climbing into the sky﴾ from the constriction of his breast.

'Ata' al-Khurasani said: ﴿as if he were climbing into the sky﴾ means: his likeness is that of one who cannot climb into the sky.

Al-Awza'i said: ﴿as if he were climbing into the sky﴾: how can one whom Allah has made constricted in breast be a Muslim?

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: This is a parable that Allah has struck for the heart of this disbeliever in the intensity of its constriction against the arrival of faith to it. He says: his likeness in refusing to accept faith and his constriction against its reaching him is like his refusal to ascend into the sky and his inability to do so, because it is not within his capacity and power.

And concerning His saying: ﴿Thus Allah places defilement upon those who do not believe﴾, he says: Just as Allah makes the breast of whomever He wills to lead astray constricted and tight, so too He empowers Satan over him and over those like him who refuse to believe in Allah and His Messenger, so he misguides him and turns him away from the path of Allah.

Ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "ar-rijs" is Satan. Mujahid said: ar-rijs is everything in which there is no good. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: ar-rijs is the punishment.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verses 126–127:

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the way of those who went astray from His path and who barred others from it, He drew attention to the noblest thing with which He sent His Messenger: the guidance and the religion of truth. So He said: ﴿And this is the path of your Lord, straight.﴾ The word "straight" (mustaqiman) is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal), meaning: this religion which We have legislated for you, O Muhammad, by revealing this Qur'an to you, is the straight path of Allah. This is as has preceded in the hadith of al-Harith, from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), concerning the description of the Qur'an: "It is the straight path of Allah, the firm rope of Allah, and it is the wise reminder." Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi narrated it in full. (Al-Tirmidhi, no. 2908, and its chain has already been mentioned in the chapter on the virtues of the Qur'an. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a sahih, gharib hadith. We only know it from the narration of Hamzah al-Zayyat, and its chain is unknown (majhul), and there is some criticism (maqal) concerning the hadith of al-Harith.")

﴿We have indeed detailed the verses﴾, meaning: We have clarified them, explained them and expounded them, ﴿for a people who take heed﴾, meaning: for those who have understanding and awareness, who grasp from Allah and His Messenger.

﴿For them is the Abode of Peace﴾, which is Paradise, ﴿with their Lord﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection. Allah described Paradise here as the Abode of Peace because of their safety in the straight path they followed, which traces the footsteps and methods of the Prophets. Just as they were safe from the calamities of crookedness, they arrive at the Abode of Peace.

﴿And He is their Protector﴾, meaning: and the Peace, who is Allah, is their Protector, that is, their Guardian, their Helper and their Supporter, ﴿because of what they used to do﴾, meaning: as a recompense for their righteous deeds. He takes them under His care and rewards them with Paradise, by His bounty and generosity.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verses 126–127:

So He said: ﴿And this is the path of your Lord, straight.﴾ The word "straight" (mustaqiman) is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal), meaning: this religion which We have legislated for you, O Muhammad, by revealing this Qur'an to you, is the straight path of Allah. ﴿And He is their Protector﴾, meaning: and the Peace, who is Allah, is their Protector, that is, their Guardian, their Helper and their Supporter, ﴿because of what they used to do﴾, meaning: as a recompense for their righteous deeds. He takes them under His care and rewards them with Paradise, by His bounty and generosity.

Ibn Kathir says: Mention, O Muhammad, in what you relate to them and remind them of: ﴿And the Day He will gather them all﴾, meaning the jinn and their allies ﴿from mankind﴾ who used to worship them in the world, seek refuge with them and obey them, and some of them inspire to others decorated speech as deception. ﴿O company of jinn, you have taken much from mankind﴾, meaning: then He says, "O company of jinn." The context of the speech indicates the omitted part.

The meaning of His saying ﴿you have taken much from mankind﴾ is: from their misguidance and their seduction, as He says ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy. And that you worship Me; this is a straight path. And he had already led astray from among you a great number, so did you not use reason?﴾ [Yasin: 60-62].

Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas: ﴿O company of jinn, you have taken much from mankind﴾, meaning: you have misled many of them. Likewise said Mujahid, al-Hasan and Qatadah.

﴿And their allies from mankind will say: Our Lord, we benefited from one another﴾, meaning: the allies of the jinn from mankind said, responding to God Most High about that, with this.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Abu al-Ashhab Hawdhah ibn Khalifah related to us, Awf related to us, from al-Hasan regarding this verse, he said: Your Lord has taken much from the people of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, and their allies from mankind said: "Our Lord, we benefited from one another." Al-Hasan said: The benefit of one from the other was only that the jinn commanded and mankind acted.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said regarding His saying ﴿Our Lord, we benefited from one another﴾: it refers to companionship in the world.

Ibn Jurayj said: A man in the Jahiliyyah would descend into a valley and say, "I seek refuge in the chief of this valley." That was their benefiting, and so they made excuses on the Day of Resurrection.

As for the benefit of the jinn from mankind, it was, as has been mentioned, what the jinn gained from mankind of exaltation of them when mankind sought their help, so they would say: "We have become masters of mankind and jinn."

﴿And we have reached our term which You appointed for us﴾. As-Suddi said: that is death.

He said: ﴿The Fire is your abode﴾, meaning: your residence and dwelling, you and your allies. ﴿Abiding therein﴾, meaning: remaining in a lasting dwelling, ﴿except as God wills﴾.

Some of them said: the meaning of this exception returns to the barzakh (intermediate state). Others said: this is a reference to the duration of the worldly life. Other opinions were also given, which will be established, God willing, at His saying in Surah Hud: ﴿Abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills; indeed your Lord is the Effecter of what He intends﴾ [11:107].

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also related in the explanation of this verse, via ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih, scribe of al-Layth, who said: Muawiyah ibn Salih related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: ﴿The Fire is your abode, abiding therein, except as God wills; indeed your Lord is Wise, Knowing﴾. He said: This verse is one which it is not appropriate for anyone to use to judge God regarding His creation, nor to make them enter Paradise or Fire.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verse 129:

Sa'id reported from Qatadah, concerning its interpretation: "Allah only places (yuwalli) people over one another according to their deeds. So the believer is an ally (waliyy) of the believer wherever he is and wherever he may be, and the disbeliever is an ally of the disbeliever wherever he is and wherever he may be. Faith is not by wishful thinking (tamanni) nor by outward adornment (tahalli)." Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) also chose this view.

Ma'mar reported from Qatadah, concerning its interpretation: ﴿We shall make some of the wrongdoers allies of others﴾, in the Fire, where some of them follow others.

Malik ibn Dinar said: "I read in the Zabur (Psalms): Indeed, I take vengeance on the hypocrites through the hypocrites, then I take vengeance on the hypocrites all together." And this is in the Book of Allah, the statement of the Exalted: ﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others﴾.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding His saying ﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others﴾, said: "The wrongdoing jinn and the wrongdoing humans." He recited: ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is his companion﴾ [Al-Zukhruf: 36], and said: "And We empower the oppressive jinn over the oppressive humans."

The hafiz Ibn Asakir has narrated in the biography of Abd al-Baqi ibn Ahmad, via Sa'id ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Karabisi, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Asim, from Zirr, from Ibn Mas'ud, raised (to the Prophet ﷺ): "Whoever helps a wrongdoer, Allah will empower him over him." [Dhikrahu Ibn Manzur fi Mukhtasar Tarikh Dimashq (14/153), and its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat), though there is some slight discussion concerning Asim.]

This is a gharib (rare) hadith. And some of the poets said:

"There is no hand but the hand of Allah is above it,
and no wrongdoer but he will be tested by a wrongdoer..."

The meaning of the noble verse: Just as We appointed these losers from mankind to the band of jinn who misled them, so too do We deal with the wrongdoers: We empower some of them over others, We destroy some of them by means of others, and We take vengeance on some of them through others, as recompense for their wrongdoing and their transgression.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verse 130:

This is also among the things with which Allah, glorified and exalted is He, rebukes the disbelievers among the jinn and mankind on the Day of Resurrection, when He asks them—and He is most knowing—"Did the messengers not convey His messages to you?" This is a question of affirmation (istifham taqrir): ﴿O company of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾, meaning: from among your whole body (min jumlatikum). The messengers were from mankind only, and there were no messengers from the jinn, as Mujahid, Ibn Jurayj, and other imams, both of the earlier generations (salaf) and the later ones (khalaf), have stated explicitly.

Ibn 'Abbas said: The messengers were from the children of Adam, and from the jinn there were warners (nudhur).

Ibn Jarir related from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim that he claimed there were messengers among the jinn, and he cited this noble verse as evidence. However, there is room for debate in using it as proof for that, because it is open to more than one meaning and is not explicit. It is—and Allah knows best—like His saying ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side. Between them is a barrier they do not transgress﴾ up to His saying ﴿From them emerge the pearl and the coral﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 19–22]. It is well known that pearls and coral are extracted only from the salt water, not from the fresh. This is clear, and all praise is due to Allah. Ibn Jarir himself transmitted this very same answer.

The proof that the messengers were only from mankind is His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him [and We revealed]﴾ up to His saying: ﴿messengers as bearers of good news and warners, so that people will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [An-Nisa: 163–165]. He also said about Abraham: ﴿And We placed in his descendants prophethood and the Scripture﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 27]. So He confined prophethood and Scripture after Abraham to his descendants, and no one has said that prophethood existed among the jinn before Abraham the Friend of Allah (peace be upon him) and then ceased among them with his mission. He also said: ﴿We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets﴾ [Al-Furqan: 20], and He said: ﴿We did not send before you any except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns﴾ [Yusuf: 109]. It is well known that the jinn follow mankind in this matter; for this reason Allah said, reporting about them: ﴿And [mention] when We turned toward you a company of the jinn listening to the Qur'an. When they attended it, they said, "Be silent." And when it was concluded, they returned to their people as warners. They said, "O our people, indeed we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what was before it, guiding to the truth and to a straight path. O our people, respond to the caller of Allah and believe in him; He will forgive you of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment. And whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah will not cause failure [to Allah] on earth, and he will not have besides Him any protectors. Those are in clear error."﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 29–32].

It has come in a hadith related by al-Tirmidhi and others that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to them Surah Ar-Rahman [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3291], in which is the saying of Allah: ﴿We will attend to you, O two burdens (ayyuha ath-thaqalan)! So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 31–32].

Allah also said in this noble verse: ﴿O company of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My verses and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?﴾ They said, ﴿We testify against ourselves.﴾ That is, they acknowledged that the messengers had indeed conveyed Your messages to us, warned us of meeting You, and that this Day is certainly coming.

Allah said: ﴿And the worldly life deceived them﴾, meaning: while they had neglected their worldly lives and perished by denying the messengers and opposing the miracles, because they were deceived by the adornments of worldly life, its finery and its desires. ﴿And they will testify against themselves﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿that they were disbelievers﴾, meaning in the world, by what the messengers brought them, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all.

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah al-An'am (6), verses 131–132:

Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿That is because your Lord would never destroy the cities unjustly while their people were unaware.﴾ That is, We only established the proof against the two weighty ones (al-thaqalan: jinn and humankind) by sending Messengers and revealing Books, so that no one would be punished for his wrongdoing when the call had not reached him. Rather, We established the proof against the nations, and We punished no one except after sending Messengers to them, as Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿There was no nation but that a warner had passed among them.﴾ [Fatir: 24] And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a Messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid the Taghut."﴾ [al-Nahl: 36] And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And We would not punish until We sent a Messenger.﴾ [al-Isra': 15] And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Every time a company is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them, "Did no warner come to you?" They will say, "Yes, a warner had come to us, but we denied him."﴾ [al-Mulk: 8, 9] The verses on this are numerous.

Abu Ja'far Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: The phrase ﴿with injustice﴾ may bear two meanings:

The first: That is because your Lord would not destroy the cities for the injustice of their people in associating partners with Allah and similar matters, while they were unaware. The meaning is: He would not hasten to punish them until He sent to them one who would alert them to the proofs of Allah against them and warn them of the punishment of Allah on the Day of their return. And it would not be heedlessness on His part to seize them, so that they could say, ﴿No bringer of good news nor warner came to us.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 19]

The second: That ﴿That is because your Lord would never destroy the cities with injustice﴾ means: He would not destroy them without alerting and reminding them through the Messengers, the signs, and the lessons, and thereby wrong them, for Allah is not unjust to His servants.

Then (Ibn Jarir) proceeded to favor the first meaning, and there is no doubt that it is stronger, and Allah knows best. [Tafsir al-Tabari (12/124)]

And (Allah) said: As for His words, ﴿And for each are degrees according to what they did﴾, the meaning is: for each doer, whether of obedience or disobedience to Allah, there are ranks and levels according to his deeds, which Allah will bring him to and reward him with: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil.

I say: It is also possible that His words ﴿And for each are degrees according to what they did﴾ refer to the disbelievers of the jinn and humankind, meaning: for each there is a degree in the Fire according to his deeds, as in His words, ﴿He will say, "For each is double, but you do not know."﴾ [al-A'raf: 38], and His words, ﴿Those who disbelieved and averted [others] from the way of Allah – We will increase them in punishment upon punishment because they used to spread corruption.﴾ [al-Nahl: 88]

﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what they do.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: That is, all of that is from their deeds, O Muhammad, with knowledge from your Lord, who counts them and records them for them with Him, so that He may recompense them for them when they meet Him and return to Him.
