He is the All-Capable, whom nothing can overpower.

Ibn Abi Hatim said in his tafsir of it: My father related to us, Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa related to us, Muhammad ibn Himyar related to us, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam, from Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "O children of Adam, if you have intellect, count yourselves among the dead. By He in whose hand is my soul, what you are promised is coming, and you cannot escape." [Also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. (10564), and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (6/91), through the route of Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa, from Muhammad ibn Himyar, with the same. Abu Nu'aym said: "Strange from the hadith of Ata', and Abu Bakr; Muhammad ibn Himyar alone narrated it."]

* *

His saying: ﴿Say, O my people, work according to your position; indeed, I am working, so you will soon know﴾. This is a severe threat and a firm warning, meaning: continue on your path and your course if you think you are upon guidance, and I will continue on my way and my method, as He said: ﴿And say to those who do not believe, "Work according to your position; indeed, we are working. And wait; indeed, we are waiting"﴾ [Hud: 121-122].

Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas: "Ala makanatikum" means "according to your side (nahiyatikum)."

﴿So you will soon know who will have the good outcome of the home. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed﴾, meaning: whether it will be for me or for you. Allah fulfilled His promise to him, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, for He established him in the lands, gave him authority over the necks of those who opposed him among the servants, opened Makkah for him, granted him victory over those of his people who denied him, opposed him and were hostile to him, and his affair became firmly established over the whole Arabian Peninsula, and likewise Yemen and Bahrain, all of this during his lifetime. Then the cities, regions and districts were conquered after his death in the days of his successors, may Allah be pleased with them all, as Allah said: ﴿Allah has decreed: "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers"﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 21], and He said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life and on the day when the witnesses stand. The day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse, and for them is the evil home﴾ [Ghafir: 51-52]. He also said: ﴿And We had already written in the Psalms after the Remembrance that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ [al-Anbiya': 105], and He said, informing about His messengers: ﴿So their Lord revealed to them: "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers, and We will surely settle you in the land after them. That is for whoever fears My standing and fears My threat"﴾ [Ibrahim: 13-14]. And He said: ﴿Allah has promised those who believe among you and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession upon the earth, as He granted succession to those before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and He will surely replace their fear with security, [so that] they worship Me, not associating anything with Me﴾ [an-Nur: 55]. Allah has done this for this Ummah, and to Him belongs praise and favor, first and last, inwardly and outwardly.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verse 136:

This is a censure and rebuke from Allah towards the polytheists who invented innovations (bida'), disbelief and association (shirk), and who made for Allah a part of His creation, while He is the Creator of everything, glorified and exalted is He above what they associate with Him. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they assign to Allah a share of what He has created of crops and livestock﴾, meaning: of what He has created and produced, ﴿of the crops﴾, meaning: of the grains and fruits, ﴿and the livestock, a share﴾, meaning: a portion and a division. ﴿They say, "This is for Allah," by their claim, and "This is for our partners."﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So what is for their partners does not reach Allah, but what is for Allah reaches their partners﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talhah and al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of this verse: The enemies of Allah, when they tilled a field or had a fruit crop, would set aside for Allah a portion of it and for the idol a portion. Whatever of the crop, fruit, or any share of the idols' portion they kept and counted carefully. If something fell from what was designated for the Samad (Allah) they returned it to what they had designated for the idol. If the water that was designated for the idol overflowed and irrigated something designated for Allah, they left that for the idol. If some of the crop or fruit designated for Allah fell and mixed with what was designated for the idol, they said, "This is poor," and did not return it to what they had designated for Allah. If the water designated for Allah overflowed and irrigated what was designated for the idol, they left it for the idol. They used to forbid from their wealth the baheerah, the saa'ibah, the waseelah and the haam, and they would dedicate them to the idols, while claiming that they forbade them for Allah. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And they assign to Allah a share of what He has created of crops and livestock﴾, to the end of the verse.

This is also what Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and others besides them said.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said in his interpretation: Every slaughter they designated for Allah, they would never eat it until they mentioned with it the names of the gods. And what was for the gods, they did not mention the name of Allah with it. He recited the verse until he reached: ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, meaning: evil is what they divide. For they erred first in the division, since Allah, the Exalted, is the Lord, Owner and Creator of everything, and to Him belongs the dominion, and everything is His and under His control, His power and His will; there is no god but Him and no lord besides Him. Then, when they made their division by their own claim, they did not even keep to that division, which was corrupt, but rather they acted unjustly within it, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they assign to Allah daughters, glory be to Him, while for themselves is what they desire﴾ [an-Nahl: 57], and Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they have made for Him a portion from His servants. Indeed, mankind is clearly ungrateful﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 15], and Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Is for you the male and for Him the female? That, then, is an unjust division﴾ [an-Najm: 21-22].

Allah the Exalted says: "And thus have the devils made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children, that they may ruin them and confuse them in their religion." No, that is not the wording; the passage reads as follows.

Allah the Exalted says: And just as the devils made attractive to these polytheists that they should assign to Allah a share of what He has created of crops and livestock, so too they made attractive to them the killing of their children out of fear of poverty, and the burying of daughters alive out of fear of shame.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah related from Ibn ʿAbbās: "And thus their associates made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children": they made attractive to them the killing of their children.

Mujāhid said: "Their associates" (shurakāʾuhum) means their devils, who command them to bury their children alive out of fear of destitution. As-Suddī said: the devils commanded them to kill the daughters. As for "to ruin them" (li-yardūhum), it means to destroy them; and as for "to confuse them regarding their religion" (li-yalbisū ʿalayhim dīnahum), that means they mix up their religion for them.

Qatādah and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said something similar.

This is like His saying: ﴿When one of them is given the good news of a female, his face becomes dark, and he is filled with suppressed grief. He hides himself from the people because of the evil of what he has been given. Shall he keep it in humiliation, or bury it in the dust? Unquestionably, evil is what they judge.﴾ [An-Naḥl: 58–59]. And He says: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked, for what sin she was killed.﴾ [At-Takwīr: 8–9].

They also used to kill children out of poverty, that is, destitution; or out of fear that poverty would befall them in their wealth. Allah had forbidden them from killing their children for that reason. All of this came from the legislation of the Devil, his adorning it for them.

Allah says: ﴿And had Allah willed, they would not have done it.﴾ That is: all of this occurs by His will, His desire, and His choice, as an existing reality, and He has complete wisdom in that. He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned. ﴿So leave them and what they invent.﴾ That is: leave them, avoid them, and what they are engaged in; Allah will judge between you and them.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: "Hijr" means forbidden: what they forbade of the wasilah (a she-camel or ewe that bore a set number of young, reckoned as sacred), and the prohibition of what they forbade.

Likewise said Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, Qatadah, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam.

Qatadah said concerning ﴿And they say: These are cattle and tilth forbidden (hijr)﴾ and the rest of the verse: it was a prohibition imposed upon them by the devils regarding their wealth, a severity and a strictness, and that was from the devils, not from Allah the Exalted.

Ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿Hijr﴾ means they only set them aside for their gods.

Al-Suddi said concerning ﴿None may eat of them except whom we will, by their claim﴾: they say, "It is forbidden that we feed anyone except whom we wish."

This noble verse is like the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Say: Have you considered what Allah has sent down to you of provision, and you have made of it forbidden and lawful? Say: Has Allah permitted you, or do you invent against Allah?﴾ [Yunus: 59], and like His saying: ﴿Allah has not instituted any bahirah, nor sa'ibah, nor wasilah, nor ham; but those who disbelieve invent lies against Allah, and most of them do not reason﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 103].

Al-Suddi said: As for ﴿and cattle whose backs have been forbidden﴾, they are the bahirah, the sa'ibah and the ham. As for the cattle over which they do not mention the name of Allah, he said: when they give birth to them, and when they slaughter them.

Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated from Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, who said: Abu Wa'il said to me: "Do you know (ta'drī) what is meant by His saying: ﴿and cattle whose backs have been forbidden, and cattle over which they do not mention the name of Allah﴾?" I said: "No." He said: "They are the bahirah; they did not perform Hajj upon them."

Mujahid said: Among their camels there was a group over which they did not mention the name of Allah in any matter concerning them: neither when they rode them, nor when they milked them, nor when they carried on them, nor when they dragged them, nor when they did anything at all with them.

﴿Fabricating against Him﴾, that is, against Allah, and a lie on their part in attributing that to the religion and legislation of Allah; for He had not permitted them to do that, nor did He approve it from them. ﴿He will repay them for what they used to fabricate﴾, that is, against Him, attributing it to Him.

Abu Ishaq al-Subai'i related from Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, from Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse ﴿They say: "What is in the wombs of these livestock is exclusively for our males"﴾ and so on, that he said: "It is the milk."

Al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿They say: "What is in the wombs of these livestock is exclusively for our males"﴾ [and so on], that he said: "It is the milk. They used to forbid it to their females, while their males would drink it. When a ewe gave birth to a male, they would slaughter it, and it was for the men alone, not the women. If it was a female, it was left and not slaughtered. If it was stillborn, they all shared in it." Allah forbade that. Al-Suddi also said the same.

Al-Sha'bi said: "The bahira: only the men would drink its milk. If any of it died, both men and women would eat it." Ikrimah, Qatadah and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam also said the same.

Mujahid said, regarding His words ﴿They say: "What is in the wombs of these livestock is exclusively for our males, and forbidden to our wives"﴾: "They are the sa'ibah and the bahira."

Abu al-Aliyah, Mujahid and Qatadah [in one report] said regarding ﴿He will surely requite them for their description﴾: that is, their statement of falsehood concerning that. This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not say, concerning what your tongues assert falsely, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," to invent lies against Allah. Indeed, those who invent lies against Allah will not succeed. [It is] a brief enjoyment¦﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Nahl: 116-117].

﴿Indeed, He is All-Wise﴾, meaning in His actions, His words, His legislation and His decree, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of the deeds of His servants, good and bad, and He will requite them for that with the most complete recompense.

Allah says: Those who did these deeds (in one manuscript: "committed these deeds") have certainly lost, in this world and the Hereafter. As for this world, they lost their children by killing them, and they constricted their own wealth for themselves, so they made unlawful things that they had invented from their own selves. As for the Hereafter, they will end up in the worst of abodes because of their lying against Allah and their fabrication, as Allah says: ﴿Indeed, those who invent falsehood against Allah will not succeed. [It is] a enjoyment in this world; then to Us is their return; then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve﴾ [Yunus: 69-70].

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said in the tafsir of this verse: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ayyub narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, Abu 'Awana narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "If it pleases you to know the ignorance of the Arabs, then recite what comes after the hundred and thirtieth verse of Surat al-An'am: ﴿Those have certainly lost who killed their children in foolishness without knowledge and made unlawful what Allah had provided for them, inventing [lies] against Allah. They have certainly gone astray and were not guided﴾."

Likewise, al-Bukhari related it singly in the Book of "Virtues of Quraysh" in his Sahih, from Abu al-Nu'man Muhammad ibn al-Fadl 'Arim, from Abu 'Awana, whose name is al-Wadddah ibn Abd Allah al-Yashkuri, from Abu Bishr, whose name is Ja'far ibn Abi Wahshiyya ibn Iyas, with the same chain [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3524].

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-An'am (6), verses 141–142:

He, may He be exalted, says, clarifying that He is the Creator of everything, of the crops, the fruits and the livestock, which the polytheists disposed of according to their corrupt opinions. They divided and apportioned them, making some of them forbidden and some permitted. So He says: ﴿And it is He who produces gardens, trellised and untrellised.﴾

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Trellised﴾ means raised on supports. In another report: "The trellised ones" are those that people trellis (train on supports), and ﴿untrellised﴾ are the fruits that grow wild in the open country and the mountains.

'Ata' al-Khurasani said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Trellised﴾ means what is trellised of the vine, and ﴿untrellised﴾ means what is not trellised of the vine. Al-Suddi said likewise.

Ibn Jurayj said regarding ﴿similar and dissimilar﴾: similar in appearance and dissimilar in taste.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said regarding ﴿Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit﴾: from its dates and its grapes.

* *

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: some of them said it is the obligatory zakat (prescribed alms).

'Amr narrated to us: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us: Yazid ibn Darham narrated to us, saying: I heard Anas ibn Malik say regarding ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾: it is the obligatory zakat.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾: he meant the obligatory zakat, on the day it is measured and its measure is known. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said likewise.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾: that was because a man, when he sowed and the day of his harvest came, would not give out anything from what he harvested. So Allah said: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾, which means that one should know its measure and its due, one out of every ten, from what people drop of its ears of grain.

Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud in his Sunan related from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban narrated to me, from his paternal uncle Wasi' ibn Habban, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered that from every cluster-bearing palm (jadd) ten wasq of dates be given, in the form of a bunch hung in the mosque for the needy. [Al-Musnad (3/359) and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1662.] Its chain of narration is good and strong.

Tawus, Abu al-Sha'tha', Qatadah, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and Ibn Jurayj said: it is zakat.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: it is charity (sadaqah) from grain and fruits. Zayd ibn Aslam said likewise.

Others said: it is a right other than zakat.

Ash'ath narrated from Muhammad ibn Sirin and Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, regarding His statement ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾, that he said: they used to give something besides zakat. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak and others narrated from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, regarding His statement ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾, that he said: one gives whoever is present that day whatever is easy to give, and it is not zakat.

Mujahid said: when the needy are present to you, you should throw some of it to them.

'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ibn 'Uyaynah, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾, that he said: at the sowing one gives a handful, and at the harvesting one gives a handful, and one leaves them, and they follow the traces of the harvesting.

al-Thawri narrated from Hammad, from Ibrahim [al-Nakha'i] [addition from A]: he said: one gives the like of a bundle (dighth).

Ibn al-Mubarak narrated from Sharik, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾, that he said: this was before zakat: for the needy, a handful, a bundle for the fodder of his animal.

In the hadith of Ibn Lahi'ah, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Sa'id, raised to the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾: it is what falls of the ears of grain. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it. [Al-Nahhas narrated it in al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh (p. 427): al-Hasan ibn Ghulayb narrated to us, 'Imran ibn Abi 'Imran narrated to us, from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, who narrates unusual reports from Abu al-Haytham.]

Others said: all of this was something that was obligatory, then Allah abrogated it (naskh) by the tithe and half-tithe. Ibn Jarir related this from Ibn 'Abbas, Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Hasan, al-Suddi and 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi. Ibn Jarir chose it, may Allah have mercy on him.

I say: there is a problem with calling this abrogation (naskh), because it was originally something obligatory, and then He explained it in detail and specified the amount and quantity to be given. They said: this was in the second year after the Hijrah. Allah knows best.

Allah, glorified is He, has censured those who fast but do not give charity, as He mentioned about the people of the garden in Surah al-Qalam (Nun): ﴿When they swore that they would surely harvest it in the morning, and did not make an exception. So there came upon it a visitation from your Lord while they were sleeping. And it became like the darkness of night (black and burned).﴾ That is, like the night when it is pitch black and charred. ﴿Then they called to one another in the morning, saying: Go early to your field if you are going to harvest.﴾ ﴿So they set out while whispering to one another: No needy person shall enter it upon you today.﴾ ﴿And they went early with determination, able [to harvest].﴾ That is, with strength, vigor and resolve. ﴿But when they saw it, they said: Indeed, we have gone astray. Rather, we have been deprived.﴾ ﴿The best of them said: Did I not tell you, why do you not glorify [Allah]?﴾ ﴿They said: Glory be to our Lord, indeed we were wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿Then some of them turned to others blaming one another.﴾ ﴿They said: Woe to us! Indeed we were transgressors.﴾ ﴿Perhaps our Lord will give us in exchange something better than it. Indeed, we are turning to our Lord [in desire].﴾ ﴿Thus is the punishment, and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.﴾ [al-Qalam 68:17–33.]

* *

His statement: ﴿And do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not like the excessive.﴾ It was said: its meaning is: do not be excessive in giving, so that you give beyond what is customary.

Abu al-'Aliyah said: they used to give something on the day of the harvest, then they competed in it and went to excess, so Allah revealed: ﴿And do not be excessive.﴾

Ibn Jurayj said: it was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who cut a palm tree (for its fruit) and said: no one will come to me today except that I feed him. So he fed people until evening, and he had no fruit left, and Allah revealed: ﴿And do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not like the excessive.﴾ Ibn Jarir narrated it from him.

Ibn Jurayj narrated from 'Ata': He forbids excess in everything.

Iyas ibn Mu'awiyah said: whatever you go beyond the command of Allah with is excess (israf).

al-Suddi said regarding ﴿And do not be excessive﴾: do not give away your wealth, so that you end up poor.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and Muhammad ibn Ka'b said regarding ﴿And do not be excessive﴾: do not withhold charity, so that you disobey.

Then Ibn Jarir chose the statement of 'Ata': that it is a prohibition of excess in everything. There is no doubt that it is correct. But the apparent meaning from the context of the verse, Allah knows best, where He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit, and give its due on the day of its harvest, and do not be excessive [indeed, He does not like the excessive]﴾ [addition from M, A], is that it refers to eating: that is, do not be excessive in eating, because of the harm it causes to the intellect and the body. As He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Eat and drink, but do not be excessive [indeed, He does not like the excessive]﴾ [addition from A] [al-A'raf 7:31]. In Sahih al-Bukhari, it is related as a suspended report (ta'liq): "Eat and drink, and clothe yourselves and give charity, without excess or arrogance." [Sahih al-Bukhari (10/252, Fath), and Ibn Abi al-Dunya connected it in Kitab al-Shukr, no. 51, narrating it through Hammam, from Qatadah, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, may Allah be pleased with him.] This is one of those, and Allah knows best.

* *

His statement: ﴿And of the livestock, beasts of burden and [animals for] flesh.﴾ That is: He produced for you from the livestock what is for carrying and what is for food. It was said: what is meant by the beasts of burden (hamulah) is what is carried upon, from the camels, and the furash (small ones, for food) are the young of them, as al-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abd Allah regarding ﴿hamulah﴾: what is carried upon among the camels, and ﴿furash﴾, and he said: the young of the camels.

al-Hakim narrated it and said: its chain is sound, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it.

Ibn 'Abbas said: the hamulah are the large ones, and the furash [are] [addition from A] the small camels. Mujahid said likewise.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And of the livestock, beasts of burden and [animals for] flesh﴾: as for the hamulah, they are the camels, horses, mules, donkeys and everything that is carried upon; and as for the furash, they are the sheep.

Ibn Jarir chose it, and said: I think it was called furash because it is close to the ground.

al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: the hamulah are the camels and cattle, and the furash are the sheep.

al-Suddi said: as for the hamulah, they are the camels, and as for the furash, they are the weaned young camels, the calves and the sheep, and whatever is carried upon is hamulah.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: the hamulah are what you ride, and the furash are what you eat and milk: a sheep that does not carry loads, you eat its meat and make from its wool blankets and bedding (firash).

What 'Abd al-Rahman said in the interpretation of this noble verse is good, and it is supported by His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Do they not see that We have created for them from what Our hands have made, livestock, and they are their owners? And We have subjected them to them, so some of them they ride, and some of them they eat.﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:71–72.] And He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And indeed, in the livestock there is a lesson for you. We give you to drink from what is in their bellies, between excrement and blood, pure milk, palatable to the drinkers [and from the fruits of the palm trees and grapes]﴾ [addition from A] ... to His saying: ﴿And from their wool, their fur and their hair, furnishings and provision for a time﴾ [al-Nahl 16:66–80]. And He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Allah is He who made for you the livestock that you may ride some of them and eat some of them. And for you in them are benefits, and that you may reach upon them a need in your breasts, and upon them and upon the ship you are carried. And He shows you His signs, so which of the signs of Allah do you deny?﴾ [Ghafir 40:79–81.]

* *

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Eat of what Allah has provided for you.﴾ That is: of the fruits, the crops and the livestock, for Allah created all of them [addition from M, A] and made them a provision for you. ﴿And do not follow the steps of Satan.﴾ That is: his paths and his commands, as the polytheists followed them, those who forbade what Allah had provided for them, of the fruits and crops, as a fabrication against Allah. ﴿Indeed, he is to you﴾ that is: Indeed, Satan, O people, is to you ﴿a clear enemy﴾, that is: plainly manifest in enmity, as He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party to be among the companions of the Blaze.﴾ [Fatir 35:6.] And He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿O children of Adam, do not let Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from Paradise, stripping them of their clothing to show them their private parts﴾ [al-A'raf 7:27, to the end of the verse]. And He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Then do you take him and his descendants as allies other than Me, while they are an enemy to you? Wretched is the exchange for the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Kahf 18:50.] And the verses on this in the Qur'an are many.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-An'am (6), verses 141–142:

He, may He be exalted, says, clarifying that He is the Creator of everything, of the crops, the fruits and the livestock, which the polytheists disposed of according to their corrupt opinions. They divided and apportioned them, making some of them forbidden and some permitted. So He says: ﴿And it is He who produces gardens, trellised and untrellised.﴾

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Trellised﴾ means raised on supports. In another report: "The trellised ones" are those that people trellis (train on supports), and ﴿untrellised﴾ are the fruits that grow wild in the open country and the mountains.

'Ata' al-Khurasani said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Trellised﴾ means what is trellised of the vine, and ﴿untrellised﴾ means what is not trellised of the vine. Al-Suddi said likewise.

Ibn Jurayj said regarding ﴿similar and dissimilar﴾: similar in appearance and dissimilar in taste.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said regarding ﴿Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit﴾: from its dates and its grapes.

* *

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: some of them said it is the obligatory zakat (prescribed alms).

'Amr narrated to us: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us: Yazid ibn Darham narrated to us, saying: I heard Anas ibn Malik say regarding ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾: it is the obligatory zakat.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾: he meant the obligatory zakat, on the day it is measured and its measure is known. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said likewise.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾: that was because a man, when he sowed and the day of his harvest came, would not give out anything from what he harvested. So Allah said: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾, which means that one should know its measure and its due, one out of every ten, from what people drop of its ears of grain.

Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud in his Sunan related from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban narrated to me, from his paternal uncle Wasi' ibn Habban, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered that from every cluster-bearing palm (jadd) ten wasq of dates be given, in the form of a bunch hung in the mosque for the needy. [Al-Musnad (3/359) and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1662.] Its chain of narration is good and strong.

Tawus, Abu al-Sha'tha', Qatadah, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and Ibn Jurayj said: it is zakat.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: it is charity (sadaqah) from grain and fruits. Zayd ibn Aslam said likewise.

Others said: it is a right other than zakat.

Ash'ath narrated from Muhammad ibn Sirin and Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, regarding His statement ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾, that he said: they used to give something besides zakat. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak and others narrated from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, regarding His statement ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾, that he said: one gives whoever is present that day whatever is easy to give, and it is not zakat.

Mujahid said: when the needy are present to you, you should throw some of it to them.

'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ibn 'Uyaynah, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾, that he said: at the sowing one gives a handful, and at the harvesting one gives a handful, and one leaves them, and they follow the traces of the harvesting.

al-Thawri narrated from Hammad, from Ibrahim [al-Nakha'i] [addition from A]: he said: one gives the like of a bundle (dighth).

Ibn al-Mubarak narrated from Sharik, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾, that he said: this was before zakat: for the needy, a handful, a bundle for the fodder of his animal.

In the hadith of Ibn Lahi'ah, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Sa'id, raised to the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾: it is what falls of the ears of grain. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it. [Al-Nahhas narrated it in al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh (p. 427): al-Hasan ibn Ghulayb narrated to us, 'Imran ibn Abi 'Imran narrated to us, from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, who narrates unusual reports from Abu al-Haytham.]

Others said: all of this was something that was obligatory, then Allah abrogated it (naskh) by the tithe and half-tithe. Ibn Jarir related this from Ibn 'Abbas, Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Hasan, al-Suddi and 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi. Ibn Jarir chose it, may Allah have mercy on him.

I say: there is a problem with calling this abrogation (naskh), because it was originally something obligatory, and then He explained it in detail and specified the amount and quantity to be given. They said: this was in the second year after the Hijrah. Allah knows best.

Allah, glorified is He, has censured those who fast but do not give charity, as He mentioned about the people of the garden in Surah al-Qalam (Nun): ﴿When they swore that they would surely harvest it in the morning, and did not make an exception. So there came upon it a visitation from your Lord while they were sleeping. And it became like the darkness of night (black and burned).﴾ That is, like the night when it is pitch black and charred. ﴿Then they called to one another in the morning, saying: Go early to your field if you are going to harvest.﴾ ﴿So they set out while whispering to one another: No needy person shall enter it upon you today.﴾ ﴿And they went early with determination, able [to harvest].﴾ That is, with strength, vigor and resolve. ﴿But when they saw it, they said: Indeed, we have gone astray. Rather, we have been deprived.﴾ ﴿The best of them said: Did I not tell you, why do you not glorify [Allah]?﴾ ﴿They said: Glory be to our Lord, indeed we were wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿Then some of them turned to others blaming one another.﴾ ﴿They said: Woe to us! Indeed we were transgressors.﴾ ﴿Perhaps our Lord will give us in exchange something better than it. Indeed, we are turning to our Lord [in desire].﴾ ﴿Thus is the punishment, and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.﴾ [al-Qalam 68:17–33.]

* *

His statement: ﴿And do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not like the excessive.﴾ It was said: its meaning is: do not be excessive in giving, so that you give beyond what is customary.

Abu al-'Aliyah said: they used to give something on the day of the harvest, then they competed in it and went to excess, so Allah revealed: ﴿And do not be excessive.﴾

Ibn Jurayj said: it was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who cut a palm tree (for its fruit) and said: no one will come to me today except that I feed him. So he fed people until evening, and he had no fruit left, and Allah revealed: ﴿And do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not like the excessive.﴾ Ibn Jarir narrated it from him.

Ibn Jurayj narrated from 'Ata': He forbids excess in everything.

Iyas ibn Mu'awiyah said: whatever you go beyond the command of Allah with is excess (israf).

al-Suddi said regarding ﴿And do not be excessive﴾: do not give away your wealth, so that you end up poor.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and Muhammad ibn Ka'b said regarding ﴿And do not be excessive﴾: do not withhold charity, so that you disobey.

Then Ibn Jarir chose the statement of 'Ata': that it is a prohibition of excess in everything. There is no doubt that it is correct. But the apparent meaning from the context of the verse, Allah knows best, where He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit, and give its due on the day of its harvest, and do not be excessive [indeed, He does not like the excessive]﴾ [addition from M, A], is that it refers to eating: that is, do not be excessive in eating, because of the harm it causes to the intellect and the body. As He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Eat and drink, but do not be excessive [indeed, He does not like the excessive]﴾ [addition from A] [al-A'raf 7:31]. In Sahih al-Bukhari, it is related as a suspended report (ta'liq): "Eat and drink, and clothe yourselves and give charity, without excess or arrogance." [Sahih al-Bukhari (10/252, Fath), and Ibn Abi al-Dunya connected it in Kitab al-Shukr, no. 51, narrating it through Hammam, from Qatadah, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, may Allah be pleased with him.] This is one of those, and Allah knows best.

* *

His statement: ﴿And of the livestock, beasts of burden and [animals for] flesh.﴾ That is: He produced for you from the livestock what is for carrying and what is for food. It was said: what is meant by the beasts of burden (hamulah) is what is carried upon, from the camels, and the furash (small ones, for food) are the young of them, as al-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abd Allah regarding ﴿hamulah﴾: what is carried upon among the camels, and ﴿furash﴾, and he said: the young of the camels.

al-Hakim narrated it and said: its chain is sound, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it.

Ibn 'Abbas said: the hamulah are the large ones, and the furash [are] [addition from A] the small camels. Mujahid said likewise.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And of the livestock, beasts of burden and [animals for] flesh﴾: as for the hamulah, they are the camels, horses, mules, donkeys and everything that is carried upon; and as for the furash, they are the sheep.

Ibn Jarir chose it, and said: I think it was called furash because it is close to the ground.

al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: the hamulah are the camels and cattle, and the furash are the sheep.

al-Suddi said: as for the hamulah, they are the camels, and as for the furash, they are the weaned young camels, the calves and the sheep, and whatever is carried upon is hamulah.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: the hamulah are what you ride, and the furash are what you eat and milk: a sheep that does not carry loads, you eat its meat and make from its wool blankets and bedding (firash).

What 'Abd al-Rahman said in the interpretation of this noble verse is good, and it is supported by His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Do they not see that We have created for them from what Our hands have made, livestock, and they are their owners? And We have subjected them to them, so some of them they ride, and some of them they eat.﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:71–72.] And He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And indeed, in the livestock there is a lesson for you. We give you to drink from what is in their bellies, between excrement and blood, pure milk, palatable to the drinkers [and from the fruits of the palm trees and grapes]﴾ [addition from A] ... to His saying: ﴿And from their wool, their fur and their hair, furnishings and provision for a time﴾ [al-Nahl 16:66–80]. And He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Allah is He who made for you the livestock that you may ride some of them and eat some of them. And for you in them are benefits, and that you may reach upon them a need in your breasts, and upon them and upon the ship you are carried. And He shows you His signs, so which of the signs of Allah do you deny?﴾ [Ghafir 40:79–81.]

* *

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Eat of what Allah has provided for you.﴾ That is: of the fruits, the crops and the livestock, for Allah created all of them [addition from M, A] and made them a provision for you. ﴿And do not follow the steps of Satan.﴾ That is: his paths and his commands, as the polytheists followed them, those who forbade what Allah had provided for them, of the fruits and crops, as a fabrication against Allah. ﴿Indeed, he is to you﴾ that is: Indeed, Satan, O people, is to you ﴿a clear enemy﴾, that is: plainly manifest in enmity, as He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party to be among the companions of the Blaze.﴾ [Fatir 35:6.] And He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿O children of Adam, do not let Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from Paradise, stripping them of their clothing to show them their private parts﴾ [al-A'raf 7:27, to the end of the verse]. And He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Then do you take him and his descendants as allies other than Me, while they are an enemy to you? Wretched is the exchange for the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Kahf 18:50.] And the verses on this in the Qur'an are many.

This is an explanation of the ignorance of the Arabs before Islam regarding what they had forbidden of the livestock. They divided the animals into categories and types: the *bahira* (a she-camel whose ear was slit and which was released, its milk and flesh forbidden), the *sa'iba* (an animal set free to roam without use), the *wasila* (a ewe that bore twins of alternating sexes, or a similar arrangement), the *ham* (a stallion camel released after it had covered a certain number of females), and other types they invented concerning livestock, crops and fruits. God showed that He created gardens, both trellised and untrellised, and that He created from the livestock both *hamula* (animals for carrying loads) and *farsh* (smaller animals close to the ground). Then He explained the kinds of livestock: sheep, which are of two colours, the white, which is the *d'an* (sheep), and the black, which is the goats, male and female; and camels, male and female; and cattle likewise. God did not forbid any of these, nor any of their offspring. Rather, all of them were created for the children of Adam, for eating, riding, carrying loads, milking and other benefits, as He said: ﴿And He sent down for you eight pairs of livestock﴾ [Az-Zumar: 6].

* *

His saying: ﴿Or do the wombs of the two females contain﴾ is a refutation of their statement: ﴿What is in the bellies of these livestock is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿Tell me with knowledge, if you are truthful﴾ means: inform me with certainty how God forbade for you what you claimed to be forbidden, of the *bahira*, the *sa'iba*, the *wasila*, the *ham* and the like?

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿eight pairs: of the sheep two and of the goats two﴾, so these are four pairs; ﴿and of the camels two and of the cattle two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females?﴾ He says: I have not forbidden any of that. ﴿Or do the wombs of the two females contain?﴾ [He means: does the womb contain anything except a male or a female? Why, then, do you forbid some and permit some?] ﴿Tell me with knowledge, if you are truthful﴾, He says: all of it is lawful.

* *

His saying: ﴿Or were you witnesses when God enjoined this upon you?﴾ is a mockery of them regarding what they invented and fabricated against God, of forbidding what they forbade of that. ﴿Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against God to mislead people without knowledge?﴾ means: no one is more unjust than him. ﴿Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

The first person to enter under this verse was 'Amr ibn Luhayy ibn Qam'a, for he was the first to change the religion of the prophets, the first to release the *sawa'ib* (released animals), to establish the *wasila*, and to make the *ham* protected, as this is established in the Sahih [Note in the source: The hadith was mentioned earlier at the verse 103 of Surat al-Ma'ida, with its takhrij there.].

The first person to enter under this verse was 'Amr ibn Luhayy ibn Qam'a, for he was the first to change the religion of the prophets, the first to release the *sawa'ib* (released animals), to establish the *wasila*, and to make the *ham* protected, as this is established in the Sahih [Note in the source: The hadith was mentioned earlier at the verse 103 of Surat al-Ma'ida, with its takhrij there.].

Allah, the Exalted, says, commanding His servant and Messenger Muhammad (may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him): Say to those who have forbidden what Allah has provided for them, fabricating against Allah: ﴿I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who eats it﴾, meaning, one who eats it. It has been said: its meaning is, "I do not find any of what you have forbidden to be forbidden, except these." It has also been said: its meaning is, "I do not find any of the animals to be forbidden, except these." According to this, the prohibitions mentioned after this in Surah al-Ma'idah and in the hadiths that were transmitted are a lifting of the implication of this verse.

Some people call that *naskh* (abrogation), but most of the later scholars do not call it naskh, because it falls under the lifting of what was originally permitted. And Allah knows best.

Al-'Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿or blood poured forth﴾: it means spilled (al-mihraq).

Ikrimah said regarding His words ﴿or blood poured forth﴾: "Were it not for this verse, people would have searched the veins, just as the Jews did."

Hammad reported from 'Imran ibn Hudayr, who said: "I asked Abu Mijlaz about blood, and about what gets smeared from the slaughter on the head, and about a cooking pot in which redness is seen." He said: "Allah only forbade blood poured forth."

Qatadah said: "What was forbidden of blood is that which is poured forth. As for meat mixed with blood, there is no harm in it."

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim, from 'A'ishah: that she did not see any harm in the meat of predatory animals, and that redness and blood that appear on the surface of the pot were not harmful, and she recited this verse. (Sound, gharib.) [Tafsir al-Tabari (12/194)]

Al-Humaydi said: Sufyan narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Dinar narrated to us, who said: I said to Jabir ibn 'Abdullah: "They claim that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the meat of domestic donkeys during the time of Khaybar." He said: "Al-Hakam ibn 'Amr used to say that from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but that scholar (meaning Ibn 'Abbas) rejected that," and he recited: ﴿Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden﴾ to the end of the verse.

Al-Bukhari narrated it in the same way from 'Ali ibn al-Madini, from Sufyan, with the same chain. Abu Dawud also narrated it through Ibn Juraij, from 'Amr ibn Dinar. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak, although it is in Sahih al-Bukhari, as you have seen. [Musnad al-Humaydi (2/379). Al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih under no. (5529), but it is from the Musnad of Jabir ibn Zayd, may Allah be pleased with him. Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan under no. (3808) through 'Amr ibn Dinar, from a man, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him. There is no fault with al-Hakim, for he narrated it in his Mustadrak (2/317) through 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, from his Musnad, and then he specified his intention with his words: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not narrate it in this form."]

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Duhaym narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Shurayk narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Abu al-Sha'tha', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The people of the Jahiliyyah used to eat some things and leave others out of disgust. Then Allah sent His Prophet and revealed His Book, and made lawful what is lawful and made unlawful what is unlawful. So what He made lawful is lawful, what He made unlawful is unlawful, and what He was silent about is pardoned." Then he recited this verse: ﴿Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who eats it [except that it be carrion, or blood poured forth]﴾ to the end of the verse.

This is the wording of Ibn Mardawayh. Abu Dawud alone narrated it through Muhammad ibn Dawud ibn Subayh, from Abu Nu'aym with it. Al-Hakim said: "This is a hadith with a sound chain, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not narrate it." [Al-Mustadrak (4/115) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3800).]

Imam Ahmad said: 'Affan narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "A sheep belonging to Sawdah bint Zam'ah died, and she said: 'O Messenger of Allah, so-and-so has died,' meaning the sheep. He said: 'Why did you not take its hide?' She said: 'Shall we take the hide of a sheep that has died?!' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: 'Allah only said: ﴿Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who eats it, unless it be carrion, or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine﴾, and you do not eat it. Tan it and benefit from it.' So she sent for it, stripped its hide, tanned it, and made a waterskin from it, until it wore out in her possession." [Al-Musnad (1/327).]

Al-Bukhari and al-Nasa'i narrated it through al-Sha'bi, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Sawdah bint Zam'ah, with that or something similar. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6686) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/173).]

Sa'id ibn Mansur said: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Numaylah al-Fazari, from his father, who said: "I was with Ibn 'Umar when a man asked him about eating the hedgehog, so he recited to him: ﴿Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who eats it [unless it be carrion, or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine]﴾ to the end of the verse. An elderly man present there said: 'I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The hedgehog was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "It is one of the vile things."' Ibn 'Umar said: 'If the Prophet (ﷺ) said it, then it is as he said.'"

Abu Dawud narrated it from Abu Thawr, from Sa'id ibn Mansur, with it. [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3799).]

* *

As for His words, ﴿But whoever is compelled, neither desiring nor transgressing﴾, meaning: whoever is forced to eat something of what is forbidden in this noble verse, while not being guilty of rebellion or transgression, ﴿indeed your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: Forgiving toward him and Merciful to him.

The explanation of this verse has already been given in Surah al-Baqarah, sufficiently.

The purpose of the context of this noble verse is to refute the polytheists who innovated what they innovated, namely forbidding things for themselves through their corrupt opinions, such as the *bahirah*, the *sa'ibah*, the *wasilah*, the *ham* (types of animals they declared forbidden), and similar things. So Allah commanded His Messenger to inform them that he does not find, in what Allah has revealed to him, that these things are forbidden. What has been forbidden is only what is mentioned in this verse: carrion, blood poured forth, the flesh of swine, and what has been dedicated to other than Allah. Anything beyond that has not been forbidden; it is merely pardoned and left unmentioned. So how do you claim that it is forbidden, and from where have you forbidden it, when Allah has not forbidden it? Accordingly, no other prohibitions remain after this, such as the prohibition against the meat of donkeys, the meat of predatory animals, and every animal with talons among birds, according to the well-known position of the scholars.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verse 146:

Ibn Jarir said: He, exalted is He, says: "And upon the Jews We forbade every animal with claws" (﴿كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٍ﴾), which means the beasts and birds that do not have cloven toes, such as the camel, the ostrich, the goose and the duck. ʿAli ibn Abi Talha reported from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding "And upon those who were Jews We forbade every animal with claws" (﴿وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ هَادُوا حَرَّمْنَا كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٍ﴾): it is the camel and the ostrich. Mujahid and al-Suddi in one narration said the same.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is that which does not have split toes, and in another narration from him: every thing with separated toes, and among them is the rooster.

Qatadah said regarding the words "And upon those who were Jews We forbade every animal with claws" (﴿وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ هَادُوا حَرَّمْنَا كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٍ﴾): it was said: the camel, the ostrich, some birds and fish. In another narration: the camel and the ostrich, and forbidden to them from among the birds was the duck and its like, and every thing that does not have split toes.

Ibn Jurayj reported from Mujahid regarding "every animal with claws" (﴿كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٍ﴾): he said: the ostrich and the camel, "shaqqan shaqqan" (split, split). I said to al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, and he related it to me: what is "shaqqan shaqqan"? He said: everything whose [hoof/foot] is not split, from among the beasts. He said: and that which is split, the Jews eat it. He said: the legs of the beasts and the sparrows are split, so the Jews eat them. He said: the leg of the camel, its hoof, is not split, nor is the hoof of the ostrich, nor the leg of the goose, so the Jews do not eat camel, nor ostrich, nor goose, nor anything whose leg is not split, and they do not eat the wild ass.

* *

As for His saying: "And from the cattle and the sheep We forbade them their fats" (﴿وَمِنَ الْبَقَرِ وَالْغَنَمِ حَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ شُحُومَهُمَا﴾), al-Suddi said: [i.e.] the caul-fat (ath-tharb) and the fat of the two kidneys. The Jews used to say: Israel forbade it, so we forbid it. Ibn Zayd said the same.

Qatadah said: the caul-fat and every fat that was like that, which is not on bone.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talha reported from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding "except what their backs carry" (﴿إِلا مَا حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُمَا﴾): meaning the fats that cling to the back.

Al-Suddi and Abu Salih said: the tail-fat, which their backs carry.

* *

As for His saying: "or the entrails" (﴿أَوِ الْحَوَايَا﴾), the Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: "al-hawaya" is a plural whose singular is hawa', hawiyah and hawiyyah, and it is what the belly contains, gathered and rounded; they are the "daughters of milk," and they are the "mabaʿir," and they are called the "marabid," and in them are the intestines.

He said: The meaning of the statement is: "And from the cattle and the sheep We forbade them their fats, except what their backs carry, or what the entrails carry."

ʿAli ibn Abi Talha reported from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding "or the entrails" (﴿أَوِ الْحَوَايَا﴾): they are the mabaʿir (dung-passages).

Mujahid said: "al-hawaya" are the mabaʿir and the marabid. Likewise said Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Abu Malik and al-Suddi.

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "al-hawaya" are the marabid in which the intestines are, lying in their midst; they are the daughters of milk, and in the speech of the Arabs they are called the marabid.

* *

As for His exalted saying: "or what is mixed with bone" (﴿أَوْ مَا اخْتَلَطَ بِعَظْمٍ﴾), that is: and except what fat is mixed with the bones, for indeed We have made it lawful for them.

Ibn Jurayj said: the fat of the tail mixed with the rump bone is lawful. And everything in the legs, the side, the head, the eye, and what is mixed with bone, is lawful. Al-Suddi said the same.

* *

As for His exalted saying: "That We requited them for their rebellion" (﴿ذَلِكَ جَزَيْنَاهُمْ بِبَغْيِهِمْ﴾), that is: this restriction was imposed upon them, and We obliged them to it, as a recompense for their rebellion and their opposition to Our commands, as He, exalted is He, says: "For the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We forbade them good things which had been lawful for them, and for their hindering many from the way of Allah" (﴿فَبِظُلْمٍ مِنَ الَّذِينَ هَادُوا حَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ طَيِّبَاتٍ أُحِلَّتْ لَهُمْ وَبِصَدِّهِمْ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ كَثِيرًا﴾) [An-Nisa: 160].

* *

As for His saying: "And indeed We are truthful" (﴿وَإِنَّا لَصَادِقُونَ﴾), that is: and indeed We are just in what We requited them with.

Ibn Jarir said: And indeed We are truthful in what We have informed you of, O Muhammad, concerning Our forbidding that to them, not as they claimed, that Israel was the one who forbade it upon himself. And Allah knows best.

ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas said: It reached ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that Samurah had sold wine, so he said: "May Allah fight Samurah! Does he not know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Allah cursed the Jews; fats were forbidden to them, so they melted them down and sold them'?"

Both [al-Bukhari and Muslim] narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah, from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, from Tawus, from Ibn ʿAbbas, from ʿUmar, with it.

Al-Layth said: Yazid ibn Abi Habib told me, saying: ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah said: I heard Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say in the year of the Conquest: "Indeed Allah and His Messenger have forbidden the sale of wine, carrion, swine and idols." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of the fats of carrion, for they are used to grease hides, to coat ships, and for people to light their lamps with?" He said: "No, it is forbidden." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said at that time: "May Allah fight the Jews! When Allah forbade them its fats, they melted it, then sold it and ate its price."

The group narrated it through various chains from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, with it [al-Bukhari no. 2236, Muslim no. 1581, Abu Dawud no. 3486, al-Tirmidhi no. 1297, al-Nasa'i (7/309), Ibn Majah no. 2167].

Al-Zuhri said, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah fight the Jews! Fats were forbidden to them, so they sold them and ate their price."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it, from ʿAbdan, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from Yunus, from al-Zuhri, with it.

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Ibrahim related to us, Isma'il ibn Ishaq related to us, Sulayman ibn Harb related to us, Wuhayb related to us, Khalid al-Hadhdha' related to us, from Barakah Abu al-Walid, from Ibn ʿAbbas: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting behind the Maqam, and he raised his gaze to the sky and said: "Allah cursed the Jews" three times. "Indeed Allah forbade them fats, so they sold them and ate their price. Indeed Allah does not forbid a people to eat something without forbidding them its price" [al-Bukhari no. 2224, Muslim no. 1583].

Imam Ahmad said: ʿAli ibn ʿAsim related to us, Khalid al-Hadhdha' informed us, from Barakah Abu al-Walid, Ibn ʿAbbas informed us, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting in the mosque facing al-Hijr, and he looked to the sky and laughed, then said: "Allah cursed the Jews. Fats were forbidden to them, so they sold them and ate their prices. Indeed, when Allah forbids a people to eat something, He forbids them its price."

Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Khalid al-Hadhdha' [and Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr in al-Tamhid (9/44) narrated it through the route of Hushaym, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', with it].

Al-A'mash said, from Jami' ibn Shaddad, from Kulthum, from Usamah ibn Zayd, who said: We entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was ill, visiting him, and we found him sleeping with his face covered with an ʿAdani cloak. He uncovered his face and said: "Allah cursed the Jews; they forbid the fats of sheep and eat their prices." In another narration: "Fats were forbidden to them, so they sold them and ate their prices" [Musnad (1/247), Abu Dawud no. 3488].

Allah, exalted is He, says: "And if they deny you (O Muhammad), those who oppose you among the polytheists and the Jews and those who resemble them, then say: ﴿Your Lord is the possessor of vast mercy﴾." This is an encouragement for them to seek the vast mercy of Allah and to follow His Messenger. ﴿And His punishment will not be averted from the criminal people﴾ is a warning to them against opposing the Messenger, the Seal of the Prophets.

Allah frequently combines encouragement (tarhib... here, targhib) and warning (tarhib) in the Qur'an, as He says at the end of this surah: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [165], and He says: ﴿And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing, and indeed your Lord is severe in punishment﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 6]. He also says: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful. And that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾ [Al-Hijr: 49-50]. He says: ﴿Forgiver of sin and Acceptor of repentance, Severe in punishment﴾ [Ghafir: 3], and He says: ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe. Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats, and He is the Forgiving, the Loving﴾ [Al-Buruj: 12-14]. The verses on this are very numerous.

This is a debate that God mentions, and a doubt the polytheists clung to in their shirk and in their prohibition of what they had forbidden. God is fully aware of the shirk they are engaged in and of the prohibitions they had imposed, and He is able to change it, by inspiring us with faith or by coming between us and disbelief. But He did not change it, which shows that it is by His will, His volition, and His pleasure that this is so. For this reason He said: ﴿If Allah had willed, we would not have associated [anything with Him], nor would our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything.﴾ This is like His saying [Exalted is He] [[Addition from M, A.]]: ﴿And they say, "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them," [they have no knowledge of that]﴾ [[Addition from M, A.]] [az-Zukhruf: 20]. Likewise is the one in An-Nahl, which is the same as this [[The verse is 35, which is His saying: "Those who associated [others with Allah] will say, 'If Allah had willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him.'"]]. God said: ﴿Thus did those before them deny,﴾ meaning: with this same doubt, those who went astray before these people went astray. It is a futile and false argument, because if it were valid, Allah would not have made them taste His punishment, would not have destroyed them, would not have made His noble messengers victorious over them, and would not have made the polytheists taste painful retribution.

﴿Say: "Do you have any knowledge?"﴾ meaning: that Allah [Exalted is He] [[Addition from M.]] is pleased with you in what you are doing. ﴿So that you may bring it out for us﴾ meaning: so that you may display it for us, clarify it, and bring it forth. ﴿You follow nothing but assumption﴾ meaning: mere illusion and imagination. The term "assumption" here means corrupt belief. ﴿And you are only guessing﴾ meaning: you are lying about Allah in what you have claimed.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah related from Ibn ʿAbbās [may Allah be pleased with them both] [[Addition from A.]]: "﴿If Allah had willed, we would not have associated﴾" and He said "﴿Thus did those before them deny﴾." Then He said "﴿And if Allah had willed, they would not have associated﴾" [al-Anʿam: 107]. They said: "Our worship of the gods brings us near to Allah in position," so Allah informed them that they do not bring them near. As for His saying "﴿And if Allah had willed, they would not have associated﴾" [[In A: "associated us," which is an error; the correct reading is "associated," verse 107 of Surat al-Anʿam.]], He says: "If I had willed, I would have gathered them all upon guidance."

* *

As for His saying [Exalted is He]: ﴿Say, "To Allah belongs the conclusive proof. So if He had willed, He would have guided you all."﴾ He says [Exalted is He] [[Addition from M.]] to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Say﴾ to them, O Muhammad: ﴿To Allah belongs the conclusive proof﴾ meaning: to Him belongs perfect wisdom, and the conclusive proof in guiding whom He guides and misguiding whom He misguides. ﴿So if He had willed, He would have guided you all.﴾ All of that is by His power, His will, and His choice. Yet He is pleased with the believers and hates the disbelievers, as He said [Exalted is He]: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance﴾ [al-Anʿam: 35], and He said [Exalted is He]: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, all those upon the earth would have believed, all of them together﴾ [[Addition from M, A.]] [Yunus: 99], and His saying [[In M: "And He said [Exalted is He]."]]: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, He would have made mankind one community, but they will not cease to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy. And for that He created them. And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind, all together."﴾ [Hud: 118–119].

Ad-Dahhak said: "No one who disobeys Allah has any proof, but to Allah belongs the conclusive proof against His servants."

* *

As for His saying [Exalted is He]: ﴿Say, "Bring forward your witnesses who testify that Allah has prohibited this."﴾ meaning: bring forth your witnesses ﴿who testify that Allah has prohibited this﴾, meaning this which you have prohibited, lying and fabricating against Allah concerning it. ﴿And if they testify, do not testify with them﴾ meaning: because in this situation they are only testifying falsely and with deceit. ﴿And do not follow the desires of those who deny Our verses and those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and they ascribe equals to their Lord.﴾

Meaning: they associate others with Him and make equals for Him.
