Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verse 151 (part 1 of 2):

Dawud al-Awdi related from al-Sha'bi, from 'Alqamah, from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "Whoever wishes to read the document of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that bears his seal, let him read these verses: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him...﴾ up to his words ﴿that you may be mindful.﴾"

Al-Hakim said in his *Mustadrak* (a collection of hadith that he added to the works of the authentic compilers): Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Sayrafi related to us in Marw, 'Abd al-Samad ibn al-Fadl related to us, Malik ibn Isma'il al-Nahdi related to us, Isra'il related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abdullah ibn Khalifah, who said: "I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: In al-An'am there are clear verses (muhkamat), they are the mother of the Book," then he recited: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you [that you associate nothing with Him]...﴾

Then he said: "Its chain is sound (sahih al-isnad), but the two (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not narrate it."

I say: Zuhayr and Qays ibn al-Rabi' both related it from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abdullah ibn Qays, from Ibn 'Abbas, with the same wording. And Allah knows best.

Al-Hakim also related in his *Mustadrak* (in the copy of the text, "in his Musnad," which is an error) a hadith from Yazid ibn Harun, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Idris, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Which of you will pledge allegiance to me upon three things?" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you,﴾ until he finished the verses, and then said: "Whoever fulfils it, his reward is with Allah; and whoever falls short in any of them and Allah punishes him for it in this world, that will be his expiation; and whoever has it deferred to the Hereafter, his affair is with Allah: if He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will pardon him."

Then he said: "Its chain is sound, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not narrate it. They only agreed on the hadith of al-Zuhri from Abu Idris from 'Ubadah: 'Pledge allegiance to me that you will not associate anything with Allah,' and so on." Sufyan ibn Husayn related both hadiths, so he should not be attributed with error in one of the two hadiths when they are combined. And Allah knows best. (The hadith agreed upon by the two Shaykhs from the narration of al-Zuhri is related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, number 18, and by Muslim in his Sahih, number 1709.)

As for its tafsir: Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet and Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): "Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who associated partners with Allah, worshipped other than Allah, forbade what Allah had provided for them, and killed their children (and they did all of this by their own opinions and the whisperings of the devils to them): ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿Come﴾, that is, come forward and approach. ﴿I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you﴾, that is, I will relate to you and inform you of what your Lord has forbidden you, as a truth, not as conjecture or guesswork, but as a revelation from Him and a command from Him: ﴿that you associate nothing with Him﴾. It is as if there is an omitted element in the speech which the context indicates, and its estimated meaning is: "And He has enjoined upon you (wa-awsakum) ﴿that you associate nothing with Him﴾." For this reason He said at the end of the verse: ﴿That is what He has enjoined upon you, that you may understand.﴾

As the poet said:
He performed the Hajj and bequeathed the slaves of Sulaymā,
that you neither see nor speak to anyone,
and her drink never ceases to be cool.

The Arabs say: "I commanded you not to stand" (amartuka alla taqum).

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Jibril came to me and gave me the good news that whoever of your nation dies without associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise." I said: "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals?" He said: "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals." I said: "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals?" He said: "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals." I said: "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals?" He said: "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals, and even if he drinks wine." In some narrations, the one who said this was Abu Dharr to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and that he, peace be upon him, said the third time: "Even if Abu Dharr's nose is rubbed in the dust." So Abu Dharr would say after completing the hadith: "Even if Abu Dharr's nose is rubbed in the dust."

In some of the Musnads and Sunan collections, from Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah the Exalted says: 'O son of Adam, as long as you call upon Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you for what you have done, and I do not mind. Even if you were to come to Me with sins as great as the earth, I would come to you with forgiveness as great as it, so long as you do not associate anything with Me. And even if you were to sin until your sins reached the clouds of the sky, then ask My forgiveness, I would forgive you.'" (Ahmad related it in his Musnad, 5/154; al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, number 2495; and Ibn Majah in his Sunan, number 4257. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a good hadith.")

There is a witness to this in the Qur'an, where Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.﴾ [al-Nisa': 48, 116]

In Sahih Muslim, from Ibn Mas'ud: "Whoever dies without associating anything with Allah enters Paradise." (Sahih Muslim, number 92.) The verses and hadiths on this are very numerous.

Ibn Mardawayh related from the hadith of 'Ubadah and Abu al-Darda': "Do not associate anything with Allah, even if you are cut to pieces, crucified, or burned." (As for the hadith of Abu al-Darda', al-Tabarani related it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir, as in Majma' al-Zawa'id (4/216), through Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda'. Al-Haythami said: "In it is Shahr ibn Hawshab, and his hadith is good, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy." As for the hadith of 'Ubadah, it follows.)

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Awf al-Himsi related to us, Ibn Abi Maryam related to us, Nafi' ibn Yazid related to us, Sayyar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman told me, from Yazid ibn Qawdhar, from Salamah ibn Shurayh, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) enjoined upon us seven qualities: "That you not associate anything with Allah, even if you are burned, cut to pieces, or crucified." (Al-Tabarani related it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir, as in the Zawa'id (4/216). Al-Haythami said: "In it is Salamah ibn Shurayh; al-Dhahabi said: 'He is not known.' The rest of its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih.")

* *

His words, the Exalted: ﴿and to parents, good treatment﴾, that is, He enjoined upon you and commanded you to treat your parents well, that is, to be good to them, as He said: ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and to parents, good treatment.﴾ [al-Isra': 23]

Some of them recited: "And your Lord has enjoined that you worship none but Him, and to parents, good treatment."

Allah the Exalted very often links obedience to Him with kindness to parents, as He said: ﴿Give thanks to Me and to your parents; to Me is the final destination. But if they strive with you to associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them, but accompany them in this world with kindness, and follow the way of those who turn to Me in repentance. Then to Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.﴾ [Luqman: 14, 15] So He commanded kindness to both of them, even if they are polytheists, according to their status. And He said: ﴿And when We took the covenant from the Children of Israel: You shall not worship except Allah, and to parents, good treatment...﴾ up to the end of the verse. [al-Baqarah: 83] The verses on this are many. In the two Sahihs, from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Which deed is most beloved to Allah?" He said: "Prayer at its proper time." I said: "Then which?" He said: "Kindness to parents." I said: "Then which?" He said: "Jihad in the way of Allah." Ibn Mas'ud said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told me these, and if I had asked him for more, he would have given me more." (Sahih al-Bukhari, number 5970; Sahih Muslim, number 85.)

The hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh related with his chain from Abu al-Darda' and from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, each of whom said: "My close friend (ﷺ) enjoined upon me: 'Obey your parents, and even if they command you to leave your worldly possessions for them, do so.'" (Both of these were already cited from the narration of al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir.)

But there is weakness in the chains of both, and Allah knows best.

* *

His words, the Exalted: ﴿And do not kill your children out of poverty; We provide for you and for them.﴾ When Allah the Exalted enjoined kindness to fathers and grandfathers, He linked to that kindness to sons and grandsons, saying: ﴿And do not kill your children out of poverty.﴾ This was because they used to kill their children, as the devils made that appealing to them: they would bury the daughters alive for fear of shame, and sometimes they killed some of the sons out of fear of poverty. For this reason it has come in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?' He said: 'That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you.' I said: 'Then which?' He said: 'That you kill your child for fear that he will eat with you.' I said: 'Then which?' He said: 'That you commit adultery with the wife of your neighbour.'" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, nor commit adultery—and whoever does that will meet a penalty.﴾ [al-Furqan: 68] (Sahih al-Bukhari, number 4477; Sahih Muslim, number 86.)

As for His words ﴿out of poverty﴾ (min imlaq), Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: it is poverty, that is, "do not kill them out of your existing poverty." In Surah al-Isra' He said: ﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty﴾ [al-Isra': 31], that is, for fear that poverty will occur in the future. For this reason He said there: ﴿We provide for them and for you,﴾ beginning with their provision out of concern for them, meaning: do not fear poverty on account of them, for their provision is upon Allah. But in this verse, since poverty was already present, He said: ﴿We provide for you and for them,﴾ because it is the more important matter here. And Allah knows best.

* *

His words, the Exalted: ﴿And do not approach the immoralities, what is apparent of them and what is concealed.﴾ This is like His words: ﴿Say: My Lord has forbidden only immoralities, what is apparent of them and what is concealed, and sin, and oppression without right, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority, and that you say about Allah what you do not know.﴾ [al-A'raf: 33] Its tafsir was already given in His words: ﴿Leave the outward and inward of sin.﴾ [al-An'am: 120]

In the two Sahihs, from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no one more jealous (aghyar) than Allah; for this reason He has forbidden immoralities, what is apparent of them and what is concealed." (Sahih al-Bukhari, number 4634; Sahih Muslim, number 2760.)

'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr related from Warrad, from his client al-Mughirah, who said: Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah said: "If I saw a man with my wife, I would strike him with the sword without turning it aside." When that reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Do you wonder at Sa'd's jealousy? By Allah, I am more jealous than Sa'd, and Allah is more jealous than I; for this reason He has forbidden immoralities, what is apparent of them and what is concealed." (Agreed upon: Sahih al-Bukhari, number 6846; Sahih Muslim, number 1499.)

Abu al-'Ala' Kamil said, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are jealous (naghar)." He said: "By Allah, I am indeed jealous, and Allah is more jealous than I, and out of His jealousy He has forbidden immoralities." (Ahmad related it in his Musnad, 2/326, through Kamil; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (4/328): "In it is Kamil Abu al-'Ala', in whom there is some criticism that does no harm; he is trustworthy, and the rest of its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih.")

Ibn Mardawayh related it, and none of the authors of the Six Books narrated it, but it meets the criterion of al-Tirmidhi, for it has been related with this chain: "The lifespans of my nation are between sixty and seventy." (Sunan al-Tirmidhi, number 2331. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a good, strange hadith from the hadith of Abu Salih from Abu Hurayrah, and it has been related through other routes from Abu Hurayrah.")

* *

And His saying, ﴿Do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right﴾. This is one of the things that Allah, blessed and exalted is He, explicitly prohibited for emphasis. Otherwise, it falls under the prohibition of abominations, "what is apparent of them and what is concealed" (Qur'an 6:151). Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrate from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The blood of a Muslim man who testifies that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah may not be shed except in one of three cases: the married person who commits adultery, a life for a life, and one who abandons his religion and separates from the community" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6878), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1676).]].

In a version narrated by Muslim: "By the One besides whom there is no god, the blood of a Muslim man may not be shed..." and he mentioned it. Al-A'mash said: I related this to Ibrahim, and he related to me from al-Aswad, from A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), the same [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1676).]].

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated from A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The blood of a Muslim man may not be shed except in one of three cases: an adulterer who is married and is stoned, a man who kills another man intentionally, so he is killed, and a man who leaves Islam and wages war against Allah and His Messenger, so he is killed, crucified, or banished from the land." This is the wording of al-Nasa'i [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (4353), and Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/101).]].

And from the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, who said while he was besieged: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "The blood of a Muslim man may not be shed except in one of three cases: a man who disbelieves after his Islam, or commits adultery after his marriage, or kills a soul without a soul." By Allah, I have not committed adultery in the Jahiliyyah or in Islam, nor have I desired to have another religion in place of mine since Allah guided me, nor have I killed a soul, so for what do you kill me? Narrated by Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan (good) hadith [[Al-Musnad (1/63), Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2158), Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/92), and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2533).]].

The prohibition, rebuke, and threat have also come concerning the killing of the mu'ahad (one under a covenant of protection), who is the musta'man (one granted safe conduct) from among the people of war (ahl al-harb), as al-Bukhari narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever kills a mu'ahad will not smell the fragrance of Paradise, though its fragrance is found from a distance of forty years" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3166).]].

And from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever kills a mu'ahad who has the protection of Allah and the protection of His Messenger, has breached the protection of Allah, so he will not smell the fragrance of Paradise, though its fragrance is found from a distance of seventy autumns."

Narrated by Ibn Majah, and al-Tirmidhi, who said: hasan sahih (good and sound) [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2687), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (1403).]].

* *

And His saying, ﴿This He has enjoined upon you that you may understand﴾. That is: this is what He has enjoined upon you, that you may understand His command and His prohibition concerning it.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verse 152:

Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Allah revealed: ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the best way﴾ and ﴿Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly...﴾ up to the end of the verse [An-Nisa' 4:10], those who had an orphan in their care separated the orphan's food from their own food and his drink from their own drink, and they would set aside some of the food, which would be kept for the orphan until he ate it, and it would spoil. This was difficult for them, so they mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah [Mighty and Majestic] revealed [[Addition from manuscript A.]]: ﴿They ask you concerning orphans. Say, "Improving their condition is best, and if you mix your affairs with them, then they are your brothers"﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:220]. He said: So they mixed their food with theirs and their drink with theirs. Narrated by Abu Dawud.

* *

As for His words: ﴿until he reaches his maturity (ashuddahu)﴾, al-Sha'bi, Malik, and many of the early scholars (salaf) said: it means until he reaches puberty (yahtalim).

Al-Suddi said: until he reaches thirty years of age. It was also said: forty years, and it was said: sixty years. He said: all of this is far-fetched here, and Allah knows best.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And give full measure and weight with justice﴾, the Exalted commands the establishment of justice in taking and giving, just as He threatened those who abandon it in His words: ﴿Woe to the defrauders, who, when they take a measure from people, take it in full, but when they give by measure or weight to them, they give less. Do they not think that they will be resurrected for a great Day, the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds?﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin 83:1-6]. Allah has destroyed a nation among the nations who used to diminish the measure and the scale.

In the Jami' of Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of al-Husayn ibn Qays Abu 'Ali al-Rahabi, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to those in charge of measure and weight: "Indeed you have been entrusted with a matter in which the nations before you were destroyed." Then he [al-Tirmidhi] said: We do not know it as a marfu' hadith except from the narration of al-Husayn, and he is weak in hadith, but it has been narrated with a sound chain from Ibn 'Abbas as a mawquf report [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1217. Also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. 5288, and Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (2/352), through al-Husayn ibn Qays Abu 'Ali al-Rahabi.]].

I say: Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it in his Tafsir, from the hadith of Sharik, from al-A'mash, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, you, the group of mawali, Allah has given you glad tidings of two qualities by which the earlier generations were destroyed: the measure and the scale" [[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (3/385).]].

* *

As for His words: ﴿We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity﴾, meaning: whoever strives to fulfil the right and to take it, if he errs after exhausting his capacity and expending his effort, then there is no blame upon him.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of Baqiyyah, from Mubashshir [[In manuscript A: "Maysar".]] ibn 'Ubayd, from 'Amr ibn Maymun ibn Mihran, from his father, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, concerning ﴿And give full measure and weight with justice, We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity﴾: "Whoever gives full measure and weight with his hand, and Allah knows the soundness of his intention in giving full measure in both, he will not be held accountable." And that is the interpretation of ﴿its capacity﴾. This is a mursal, gharib report [[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (3/384) without attributing it to anyone else; its chain includes Mubashshir ibn 'Ubayd al-Himsi. Ahmad said: he used to fabricate hadith, and al-Bukhari said: Baqiyyah narrated from him; he is munkar al-hadith.]].

* *

As for His words: ﴿And when you speak, be just, even if it concerns a relative﴾, as Allah said: ﴿O you who believe, be persistent in upholding justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 5:8], and similarly the verse like it in Surah An-Nisa' [4:135], the Exalted commands justice in deeds and words, toward the near and the far, and Allah commands justice for everyone, at all times, and in every state.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And fulfil the covenant of Allah﴾, Ibn Jarir said: That is, and fulfil the commandment of Allah which He enjoined upon you. Fulfilling it means that you obey Him in what He has commanded and forbidden you, and act upon His Book and the Sunnah of His Messenger, and that is fulfilling the covenant of Allah.

﴿This He has enjoined upon you that you may remember﴾: the Exalted says: this He has enjoined upon you, commanded you with, and emphasised for you, ﴿that you may remember﴾, meaning: that you may be admonished and refrain from what you were engaged in before this. Some of them read it with the "dhal" shaddah (tashdid), and others with its lightening (takhfif).

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿So follow it, and do not follow other ways, lest they separate you from His way﴾, and His saying: ﴿Establish the religion, and do not be divided therein﴾ [Ash-Shura 42:13], and similar to this in the Quran. He said: Allah commanded the believers to unity (al-jama'ah), and forbade them from disagreement and division, and informed them that those before them were destroyed only through disputation and quarrels concerning the religion of Allah, and the like of this. This was said by Mujahid and others.

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Al-Aswad ibn Amir Shadhan narrated to us, Abu Bakr (that is, Ibn Ayyash) narrated to us, from Asim (that is, Ibn Abi an-Nujud), from Abu Wa'il, from Abdullah (that is, Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ drew a line with his own hand, then said: "This is the way of Allah, straight." And he drew lines to his right and to his left, then said: "These are the ways, there is not one of them except that upon it is a devil calling to it." Then he recited: ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow other ways, lest they separate you from His way﴾.

Al-Hakim also narrated it, from Al-Asamm, from Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, with the same chain. He said: its isnad is sahih, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it.

Abu Ja'far ar-Razi, Warqa' and Amr ibn Abi Qays also narrated it similarly, from Asim, from Abu Wa'il Shaqiq ibn Salamah, from Ibn Mas'ud, with the same, traced to the Prophet ﷺ (marfu').

Yazid ibn Harun, Musaddad, and an-Nasa'i narrated it, from Yahya ibn Habib ibn Arabi, and Ibn Hibban (through the narration of Ibn Wahb), all four from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Asim, from Abu Wa'il, from Ibn Mas'ud, with the same.

Ibn Jarir also narrated it, from al-Muthanna, from al-Hammani, from Hammad ibn Zayd, with the same.

Al-Hakim narrated it from Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq, from Isma'il ibn Ishaq al-Qadi, from Sulayman ibn Harb, from Hammad ibn Zayd, with the same. He said: sahih, though they did not record it.

An-Nasa'i and al-Hakim also narrated this hadith, through Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus, from Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, from Asim, from Zirr, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, with the same, traced to the Prophet ﷺ (marfu').

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh likewise narrated it through Yahya al-Hammani, from Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, from Asim, from Zirr, with the same.

Al-Hakim authenticated it, as you have seen, through both routes. Perhaps this hadith is with Asim ibn Abi an-Nujud, from Zirr, and from Abu Wa'il Shaqiq ibn Salamah, both from Ibn Mas'ud, with the same. And Allah knows best.

Al-Hakim said: The corroboration of this hadith is the hadith of ash-Sha'bi from Jabir, through a route that is not relied upon.

This refers to the hadith which Imam Ahmad and Abd ibn Humayd both related, and the wording is Ahmad's: Abdullah ibn Muhammad (that is, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah) narrated to us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar informed us, from Mujalid, from ash-Sha'bi, from Jabir, who said: We were sitting with the Prophet ﷺ, and he drew a line in front of him like this, and said: "This is the way of Allah." And two lines to his right, and two lines to his left, and he said: "These are the ways of Satan." Then he placed his hand on the middle line, then recited this verse: ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow other ways, lest they separate you from His way. That He has enjoined upon you, that you may be righteous﴾.

Ibn Majah in the Book of the Sunnah of his Sunan, and al-Bazzar, narrated it from Abu Sa'id Abdullah ibn Sa'id, from Abu Khalid al-Ahmar, with the same. Al-Busiri said in az-Zawa'id (1/45): "This isnad contains weakness because of Mujalid ibn Sa'id."

I say: Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it through two routes, from Abu Sa'id al-Kindi, from Abu Khalid, from Mujalid, from ash-Sha'bi, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ drew a line, and drew a line to his right, and drew a line to his left, and placed his hand on the middle line, and recited this verse: ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it﴾. In its isnad is Mujalid ibn Sa'id, concerning whom there is discussion.

However, the reliance is upon the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, together with the disagreement in it, if that is influential, and it has also been narrated as a statement of Ibn Mas'ud (mawquf).

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Aban, that a man said to Ibn Mas'ud: What is the straight path? He said: Muhammad ﷺ left us at its beginning, and its end is in Paradise, and to its right are side-paths, and to its left are side-paths, and there are men there calling whoever passes by them. Whoever takes one of those side-paths, it ends with him in the Fire, and whoever takes the path, it ends with him in Paradise. Then Ibn Mas'ud recited: ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow other ways, lest they separate you from His way﴾, and so on [Tafsir at-Tabari 12/230].

Ibn Mardawayh said: Abu Amr narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, Adam narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ayyash narrated to us, Aban ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Muslim ibn Abi Imran, from Abdullah ibn Umar: Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) was asked about the straight path, and Ibn Mas'ud said to him: Muhammad ﷺ left us at its beginning, and its end is in Paradise, and he mentioned the rest of the hadith as previously stated. And Allah knows best.

It has also been narrated from the hadith of an-Nawwas ibn Sam'an something similar. Imam Ahmad said: al-Hasan ibn Sawwar Abu al-Ala narrated to us, Layth (that is, ibn Sa'd) narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, that Abd ar-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr narrated to him, from his father, from an-Nawwas ibn Sam'an, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Allah has struck a parable: a straight path, and on either side of the path are two walls, in which are open doors, and over the doors are hanging curtains. At the entrance of the path is a caller saying: 'O people, enter the straight path all together, and do not scatter.' And a caller calls from above the path. When a person wants to open any of those doors, he says: 'Woe to you! Do not open it, for if you open it you will enter it.' So the path is Islam, the two walls are the limits of Allah, the open doors are the prohibitions of Allah, the caller at the head of the path is the Book of Allah, and the caller above the path is the admonisher of Allah in the heart of every Muslim."

At-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i narrated it, from Ali ibn Hujr (an-Nasa'i added) and Amr ibn Uthman, both from Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid, from Bahir ibn Sa'd, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from an-Nawwas ibn Sam'an, with the same [Musnad 2/182; Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. 2859; an-Nasa'i in al-Kubra no. 11233]. At-Tirmidhi said: hasan gharib.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So follow it, and do not follow other ways, lest they separate you from His way﴾, He (glorified be He) used the singular for "His way" because the truth is one; and for "ways" He used the plural because of their division and dispersion, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿Allah is the Protector of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light. And those who disbelieve, their protectors are the Taghut; they bring them out of light into darknesses. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:257].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Sufyan ibn Husayn narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Idris al-Khawlani, from Ubadah ibn as-Samit, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Which of you will pledge allegiance to me upon these three verses?" Then he recited: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you﴾ until he finished the three verses. Then he said: "Whoever fulfils them, his reward is with Allah; and whoever falls short of any of them, if Allah punishes him in this world, that is his punishment; and whoever postpones it to the Hereafter, his matter is with Allah: if He wills, He punishes him, and if He wills, He pardons him." [Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2/318 through the route of Yazid ibn Harun.]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verse 154–155:

Ibn Jarir said: ﴿Then We gave Moses the Book﴾. Its implied sense is: "Then say, O Muhammad, informing on Our behalf that We gave Moses the Book," based on His saying: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you﴾.

I say: There is room for scrutiny in this. Here, "thumma" (then) is only used to link one report to another report, not to indicate sequence here, as the poet said:

"Say to whoever became chief, then his father became chief, and before that his grandfather had become chief..." [[I have not identified its author.]]

Here, when Allah the Exalted informed about the Qur'an with His saying: ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it﴾, He linked it to praising the Torah and its messenger, saying: ﴿Then We gave Moses the Book﴾. Often Allah, glorified is He, [[In A: "Allah the Exalted".]] pairs the mention of the Qur'an with the Torah, as in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And before it was the Book of Moses, a guide and a mercy. And this is a Book confirming it in the Arabic tongue﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 12], and His saying at the beginning of this surah: ﴿Say: Who sent down the Book which Moses brought, as a light and guidance for the people, which you make into pages, displaying them and concealing much﴾ [verse 91], and after it: ﴿And this is a Book We have sent down, blessed﴾ [al-An'am: 92] and so on. And Allah the Exalted said, informing about the polytheists: ﴿But when the truth came to them from Us, they said: Why was he not given the like of what was given to Moses?﴾ Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before? They said: Two kinds of magic supporting each other, and they said: Indeed, we are disbelievers in all of it﴾ [al-Qasas: 48]. And Allah the Exalted said, informing about the jinn that they said: ﴿They said: O our people, indeed we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what came before it, guiding to the truth and to a straight path﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30].

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Complete [favour] upon the one who did good and a detailed explanation of all things﴾, meaning: We gave him the Book which We revealed to him, complete and perfect, comprehensive of everything he needed in his law, as He said: ﴿And We wrote for him on the tablets of everything﴾ [al-A'raf: 145].

* *

His saying: ﴿upon the one who did good﴾, meaning: as a reward for his good in action and his standing in Our commands and obedience, as in His saying: ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ [al-Rahman: 60], and as in His saying: ﴿And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them, He said: Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people. [He said: And of my descendants? He said: My covenant does not include the wrongdoers.]﴾ [al-Baqarah: 124], and His saying: ﴿And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and were certain of Our signs﴾ [al-Sajdah: 24].

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas: ﴿Then We gave Moses the Book, complete upon the one who did good﴾ — he says: "who did good in what Allah gave him."

Qatadah said: "Whoever does good in this world, that is completed for him in the Hereafter."

Ibn Jarir chose that the sense of the sentence is: ﴿[Then] We gave Moses the Book, complete﴾ [[Added from A.]] upon his goodness. So it is as if he made "alladhi" (the one who) a verbal-source particle, as is said in His saying: ﴿And you plunged as those who plunged﴾ [al-Tawbah: 69], meaning: as their plunging. Ibn Rawahah said:

"So Allah established what He gave you of goodness among the messengers, and victory like that with which they were victorious."

[[The verse is in Ibn Hisham's al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (2/374).]]

Others said: "alladhi" here means "alladhina" (those who).

Ibn Jarir said: It is reported from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that he used to recite it: "Complete upon those who did good."

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid: ﴿Complete upon the one who did good﴾ — he said: upon the believers and the doers of good; and Abu Ubaydah said likewise. Al-Baghawi said: "Those who do good" are the prophets and the believers, meaning: We made manifest His favour over them.

I say: As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He said: O Moses, I have chosen you above the people by My messages and My speech﴾ [al-A'raf: 144]. And his being chosen does not necessarily entail his being preferred over Muhammad ﷺ, the seal of the prophets, and over the Friend (Abraham), peace be upon them both, for other proofs.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' related from Yahya ibn Ya'mur that he used to recite it: ﴿Complete upon the one who is best﴾ with a nominative ending, with the interpretation "upon the one who is best." Then he said: This is a reading I do not consider permissible to recite with, though it has a sound grammatical basis in Arabic.

It was also said: its meaning is: complete upon Allah's goodness to him, in addition to what Allah had already bestowed upon him. Ibn Jarir and al-Baghawi related this.

There is no contradiction between this and the first view, and Ibn Jarir reconciled them as we have explained, and to Allah belongs all praise.

* *

His saying: ﴿And a detailed explanation of all things, and guidance and mercy﴾ contains praise of His Book which Allah sent down to him. ﴿That they may believe in the meeting with their Lord﴾ [...] ﴿And this is a Book We have sent down, blessed, so follow it and be mindful of Allah that you may receive mercy﴾ contains the call to follow the Qur'an, and describing it as blessed for whoever follows it and acts by it in this world and the Hereafter.

* *

His saying: ﴿And a detailed explanation of all things, and guidance and mercy﴾ contains praise of His Book which Allah sent down to him. ﴿That they may believe in the meeting with their Lord﴾ [...] ﴿And this is a Book We have sent down, blessed, so follow it and be mindful of Allah that you may receive mercy﴾ contains the call to follow the Qur'an, and describing it as blessed for whoever follows it and acts by it in this world and the Hereafter.

Ibn Jarir said: Its meaning is: "And this is a Book We have sent down so that you will not say: 'The Book was only sent down to two groups before us.'"

That is, so that their excuse may be cut off, as He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And if not that a misfortune should befall them for what their hands have sent forth, and they should say, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could follow Your verses and be among the believers?"﴾ [Al-Qasas: 47].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿upon two groups before us﴾, 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: they are the Jews and the Christians. Likewise said Mujahid, al-Suddi, Qatadah, and others.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And indeed we were unaware of their study﴾, meaning: we did not understand what they were saying, because they were not of our language, and we were, in addition to that, occupied and heedless of what they were engaged in.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Or you should say, "If the Book had been revealed to us, we would have been better guided than they."﴾, meaning: and We have cut off your pretext by which you would say: "If what was revealed to them had been revealed to us, we would have been better guided than them in what they were given," like His saying: ﴿And they swore by Allah their strongest oaths that if a warner came to them, they would be better guided than any of the nations. But when a warner came to them, it increased them only in aversion﴾ [Fatir: 42]. And so He says here: ﴿There has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord, and guidance and mercy﴾, meaning: There has certainly come to you from Allah, through the tongue of Muhammad (ﷺ), the Prophet of the Arabs, a great Qur'an, in which there is clarification of the lawful and the unlawful, and guidance for what is in the hearts, and mercy from Allah to His servants who follow it and act upon what is in it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So who is more unjust than one who denies the signs of Allah and turns away from them?﴾, meaning: he has not benefited from what the Messenger brought, nor followed what he was sent with, nor abandoned others; rather he turned away from following the signs of Allah, i.e., he diverted people and prevented them from that. This is what al-Suddi said.

And from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah: ﴿and turns away from them﴾ means: he turned away from them.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verse 158 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says, warning those who disbelieve in Him, who oppose His messengers, who deny His signs, and who turn people away from His path: ﴿Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them, or that your Lord should come?﴾ That will occur on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Or that some of the signs of your Lord should come [on the day when some of the signs of your Lord come]﴾ [[Addition from manuscript M.]] ... the verse. That will occur before the Day of Resurrection, as one of the signs (amarat) and portents (ashrat) of the Hour. Al-Bukhari said in his tafsir (exegesis) of this verse:

Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, 'Umarah narrated to us, Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Hour will not come until the sun rises from its place of setting. When people see it, everyone on earth will believe, and that is the time when ﴿faith will not benefit a soul that did not believe before﴾."

Ishaq narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Hour will not come until the sun rises from its place of setting. When it rises and people see it, they will all believe, and that is the time when faith will not benefit a soul." Then he recited this verse.

This hadith has been narrated through these two chains [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (4635), (4636).]]. Through the first chain, the rest of the compilers of the six books (al-Jama'ah) also narrated it in their books, except al-Tirmidhi, through several routes, from 'Umarah ibn al-Qa'qa' ibn Shubrumah, from Abu Zur'ah ibn [[In manuscript A: "from".]] 'Amr ibn Jarir, from Abu Hurayrah, with it [[Sahih Muslim, no. (157); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (4312); al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11177); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (4068).]].

As for the second chain, it was narrated from Ishaq, who is not identified by lineage. It is said he is Ibn Mansur al-Kawsaj, and it is said he is Ishaq ibn Nasr [[The hafiz Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari (8/297): "Khalaf asserted that he is Ibn Nasr, and Abu Mas'ud asserted that he is Ibn Mansur, and Khalaf's statement is stronger."]]. And Allah knows best.

Muslim also narrated it from Muhammad ibn Rafi' al-Nisaburi; both of them (Ishaq and Muhammad ibn Rafi') narrated from 'Abd al-Razzaq, with it [[Sahih Muslim, no. (157).]].

This hadith has also come through other routes from Abu Hurayrah. Muslim alone narrated it from the hadith of al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'qub, mawla (freedman) of al-Huraqah, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, with it [[Sahih Muslim, no. (157).]].

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three things, when they come forth, ﴿faith will not benefit a soul that did not believe before, or that had not earned good through its faith﴾: the rising of the sun from its place of setting, the Dajjal (the Antichrist), and the beast of the earth."

It was also narrated by Ahmad, from Waki', from Fudayl ibn Ghazwan, from Abu Hazim Salman, from Abu Hurayrah, with it, and in his version is: "and the smoke (al-dukhan)."

Muslim narrated it from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Harb, from Waki' [[Tafsir al-Tabari (12/265); al-Musnad (2/445); Sahih Muslim, no. (158).]].

Muslim and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it, through more than one route, from Fudayl ibn Ghazwan, with it [[Sahih Muslim, no. (158); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3072).]].

Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah al-Farawi narrated it from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah. However, none of the authors of the books narrated it through this route, because of the weakness of al-Farawi. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Rabi'ah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Hour will not come until the sun rises from its place of setting. When it rises, all people will believe, and that is the time when ﴿faith will not benefit a soul that did not believe before﴾," the verse [[Tafsir al-Tabari (12/255).]].

It was also narrated by Ibn Lahi'ah, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, with it. Waki' narrated it from Fudayl ibn Ghazwan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, with it.

The hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh collected all these routes in his tafsir.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever repents before the sun rises from its place of setting, his repentance will be accepted."

No one from the authors of the Six Books (al-Kutub al-Sittah) narrated it [[Tafsir al-Tabari (12/256); Ahmad in his Musnad (2/275) narrated it through 'Abd al-Razzaq with it.]].

Another hadith, from Abu Dharr al-Ghifari: in the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim) and others, through several routes, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid ibn Sharik al-Taymi, from his father, from Abu Dharr Jundub ibn Junadah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you know where the sun goes when it sets?" I said: "I do not know." He said: "It goes until it reaches beneath the Throne, then it prostrates, then it rises again, until it is said to it: 'Return,' and it is about to be said to it: 'Return from where you came.' That is the time when ﴿faith will not benefit a soul that did not believe before﴾" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4803); Sahih Muslim, no. (159).]].

Another hadith, from Hudhayfah ibn Asid Abu Sarihah al-Ghifari, may Allah be pleased with him:

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Furat, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Hudhayfah ibn Asid al-Ghifari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked down upon us from an upper room while we were discussing the Hour, and he said: "The Hour will not come until you see ten signs: the rising of the sun from its place of setting, the smoke (al-dukhan), the beast, the emergence of Gog and Magog (Ya'juj and Ma'juj), the emergence of 'Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus, son of Mary), the Dajjal, and three eclipses: an eclipse in the west, an eclipse in the east, and an eclipse in the Arabian Peninsula; and a fire that will come out from the bottom of 'Adan, driving (or gathering) the people. It will spend the night with them wherever they spend the night, and take its midday rest with them wherever they rest at midday."

Muslim and the authors of the four Sunan narrated it in this way [[Al-Musnad (4/7); Sahih Muslim, no. (2901); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (4311); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2183); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (4041).]], from the hadith of Furat al-Qazzaz, from Abu al-Tufayl 'Amir ibn Wathilah, from Hudhayfah ibn Asid, with it. Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih (good and sound).

Another hadith, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may Allah be pleased with him:

al-Thawri said, from Mansur, from Ribi, from Hudhayfah, who said: I asked the Prophet [[In manuscript A: "Messenger of Allah".]] (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the sign of the sun's rising from its place of setting?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "That night will be prolonged until it is as long as two nights. While those who used to pray during it are doing what they used to do before it, and the stars do not move, and they have stayed in their places, then they sleep and wake up and pray, then sleep and wake up again, and their sides are stretched out on them, until the night lengthens over them, and people become frightened and do not see the morning. Then, while they are waiting for the sun to rise from its east, it rises from its west. When people see it, they will believe, but their faith will not benefit them."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it, and it is not in the Six Books through this route [[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-La'ali' al-Masnu'ah (1/31). Ibn Mardawayh said: "Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Razi narrated to us, Idris ibn 'Ali al-Razi narrated to us, Yahya ibn al-Darris narrated to us, from Sufyan al-Thawri," and he mentioned it.]]. And Allah knows best.

Another hadith, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, whose name is Sa'd ibn Malik ibn Sinan, may Allah be pleased with him and be pleased with him:

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Ibn Abi Layla narrated to us, from 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, faith will not benefit a soul﴾ he said: "The rising of the sun from its place of setting."

al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Sufyan ibn Waki', from his father, with it. He said: gharib (unusual). Some of them narrated it without attributing it to the Prophet (ﷺ) [[Al-Musnad (3/31); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3071). Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it in al-Musannaf (15/179) through Waki', from Ibn Abi Layla, with it, as a statement of a Companion (mawquf).]].

In the hadith of Talut ibn 'Abbad, from Fadal ibn Jubayr, from Abu Umamah Suday ibn 'Ajlan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first of the signs is the rising of the sun from its place of setting." [[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, as in Majma' al-Zawa'id (8/9). Al-Haythami said: "In its chain is Fadal ibn Jubayr, who is weak, and this hadith has been denounced."]].

In the hadith of 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Safwan ibn 'Assal, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed, Allah has opened a door before the west, its width is seventy years, for repentance." He said: "It will not be closed until the sun rises from it." Al-Tirmidhi narrated it and authenticated it, al-Nasa'i authenticated it, and Ibn Majah narrated it in a long hadith [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3536); Sunan al-Nasa'i (1/83); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (4070).]].

Another hadith, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa:

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Duhaym narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, Dirar ibn Surd narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Zayd, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "A night will come upon the people that equals three of your nights. When that happens, those who perform voluntary prayers will know it. One of them will stand and recite his portion (hizb) of the Qur'an, then sleep, then stand and recite his portion, then sleep. While they are in this state, people will shout to one another, saying, 'What is this?' They will run to the mosques, and suddenly the sun has risen from its place of setting. The people will cry out in one voice, until it reaches the middle of the sky, then it returns and rises from its rising-place." He said: "At that time, ﴿faith will not benefit a soul﴾."

This is a gharib (unusual) hadith through this route [[Also narrated by 'Abd ibn Humayd, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (3/392).]], and it is not in any of the Six Books.

Another hadith, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr [[In manuscript A: "'Umar".]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 6, verse 158 (part 2 of 2):

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu Hayyan narrated to us, from Abu Zur'ah ibn 'Amr ibn Jarir, who said: Three men from among the Muslims sat with Marwan in Madinah, and they heard him say, while he was speaking about the signs: "The first of them is the emergence of the Dajjal." He said: The men went to 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr and told him what they had heard from Marwan about the signs. So 'Abdullah said: "Marwan has not said anything. I have memorised from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a hadith concerning such matters, which I have not forgotten. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'The first of the signs to emerge will be the rising of the sun from its west and the emergence of the Beast in the forenoon. Whichever of them occurs first, the other will follow soon after it.'" Then 'Abdullah said, and he used to read the earlier scriptures: "I think the first of them to emerge is the rising of the sun from its west, for whenever it sets, it goes beneath the Throne, prostrates, and asks permission to return. Permission is granted to it to return. Then, when Allah wills that it should rise from its west, it does as it used to do: it comes beneath the Throne, prostrates, and asks permission to return, but nothing is answered to it. Then it asks permission to return, and nothing is answered to it. Then it asks permission, and nothing is answered to it, until, when a portion of the night has passed that Allah wills to pass, and it knows that if permission is granted to it to return it will not reach the east, it says: 'My Lord, how far is the east! Who will take care of the people for me?' Until, when the horizon becomes like a collar, it asks permission to return, and it is said to it: 'Remain where you are and rise.' So it rises upon the people from its west." Then 'Abdullah recited this verse: ﴿The faith of a soul will not benefit it if it had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith﴾, to the end of the verse.

Muslim included it in his Sahih, and Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah in their Sunan, from the hadith of Abu Hayyan al-Taymi, whose name is Yahya ibn Sa'id ibn Hayyan, from Abu Zur'ah ibn 'Amr ibn Jarir, with it.

Another hadith from him:
al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Khalid ibn Hayyan al-Raqqi narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Zibriq al-Himsi narrated to us, 'Uthman ibn Sa'id ibn Kathir ibn Dinar narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Hayyi ibn 'Abdullah, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "When the sun rises from its west, Iblis will fall prostrate, calling out and crying aloud: 'My Lord, command me to prostrate to whomever You wish.'" He said: "Then his helpers will gather around him and say: 'O their master, what is this supplication?' He will say: 'I only asked my Lord to grant me respite until the appointed time, and this is the appointed time.'" He said: "Then the beast of the earth will emerge from a crack in al-Safa." He said: "The first step it takes will be at Antioch, and it will come to Iblis and strike him..."

This is a very strange hadith and its chain is weak. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/8): "In it is Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Zibriq, who is weak." It may be from the two loads of books that 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr lost at the Battle of Yarmuk. As for its attribution to the Prophet ﷺ, it is munkar (rejected). And Allah knows best.

Another hadith from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, and Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, may Allah be pleased with them all:
Imam Ahmad said: al-Hakam ibn Nafi' narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Damdam ibn Zur'ah, from Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd, tracing it back to Malik ibn Yukhamir, from Ibn al-Sa'di, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Emigration does not cease as long as the enemy is fighting." Then Mu'awiyah, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, and 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Emigration consists of two qualities: one of them is abandoning evil deeds, and the other is emigrating to Allah and His Messenger. It does not cease so long as repentance is accepted, and repentance will remain accepted until the sun rises from the west. When it rises, a seal is placed upon every heart according to what it contains, and people are relieved of works." This hadith has a sound chain (hasan al-isnad), and none of the authors of the six books has recorded it. And Allah knows best.

Another hadith from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him:
'Awf al-A'rabi said, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: Abu 'Ubaydah narrated to me, from Ibn Mas'ud, that he used to say: "All the signs that have been mentioned have passed except four: the rising of the sun from its west, the Dajjal, the beast of the earth, and the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj." He said: And he used to say: "The verse with which deeds will be sealed is the rising of the sun from its west. Do you not see that Allah says: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, the faith of a soul will not benefit it...﴾, the whole verse, meaning the rising of the sun from its west." Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (12/260).

Hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both:
Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his Tafsir from the hadith of 'Abd al-Mun'im ibn Idris, from his father, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, from Ibn 'Abbas [may Allah be pleased with him], as a marfu' report, in which he mentioned a long and strange hadith, whose attribution to the Prophet is munkar. In it: "The sun and the moon will rise on that day joined together, and when they reach the middle of the sky they will return, then go back to what they were upon." It is a very strange hadith, indeed munkar, indeed mawdu' (fabricated), if it is claimed to be marfu'. As for its being mawquf (stopping) at Ibn 'Abbas or Wahb ibn Munabbih, which is more likely, that is not rejected. And Allah knows best.

Sufyan said, from Mansur, from 'Amir, from 'A'ishah [may Allah be pleased with her], who said: "When the first of the signs emerges, the pens will be cast aside, the guardian angels will be detained, and the bodies will bear witness to the deeds." Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

As for His saying [Mighty and Majestic is He]: ﴿The faith of a soul will not benefit it if it had not believed before﴾, meaning: if a disbeliever brings about faith on that day, it will not be accepted from him. As for one who was a believer before that, if he was righteous in his deeds, he has great good; and if he was mixed (in his deeds) and then made repentance at that time, his repentance will not be accepted from him, as the previous hadiths indicate. It is in this light that His saying, the Exalted, should be understood: ﴿or had not earned good through its faith﴾, meaning: nor will any deed of righteousness be accepted from it if it had not been doing it before that.

* *

His saying: ﴿Say: Wait, indeed we are waiting﴾ is a severe threat to the disbelievers and a firm warning to whoever delays his faith and repentance until a time when that will no longer benefit him. The ruling was only this at the rising of the sun from its west, due to the approach of the Hour and the appearance of its portents, as He said: ﴿Do they await anything but the Hour, that it come upon them suddenly? But its portents have already come. So how will they have their reminder when it has come to them?﴾ [Muhammad: 18]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So when they saw Our might, they said: "We believe in Allah alone, and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him." But their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might. (This is) the way of Allah which has passed among His servants, and the disbelievers were lost therein﴾ [Ghafir: 84-85].

Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: This verse was revealed about the Jews and the Christians.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects﴾. He said: That is because the Jews and the Christians differed before Muhammad ﷺ was sent, and they split apart. Then when Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ, He revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects, you have no part in them whatsoever﴾, and so on.

Ibn Jarir said: Sa'd ibn 'Amr al-Sakuni narrated to me, Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated to us: 'Abbad ibn Kathir wrote to me, Layth narrated to me, from Tawus, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, in this nation are ﴿those who have divided their religion and become sects, you have no part in them whatsoever﴾; and they are not from you. They are the people of innovations, the people of doubtful matters, and the people of misguidance from this nation."

However, this chain is not authentic, for 'Abbad ibn Kathir is abandoned in hadith (matruk al-hadith). He did not fabricate this hadith, but he erred in raising it (to the Prophet ﷺ). Sufyan al-Thawri narrated it from Layth - who is Ibn Abi Sulaym - from Tawus, from Abu Hurayrah, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects﴾, and said: It was revealed about this nation.

Abu Ghalib narrated from Abu Umamah regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who have divided their religion [and become sects]﴾, and said: They are the Kharijites. It is also narrated from him as a marfu' report, but it is not authentic.

Shu'bah narrated from Mujalid, from al-Sha'bi, from Shurayh, from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to 'A'ishah: ﴿Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects﴾, and said: "They are the people of innovations."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated this, and it is also strange (gharib), and its raising (to the Prophet ﷺ) is not authentic.

The apparent meaning is that the verse is general, covering everyone who separates from the religion of Allah and opposes it. Allah sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion, and his law is one, with no difference or division in it. So whoever differs regarding it ﴿and become sects﴾, meaning factions, like the people of creeds and sects (al-milal wa'l-nihal, i.e., religious communities and schools of thought), which are desires and misguidances, then Allah has absolved His Messenger of what they are in. This verse is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He has ordained for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus: that you establish the religion and do not be divided therein﴾ [al-Shura: 13], and in the hadith: "We, the company of the Prophets, are sons of one father (awlad 'Allat); our religion is one."

This is the straight path, which is what the Messengers brought: worshipping Allah alone, without partner, and adhering to the law of the last Messenger. Whatever contradicts that is misguidance, ignorance, opinions and desires, from which the Messengers are free, as He said: ﴿you have no part in them whatsoever﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿Their affair is only with Allah; then He will inform them of what they used to do﴾ is like His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews and the Sabeans and the Christians and the Magians and those who associated [others with Allah] - indeed, Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is over all things Witness﴾ [al-Hajj: 17], then He explained His bounty on the Day of Resurrection in His judgment and justice, saying:

This noble verse explains in detail what was stated in general terms in another verse, namely His saying: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like of it﴾ [al-Anam: 160]... 

Wait, the verse cited in the text is ﴿مَنْ جَاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ خَيْرٌ مِنْهَا﴾ [an-Naml: 89], which means: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it﴾ [an-Naml: 89].

Here is the full translation:

This noble verse explains in detail what was stated in general terms in another verse, namely His saying: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it﴾ [an-Naml: 89]. Traditions have been reported that agree with this verse, as Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Affan related to us: Ja'far ibn Sulayman related to us: al-Ja'd Abu Uthman related to us, from Abu Raja' al-Utaridi, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), what he relates from his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is Merciful. Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, a good deed is recorded for him; if he does it, ten to seven hundred is recorded for him, up to many multiples. And whoever intends an evil deed but does not do it, a good deed is recorded for him; if he does it, one is recorded for him, or Allah erases it, Mighty and Majestic. And none perishes before Allah except one who is destined to perish."

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and al-Nasa'i related it from the hadith of al-Ja'd ibn Abi Uthman, with the same wording. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6491) and Sahih Muslim no. (131).]

Imam Ahmad also said: Mu'awiyah related to us: al-A'mash related to us, from al-Ma'rur ibn Suwayd, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: Whoever does a good deed, for him is ten times its like and more. Whoever does an evil deed, its recompense is its like, or I forgive. Whoever comes to Me with the earth's full measure of sin, then meets Me without associating anything with Me, I will give him its like in forgiveness. Whoever draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit; whoever draws near to Me a cubit, I draw near to him a fathom; and whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him running."

Muslim related it from Abu Kurayb, from Abu Mu'awiyah, with the same. And from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Waki', from al-A'mash, with the same. [al-Musnad (5/153) and Sahih Muslim no. (2687).] Ibn Majah related it from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi, from Waki', with the same. [Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3821).]

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Shayban related to us, Hammad related to us, Thabit related to us, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, a good deed is recorded for him; if he does it, ten are recorded for him. And whoever intends an evil deed but does not do it, nothing is recorded against him; if he does it, one evil deed is recorded against him." [Musnad Abi Ya'la (6/170); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/145): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

Know that the one who abandons an evil deed, not doing it, is of three types. Sometimes he leaves it for Allah, Mighty and Majestic; for him a good deed is recorded because of his restraint from it for the sake of Allah the Exalted. This is both an action and an intention; therefore it has come that a good deed is recorded for him, as occurs in some wordings of the Sahih: "He only left it because of Me," i.e., for My sake. Sometimes he leaves it through forgetfulness and heedlessness of it; this one has neither credit nor liability, because he did not intend good nor did he do evil. Sometimes he leaves it through inability and laziness after striving toward its causes and engaging in what brings him close to it; this one is treated as its doer, as came in the hadith in the two Sahihs: "When two Muslims confront each other with their swords, both the killer and the killed are in the Fire." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is the killer, but what about the killed?" He said: "He was eager to kill his companion." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (31) and Sahih Muslim no. (2888), from the hadith of Abu Bakrah Nufay' ibn al-Harith, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Imam Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Mujahid ibn Musa related to us, Ali related to us, and al-Hasan ibn al-Sabbah and Abu Khaythamah related to us, both said: Ishaq ibn Sulayman related to us, both from Musa ibn Ubaydah, from Abu Bakr ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Anas, from his grandfather Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever intends a good deed, Allah records a good deed for him; if he does it, ten are recorded for him. And whoever intends an evil deed, it is not recorded against him until he does it; if he does it, one evil deed is recorded against him; if he abandons it, a good deed is recorded for him. Allah the Exalted says: He only left it out of fear of Me."

This is the wording of the hadith of Mujahid—i.e., Ibn Musa. [Mentioned by al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar in al-Matalib al-Aliyah (3/218) and attributed to Abu Ya'la; its chain contains Musa ibn Ubaydah al-Rabadhi, who is weak.]

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, Shayban ibn Abd al-Rahman related to us, from al-Rukayn ibn al-Rabi', from his father, from his paternal uncle Fulan ibn Amilah, from Khuraym ibn Fatik al-Asadi, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "People are of four kinds, and deeds are of six. As for people: one whose provision is expanded in this world and the Hereafter; one whose provision is expanded in this world but restricted in the Hereafter; one whose provision is restricted in this world but expanded in the Hereafter; and one who is wretched in this world and the Hereafter. As for deeds: there are two that are inevitable, and equal-for-equal, and ten-fold, and seven hundred-fold. The two inevitable ones: whoever dies as a Muslim, a believer, not associating anything with Allah, the Garden is obligatory for him; whoever dies a disbeliever, the Fire is obligatory for him. Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, Allah knows that he has made it dear to his heart and eagerly desired it, so a good deed is recorded for him. Whoever intends an evil deed, it is not recorded against him; and whoever does it, one is recorded and it is not multiplied against him. Whoever does a good deed, for him it is ten times its like. Whoever spends in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, it is for him seven hundred-fold." [al-Musnad (4/345).]

al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i related it from the hadith of al-Rukayn ibn al-Rabi', from his father, from Bashir ibn Amilah, from Khuraym ibn Fatik, with part of it. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1625) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11027). al-Tirmidhi said: "The hadith is also reported from Abu Hurayrah; this is a good hadith, and we only know it from the hadith of al-Rukayn ibn al-Rabi'."] And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah related to us, Ubayd Allah ibn Umar al-Qawariri related to us, Yazid ibn Zurayʿ related to us, Habib al-Mu'allim related to us, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Three men attend the Friday prayer: a man who attends with idle talk, so that is his share of it; a man who attends and supplicates, so he is a man who calls upon Allah—if He wills He gives him, and if He wills He withholds from him; and a man who attends with attentive listening and silence, does not step over the neck of a Muslim, and does not harm anyone—so it is an expiation for him until the next Friday, and three additional days. That is because Allah says: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like of it﴾." [Abu Dawud no. (1113) and Ibn Khuzaymah in his Sahih no. (1813), by way of Yazid ibn Zurayʿ.]

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Hashim ibn Marthad related to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, my father related to me, Damdam ibn Zur'ah related to me, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Friday is an expiation for what is between it and the Friday that follows it, and three additional days; that is because Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like of it﴾." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/298); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (2/173): "It contains Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash from his father; Abu Hatim said: he did not hear from his father anything."]

And from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever fasts three days of every month, it is as if he has fasted the whole of time."

Imam Ahmad related it—and this is his wording—as did al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah and al-Tirmidhi [al-Musnad (5/145); Sunan al-Nasa'i (4/219); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1708); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (762)], adding: "Then Allah revealed in His Book confirmation of that: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like of it﴾—today, ten days." Then he said: This is a good hadith.

Ibn Mas'ud said: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like of it﴾ means whoever brings "There is no god but Allah." ﴿And whoever brings an evil deed﴾ means, he says: with shirk.

Similar has been reported from a group of the early generations (al-salaf).

A raised (marfu') hadith has also been reported concerning this—Allah knows its authenticity, but I have not seen it through a sound route. The hadiths and reports on this are very numerous, and what has been mentioned is sufficient, Allah willing, and in Him is trust.

Allah says, [commanding His Prophet ﷺ, the master of the messengers, to inform (people) of the blessing Allah has bestowed upon him: the guidance to His straight path, which has no crookedness or deviation in it]: ﴿A correct religion, the creed of Abraham, a man of pure faith, and he was not of the polytheists﴾, meaning: upright and firm. [It is] like His saying: ﴿And who would turn away from the creed of Abraham except one who makes a fool of himself?﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 130], and His saying: ﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty. [It is] the creed of your father Abraham﴾ [Al-Hajj: 78], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah, a man of pure faith, and he was not of the polytheists. [He was] grateful for His favors. He chose him and guided him to a straight path. And We gave him good in this world, and indeed he, in the Hereafter, is among the righteous. Then We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], to follow the creed of Abraham, a man of pure faith, and he was not of the polytheists﴾ [An-Nahl: 120–123].

It does not necessarily follow from his (ﷺ) being commanded to follow the upright creed of Abraham that Abraham was more perfect than him in it. This is because he (ﷺ) upheld it with a great uprightness, and it was completed for him in a complete perfection that no one before him attained. Therefore he was the Seal of the Prophets, the master of the descendants of Adam without exception, and the possessor of the Praiseworthy Station, to which all creation will turn (in desire), even Abraham the Friend of Allah, upon him be peace.
