Allah says: "Say," O Muhammad, to these polytheists who associate others with Allah in sincerely directing worship to Him and in placing trust in Him: "Shall I seek a lord other than Allah?" That is, shall I seek a lord besides Him, when He is the Lord of everything, who nurtures me, protects me, watches over me and manages my affairs? That is, I will not place my trust in anyone but Him, nor turn in repentance to anyone but Him, because He is the Lord and Sovereign of everything, and to Him belong the creation and the command.

This verse contains the command to sincerely place one's trust in Allah, just as the verse before it contained the sincere devotion of worship to Him, with no partner. These two meanings are often mentioned together in the Qur'an, as when Allah instructs His servants to say: "You alone do we worship, and You alone do we ask for help" (al-Fatihah 1:5); and His saying: "So worship Him and put your trust in Him" (Hud 11:123); and His saying: "Say: He is the Most Merciful; we have believed in Him and upon Him we have relied" (al-Mulk 67:29); and His saying: "Lord of the East and the West; there is no god but Him, so take Him as a guardian" (al-Muzzammil 73:9); and similar verses.

* *

As for His saying: "And no soul earns [blame] except against itself, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another" (6:164), this is a report of what will happen on the Day of Resurrection, concerning Allah's recompense, His judgment and His justice: that souls are only repaid for their deeds, good for good and evil for evil, and that no one's sin is carried by another. This is part of His justice, as He said: "And if a heavy-laden soul calls [another] to its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a close relative" (Fatir 35:18). And His saying: "He will not fear injustice or diminution" (Ta-Ha 20:112). The scholars of tafsir (ʿulama al-tafsir) said: he will not be wronged by having the evil deeds of others laid upon him, nor will he be diminished by having some of his good deeds reduced. And Allah said: "Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned, except the companions of the right" (al-Muddaththir 74:38-39). Its meaning: every soul is held in pledge by its evil deed, except the companions of the right, for the blessings of their righteous deeds may extend to their offspring. As He said in Surah al-Tur: "And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith — We will join them with their descendants, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds" (al-Tur 52:21). That is, We will join their descendants with them in the lofty station in Paradise, even if the descendants did not share in their deeds but only in the root of faith. "And We will not deprive them" means: We will not diminish those noble, elevated ones in their deeds at all, so as to make them equal to those of lower rank; rather, Allah raises them to the station of their fathers by the blessing of their deeds, by His grace and favor. Then He said: "Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned" (al-Tur 52:21), meaning: for evil.

* *

As for His saying: "Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about that over which you used to differ" (6:164): that is, act according to your position, for we are acting according to what we are upon; you will be presented [before Him] and we will be presented before Him, and He will inform us and you of our deeds and your deeds, and of that about which we used to differ in the worldly abode, as Allah said: "Say: You will not be asked about what we committed in sin, nor will we be asked about what you do. Say: Our Lord will bring us together, then He will judge between us with truth, and He is the Judge, the All-Knowing" (Saba' 34:25-26).

Allah says: ﴿It is He who has made you successors (khala'if) upon the earth﴾, meaning: He has made you inhabit the earth generation after generation, and century after century, one predecessor after another. This was said by Ibn Zayd and others, as in His saying: ﴿And if We willed, We would have made from you angels upon the earth succeeding (one another)﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 60], and His saying: ﴿and makes you successors of the earth﴾ [An-Naml: 62], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority (khalifah)﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 30], and His saying: ﴿It may be that your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors upon the earth, and then He will observe how you act﴾ [Al-A'raf: 129].

And His saying: ﴿and has raised some of you above others in degrees﴾, meaning: He has differentiated among you in provision, in character, in good and bad qualities, in appearance, in forms and in colors, and He has wisdom in that, as in His saying: ﴿We have divided among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and We have raised some of them above others in degrees so that some of them may take others in service﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 32], and His saying [Exalted is He] [[Addition from manuscript A.]]: ﴿Look how We have preferred some of them over others; and the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference﴾ [Al-Isra': 21].

And His saying: ﴿to test you in what He has given you﴾, meaning: to test you regarding that with which He has blessed you and tried you. He tests the rich in his wealth, asking him about his gratitude, and the poor in his poverty, asking him about his patience.

Muslim related in his Sahih, from the hadith of Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, this world is sweet and green, and indeed Allah makes you successors in it, that He may observe how you act. So beware of the world, and beware of women, for indeed the first trial of the Children of Israel was with women." [Sahih Muslim, no. (2742)].

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ is both a warning (tarhib) and an encouragement (targhib): His reckoning and punishment are swift for whoever disobeys Him and opposes His messengers, ﴿and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ toward whoever allies with Him and follows His messengers in what they brought of good and seeking.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The servants are shown mercy according to what is in them. Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

Allah often joins these two attributes together in the Qur'an, as He said [Exalted is He] [[Addition from manuscript A.]]: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾ [Al-Hijr: 49-50], and [His saying] [[Addition from manuscript A.]]: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing, but indeed your Lord is severe in penalty﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 6], and other verses containing encouragement and warning. Sometimes He calls His servants to Himself with desire, describing Paradise and what is with Him, and sometimes He calls them with fear, mentioning the Fire, its shackles and punishment, and the Resurrection and its terrors, and sometimes with both, so that it may take effect in each according to its measure. May Allah make us among those who obey Him in what He commands, leave what He forbids and restrains, and believe Him in what He informs, for He is Near, Responsive, Hearer of supplication, Generous, Bountiful, the Giver.

Imam Ahmad said: Abdur-Rahman narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, from al-Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurairah [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If the believer knew what is with Allah of punishment, no one would hope for Paradise; and if the disbeliever knew what is with Allah of mercy, no one would despair of Paradise. Allah created one hundred mercies, and He placed one of them among His creation, by which they show mercy to one another, and with Allah are ninety-nine."

At-Tirmidhi related it from Qutaybah, from Abd al-Aziz al-Darawardi, from al-Ala' with it, and said: Hasan [Sahih] [[Addition from manuscript A.]]. Muslim related it from Yahya ibn Yahya, Qutaybah and Ali ibn Hujr, all three from Isma'il ibn Ja'far, from al-Ala' [[Al-Musnad (2/484), Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (3542), and Muslim in his Sahih no. (2752) narrated from Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah and Ibn Hujr, from Isma'il ibn Ja'far with it.]].

[End of the commentary on Surah al-An'am, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace]
